Malayalam source paragraphs GV1:P0001 to GV1:P0023
English line for line; each paragraph carries its Malayalam source number.

[GV1:P0001] Guruvani

[GV1:P0002] April 1977

[GV1:P0003] Question: When there is devotion, many extraneous thoughts that are incompatible with devotion also tend to arise. What is the reason for this?

[GV1:P0004] Answer: No matter how extraneous thoughts arise, they will not be able to overcome true devotion. Devotion is the perfection of love. The nature of true devotion is to view one's chosen deity or guru as God. Above all, a person who desires the love of God may have to experience extreme sorrows from the deity or the trusted guru. On such occasions, one should find peace in the thought that all this is meant to cleanse the impurities arising from one's sinful karma, and must remain steadfast in love again and again. If one observes the sacrifice of such an individual, it will not even appear as a sacrifice. This is because he is able to perceive all sorrows as full of love and as nectarine. The love he develops towards all living beings will depend on the nature of his surrender to God.

[GV1:P0005] Question: Why do such people experience sorrow from others?

[GV1:P0006] Answer: Sorrow must occur. It is meant to come. Even if he is convinced that everything he does is good, if the people around him readily accept it, he would never know what sorrow is.

[GV1:P0007] Question: He is only doing such good deeds, isn't he? Then why does he have to experience sorrow?

[GV1:P0008] Answer: That is true. Firstly, without experiencing some sorrow, he cannot understand what sacrifice is. If he did not have sorrow, the very concept of sacrifice could not exist in this human world. Or suppose it happens to him without any sorrow; would he be able to understand the sorrow of another person? In that case, he can neither learn through his own experience nor understand the sorrow of others.

[GV1:P0009] Question: What exactly should be the complete nature of a true devotee?

[GV1:P0010] Answer: The nature of a true devotee is exactly what was mentioned above. However, let me elaborate further. His greatest asset is maintaining the purity of character to hate nothing and to perceive everything with love. Acknowledging any sorrow, behaving affectionately, and transforming it into one's own experience by deeply understanding it. This implies that he himself becomes the seat of both sorrow and happiness. Perceiving the earth as a bed of flowers. Viewing deep forests filled with stones and thorns as beautiful gardens. The profound experience he gets upon reaching such a place—he will then relish all the beauty of the world. Through that, he might even perceive God. Thus, the fulfilled mind that sees God in everything can be summed up in a single term: supreme wisdom.

[GV1:P0011] Question: If so, what do you say is the nature of true devotion?

[GV1:P0012] Answer: Everything else is merely for the fulfillment of various desires. All of this will ultimately lead to disappointment.

[GV1:P0013] Question: Just because devotion has been somewhat compromised, why should it lead to sorrow?

[GV1:P0014] Answer: Sorrow did not arise because there was a compromise in devotion. It is because the mountain of their desires has collapsed.

[GV1:P0015] Question: He might not have desired it; isn't it merely that a deficiency occurred in his devotion?

[GV1:P0016] Answer: That is true. Haven't you seen it? The kind of devotion where people stand in front of temples and burst into tears. Do you know in how many different ways they cry?

[GV1:P0017] Question: How does a devotee experience numerous such outbursts of crying?

[GV1:P0018] Answer: Excellent. It is unlikely that anyone else cries as much as a devotee does. Even a true devotee experiences a great deal of crying; then, for a devotee who compromises, it will be a multitude of tears.

[GV1:P0019] Question: If that is the case, devotion is not good, is it? Won't devotion only leave time for crying?

[GV1:P0020] Answer: I told you earlier that a true devotee does not cry.

[GV1:P0021] Question: But you also mentioned that a true devotee experiences a lot of crying. You spoke in a contradictory manner at the same time. It would be good if you could explain this.

[GV1:P0022] Answer: A true devotee beholds the form of his chosen deity in all animate and inanimate beings with utmost joy. Then, unknowingly, he is moved to tears by the love he feels upon experiencing the glory of God. Thus, a devotee who has realized this in various ways will cry out of love. Despite doing all this, when those who lack the wisdom to comprehend this love sadden him by spreading false tales about him, he may also weep thinking, "They are hurting me out of ignorance; doesn't God see this?"

[GV1:P0023] Guruvani

============================================================

GURUVANIKAL · May 1977 · Volume 1
Malayalam source paragraphs GV1:P0024 to GV1:P0043
English line for line; each paragraph carries its Malayalam source number.

[GV1:P0024] May 1977

[GV1:P0025] Question: You mentioned that for a true devotee, sorrow is nectarine. So, when a guru experiences sorrows from ordinary people, should the guru grieve over it?

[GV1:P0026] Answer: No. Mothers often cry when their child falls ill. However, they do not throw the child away. There are times when a mother, wife, or husband has to nurse their loved ones through great sorrow. Because of that, no one severs that relationship. Just because a boil appears on the body, one does not discard that body part. All this teaches us that we must endure sorrow to reclaim love. Only such love can transform into something divine.

[GV1:P0027] Question: In what forms do the tests from a guru appear?

[GV1:P0028] Answer: Firstly, the guru will adopt measures to increase their knowledge. If the disciple lacks the understanding to comprehend and act accordingly, it will inevitably create a massive distance. Then, the disciple might perceive it as pain or as a test.

[GV1:P0029] Question: This guru-disciple relationship is one where both the guru and the disciple act with mutual understanding, isn't it? Then why is this gap created?

[GV1:P0030] Answer: In a workshop, school, or college, do all the students pass the exam? No. What was taught to them was not flawed. What was demonstrated was also exactly the same for everyone. Similarly, among the students of Brahma Vidya (divine knowledge) and Sidha Vidya, the teachings may not yield identical results for everyone. That is why this gap is created.

[GV1:P0031] Question: It is recorded in certain Puranas that the guru and the disciple will act with mutual understanding, isn't it? Why is it recorded that way?

[GV1:P0032] Answer: The same explanation given earlier applies to this as well. Just because they have understood the guru, it does not mean everyone will act in the same way.

[GV1:P0033] Question: Suppose a person without intellect or capability develops devotion—what should he do?

[GV1:P0034] Answer: It is much easier for him to sustain his devotion than the people mentioned earlier. Since he lacks capability, he will not try to deeply scrutinize anything. He desires to maintain his devotion and affection by offering service in accordance with what he observes.

[GV1:P0035] Question: Then, will he reach the ultimate reality?

[GV1:P0036] Answer: He does not think about whether he will reach the ultimate reality or not. He only considers whether there is any merit in what he is doing. That will be serving him in accordance with his intellect and experience. So, isn't he the smart one!

[GV1:P0037] Question: Suppose a girl develops such true devotion. How will she fulfill it?

[GV1:P0038] Answer: Do you assume that a girl is not a human being?

[GV1:P0039] Question: It is said that girls are not allowed to participate in such devotional matters during certain times. That is why I asked.

[GV1:P0040] Answer: Is it something you have heard, or something you have read?

[GV1:P0041] Question: That is what is heard and is the widely held belief.

[GV1:P0042] Answer: What you have heard is merely the chatter of ignorant people. The belief also originated in the same way. History records that many sages lived among us Hindus. History proves that most of the sages were accompanied by women. It is only among some yogis that we do not see women residing with them. There is no mention of Shuka getting married or living with women. Neither is there any such mention about Narada. We do not see it concerning Bhogar, the guru of Subramanya, either. But Bhogar is not described as someone with diminished lust; he is a siddha and a wise man.

[GV1:P0043] Kulapathi Speaks

============================================================

GURUVANIKAL · May 1977 · Volume 1
Malayalam source paragraphs GV1:P0044 to GV1:P0063

[GV1:P0044] May 1977

[GV1:P0045] Dear ones,

[GV1:P0046] The religion I believe in is one of friendship, brotherhood, and truth. Neither I nor my mission desire to move toward a path of self-destruction by blindly believing in anything and standing divided. There are rays of love in everyone, and I wish for everyone to live in harmony and happiness. For this purpose, I perform my duties. I desire to bring you to my path, to the way that has evolved from my penance. I consider that as one of my goals.

[GV1:P0047] Let me now clarify what my paths are. Today, our entire society is polluted. Standing divided, it is moving towards the abyss of destruction every moment. No one has any certainty about where to go or in which direction. What we see is everyone staring at each other blankly. What is the solution to this? That is what needs to be found. Many face various hardships and destroy themselves. They are reeling under incurable, fatal diseases. Economic instability stares many in the face. Thus, I see a large multitude of a deeply disturbed human society around me. They have no idea what to do. Brothers and sisters who consider this human birth a curse, I have only one thing to say to you: I am willing to bestow my strength upon you.

[GV1:P0048] What is the power within me? I know many of you will ask this very question. I shall explain it in detail. My power has been acquired through ceaseless penance. For years, I performed austerities for it. I endured sacrifices. Those sacrifices made me who I am, and they dissolved my very self. You might wish to know where it comes from and what it is. That is natural. Before clarifying that, I wish to take you to our heritage, to the spiritual essence of India.

[GV1:P0049] If one looks into the spiritual eminence of India, it can be seen that a small group of great sages worked with the welfare of humanity as their goal. Through their penance, they elevated our Hindu culture across various stages. Swami Vivekananda and Sri Ramakrishna Paramahamsa were all resplendent luminaries of that tradition. Not many have been able to walk their path. Leaving that aside, let us come to our Kerala.

[GV1:P0050] Three eminent sages were born here. The first one who rushes to our memory among them is Sankaracharya. The other two are Sri Narayana Guru and Chattampi Swamikal. Their blessings have forever enriched our little Kerala. We continue to see its movements. However, as eras pass, many changes are occurring in the minds of the people. A situation has been created where it is difficult for generations to come forward holding firm to those directives. There is no point in blaming anyone for that. It is something that happens, and it is liable to happen.

[GV1:P0051] The necessity to provide guidance to the people at various periods is increasing immensely today. Only that will bring them peace. Behind the survival of Christianity and Islam, there has been such guidance. Many interpret it in various ways and present it in new forms and expressions. People find it impossible in the present times to blindly cling to old doctrines. The resurrection of these splinter groups is the ultimate consequence of this.

[GV1:P0052] This does not end here. As an unending process, it will continue to exist as long as humans are on the face of this earth. Each religion undergoes different kinds of changes. But its fundamental tenets may not necessarily change. Even so, what I am indicating is that it will take shape in accordance with the era.

[GV1:P0053] In this context, I invite your attention to the problems of Hinduism. Hinduism stands like a massive tree. It has numerous branches. Are there not further branches within those branches? Thus, all of it stands distorted and mutually disconnected. There is a lot to be said about the problems of Hinduism. I believe that what has crystallized within me today is a form derived from years of contemplation regarding this. I have been able to see, hear, and experience many things.

[GV1:P0054] All those are heart-melting incidents of prolonged suffering. My conscience ached at the thought of our society's degradation. From that pain and sorrow, I was able to generate a special vitality. Even as a very young child, I was suppressed by its power. I approached many places for the clarification of doubts, and I understood many things. Finally, the journey towards my goal began. The sacrifice I undertook to reach that goal has made me who I am today.

[GV1:P0055] A time when caste-based sectarianism reigned supreme. I was not imagining that era; I was witnessing it directly. Seeing that, a fire blazed in my mind. There were many instances when I felt that I myself would be consumed by that burning fire. There, I found someone. I became his disciple. I was able to learn a lot from that Guru. When I say that it was solely due to my endurance, do not misunderstand. I had to exercise immense patience. I had to wander aimlessly. I had no thought whatsoever of whether I would succeed there or not. Just one goal. The effort for it. Finally, I found it.

[GV1:P0056] I spoke about the corrupt practices of society. I have a few things to say there. It is about the Aryans who arrived here. They were giving instructions. According to those instructions, those poor folks fought. They were made to believe that they were strong. The poor souls were mesmerized by it. Directives were given to view the remaining sections as despicable creatures and to destroy them upon sight. Following that, that group kept performing those valiant acts. All the other sections were tolerating it. What could they do?

[GV1:P0057] In these circumstances, the section designated as the downtrodden could not organize themselves. Suppressing their pain, those people were cursing. Do you know who bore the brunt of that curse? Those who orchestrated these evil deeds and those who executed them. With that, our communities began to degenerate. When various factions within Hinduism fought each other, all sections were being destroyed. These poor humans were unaware of it. We see in the political arena a process of ascending to power by making people fight and destroy each other, don't we? It means the same existed in our Hindu community as well. As a result of it, there is a large section here that has slipped into ruin.

[GV1:P0058] That group which received the curse, and another group which was branded as downtrodden and marginalized. They are the two groups I see around me here. Both of them have begun to realize that they committed wrong actions. What they need now is upliftment. An ascent from the lowest step. What is required for that?

[GV1:P0059] That is where I firmly assert that a path must be cleared. Only by traversing that path can you attain salvation from these sins. I know numerous families steeped in misery. I am ready to offer my strength to them. Many have already approached me. To all of them, I have only one piece of advice. Move forward with righteous deeds. Seek atonement for your sins. Seek the counsel of Gurus for that.

[GV1:P0060] When speaking of Gurus, I have another matter to remind you of. Today, the Marwaris, Gujaratis, and Sikhs are living prosperously in North India. Many among them are industrialists. They lead an affluent life. They have Gurus to guide them. It is in accordance with the directives of those Gurus that they make their moves in life. You can understand without my saying that they achieve tremendous success in their lives due to this.

[GV1:P0061] Along that path, Gurus are ready to provide guidance in our Hindu community as well. But our people must be willing to recognize and honor them. If so, I firmly believe that we can secure a bright future.

[GV1:P0062] - Santhigiri Karunakara Guru

[GV1:P0063] The Kulapathi Speaks

============================================================

GURUVANIKAL · June 1977 · Volume 1
Malayalam source paragraphs GV1:P0064 to GV1:P0080
English line for line; each paragraph carries its Malayalam source number.

[GV1:P0064] June 1977

[GV1:P0065] Dear Ones,

[GV1:P0066] We live in a highly advanced era. However, we face a multitude of problems. Overcoming them is an absolute necessity; otherwise, we will face failure in life. Thus, we must find a way to escape from all these difficulties and hardships. That is precisely what I intend to discuss now.

[GV1:P0067] There exists a large segment of the population that remains steeped in ignorance. It would be inappropriate to leave them unguided in such a state. We must be capable of instilling in them a clear understanding of this world and of life itself. I am not referring to those who display reluctance and prefer to remain secluded. Rather, I speak of those who yearn to comprehend the essence of this magnificent life. If we can provide them with a guiding light, they will be able to build a fulfilling life. This is what we must strive to achieve.

[GV1:P0068] Imparting knowledge to this group is the need of the hour. What methods can be adopted for this? Merely memorizing a few books does not seem to serve the purpose. Nor should one assume that blindly reciting our *Puranas* will achieve this goal. However, if the stories and teachings presented in these *Puranas* and other texts are categorized and analyzed with discerning intellect, much can be grasped from them. When such a mindset of rational discrimination becomes deeply rooted, we will be able to acquire the strength to think and act pragmatically concerning other problems as well.

[GV1:P0069] It is my opinion that the youth of today show reluctance towards this. They do not seem to have much affinity for our ancient culture. That is incorrect. We can evaluate today's problems only if we study the events of yesterday. Therefore, our youth must understand a little about our cultural heritage with a sense of dedication. Subsequently, they should pass on some aspects of it to the next generation. They will accept what is good and discard what needs to be discarded. Leave that to the hands of time.

[GV1:P0070] It is already evident that our *Puranas* have survived through all ages. How much strength have the *Mahabharata*, the *Ramayana*, and the *Bhagavata* bestowed upon us! We are well aware of the fact that their concepts are so profound that they can never be exhaustively interpreted. How did those great sages achieve this? In our conception, what an immense revolution these gems of thought, formulated by them while dwelling deep within the forests, have brought about for mankind! Is this all? Are there any realms they have not traversed? Are there any subjects they have not spoken of? When we reflect upon this, the immense power of that tradition astonishes us. We are driven not by the question of how they accomplished it, but by a deep yearning to understand what that power was.

[GV1:P0071] That remarkable power was attained through sacrifice. If we wish to understand what that sacrifice entailed, or what that specific power was, we must cast a glance into the past. What was the power achieved by Lord Buddha, Sankaracharya, the Prophet, and Jesus Christ? Can any political philosopher stand before those supreme powers? Can they even approach their capabilities? What profound changes have been brought about in human society by Buddha, the very embodiment of compassion, and by Sri Sankara, who provided guidance by evaluating the scriptures and the *Upanishads*? Has anyone else here been able to accomplish even a small fraction of their work? For that matter, could any prominent political figure ever surpass the path laid down by Sree Narayana Guru—who, having mastered the essence of Vedanta, guided the masses around him onto the right path through the avenue of faith—or by Sree Chattampi Swamikal, who awakened the people by exposing the Vedic practices that had lost their foundation over the course of time? Everyone knows that the answer is no.

[GV1:P0072] What guided those noble sages there was a unique power rooted in tradition. Our people were ready to perceive it and accept them. Initially, they all had to face hardships. They had to practice immense sacrifice. Yet, with unfaltering steps, those great souls advanced, bearing witness to that unearthly radiance.

[GV1:P0073] The essence, therefore, is that a great power guides us. We are moving along the path that has been illuminated for us. By treading this path rooted in tradition, we achieve only elevation. What we must possess is an inner thirst to discover it. It is for this that the youth of today must strive. Only then will your next generation step into a life of happiness and contentment.

[GV1:P0074] This should not be interpreted to mean that I reject progressive ideologies. Why cannot we aspire for progress while remaining firmly rooted in our tradition? It appears that many today harbor misconceptions—believing that our ancient *Arsha Bharata* culture consists merely of outdated systems and must be entirely replaced. That is the mindset we need to change. If we change it, we can build a novel stream of thought in our cultural sphere. You can realize this even without my stating it. It is imperative that the cultural realm achieves elevation. Only then can a large section of the people be guided onto the right path. We have already seen that such modernization has occurred across various eras. Its movements continue to evolve. It is just that when it becomes outdated, there is a need to create a sense of novelty once again.

[GV1:P0075] As previously mentioned, the problems of materialistic life constantly afflict us. How can a solution be found for this? How can we confront this calamity that stares everyone in the face? This is a thought that many might raise. To this, there is only one thing to say. Provide peace to your mind, which is the epicenter of all problems. Grant it tranquility. If you can provide that peace, the problems are resolved. No matter how severe they may be, you will realize that their intensity is gradually diminishing. Thus, the problems will be solved in due course.

[GV1:P0076] How does one provide peace to the mind? That is where the contradictions between concepts reside. How can a mind that is boiling over and ready to explode be restrained? There have been numerous instances where it has been successfully restrained. We observe that there is a power in this world that transcends our human strength. We must believe in that power. Only if we believe can we truly discover it. The radiance of that power has been visible since the dawn of humanity. Since then, humans have begun to worship that power. That worship continues today. And it will endure as long as humanity exists.

[GV1:P0077] We are moving forward through the light shown by those lives. Even though humans have progressed immensely, they are unable to distance themselves from that power—such is the magnitude of that power. That is God. We visualize that governing force in our minds. We present our problems to it. It compels us to live as rational and wise beings.

[GV1:P0078] It is true that this power has been divided into various factions. They were named religions. The essence of all these religions is fundamentally the same: to achieve peace, harmony, and fulfillment in life through them. That is what all the *Vedas* and *Puranas* urge us to do.

[GV1:P0079] As stated in the *Rig Veda*, let noble thoughts come to us from every side. Through them, lead a peaceful life. To achieve this, concentrate the mind. To attain concentration, worship that power consistently. It will instill courage in life. It will show the right path. Live according to that path. Let that be our ultimate goal.

[GV1:P0080] Guru Vani

GURUVANIKAL · June 1977 · Volume 1
Malayalam source paragraphs GV1:P0081 to GV1:P0102

[GV1:P0081] June 1977

[GV1:P0082] Question: It is said that he is a realized soul (*Siddha*) and a wise one (*Jnani*). Then how did it remain unchanged?

[GV1:P0083] Answer: There are certain residual karmic effects required to expel some ingrained tendencies (*Vasanas*). No matter how wise a person may be, it might not be efficacious for everyone.

[GV1:P0084] Question: What is the reason it did not prove efficacious for him? Can you explain?

[GV1:P0085] Answer: Some things can be explained, but not everything. A true devotee does not focus on destroying his vigor or preserving it like a precious jewel. Let whatever is meant to happen, happen. For him, devotion is the only refuge—thus, the glory of God is his sole sanctuary.

[GV1:P0086] Question: Are you implying that figures like Bhogar and Narada are not genuine devotees?

[GV1:P0087] Answer: Consider a father with ten children. They all address him as 'Father.' Their mother is also the same. The ten individuals act with ten distinct characteristics. Their innate inclination towards their father is identical. However, true love may only be evident in two or three of them. Only the father and mother can comprehend that; outsiders cannot. Similarly, there are those who practice Yoga through devotion. Some ritualists exhibit bodily purity and follow ritualistic practices according to Vedic traditions. A wise person observes all these with moderation and understands each individual's course of action. Regardless of the action performed, a devotee constantly perceives God alone as a sweet, pervasive presence.

[GV1:P0088] Then, irrespective of the devotee's greatness, God behaves with them like an ignorant child, embodying the attitude, "I know nothing." At that time, God is consistently perceived acting within them, akin to a mother fondling an ignorant child. A karma yogi (ritualist) and a yogi might speak of their operational capabilities. They may discuss the specific qualities of medicine or the qualities of actions. God continuously fondles the devotee, much like a mother who does not allow her child to cry. A beloved child will eventually have to do certain things on their own. However, all are indeed children.

[GV1:P0089] Question: Are you suggesting that a devotee lacks knowledge?

[GV1:P0090] Answer: Does it imply that? It merely means they are at ease because they are devoid of the attitude of having acquired knowledge, or the ego of believing they are everything.

[GV1:P0091] Question: Then, are you stating that Bhogar preserved his vitality by transmuting it into a bead using medicine?

[GV1:P0092] Answer: Yes, it is preserved.

[GV1:P0093] Question: At the Santhigiri Ashram, which propagates monotheism, certain framed pictures are worshipped. Is this appropriate?

[GV1:P0094] Answer: Initially, humanity adopted various mediums to assign forms. All concepts prevailing to this day originated in this manner. Even the use of lamps is analogous. Meditation practices encompass numerous natures, such as formless meditation and meditation with form. The individuals who discovered these methods might have initiated a philosophical discipline—it may not be immediately comprehensible. Until one grasps it, by remaining steadfast and fixing upon it, and until the essence of other concepts is understood, if one stays firm in their belief, the mind's wavering will cease, and this can be discarded once the nature of wisdom dawns.

[GV1:P0095] Question: A devotee was heard mentioning the term '*Trikalajnana*' to a friend. I wish to know more about *Trikalajnana*.

[GV1:P0096] Answer: *Trikalajnana* is experienced by all individuals. It goes unnoticed simply because it is an unrecognized experience. Only the wise comprehend its true nature. Firstly, one must learn what its true form is. Subsequently, it can be known and understood.

[GV1:P0097] Question: Why is the final phase of the lives of great souls fraught with sorrow?

[GV1:P0098] Answer: Great souls do not attain greatness based on their physical constitution. The fundamental question is what they stood for. Recall the words of Manu. One should not ponder the origin and the fall of a river—similarly, do not contemplate the birth and death of great souls.

[GV1:P0099] Question: It is considered that Monday is auspicious for prayer. Furthermore, prayers are conducted every month on the day of the full moon (*Pournami*). What is the rationale behind this?

[GV1:P0100] Answer: It is a common belief among all people, not just ordinary Hindus, that Mondays and Thursdays are auspicious. Adherents of the *Shakteya* tradition consider Fridays and Tuesdays to be auspicious. For self-knowledge (*Atma Vidya*), Mondays and Thursdays are deemed auspicious across all religions. Sunday is also considered favorable. For sacrifice, Wednesdays and Saturdays are regarded as auspicious. This is calculated based on the spheres—specifically, planetary positions viewed as spheres. The planetary positions are determined based on the nine planets (*Navagrahas*). Days are deemed auspicious in reverence to the periods when they orbit and approach the earth.

[GV1:P0101] The special significance attributed to the day of *Pournami* (full moon) stems from the division of a month into two lunar fortnights: the dark fortnight (*Karuthavavu*) and the bright fortnight (*Veluthavavu*). The bright fortnight culminates on the day the moon rises completely. The bright fortnight is characterized by the light directly transmitted from the solar sphere to the lunar sphere without any obstruction. Sages have deemed the *Pournami* vow auspicious based on the microscopic particles that reach the earth via the moonlight. These particles descend upon all animate and inanimate entities. This phenomenon gives rise to two distinct outcomes: firstly, it grants liberation to those who lead lives guided by *sattvic* thoughts, vows, and prayers; secondly, it is postulated that those engrossed in worldly thoughts on that day become entangled in worldly existence. It is based on this principle that the sages have instructed us that this day is conducive to prayer.

[GV1:P0102] The Kulapathi speaks

[GV1:P0103] July 1977

[GV1:P0104] The Glory of Sacrifice

[GV1:P0105] Beloved ones,

[GV1:P0106] My aspiration to dedicate my life solely to virtuous deeds commenced during my early childhood. I must have been around seven years old at the time. I exhibited a profound interest in visiting temples for worship. You must not misconstrue my statement. This was an innate desire. Do you not possess similar innate inclinations? It is highly probable. Some individuals are predisposed to malevolent tendencies, ultimately culminating in their ruin. Simply put, I possessed an inherent obstinacy to avoid such a trajectory.

[GV1:P0107] I began attending school. However, my focus was not on academics. I would incessantly ponder subjects related to devotion. A teacher inevitably noticed this characteristic. He inquired into the reasons behind my silence and unusual behavior. I could not refrain from telling him. My singular thought was that I must reach an ashram somehow. My family members raised objections. However, none of that deterred me. That childhood obstinacy ultimately led me to the Aluva Advaita Ashram. My pursuit of knowledge commenced there.

[GV1:P0108] I gained substantial insight into ashram life during my time there. One crucial aspect—I had reached my destined location. That became my educational institution. My learning was to proceed from there. Subsequently, I arrived at Sivagiri. At Sivagiri, I resolved to establish a firm foundation for my endeavors. This is precisely what I intend to discuss. I can encapsulate it in a single word: sacrifice. After completing my own duties, I would fulfill the responsibilities of others as well. I never experienced any reluctance in doing so. This readiness for sacrifice became the defined objective of my life. I am articulating this specifically for the benefit of the younger generation. Cultivate this attitude during your formative years. If you do so, success is undoubtedly assured.

[GV1:P0109] During this period, individuals from various regions would visit the ashram. I would readily offer them the necessary assistance. Consequently, they would naturally feel inclined to offer something in return to a child exhibiting such behavior. However, the moment I sensed they were about to offer monetary compensation, I would flee the premises. They would typically search for me precisely when they were preparing to depart. Yet, they would be unable to locate me anywhere. One could say this served as a form of amusement for me. I derived a sense of satisfaction from it.

[GV1:P0110] At this juncture, I am reminded of another story about the greatness of sacrifice. It happened a long time ago, during the time of Chandragupta Maurya. A famous person from China arrived in India. He desired to meet and converse with everyone here. Accordingly, he got permission to meet Chanakya, the minister of Chandragupta. How would the minister of a great emperor live? The traveler pondered over it. When he reached near the minister's house one evening, he saw Chanakya sitting in a small hut near a small lamp, looking at the files of important problems of the country. He stood amazed. What kind of minister is this? Suddenly, Chanakya extinguished that lamp and lit another one. The prominent traveler could not help but ask why it was done. Chanakya said: "That belongs to the state, and this lamp is my own. Now we can talk."

[GV1:P0111] The traveler could not help but respect the humility and sense of justice of the statesman named Chanakya. He went back to China with a great experience. What do we understand from this? Since those ancient times, our Indians were renowned for their humility, service, and righteousness. Their sacrifice highlighted the greatness of our country. It also provided an inspiration to be noticed all over the world.

[GV1:P0112] Now another matter needs to be pointed out here. Each of us has different paths in life. We move forward accordingly. When seeing someone prosper, many people get jealous. That behavior pattern needs to be changed. It cannot be changed suddenly. For that, good thoughts must spread within us and wash away the impurities inside. Only then can it be said that one has lived as a human being, and only then will there be satisfaction. We have seen many people being dissatisfied and restless. Do you know the reason for that? Excessive greed. First, remove those greedy thoughts. That is why we must control our minds.

[GV1:P0113] The goal of our life is realized when a systematic path is adopted. Some people set out to become monks while they still have all the obligations in life. Such monkhood is of no use to them. Those who are householders must fulfill their respective duties. Children must be raised through the right path. It is an essential factor for the progress of the country. When they grow up, they will find the ways for their employment on their own. Parents should prepare the paths for them to find it. And then, we should become proficient in activities for our peace of mind.

[GV1:P0114] But there are some people. They lament over the future of their children. The pain of not being able to give them anything. Others, however, just earn money for their children. They amass unlimited wealth. I do not think there is a need for that either. If a son or daughter does not come through the path we intend, let them go their own way. There is no use in remembering that and lamenting over it. This life of ours is not for lamenting like that. We must live it completely.

[GV1:P0115] We have to learn this matter by looking at the Westerners. We know how they raise their children and so on. They give the necessary instructions. They encourage them to do any job. There is no objection in that. Anyway, a job is a job. We cannot but respect it. Here, if someone has a little education, they are stubborn that they must get a job commensurate with it. Because of this, we can see countless youths who are jobless and do not do any work. They will experience the problems of life very seriously.

[GV1:P0116] How can those who have thus become lazy by themselves be reformed? One can also see parents lamenting over it. What I have to say is that there is no point in that. Once the children reach a stage to stand on their own feet, the duty is fulfilled. After that, there is no wrong in even accepting monkhood. One's duty has been fulfilled. That is the path of a complete life.

[GV1:P0117] Acquiring knowledge in childhood,

[GV1:P0118] Seeking worldly enjoyments in youth,

[GV1:P0119] Adopting a sage's conduct in old age,

[GV1:P0120] And relinquishing the body in yogic bliss.

[GV1:P0121] It is a necessity to acquire knowledge in childhood. Along with that, one must adhere to righteousness in life. Only then can a purification be built up even in later times. What is needed to maintain that discipline? Guidance! Instructions from a wise and mature Guru! That will provide immense solace. That will nurture the good tendencies within us. With that, a complete understanding of what Vanaprastha is and its full form will emerge within us. The knowledgeable ones say that it is the householders who can engage more in this matter. One can point out countless examples for that. The very fact that all the authors of the Puranas were householders is sufficient proof. That is the complete life. We must truly respect it.

[GV1:P0124] Question: What could be the result of that preservation?

[GV1:P0126] Question: Even with these Yoga disciplines, if it does not calm down, then how can the mind be controlled?

[GV1:P0127] Answer: The nature of controlling the mind when we face numerous sorrows - when we have no one to help us, or when a child dies, or when a husband dies - we often see women crying out loudly. It has been learned from them that when they repeat this for some time, their sorrow subsides, and within three months, the sorrow goes away. Similarly, one can surrender their sorrow by crying upon seeing a deity, a Guru, or a devotee who manifests divine light. Then he attains peace from that. A devotee who has none of this can pray and express his grievances to God by surrendering all his emotions with devotion. He attains peace from that.

[GV1:P0128] Question: You did not finish explaining how women can fully experience devotion to God?

[GV1:P0129] Answer: It is much easier for women than men to attain God through devotion. They have passed on many illusions to the people using money, knowledge, and wealth. Devaluing the deeds of ordinary devotees, poets and Rajarshis lined up behind them. Secondly, administrations changed in respective times, people of different religions ruled and brought their own religious customs, highlighting the malpractices of Hinduism and thereby covering up true devotion. They have also destroyed such historical records. Just as 'a tiger will eat grass if it has no other way', the scientific methods that came through them have instilled a business-style approach in us. Thus, the tradition of striving hard for worldly matters got ingrained in us.

[GV1:P0133] August 1977

[GV1:P0134] Dear ones,

[GV1:P0135] I had mentioned a few things about the greatness of sacrifice last time. However, what I have to say does not end there. There are many things I have gained from experience and understood by seeing and hearing. I have a strong desire to share them with you one by one. I feel that only then will you be able to understand its essence at least to some extent.

[GV1:P0136] No matter how agonizing the problems I faced were, I tried to handle things with great equanimity. As a result, my problems were resolved. I can assert with certainty that there has never been a situation where they remained unresolved. To be more specific, I grew up in a desert. I did not collapse in its terrible heat. I moved forward every moment by gathering strength. Had I felt a little mental distress back then and given up everything, I would not have reached anywhere today. I would have been destroyed, entangled in the web of my own problems. Regardless, I do not know how I was able to gather such inner strength during those times.

[GV1:P0137] Seeing this approach of mine, many well-wishers have given me various pieces of advice. They have tried to dissuade me from many of my actions. But even as I listened to all their advice, I continued to forge ahead on my own path. I want to clarify one thing here. We should not displease anyone. They might be saying such things with good intentions. However, accepting the good aspects of what they say while striving to find our own path is absolutely essential for success in life. We may perhaps not get its results very quickly. Even so, there is no doubt that the results will definitely be attained over time.

[GV1:P0138] I started speaking about sacrifice. All the noble souls who have existed in the world have achieved sacrifice through their actions. Only they have been able to do something eternally lasting here. Look at the lives of great figures like Jesus Christ, Prophet Muhammad, and Buddha. You can find a vast abundance of sacrifice there. Why, were those lives not the very embodiment of sacrifice itself? We need not look elsewhere. Just take a look at Mahatma Gandhiji, who shines brightly as the apple of our India's eye. How incredibly magnificent is the message imparted by that life, which evolved through the greatness of sacrifice.

[GV1:P0139] Was he not able to bring a superpower, which ruled over a vast nation, to its knees with a mere message of peace? I do not think anything like that has ever happened anywhere else in the world. Nor do I think such greatness could be achieved by anyone other than someone from India. Indians are people who have evolved through such a great deal of tolerance and tradition. Their life is one of friendship and peace. No power in the world has been able to surpass that.

[GV1:P0140] Great souls have taken birth in this land of India in every era. Through their powerful sacrifices, they have bestowed vitality and life upon the entire human race. We must understand this clearly. That alone has endured, and that alone will endure in the future. Sree Narayana Guru is another great soul who brought about change to a certain extent through sacrifice. After Sree Sankara Bhagavatpada, it is difficult to find another Karma Yogi who brought about such a massive social revolution in our India. His supremely sacrificial life must be given its due value. If we can perform such a sacrifice or cultivate a discipline rich in sacrifice, there is no greater service than that.

[GV1:P0141] This does not necessitate that we must rise to the level of those great souls. Their sacrifices attained a grand stature. Therefore, we need not be bewildered by the thought that we cannot even peek into that realm. It is through their relentless effort and readiness that they reached that supreme position. We should not retreat just by thinking about it. If we try to advance at least a little in that richness of sacrifice, we will receive its corresponding reward. The only thing is that its measure will be strictly in accordance with that sacrifice. Even so, there is no doubt that it will indeed culminate in success in life.

[GV1:P0142] Then there is another aspect as well. Let me say that it is somewhat spiritual. It concerns the trajectory of our karma. Some people will not move forward no matter how hard they try, whereas some only need to try a little to reach their intended position. What is the reason for this? We can see many people feeling mentally pained thinking about it. One thing can be pointed out there. It is the variations in karma. One group of people might be striving in a state where the karmas or sacrifices performed in past lives are eagerly waiting for their completion. Thus, they achieve results very quickly. For others, the trajectory of karma might not have been completed in their past lives. There, this trajectory of karma can be completed only through sacrifice. Moreover, if we state the reason for soaring to great heights, it is because that person's very birth in this life is destined for it. They would have fulfilled all its aspects by performing sacrifices in their past lives itself. For such people, just a little effort is enough to attain it. So, one thing to remember is that the elevated position currently attained is the consequence of those good deeds practiced over multiple lifetimes.

[GV1:P0143] The karmic trajectories of lifetimes take various forms. Many people do not seem to believe in it. It is good for us to remember one thing. If we take the different kinds of vicissitudes of life and analyze them, we will be convinced of that absolute truth. Many have to lead different kinds of lives. A blind child is born in the house of a rich man. In some places, children are born with stunted limbs. In other places, deformed births occur. We need to see and pay attention to all these things. What is all this? Is this not the resurrection of the cursed elements from past lives? How can we not believe these things? Thus, it implies that the baseness and good deeds of past lives follow us. There are many reasons why we emphasize this. And this is indeed something that others should reflect upon.

[GV1:P0144] Now, let me say a little about the general life of human beings!

[GV1:P0145] When a human being becomes sorrowful, they forget everything and wander around seeking refuge. In prosperity, they forget everything. That is a common trait. However, one must be able to cultivate a presence of mind that remains unshaken and unwavering under any circumstance. For that, they need to remember the Controller of this universe. They must act knowing that. Only then will sacrifice emerge in them. And only that will attain a permanent state.

[GV1:P0146] All the great sacrificers the world has seen today are those who have worked unceasingly while standing behind that power. We can all clearly know what they have achieved as a result of it. People continue to follow their path. They find solace in it. Thus, their words inspire us to lead a contented life.

[GV1:P0147] I spoke about the life of Jesus Christ earlier, didn't I? Was that life itself not offered up for the sake of sacrifice? What could be greater than that? Even in those final moments, he said, "Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do." Do the words of that great man, who showcased that greatness by sacrificing even his own life, not echo everywhere even today? The case of the great Buddha is no different from this. Is he not the magnanimous soul who renounced all the royal pleasures of this world and set out for the welfare of the people? Who can lay claim to the magnificence of that sacrifice? How incredibly great have its achievements become! Thus, we can see that all the great souls who achieved immortality in life were the very embodiments of sacrifice.

[GV1:P0148] Here, the foundation of our material life also requires such a sacrifice. If we wish to start any movement, that too requires sacrifice. The success of that institution will depend on the degree of this sacrifice. If we examine the lives of many people who have risen to prominence here today, we can understand this fact. But if the seeds of ego fall into their path of thought, we can see that not only the person but also the movement they built gets destroyed. So, when moving forward towards a goal through sacrifice, we must acquire all the knowledge related to it. What is that knowledge? What is it for? Ego dwells in the human mind. Therefore, the first thing needed is the removal of ignorance. Only that will lead to success. What is needed for that? We must understand the life perspectives of great people. We should think about it. Then, we must try to put it into practice. If we try step by step like this, we can reach our intended destination. That systematic life is, in a way, a sacrifice. We should strive for that. Perhaps many of you would like to know what its benefits are. Firstly, liberation from our karmic bonds. That leads to merging with God. Another is life's satisfaction. We will attain both of these. Through that, we will be led to the ethereal supreme state. What more does a human birth need than that?

[GV1:P0151] Question: How can one believe the stories of the Rajarshis recorded in these Puranas?

[GV1:P0152] Answer: Currently, during the tenure of many rulers, some political enthusiasts often write histories to destroy the goodness of certain individuals. In this, we seem to have forgotten the national leaders who endured the sacrifices of holy souls. It appears to have been omitted from the histories written after attaining independence. The stories of contemporaries, fellow students, and colleagues are the ones that have been left out. And that too, in this democratic rule. Then is it any wonder if it was omitted by those who ruled in an absolute dictatorship?

[GV1:P0153] Question: Looking at this experience, is it only the Rajarshis who have done so?

[GV1:P0154] Answer: Not only among the Rajarshis, but also among common people and in the deity system, there are people who have attained direct realization and through it performed certain occult powers and magical feats. The shortcoming is that strong historical records could not be created for all of them. It was only through alliances at some administrative level, or through some other kind of knowledge or wealth, that it could be brought into a record. Those that have come through a true devotional nature are exceedingly rare.

[GV1:P0155] Question: So, do you give importance only to devotion?

[GV1:P0156] Answer: I do not give importance only to devotion like that. I am one who believes that everything has its own goodness in its respective measure.

[GV1:P0157] Question: Isn't it easier to lead a family life in the path of devotion?

[GV1:P0158] Answer: Yes. The path of devotion is the most suitable for family life.

[GV1:P0159] Question: What is the reason for you to feel that nothing else is easy?

[GV1:P0160] Answer: Practicing yoga techniques requires considerable time, and it involves certain changes in dietary habits depending on place and time. None of that may be convenient for family people. Therefore, there is quite a delay in carrying forward yoga practices. There are some ritualists who practice Vedic methods. They too have a specific time schedule for mantras and tantras. They will experience it as quite a delay.

[GV1:P0161] Question: Then what about the state of a Jnani (wise one)?

[GV1:P0162] Answer: The Jnani truly evaluates all these aspects. Viewing all these moderately, experiencing an inspiration from God, he moves forward acting on his own.

[GV1:P0164] October 1977

[GV1:P0165] Question: Some Vedantins are heard saying this, aren't they? I am not born, I do not die, there are no births and deaths in the world, the universe is an illusion. What is the reason?

[GV1:P0166] Answer: Vedanta is correct. The reason Vedanta came to be is because there was something else, isn't it? Those who said this universe is an illusion were living beings, weren't they? With the help of the five elements, with the help of the five senses, and thus with the help of the koshas (sheaths), the soul, which is enclosed in this body within a form created by God, ranging from the nature of the annamaya kosha to the anandamaya kosha, is brought through the jnanamaya kosha to the vijnanamaya kosha. Thus, the whole world can know only through this. When the knowledge that comes in this way turns one into a subtle thinker, it is often called jnana thought, vijnana thought, and ajnana thought. Based on this, some experience it in the formed, the formless, and the undivided.

[GV1:P0167] Question: These Siddhas are assumed to be Jnanis, aren't they? Then what made you distinguish between Siddhas and Jnanis?

[GV1:P0168] Answer: Siddhi and Jnana are indeed two different things. Siddhi utilizes certain mantras and tantras, worshiping through certain deity systems or Yogishwara systems, experiencing it, and creating some minor experiences among the people - acting like the nature of a yogi or a deity oneself. A Jnani does not do this. Through the path originating from the Guru's teaching, recognizing everything that can come into the light, even realizing what sustenance of life or sustenance of prana is, the Guru's teaching is an instrumental path capable of perceiving even the unique virtue of those koshas in which that prana operates. But a Siddha is not like that; a Siddha proceeds by believing only the words received from the guidance he prefers. There is only a very distant relationship between a Siddha and a Jnani.

[GV1:P0169] Question: You mentioned the Guru's teaching. He comes forward by giving the form of some favorite deity like this, doesn't he?

[GV1:P0170] Answer: That is correct. We can record it here like an administration. The peons standing near the king are also called peons. In courts, every bench clerk has peons. Likewise, there are some in certain companies. There are peons in all offices and schools. Village officers have peons. But the status and privileges enjoyed by a peon who can meet the king and discuss matters may not be found among these peons or superior officers. Similarly, one practices yoga, one practices Guruhood. It exists in many states and many justifications. All this exists through justification as well. Certain shifts in position are the reason for this.

[GV1:P0172] November 1977

[GV1:P0173] Question: So, what should be understood from this is that the Gurus you speak of themselves exist in numerous natures like this, and their states themselves exist in various ways, right?

[GV1:P0174] Answer: Yes.

[GV1:P0175] Question: If so, what kind of Gurus should actually lead this?

[GV1:P0176] Answer: Gurus of all kinds can show the reality. But that is solely dependent on their growth.

[GV1:P0177] Question: Are you referring to the growth in the path of each one, or the overall growth?

[GV1:P0178] Answer: There are Gurus who reach reality through the growth of each one. There are also Gurus who reach reality by seeing it as a whole.

[GV1:P0179] Question: You said that there are Gurus who reach through the growth of each one. How is that?

[GV1:P0180] Answer: A devotee is a traveler of a path. A yogi is a traveler of a path. A karma yogi is a traveler of a path. The Jnani, who grows by bringing all these together, is a visionary. There are also Gurus born at the beginning and end of yugas (epochs). The names of the Gurus concerning the yugas are Avatara Purushas (incarnations). They will also have some special characteristics.

[GV1:P0181] Question: What would those special characteristics be?

[GV1:P0182] Answer: We have seen some historical records, haven't we? Sree Rama, Sree Krishna, and Balarama were all born in different eras. Among them, Sree Rama was born in the Treta Yuga and showed many special characteristics. But none of the previously mentioned ones were able to show such great special characteristics as Sree Krishna.

[GV1:P0183] Question: What could be the reason for that?

[GV1:P0184] Answer: When changes in the epochs (yugas) occur, certain specific changes will also be seen in the prominent figures (Yugapurushas) born in those respective epochs. A Chaturyuga is completed by four yugas. Therefore, the gurus born at the beginning and end of that epoch will possess greater capabilities. The authorities of this Chaturyuga are the Manus.

[GV1:P0185] Question: What is your opinion regarding the authority of individuals like Sri Krishna in this context?

[GV1:P0186] Answer: Sri Krishna is the final guru of the Dwapara Yuga and the first guru of the Kali Yuga.

[GV1:P0187] Question: What is the reason for you to state both together?

[GV1:P0188] Answer: Sri Krishna has exhibited many independent actions. His glory will continue to be reflected to some extent until the final phase of this Kali Yuga. That is what stems from that independence. It is not mere independence; rather, whatever is necessary emerges appropriately at that very moment. If one examines the lives of other incarnations (Avataras), the concept of acting 'according to command' can be observed. However, Sri Krishna operated entirely independently. The names of the gurus and incarnations who have appeared thus far continue to be repeated. Yet, in practical application and in the enthusiasm of the people, is it not Sri Krishna who is seen at the forefront?

[GV1:P0189] Question: What is the reason for this independence being reflected in Sri Krishna?

[GV1:P0190] Answer: When referring to Kali, does it not evoke the impression of doing anything with an independent nature? Yes, it does. If one closely observes Sri Krishna, it becomes evident that, like a primordial trait, he reinforced that independence and the outdated historical records right at its inception. Similarly, he led his life in a manner that suggested the impending future would possess distinctive characteristics. Next is the nature of the visionaries belonging to the lineage of the aforementioned Manus. They acquired knowledge over long periods and documented certain teachings and guidelines. Through this, profound foresight is also seen to flourish. However, the sages (Rishis) who evolve within the lineage of the incarnations continue certain hymns and traditions of service. They demonstrate various practices of mystical powers (Siddhis). The realized souls (Jnanis) who grow in the lineage of Manu merely advise and disseminate knowledge suitable for their respective times. There are Siddhas and Jnanis who fail to recognize this distinction. They often criticize various matters, offer advice, and depart. It is merely akin to certain Vedantins attempting to portray themselves as Jnanis by quoting the words of the realized ones without possessing any experiential knowledge. The majority of the Jnanis we encounter on this earth are those who flaunt their erudition by solely consolidating the maxim, 'Brahma Satyam, Jagan Mithya' (Brahman is the truth, the world is an illusion).

[GV1:P0191] For a true Jnani, knowledge means self-knowledge (Atma Vidya). It is that which self-illuminates within one's own soul. Such Jnanis are the true assets we possess. For instance, consider the science of Ayurveda. Similarly, Mantra Vidya, Tantra Vidya, and Shastra Vidya. If one were to examine each of these individually, they would appear as the ultimate truth. It is through these disciplines that we practically comprehend the documented experiences of the great sages and a select few ascetics.

[GV1:P0193] December 1977

[GV1:P0194] Question: Why did you differentiate between the great sages (Rishis) and the ascetics (Sanyasis)?

[GV1:P0195] Answer: The great sages are those who attain experiential knowledge and document everything in a manner that is highly beneficial to the common people, while also demonstrating its practical application. Only a few among the ascetics acknowledge this. They remain aloof from everything. They maintain no attachments and possess a sense of complete detachment towards all things. They merely exhibit certain imitative behaviors solely for the purpose of sustenance.

[GV1:P0196] Question: So, is it not about such ascetics that our people have been speaking?

[GV1:P0197] Answer: Yes, people simply amuse themselves by recounting tales of those who practice certain yoga disciplines and survive without even needing dry leaves or plain water. They waste their time unnecessarily discussing these stories without any understanding of how useful this is to the public or how people can attain such states. Some individuals, tempted by the intensity of mystical powers (Siddhis) and erudition, waste their time praising them. A true Jnani is one who respects these various aspects by assigning them their appropriate value. This Jnani evaluates everything, demonstrates the validity of all paths to the people, and attempts to impart knowledge by giving it a distinct character.

[GV1:P0198] Question: What exactly did you mean by the distinct character of knowledge?

[GV1:P0199] Answer: By documenting that specific events occurred in certain periods, they perceive only the unadulterated truth within the nature of the Jnanis, and they eventually convince us that there is only one ultimate truth.

[GV1:P0200] Question: You mentioned the Manus earlier. In what context are you referring to them?

[GV1:P0201] Answer: The Manus are the ones who encompass all the descriptions of the world. Upon closer examination, they are the absolute authorities governing creation, preservation, and destruction. The governance of this world is characterized by fourteen Manus leading up to the great deluge (Pralaya). Such great souls have recorded that the duration of each Manu consists of seventy-one Chaturyugas. If their guidance falters, and if the world strays, it will be plunged into perpetual blindness. Until a specific birth occurs to rectify it, the world will have to continue traveling on that misguided path.

[GV1:P0202] Question: Has any of the Manus ever made such a mistake?

[GV1:P0203] Answer: Yes. We shall discuss that later.

[GV1:P0204] Question: What types of worship practices do you think are most desirable to adopt during this period?

[GV1:P0205] Answer: Four modes of worship practices are considered the most ideal.

[GV1:P0206] Question: Which are they?

[GV1:P0207] Answer: Karma, Yoga, Jnana, and Bhakti. It is difficult for Karma and Yoga to be fully reflected in this era. The Karma Yoga spoken of by an ascetic is different. An ascetic considers any action undertaken as Karma. Ordinary people perform actions adhering to certain rules and regulations. This cannot be effectively mirrored in current times. Similarly, Yoga also poses difficulties for common people. Jnana can be manifested in any era. Even if not manifested, nothing else can affect Jnana. Bhakti holds significance in all times. Nothing can reach completion without devotion. Particularly, Bhakti is the most suitable path in this age.

[GV1:P0208] Question: Since you mentioned that Bhakti is the most beneficial in this era, would you be willing to explain how one should practice this devotion, and how it can remain effective from the beginning, through the middle, and until the end of time?

[GV1:P0209] Answer: Initially, learn to practice all the disciplines of a devotee to the point of turning them into experiential nature. Even if we attain a minor spiritual experience in such a manner, the assistance of a Guru in the absolute nature of devotion is required in every way to gain clarity over it. Regardless of whatever flaws may exist in that Guru's conduct, the one who believes will be able to find a way to derive spiritual satisfaction from it.

[GV1:P0210] Question: What do you mean by stating "regardless of whatever flaws"? Can there be various types of flaws like that?

[GV1:P0211] Answer: There are flaws in many ways. When a person practices devotion, if the knowledge attained is not complete or accompanied by humility, an arrogance will arise regarding the knowledge itself. It is specifically termed as 'Satvik Ahankara' (righteous ego). You are all well aware of the consequences that follow when arrogance takes root!

[GV1:P0212] Guruvani

[GV1:P0213] January 1978

[GV1:P0214] Question: To prevent that, how does one acquire and reach a state of flawless devotion by understanding the right aspects?

[GV1:P0215] Answer: When a person who earnestly desires fulfillment seeks it, there will be a sense of completion in whatever they reach. In that state, they will discover it themselves and accept such a Guru. If it is a devotion lacking this quality, the Bhagavata details the concept of twenty-four Gurus. Even at that level, one who reveres devotion will be able to attain the goal.

[GV1:P0216] Question: When you say that, does it not attract certain other flaws? Is this not the Kali Yuga? There are indeed certain defects in adopting such conditions. How can that be rectified?

[GV1:P0217] Answer: That is precisely why it was stated that in this era, the Guru must be someone who has attained perfection in devotion and is currently living.

[GV1:P0218] Question: What should be done if we lack the ability to visually perceive and act upon it?

[GV1:P0219] Answer: When one becomes a devotee, even without knowledge, an inquiring nature is inherent to him. In the course of such inquiry, one will find a person who is free from exaggeration, does not have a nature that forcefully attracts through magical feats, does not have the nature of soothing the eyes and pleasing the mind with costumes and ornaments, and lacks the knowledge that mesmerizes by reciting learned scholarship. Once such a person is found, one may feel satisfaction in him. When satisfaction is felt, we will naturally be compelled to spend some time there to get to know him better. From that, the skillful action of the wise one (*Jnani*) who behaves with a complete nature will occur in him and in those who desire like him, in a divine manner, even without the knowledge of the one called the wise one.

[GV1:P0220] Question: Even if it happens, aren't most people unaware of it?

[GV1:P0221] Answer: Yes, it happens so partly due to the deficiency in the course of their karma. Even so, by understanding it in that manner and trying somewhat, they will realize it as the truth and reach a path where they cannot find fault with it.

[GV1:P0222] Question: Suppose one is actually living with a Guru. What would be his characteristics and capabilities?

[GV1:P0223] Answer: First, the locals and those close to him will feel that there is a goodness in him greater than anything else. A spontaneous affection will be felt towards him without his knowledge. Secondly, if one observes his actions carefully, it will be evident that there is greater weight and depth in all his deeds. Thirdly, in his manner of interacting with people, even if he lacks formal education, he will habitually act with the knowledge characteristic of someone possessing education and wealth. One will mostly see from him actions that please a majority of people. Even if someone speaks disapprovingly, he will not stand to strongly oppose and argue with them. Or if he does oppose, it will only be to contradict for the sake of the matter at that moment and then move on.

[GV1:P0224] It is difficult to sustain any harsh, strong, or permanent opposition in him. Fourthly, actions imbued with empathy, kindness, and compassion, sweetness of words, humility upon seeing virtuous people, loving them more than one's own kin, not violating the words of the Guru, not feeling satisfied upon hearing words that disrespect Gurus, opposing and defeating such words if possible, being able to do good in that position, always pursuing the love of God in any sorrow, happiness, danger, or affection—thus, the knowledge to completely understand the Guru will be inherently vested in him.

[GV1:P0225] Now, the second type of devotee will only exhibit all these aforementioned qualities to half their extent. In certain matters, he will feel the need to prioritize his own actions. To celebrate and show off its merits, some mischievousness will emerge in him. Even if he has love for the Guru, he tries to highlight and maintain certain things. However, even if there is a feeling of complete love, there will be circumstances where he is unable to love completely.

[GV1:P0226] The third type of devotee will accept everything and continue to work. However, if there is a situation where he lacks freedom or if the Guru himself reprimands him, he will just walk away as if that were the final straw. When the fourth type acts, he will do everything well. He will not show stinginess in spending money or in other matters. If something he dislikes is said, he will constantly show an opposing nature in his actions. He will constantly display his greatness born of wealth and splendor. He will absolutely not have the nature of giving what is useful in his hand to others.

[GV1:P0227] If opposed, he will behave worse than a wicked person and will be inclined to destroy. Even if it is the Guru, he will push them into a dangerous zone. If necessary, it will even lead to destruction. It may also completely hinder the growth of the movement. Amidst all this, the Guru will continue to work with all of them in the same field. Primarily, according to the fortune of the Guru, there is a convention of having the most perfect disciple. With the attitude that there is no counter-word to a word, filled with sacrifice, humility, love, and richness in every action, it will seem to us as though a devotion entirely absorbed in God and the Guru overflows in him.

[GV1:P0228] His final stage will be seen as akin to the Guru or magnified tenfold. The world will make its judgment. It is the service of such individuals that benefits the world forever.

[GV1:P0231] Question: There is a state where, through devotion, one gains experience and develops a visionary nature, isn't there?

[GV1:P0232] Answer: Yes, it is true that there is a visionary nature. In our own experience, we clearly see it here in both children and adults, don't we? It is our experience that this visionary nature has been seen in followers of all religions to date. In Moses and his followers, in Jesus, in the Prophet and his followers, this nature can be seen reflected more or less—similarly in Buddha and the Indian sages. It is seen reflecting in the sages of the past and the present. In recent times, the same is seen in Chattampi Swami and Narayana Guru. It is clearly reflected in the poems of Narayana Guru Swami. It can be seen throughout the *Subramanya Stuthi* as well. He has spoken in exactly this manner about Shiva and Krishna. Look at how he has concluded in a verse about the Guru of Subramanya.

[GV1:P0233] Turning southwards with compassion, under the banyan tree-

[GV1:P0234] May the deity who sat in the shade protect us.

[GV1:P0235] About Subramanya

[GV1:P0236] He has twelve eyes, ears, and hands correspondingly-

[GV1:P0237] seeing that, is there such compassion-

[GV1:P0238] No one else has it this way, have you not seen the suffering this slave undergoes here?

[GV1:P0239] People who see me scold me, with one ear at least-

[GV1:P0240] haven't you heard it?

[GV1:P0241] Relieving my distress and granting me refuge-

[GV1:P0242] Don't you need just one hand to do so?

[GV1:P0243] In this way, all these mentioned hymns are manifestly evident.

[GV1:P0244] Furthermore, if we examine *Darshanamala* and *Atmopadesa Satakam*, some independent visionary nature can be seen. Such visionary nature will contribute to many good traits and many bad traits.

[GV1:P0245] Question: What is that, if the vision is not good, why is such a visionary nature seen reflected in both good and bad?

[GV1:P0246] Answer: That is to say, vision (*Darshana*) means discerning the bad and the good to realize the Truth (*Sat*). That is exactly what is reflected in the first verse of the Gita. There are many confusions in the interpretations of scholars. By mixing grammatical nuances, ordinary people are confused and perplexed by it. When looking at reasonably accurate recent interpretations of this, some flaws can still be seen. In Vinoba Ji's interpretation, Dr. Radhakrishnan's interpretation, and Dr. Nataraja Guru's interpretation, what emerges is only the nature of having beautifully examined and understood the stage of a play. The nature of the person who wrote, created, and acted in the play is not seen. Similarly, when the art of dance is performed, everyone knows how to say it is good or not bad. The dual meaning applied in the physical grace of the dance art can only be observed closely by those who practice and teach dance. Just as a butcher can preach and train in self-knowledge (*Atmavidya*), or a tribal person making a living by hunting can attain self-realization (*Atmadarshana*), it is clear that by fortune, the attainment of God can be achieved in all virtuous natures.

[GV1:P0247] Question: What is the reason for you speaking in such a roundabout manner? Your answer seems to exceed the bounds of the question asked.

[GV1:P0248] Answer: It is so that you do not confuse a good matter by asking numerous questions.

[GV1:P0249] Question: Do you have a dislike for questions being asked? Should we assume that is why you spoke so harshly?

[GV1:P0250] Answer: No, there is no need to assume that. When numerous questions are raised and asked, it becomes impossible to state the reality clearly. I only intended this much in what I said. There is a misconception that self-knowledge (*Atmavidya*) is useful only if one lines up scholarship and numerous qualifications. Self-knowledge is solely the grace of God.

[GV1:P0251] Question: In your experiential nature, what do you mean by visionary nature?

[GV1:P0252] Answer: I also have a lesson of experience that one should attempt to impart visions (darshana) to people only after carefully understanding their nature and handling them beautifully for twelve years through corrections received directly from a guru. Within two or three years of having a vision, there are situations where we can reflect some experiences through others. At that time, we might feel that we have almost achieved it. Many have thus reached the danger zone. We too have not been immune to such things.

[GV1:P0253] Question: So the vision is true, and you said that this truth should be preserved in its entirety, didn't you?

[GV1:P0254] Answer: Yes.

[GV1:P0255] Question: Then, in your opinion, how should this aspect of vision be brought about without errors?

[GV1:P0256] Answer: The aspect of vision—firstly, it involves describing the macroscopic and microscopic causes that occur in the immense and the infinitesimal, both big and small. It is about the causes of creation and destruction of the past, future, and present. Even as one sees this, one will not get any idea of what it is or how it is. This is because all these are seen in a mixed-up, chaotic state. Such people are prone to making many blunders.

[GV1:P0257] Question: What kind of blunders would these be?

[GV1:P0258] Answer: Recently, about six or seven years ago, there was a warning from somewhere in the Western countries that the world was going to end. Accordingly, during those two months, some people engaged in charity, went to temples, and there was even an incident of mass bell-ringing in churches. These are some of the blunders that happened like that. Secondly, there are some visions that exhibit demonic characteristics. The blunders that occur due to not recognizing it - thus, the main blunder in this is the inability to distinguish between good and bad.

[GV1:P0259] Question: So, are you saying that we can see what is called demonic?

[GV1:P0260] Answer: Certainly, it can be seen. The nature of visions is difficult until that demonic aspect is removed and divinity pervades - this can only be corrected by familiarizing and rectifying it for at least twelve years.

[GV1:P0261] Question: Is it possible to convince the people of what has been described, in any way?

[GV1:P0262] Answer: There is no use in recording it like telling a few stories. No one can examine and understand it. Undisdainful devotion, respect, and knowledge that respects the greatness and smallness of the Guru are its basis. If one has scholarship and devotion, and if he also has faith, it will be a blessing like an extended helping hand.

[GV1:P0273] There are gurus in four paths. Karma, Yoga, Jnana, and Bhakti. A person who has perfected at least one of these can correct such things. Whatever path the vision belongs to, at first it will be a vision mixed with the demonic. Secondly, one mixed with divinity. Thirdly, one filled with godliness. If one does not act by recognizing it, or if the guru who makes one act is not such, one should not expect anything but ruin in every way. We can see many people who have been confused by visions like this. We have seen some of them in front of us too. It is because you do not notice it. That is to say, there are some people who lead a very pure life and live with devotion to God according to rules and regulations. This is seen in all religions and in all systems of yoga, devotion, and karma. Such dangers are mostly seen in them.

[GV1:P0274] Question: What could be the reason for that?

[GV1:P0275] Answer: They read and know a little something, and by increasing the weight of goodness in that very model, they learn about the things stated and do them. Then they are doing it with some firm resolve. At that time, they will experience the aforementioned visions. Truly, in a way that cools their minds, what they desired and what they experienced will unite. Because they have learned what was written, they will hold fast to it. But they will be unable to know or inform about the past, future, and present, or about the existing descriptions, or about the details of what is in the subtle visions. Then what agreed at first will no longer agree later. At this point, their minds will reach the verge of breakdown. It might even lead to madness. This is the defect of not having a guru. However, if it is a scholarly guru, he will restrain him to some extent with his scholarship. But if it goes out of hand, the jumping will repeat without stopping anywhere. I have had the opportunity to be acquainted with many such gurus and disciples. Thus, I have been able to bring back some people and even stabilize their family lives. I have also been able to turn some people towards goodness and leave them to their spiritual goals. Isn't that itself complete proof for us?

[GV1:P0322] Question: So, should we consider that the medium you intend is a householder (Grihasthashrami)?

[GV1:P0326] Question: But if that happens, is your intention that the nature of today's government should change?
