[GV1:P0328] Once you believe, there is no such thing as "I". If there is, it is only that which I believe in. Then I became that. It means that became me. Otherwise, if we go by the way seen even in people who believe they have known it today, we will never be able to see and know or experience it at any time. Let what I intend happen, then I will believe. So, if God does not wait for him and make it happen, he does not believe. Then we can see what the depth and weight of their belief really is.

[GV1:P0329] Question: You mentioned in a word that some gurus are also seen, didn't you?

[GV1:P0330] Answer: Yes, that is true. There are many such gurus. Such gurus will convince them that some experiences in the early days are true, and seeing that they are true, they will fully believe the guru. Growing like that, he will reach the level of the guru. The growth that happens after that will reach a state where the guru cannot correct it or the disciple cannot bear it. Danger will happen in such places. Then they will abandon him saying, "My son has grown beyond me." I personally have one or two such experiences.

[GV1:P0331] Question: What are the measures to be adopted to prevent that from happening?

[GV1:P0332] Answer: Devotion—we have been talking about the story of the one who is complete. But for those whose devotion is not complete, preceptors have shown certain paths according to the times. The matter of those who changed according to the times is what was mentioned in between. There are three types of devotion: blind devotion (Mudha Bhakti), pure devotion (Sattvic Bhakti), and devotion of knowledge (Jnana Bhakti).

[GV1:P0333] Question: What is meant by this blind devotion (Mudha Bhakti)?

[GV1:P0334] Answer: There are certain practices that ask if they can show some results by dancing in a trance using ghosts, spirits, and demons. All this is referred to as blind devotion (superstition). We might feel that some human beings themselves are incapable of manifesting some of its minor experiences. For example, if we go to an unfamiliar place ڊ if we visit a place where there is trance-dancing and such ڊ they often reveal details about the vehicles we arrived in, the characteristics of our home and parents, and some minor incidents that have occurred until then. They describe things like the house experiencing joys and sorrows due to such and such reasons ڊ they detail all of this.

[GV1:P0335] These are matters that are difficult to explain even for a true rationalist, or even for psychologists. Despite all this, because of these distortions, it is classified under foolishness. A path to self-realization is not seen through this either. The special devotion above this is called Satvic thought, Sakara thought (thought with form), and Nirakara thought (thought without form).

[GV1:P0336] Sakara thought makes humans Satvic through direct inference by means of certain manifestations and the awakenings resulting from them. Thirdly, by means of the nature of luminous spheres and the resonances arising from them, the nature of creation and dissolution is described and understood, and the state of complete eternity is experienced. It is the description of these three in manifold ways that is referred to as Puranas, Upanishads, and Vedas. The light of experience thus far is that not everyone is equally capable of understanding all these in detail and reaching the state of experience. These matters are seen shining in their complete form only in a very few blessed souls.

[GV1:P0338] July 1978

[GV1:P0339] Question: What do you describe as Sakara thought?

[GV1:P0340] Answer: When we speak of a deity of worship, it is not deities like Madan or Yakshi. They are deities belonging to the nature of the Trinity, or Gurus who have imparted some experiential nature in the same manner. If one holds on to any one form of the Trinity, the devotee's desire—its physical beauty, its glorious power, and its compassionate glance overflowing with devotion—will entirely come together, and we will personally experience the mind thrilling with overflowing, joyful devotion. All these harmonious imaginations are creatively formed in the devotee's own mind. Thus, with the manifestation of any of these, its primordial experience can be seen in dreams, deep sleep (sushupti), and the fourth state (turiya). Following this, it will continue in the waking state as well. When this happens, the devotee's mind will begin to overflow with joy. The sub-deities of such gods, as well as certain souls who are devotees believing in these gods, will also manifest along with it.

[GV1:P0341] Question: Once that manifestation has occurred, then there is no need to have an aversion towards other things, is there?

[GV1:P0342] Answer: I did not understand what you meant by other things.

[GV1:P0343] Question: By other things, I mean that once the deity manifests to him, he will be able to understand more or less everything.

[GV1:P0344] Answer: Some minor things about the deity will be understood. It will also be understood that this is a manifestation. However, not much help will be gained from it to enter into spirituality.

[GV1:P0345] Question: Why is that, isn't this spiritual?

[GV1:P0346] Answer: If you wish, you can call this the stepping stone to spirituality. Beyond that, this cannot be called spirituality.

[GV1:P0347] Question: Then what can we achieve with this Sakara thought?

[GV1:P0348] Answer: We often say in ordinary words that we attained a sort of liberation through this. First of all, this can make one experience it like a perfect, obedient servant who has believed and served. Secondly, it is difficult for the nature of atheism to reach him later. At the same time, he becomes firmly convinced that faith has a complete theistic existence (foundation). Other than these and similar things, it does not reach the true nature of spirituality.

[GV1:P0349] Question: Then what would be the other results if these gods are believed and worshipped so earnestly?

[GV1:P0350] Answer: The believers in the world will be able to receive some minor things from this person who made them experience it, like words that seem to have been suddenly experienced, and they will accept and act upon them. People will also enthusiastically start making minor offerings and the like. This can be carried forward up to a certain point. After that, both the one who believed and acted, and the one who made them act, may end up stagnating like water in a pond that never dries up.

[GV1:P0351] Question: I didn't understand that, it would be good if you could explain it once more.

[GV1:P0352] Answer: If gods and conditions are accepted, a human can test it and show results only up to a certain limit. After a long period like this, he may reach the position of that god. Thus, that ability of the god may not fully manifest in him, and even if it does, it will result in dissatisfaction. When that happens, the god himself will create adversities against him. Then he will hold on even tighter, pray, and perform even more rituals. The results might then increase slightly. But the results will turn adverse, making it seem as if the actions have become entirely futile. At that point, due to his mental distress, he will lose his mental balance entirely and turn into an incompetent person who causes more danger than an atheist.

[GV1:P0353] Question: Why does it happen like that? What is the reason for such a thing happening to him despite being so great?

[GV1:P0354] Answer: We have known from the Puranas that even for a deity, it is about living happily in the concept of heaven for a certain period of time. That is also what is known from wise sages. That is our experience as well.

[GV1:P0355] Question: Then, isn't it said in these Puranas and elsewhere that in the past, these deities were made to manifest, and great things were accomplished?

[GV1:P0356] Answer: That is more or less true. When the knowledge, qualifications, and intellect of the writers are mixed into it, errors occur in the Puranas. Those who study such errors, accept them as truth, and practice them will face the same blunder. They are the ones who are said to commit worse mistakes than atheists. It will require a very difficult phase for their souls to attain liberation.

[GV1:P0357] Question: What do you state as the reason for that?

[GV1:P0358] Answer: Because this soul learns to act in this manner and remains somewhat aware and unaware of the results of its actions, it may fail to live a respectable life while alive. The reason for this is the arrogance of feeling that one has experienced and known many things. Beyond that, there is an unwillingness to acknowledge anyone else. With this, all their actions become wrong, and at the same time, they lead a life unsuitable for ordinary people. They will be unable to speak about highly spiritual people and will even reject them.

[GV1:P0359] Many people of this kind can be seen in various places during the same period. Leaving their physical bodies, their souls will remain suspended in the atmosphere. They will not get a rebirth immediately. Standing there, they will gather souls lower than themselves to join them. Thus, they will form a group. They will trouble ordinary people and lead noble devotees astray.

[GV1:P0361] October 1978

[GV1:P0362] Question: Why was it stated in two different ways?

[GV1:P0363] Answer: Ordinary people sometimes face afflictions from ghosts and evil spirits. If it is under the control of such a fallen yogi (*Yogabhrashta*), it becomes difficult to remove. If the person is a ritualist or a devotee, it will lead the ritualist astray in his rituals. For a devotee, it will first invoke the deity worshipped by the fallen yogi, or manifest a mixed form of the deity the devotee believes in, ultimately bringing the devotee to the position of the fallen yogi. Thus, after passing many ages, if any great souls are born, when these spirits go there to cause trouble, they might be liberated. Alternatively, with the birth of a Guru belonging to the lineage of Manu, such souls might attain liberation. If they still do not get it, that soul might wander in the atmosphere until the end of the eon (*Kalpa*).

[GV1:P0364] Question: How do you determine this period of Manu?

[GV1:P0365] Answer: The period of one Manu is seen in the Puranas and Vedas as seventy-one Chaturyugas. During these Chaturyugas, when Gurus belonging to the lineage of Manu are born here and there, they liberate such souls either because the spirits troubled them or because the Gurus themselves became aware of them. Only those belonging to the lineage of Manu have the authority to do this. Gurus who worship deities, or those who come to guide people to the righteous path for two thousand or three thousand years, do not have this authority.

[GV1:P0366] Question: In which eras do such Gurus get born?

[GV1:P0367] Answer: Such Gurus are born in all eras.

[GV1:P0368] Question: How do humans understand this, and how do they deal with it in the world?

[GV1:P0369] Answer: Gurus born in the *Satyayuga* only have the task of convincing the people, through writing and speaking, about the knowledge of how the world should function in specific ways. It is a time when people truly see and respect the deities. Nothing stands in conflict with each other. That is due to the uniqueness of the era. That is why it is named *Satyayuga*. As the period of *Tretayuga* begins, certain deviations start appearing among the people themselves.

[GV1:P0370] Question: What is meant by saying "Mother, Father, Guru, God"?

[GV1:P0371] Answer: The first Guru is the mother. We do not know the father. From pointing out and introducing the father, that process takes place through the mother to a certain extent. Then, to an extent, the father leads, up to the limit of his knowledge. Beyond that, the father points out the Guru. That Guru provides the experience of God. Thus, the Guru as mother, the Guru as father, the Guru who knows God, and God as Guru—in this way, from birth, one must climb the steps of knowledge, further knowledge, and ultimate knowledge to seek peace. That itself is the goal. That itself is liberation, and human birth is precisely for that.

[GV1:P0372] Question: I wished to know your opinion about accepting *Sannyasa* (renunciation).

[GV1:P0373] Answer: *Sannyasa* is not a ritual like tying the nuptial thread in a wedding. It has been written in some places in what we call our scriptures that it is so. Such things are distortions that crept into our true lives over time, like adding water to milk. *Sannyasa* is not retreating to some corner to escape from actions, like closing one's eyes to make it dark. The body is meant to perform actions. Even the worship of God is an action. Therefore, the duty of a *Sannyasi* is to handle the problems of society. It was like that in the past. In the holy land of Bharat, that was the duty of a *Sannyasi*. From the day hypocrisy started in the name of *Sannyasa*, the downfall of Bharat began.

[GV1:P0374] Question: Previously, you had mentioned about the prayers to favorite deities (*Ishta Devata*) in certain places; it would be a blessing to hear about that.

[GV1:P0375] Answer: I shall tell you. The father might be highly proficient in mantras, and a universal preceptor (*Lokacharya*) in tantra. The favorite deity (*Ishta Devata* or *Paradevata*) would be a fierce male or female entity claiming paternity or maternity over all ghosts and evil spirits. To destroy anyone in the land, they will perform sorcery inside the heads of cats or chickens. They will make a roasted chicken fly. The liquor of a whole tavern won't be enough; they will still call out, "Bring more, bring more." Upon hearing that call, all fourteen worlds will tremble. This is how the glories of one's ancestral position go. Even today, such boasting can be heard in some villages and towns.

[GV1:P0376] Then the second stage. The father dies. There are minor troubles at home. What the astrologer who conducted the *Prashna* (astrological query) said, and what the maternal aunt's second son blurted out while in a trance, are exactly the same. There is not a single difference. The fiercely powerful father must be enshrined. The father will not let go. Thus, to purify the father, another sorcerer just like the father was brought in. Snapping fingers like purifying the *Koduveli* tuber, a chicken was sacrificed, and the father's spirit was invoked into a granite stone and consecrated under the shade of a tree in the compound. A lamp was lit, and prayers were offered. Needs were stated. Through dancing, swaying, and annual rituals, it became a custom. As generations passed, the dead sorcerer-father became a god.

[GV1:P0377] Excluding today's Vedanta preachers who claim everything is Brahman, let me ask a question: where will this worship—which bears witness to the spiritual essence of this man who captured and worshipped all evil spirits, and who did nothing but create notorious rumors in the land—lead the future generations? Is this the worship of God? Is this Indian culture? Is this the spiritual guidance of this holy land?

[GV1:P0380] Question: What is the initial nature of devotion?

[GV1:P0381] Answer: Attentiveness. There will be a nature of paying attention to whatever is seen. According to the Hindu tradition, there are numerous deities. In the beginning of devotion, the devotion towards gods and goddesses will keep changing. We might feel that we are good. In reality, if we observe closely, we will understand if there is anyone worse than us. A Guru is there to change the course of karma from previous births.

[GV1:P0382] Question: When devotion arises, will there be any flaws in it?

[GV1:P0383] Answer: When devotion arises, although great love and glory may come at first, there are some flaws in it too. That is—those living in the next house might have base qualities. Looking at them, one might say, "Alas, they are wretched people." They will also retort, "Oh! Such devotion—chanting starts as soon as it dawns." When all this devotion comes to us, some among lust, anger, greed, delusion, arrogance, pride, and jealousy will disappear, while some others will surge up.

[GV1:P0384] Question: What is the reason for that?

[GV1:P0385] Answer: Didn't I say that desire (*Kama*) stands at the forefront in devotion? It will eagerly jump forward for a good color, a good object, and everything else.

[GV1:P0386] Question: You mentioned that three things can be understood through philosophical vision, didn't you? How can this be understood?

[GV1:P0387] Answer: One can know it by paying special attention to its color. However, it is not the same for a devotee, a yogi, a wise man (jnani), and a man of action (karmi). If it is a devotee, they see everything through the Guru. If it is a yogi, they might wander off the path. If the Guru is there to guide closely, then let them wander. If it is a jnani, they can see with discrimination. However, for a karmi, it can be seen only when combined with their own effort.

[GV1:P0388] Question: O Guru! What is the reason for attaining it in such various natures?

[GV1:P0389] Answer: I shall explain. If it is a devotee, there is no sense of 'I'. They will surrender everything to the Guru. If it is a yogi, it will be in the manner of 'I am everything'. They will give priority to their own affairs. They will speak of everything trivially. No matter what thoughts arise, not denying anything and not blaming anything is one of the greatest fortunes.

[GV1:P0392] If we say we must become one, as long as this order of worship remains uninterrupted, it cannot be removed from the human community. [GV1:P0393] Question: What is the reason for you to say so?

Why was it not conducted? That cannot be stated in this context. It will only help in creating agitation among the people. It was mentioned merely for the sake of knowing.

[GV1:P0395] Another thing: In Sivagiri, known as the Swami's samadhi place, innocent sanyasis and innocent brahmacharis have had to experience situations for ten years in a manner that no one else could know how they happened. Although many among them are still alive today, a person who lives with the knowledge of having experienced it is the Retd. Ayurveda College Principal, Sri. V. Bhargavan Vaidyar.

[GV1:P0396] All this originates from a culture that lacks the ability to respect and understand. Because of this, righteous sanyasis and brahmacharis vanished from the field of action. That continues even today. Apart from a few changes, it has not clearly resolved, and the disputes among the institutions caused by it have not ended even today. I merely mentioned these things as they are part of my daily experience. We, along with the people, still need to awaken and think so that this can deeply penetrate the very depths of the hearts of today's little children of the coming generations and be absorbed by them. I have a lot to say about all this.

[GV1:P0399] Question: Guru, please explain what the special benefit of the Pournami prayer is.

[GV1:P0400] Answer: Regarding its result, there is an outcome that cannot be diminished by anything else . Pournami is what fulfills the purity of intention of many births, acted upon knowingly and unknowingly. The Pournami fast provides the benefits of all other fasts. This is the day when observing all these fasts makes the ultimate Guru worthy of liberation . Similarly, it is a day that brings perfection to worldly life as well. Darkness does not spread even a little bit . On one side, there is a quality of joy and coolness, and on the other, the ability to conquer everything . In this coolness , seeds gain more vitality. The quality to generate and sustain it will also be attained.

[GV1:P0401] If one attains Samadhi on a full moon day after accumulating merit over numerous lifetimes, it is considered complete Samadhi. The atmosphere is also serene. As one sets, another rises. Wherever their rays fall, this virtue flows there as well. This vow assists the Guru in merging with God and dissolving into Brahman. The Pournami (full moon) prayer provides an opportunity for everyone to gather and pray collectively.

[GV1:P0402] The fundamental resolve is that, whether one contemplates its benefits or not, our prayers should enable the eradication of all our flaws and facilitate world peace by distinguishing between good and evil in the world, in a manner that benefits all sentient and insentient beings.

[GV1:P0403] A unique alignment occurs among the planets, through which a special energy is imparted for the welfare of the world. A genesis beneficial to the entire world may also occur on that day. This is an opportune time for both creation and dissolution. Just as this state can be envisioned in a mango blossom, it is understood to function similarly within human beings.

[GV1:P0406] Question: Guru, kindly elaborate on the remainder of what you explained last time regarding the specific benefits of the Pournami prayer.

[GV1:P0407] Answer: Although the spiritual and the material are similar, whichever we give more weight to is what will grow. The mother of a child born on Pournami must be conscious. If the pain experienced in a single moment can have such an immense impact, it is impossible to articulate the consequences of the actions we perform in pain over time, and the results of prayers offered in agony.

[GV1:P0408] Question: Guru, could you please explain about the special prayers in this ashram?

[GV1:P0409] Answer: This ashram has a specific purpose. It is not the mainstream convention that is followed here, but our own equivalent tradition. Our mode of worship is the most advanced among all those that have existed until now. One must understand what it is—its true value. There have been Gurus and lineages in the past as well. They all provide the guidance of their predecessors. Here, there are no predecessors. All of that is integrated into this. This is how one studies about a Guru. No one realizes that we are not merely clinging to a path shown by someone else. In ancient times, it was said that divine messengers received words. They called it an ethereal voice (Ashariri).

[GV1:P0410] Words are received from the light. We implement them while we are still alive. Previously, such knowledge was kept secret and preserved, only to be revealed through a disciple after the master's time. This is the difference. We did not create this. There is a profound greatness to it.

[GV1:P0429] June 1979

[GV1:P0430] Question: Guru, please explain the remaining details regarding the special prayers in this ashram.

[GV1:P0431] Answer: I have reminded you about our prayer once before. It is received from nature as an ethereal voice. Sages often receive it in this manner. However, even in this, it will not be perfected until a certain stage is crossed.

[GV1:P0432] Question: What is this stage that you mentioned?

[GV1:P0433] Answer: There are four stages of demonic entities.

[GV1:P0434] Question: What could be the reason for stating that demonic entities have four stages?

[GV1:P0435] Answer: Pey, Madan, Marutha – two stages. There is a category known as Manthramoorthi—a stage achieved by mastering mantras. One can attain mastery over Madan, Pey, and Marutha through mantras. Similarly, one can attain mastery over Bhadrakali, Mahalakshmi, Shiva, and Vishnu through mantras. At the same time, there is a stage for those who aspire to become enlightened beings. It is referred to as Brahmarakshas. Bhadrakali is also perceived as Brahman. That is Brahmarakshas. Even Lord Shiva is perceived as Brahman. That too becomes Brahmarakshas. Vishnu is also perceived as Brahman. That as well becomes Brahmarakshas. The forces starting from Bhadrakali onwards will cause harm during different phases of human life.

[GV1:P0436] Question: What is meant by phases?

[GV1:P0437] Answer: The phases refer to the era of Manu. You must have heard of something called the Manusmriti, haven't you?

[GV1:P0438] Question: What is Manusmriti?

[GV1:P0439] Answer: One can only understand it by studying it.

[GV1:P0440] Question: How can we study matters that we haven't even heard being spoken about properly?

[GV1:P0441] Answer: We were unable to comprehend this due to the detriments of the Varnashrama Dharma and the mode of worship rooted in the Trimurti system. We could not differentiate between righteous and unrighteous deeds. The Indian tradition—the earliest creations—comprised Rishis (sages) and Sanyasis (ascetics) in every aspect.

[GV1:P0442] Question: What is the reason for you to specifically differentiate and explain the concepts of a Rishi and a Sanyasi?

[GV1:P0443] Answer: There is no significant difference between a Rishi and a Sanyasi. However, the distinction lies only in certain aspects of how they manifest and function. A Rishi is one who harmonizes with everyone and acts in an all-encompassing manner.

[GV1:P0444] Question: I did not understand that. Kindly elaborate.

[GV1:P0445] Answer: That is, a Rishi is one who observes everything—whether right or wrong—without blaming anyone, enduring and forgiving entirely, consoling himself by accepting all faults as his own, and applying this equanimity among the people. A Sanyasi is not like that. He firmly believes that his actions are unequivocally right and desires to be respected by others.

[GV1:P0446] Guruvani

[GV1:P0447] July 1979

[GV1:P0448] Question: Guru, it would be beneficial if you could elaborate further on the differences between a Sanyasi and a Rishi that you explained last time.

[GV1:P0449] Answer: I have already stated that a Sanyasi believes his actions are right and expects others to revere him. If he is displeased with the actions of others, he may even abandon them entirely. Alternatively, much like Sage Durvasa, he might adopt a stance of destroying the wrongdoers before proceeding further. He believes that his will must prevail, regardless of who is destroyed in the process.

[GV1:P0450] However, an individual who is both a devotee and a Rishi will attain that position without much deviation. With compassion and mercy towards everything, and mindful that everything should be forgiven as ordained by God, he is able to function moderately and appropriately in due time. Such individuals do not desire occult powers (*Siddhis*) at all. A Rishi is one who acts with the conviction that whatever grace God bestows upon him through his sacrifices is sufficient. This is the difference between a Sanyasi and a Rishi.

[GV1:P0451] Question: Then you had mentioned the matters ranging from Madan, Marutha to Mantramoorthi.

[GV1:P0452] Answer: Yes, I did not mention the Yogi. The other entities—ranging from Madan up to Mantramoorthi—exhibit various forms to display their occult powers and make humans experience them. Consequently, people quickly notice this and propagate that he is a realized soul, which brings about a multitude of other consequences. Deluded by this, they become arrogant, assuming this to be the entirety of knowledge. As a result, their devotion and righteous actions falter, and many become ensnared. That soul itself will be deprived of liberation and will have to wander and undergo rebirths for a very long time.

[GV1:P0453] Question: Regarding rebirth—were you referring to previous births?

[GV1:P0454] Answer: Yes.

[GV1:P0455] Question: So, are we to understand from your statement that one can perceive past births and related matters?

[GV1:P0456] Answer: Yes, one can observe the soul entering other lower life forms and different wombs, up to its meritorious aspects. It is such individuals who have evaluated and spoken about birth and death.

GURUVANIKAL · October & November & December 1979 · Volume 1
Malayalam source paragraphs GV1:P0474 to GV1:P0504
English line for line; each paragraph carries its Malayalam source number.

[GV1:P0474] October, November, December 1979

[GV1:P0475] Disciple: What is the necessity for having firmness in faith?1

[GV1:P0476] Guru: An explanation for this was given in the Santhigiri magazine here, haven't you read it?

[GV1:P0477] Disciple:2 Even though we read it from time to time, our doubts have still not been cleared.

[GV1:P0478] Guru: It is difficult to instantly convince you about what faith is, as it is hard for a heart lacking inherent tendencies (*Vasana*) to grasp it merely through words. *Vasana* refers to the resultant fruits of the merits and demerits (*Punya* and *Papa*) that you have accumulated at the time of your birth. Merits and demerits imply the characteristic qualities present in our soul prior to our birth.

[GV1:P0479] Disciple: How is that so? What do you mean by the characteristic qualities present before birth?

[GV1:P0480] Guru: Our Hinduism or Sanatana Dharma (*Sanatana* refers to the culture of the Gurus of respective eras; meaning that which is eternally applicable). We neither had the opportunity to study that culture beforehand, nor do those currently present possess the knowledge to impart it. As an obstruction and a stumbling block to this, it was deliberately manipulated so that it would not be accessible to anyone other than the Brahmins. The Trimurti system and the Vedic system subdued the Varnashrama Dharma, which was considered superior, and reduced it to mere class distinctions. However, it did not benefit the aforementioned Brahmins either. The reason it was of no use was that the Vedic rituals advanced among the Brahmins and reduced their duties to mere Tantric practices.

[GV1:P0481] The Trimurti system was a framework designed to manage not just life, but also governance through these duties. When governance and mythological epics were thus integrated and elevated in a way that made them appear as the visible gods themselves, and as they prepared to study and teach it, the memory of Manu, the primordial Guru, faded away from among us. Through this, no true knowledge could be attained either. At the same time, extremely degraded modes of worship were prescribed for castes from the Nairs downwards.

[GV1:P0482] 1. This Guru-Disciple dialogue was given the title *Human Community—Yesterday, Today, and Tomorrow*. Later, it became a part of the book under the title *Humanity—Yesterday, Today, and Tomorrow*.

[GV1:P0483] 2. The disciple's name is printed as Vellayani Appukuttan Nair in the magazine.

[GV1:P0484] Through that worship, not only were we unable to comprehend the path forward, but it also became impossible for them to provide us even a hint—or for themselves to attain—the knowledge of what was required for us in different eras. In this context, the matter of faith that you asked about remains merely in name, aimlessly circling like an enigma.

[GV1:P0485] Only those who have experienced and known faith can completely articulate its form. If such experiential matters are spoken to anyone other than those approaching that experience, it will become an object of ridicule. Thus, it can only be explained to you through simpler examples. Faith is love. The love towards one's father and mother. The love between siblings, the love between husband and wife, the love for relatives, the love for friends, the love for things that are dear, and among those dear things, the love towards the medium called God. What needs to be specifically understood is how this medium called God is utilized.

[GV1:P0486] That love or medium called God is truth. Our ancestors have reminded us that it is love, glory, and lightness. Truth, righteousness (*Dharma*), compassion, love, and empathy are all noble terms associated with this. The Guru is the one who harmonizes and actualizes all these together. When one acts with faith in the words of the Guru, it is experienced as truth and as God. Thus, it became evident that the Guru is the supreme path to realizing the concept of God. It is in this era that the Guru illuminates before us in an absolute and complete form.

[GV1:P0487] Disciple: What is the reason for giving such prominence to the Guru in this era? There were Gurus in the past as well, weren't there?

[GV1:P0488] Guru: In the past, that is, before the time of Krishna, actions were in accordance with the *Yugadharma* (the duty of the age). Except for a few shortcomings, things were progressing according to the *Yugadharma*. *Yugadharma* encompasses the *Krita Yuga*, *Treta Yuga*, *Dvapara Yuga*, and *Kali Yuga*. This is how the four ages (*Chaturyuga*) are established. Among these, during the *Satyayuga* (*Krita Yuga*), all of us human beings lived truthfully together, without any discrimination. However, when the age changed, that form of light which was perceived as truth, reality, and love, disappeared. While the bewildered humans remained confused for a long time without knowing what it was, some intelligent and curious individuals began to spend their time in penance and prayer deep inside the forests, on riverbanks, in desolate places, and on seashores. After prolonged efforts, depending on the extent of their spiritual elevation, certain forms and lights began to briefly appear and vanish here and there. After a long time passed in this manner, some began to draw what they had seen in the forest on trees using green leaves. Those on the seashore began to record the nature of the light and the sunbeams they saw on the horizon.

[GV1:P0489] Thus, as time progressed, various forms and expressions were drawn and recorded, adapting to the times, as if it were a creation. Subsequently, a desire emerged to assign words to these. When they prayed for this, they began to receive words from the atmosphere, both through light and otherwise. They named this *Ashariri* (a disembodied voice).

[GV1:P0490] Later, when letters were invented, scholars attempted to inform us by recording all these through writing. Thus, the term *Mantra* originated. They started praying by assigning a specific mantra to each form. Mantras, *tantras*, and *homas* (fire rituals) were uniquely prescribed for deities of different forms, establishing a formal system of worship. In this way, they evolved into various distinctive rules and injunctions.

[GV1:P0491] Thus, mantras and tantras transformed into prescribed rules, and with the advent of the *Dvapara Yuga*, they became manifestations. Consequently, the deities of the *Treta Yuga* and the *Dvapara* period became manifest deities. Beyond that, when neither we nor our lineage were able to utilize the words of the Guru, which carry an illuminating commanding power, we had to remain content with the mantras and tantras used for worshipping the deity as a manifest god. Furthermore, these tantric and mantric practices were handled in such a way as to imply that even Vaishnavism and Shaivism were unsuitable for the Dravidians.

[GV1:P0492] Over time, the Dravidian practice of finding satisfaction in worshipping through the remaining *Shakteya* (Goddess-centric) traditions became distorted, turning into absolute madness and frenzy. Thus, *Yakshis*, *Madans*, and *Mantramurthis* became gods. In this manner, the glory of God was reduced to mere swaying and delirious dancing. Among these frenzied people, who lacked any literacy or other informative knowledge, even if one or two good individuals emerged within that large community, they were left unable to do anything, forced to stand by in utter bewilderment, not knowing what ought to be done.

[GV1:P0493] This situation gradually accumulated and began to manifest as claims of 'our caste' and 'our religion'. Adequate guidance to grasp the deeper meaning of any of this was largely unavailable. However, after a long time had passed in this manner, the concept of freedom emerged from the evolving thoughtful nature among them. During the period when people were enamored with systems of imitation, they suffered without freedom, facing immense hardships, and were even denied the right to education. Human beings grew like wild plants, completely unable to leap toward true knowledge.

[GV1:P0494] Thus, the desire for freedom occasionally surged among the people who had been trampled upon and kept like mere grass for a long time by the combined forces of mighty rulers and cunning *tantriks*. Then times changed. By that time, the Westerners had discarded their obsolete forms of worship and adopted new ones, a process that began with Moses and was completed during the time of Jesus. The Arabian people, adhering to the words of the Prophet, renewed their worship protocols and learned to live systematically. Through their prophethood, which served as the words of a Guru, they were able to pursue a creative life in a manner suitable for their times. Thus, they strove to make their nations whole and perfect through art and prosperity.

[GV1:P0495] In this way, even if their isolated islands were geographically inhospitable, they inherently possessed the intelligence and freedom to live and sustain life in that environment. Thus, as their lifestyles were repeatedly renewed over time, and as education and intellectual enlightenment flourished, they set out to investigate whether any other human societies were living in a similar manner. That is how they discovered this land. Though their initial intentions might have been rooted in goodness, selfishness is, after all, an inherent human trait. Arriving here in various capacities, engaging in trade and other crafts, those intelligent individuals who understood the cultural values, as well as the highs and lows of the local populace, discovered the vulnerabilities to exploit. Using their financial power, they thoroughly grasped the deep-rooted inequalities and divisions among the impoverished people—divided by caste upon caste. They assisted the upper classes with wealth and helped the lower classes by providing food and clothing. By winning them over, they utilized their self-serving interests to seize and consolidate political power. They subsequently implemented their willful propaganda and their version of religious freedom.

[GV1:P0496] As a result, when education, wealth, and enlightenment grew among some of these poor people, those who previously had no religious freedom or knowledge about religion grew under a different shade; some attained the goal of religious freedom and remained content with it. Thus, it became undeniable to say that everything fell into their hands. However, they also acted in a way that imparted a level of civilization to us, aligning with their own standards of civilization. If we carefully observe their actions, we can understand the true motive behind all of this.

[GV1:P0497] The foremost among these is that a great soul named Krishna was born in a downtrodden community known as the Yadava clan. They were categorized as the Krishna group and brought under control. By feeding them with tantras and mantras, they were manipulated and kept in their marginalized state. The words of the preceptor failed to uplift them. Following this was the advent of Buddha. Although previously born among the downtrodden, he was then born among the Kshatriyas. Just as what could not be completed during the time of Moses was fulfilled through Christ, God orchestrated various maneuvers here, back and forth, to bring it to completion.

[GV1:P0498] What that means is, among the Westerners during the time of Moses, the question asked was, 'Oh, are you the Son of God? Is this going to happen through you?' To fulfill this, God blessed by making a son with no claimed paternity into a prophet. Thus, leaving a people who refused to accept him—despite being given noble lineage, capability, and simplicity—to wander on an ignorant path for two thousand years, he was eventually placed in the womb of a carpenter's daughter, who had no profound knowledge, capability, or wisdom, and was born in a manger, transforming him into a prophet. Over here, however, even before that, Krishna was born among downtrodden humans, suited to the times. Over two thousand years later, since that did not take full effect, Buddha was born. He advised setting aside the conventional modes of worship practiced up to that point, suggesting that the *Panchashila* (Five Precepts) was sufficient, aiming to instill a greater sense of freedom. Since the authority of kings and other freedoms existed, it was accepted and practiced to some extent. But because the *Varnashrama Dharma* (the caste system), the *Trimurti* tradition, and a certain degree of Brahminical hegemony persisted, it became impossible to render the path—which operated on the ideology of religious freedom among ignorant people—completely pure and holy.

[GV1:P0499] During that period, this somewhat aged concept of freedom drove away the Guru tradition, firmly re-establishing the *Varnashrama* and the *Trimurti* system in its place. In such an era, with the intention of imparting a bit more knowledge to humanity, by the same divine fortune that brought forth Jesus, Buddha, and the Prophet, Shankaracharya was born in another place. In order to convince the people that their understanding was flawed, he spoke accordingly, established four *Mathas* (monasteries) to put this into practice, and founded *Advaita* (non-dualism) with the intent that a contemporary system of worship should emerge among you.

[GV1:P0500] By integrating this into the aforementioned Trimurti tradition, and deliberately withholding the philosophical insights of Vedanta, it was amalgamated with the Puranas and the Trimurti system, thereby institutionalizing absolute Vedic hegemony. Simultaneously, former Buddhist monasteries (*viharas*) were appropriated and transformed into Devi temples. Furthermore, they inculcated in these ignorant masses a depraved mode of worship characterized by animal sacrifice, arson, and abusive rituals.

[GV1:P0501] Consequently, *yakshis* (demi-goddesses) and ghouls once again became their deities. It was perhaps upon careful observation of these developments that the poet Kumaran Asan was prompted to remark that it was "fortified by the Smritis in the past." Although all the great spiritual luminaries articulate this, the process of rectification necessitates substituting an existing paradigm with a new one in order to dismantle the former; it is precisely this principle that figures like the Buddha, Sankaracharya, and Sree Narayana Guru elucidated through their teachings.

[GV1:P0502] However, the implementation of such rectification is obstructed by an impregnable systemic framework, firmly entrenched by the aforementioned political regimes and religious adherents. Prior to dismantling this structure, one must possess the requisite discernment to evaluate the stature and contributions of the preceptors who have emerged thus far. Naturally, such knowledge can only be gleaned through their foundational texts, followers, and direct disciples. Consequently, by appropriating every spiritual master who has appeared to date and obstinately asserting that salvation or liberation can exclusively be attained through their specific lineage, individuals become ensnared in an intellectual gymnasium; they unwittingly devolve into automated entities, ultimately succumbing to subjugation once more.

[GV1:P0503] Human Society: Yesterday, Today, Tomorrow

[GV1:P0504] (Brahmasri Karunakara Guru)

[GV1:P0505] January 1980

[GV1:P0506] Question: Why is it that even after attaining complete spiritual knowledge, one is unable to apply it in practice and progress?

[GV1:P0507] Guru: There is no other recourse to this than accepting an experientially perfect Guru as one's preceptor and seeking their guidance. It was when the intellect became exhausted by observing all this that we witnessed the emergence of individuals like Ramasamy Naicker, who founded the Dravidar Kazhagam. The predicament they faced was identical. There was no alternative paradigm to offer in its stead. They merely presented and justified two discourses before the public: rationalism or liberationism. Like a mirage, these concepts merely resonate in the realm of imagination and cannot be experientially realized. Furthermore, even if experienced individuals imparted this knowledge, the prevailing administrative system and followers lacked the capacity to assimilate and act upon it, or to propel forward those who did.

[GV1:P0508] Question: Advocate, why do you say so? Just as there are followers of the Prophet and Christ, are there not people in India who have accepted figures ranging from the Buddha and Sankaracharya up to Sree Narayana Guru?

[GV1:P0509] Guru: I have already acknowledged that this is the case. It is true that the teachings of Christ and the Prophet were adhered to up to a certain extent. I do not assert that it was absolute. In India, acknowledging this fact poses significant difficulty; having ousted them from their true essence, great luminaries like Sankaracharya, Sree Narayana Guru, and Chattampi Swami have been appropriated by their respective communities, thereby completely repudiating their foundational ideologies.

[GV1:P0510] Question: Today, Narayana Guru, as well as Sankaracharya as a world preceptor, are widely celebrated. Similarly, Chattampi Swami is recognized and revered precisely for being an erudite sage, is he not?

[GV1:P0511] Guru: Did I not previously confirm that such recognition exists? However, they are manipulating all of it to align with their own vested interests. Sankaracharya, who propounded Advaita, undoubtedly deserves to be venerated as a world preceptor. Yet, the monasteries administered by his followers historically refused to even serve food to non-Brahmins. Even during Sree Narayana Guru's lifetime, history records that those who followed and worked with him later claimed that his legacy belonged exclusively to a specific community, asserting that it was the community that created and sustained these institutions. There is a monument at Kaithamukku commemorating his sixtieth birthday (*shashtipoorthi*). Following its completion, during a ceremony convened to welcome him at the Keedangamparambu temple, the poet Asan composed and recited the verse "Narayanamoorthe Guru Narayanamoorthe" in the Guru's presence; this is the very hymn that everyone utilizes today for daily recitation. Because it is used for daily recitation, the complete essence of accepting him as the Guru is embedded within that prayer chant. They conflated this acceptance, which was originally intended for their specific objectives, in accordance with their own interests. Furthermore, the Murukkumpuzha temple and the Kalavamkodam temple, where he consecrated the deities, are frequently cited by all of us. At the Murukkumpuzha temple, where the ideals of "Truth, Righteousness, and Compassion" were inscribed, the temple authorities of that era subsequently installed a *kuzhavi* (stone pestle) in front of the original consecration and named the deity Kalakanteswaram. Similarly, in front of the mirror consecrated at Kalavamkodam, they installed an Ardhanareeswara idol. Moreover, intertwined with this is the history of them persecuting him for over ten years over property and assets.

[GV1:P0512] Question: I have a desire to hear and understand this history.

[GV1:P0513] Guru: It is inappropriate to state it in that manner. I shall elaborate briefly. The community fundamentalists of that era, particularly those possessing some degree of privilege and prestige, completely refused to acknowledge the Guru. Realizing that his overarching objectives could not be fully realized through them, in the eleventh year, he convened a group comprising fourteen members at Koorkanchery in Thrissur. It was officially registered there. It was christened the Sree Narayana Dharma Sangham. The members of the Sangham held its inaugural board. When the photograph of that event was taken, it included Sree Sankarananda Swami, who served as the head of the Sivagiri Mutt and attained *samadhi* recently, as well as Nataraja Guru.

[GV1:P0514] Question: Then why was Nataraja Guru not present in the Dharma Sangham?

[GV1:P0515] Guru: According to the bylaws of the Dharma Sangham, two signatures were required to become a member. He affixed only one signature and refrained from signing the second time. To my knowledge, the Swami himself inquired about this, to which he replied, "Swami, I also need footwear and shirts." The Swami responded, "That is permissible." Nevertheless, he declined to sign.

[GV1:P0516] Question: But people often claim that he was chased away from Sivagiri.

[GV1:P0517] Guru: To the best of my knowledge, that is inaccurate. It is true that in subsequent years, he served as an advisor there. That occurred during the period when Achuthanandaji was the head of the Mutt.

[GV1:P0518] Question: Then what was the reason for him leaving Sivagiri again?

[GV1:P0519] Guru: He had already relocated from Sivagiri prior to that. The Gurukulam in Varkala existed even before he assumed the role of advisor. It is understood that the Gurukulam in Ooty was established after seeking the Swami's permission. During his tenure as advisor, a young man named G.N. Das was serving alongside Achuthananda Swami in Sivagiri. Assuming he had committed some transgression, Achuthananda Swami physically struck him. Asserting that the punishment was excessive, he took the young man along with him to the Gurukulam and never returned. This is the factual truth of the matter.

[GV1:P0520] Question: Therefore, the Sree Narayana Dharma Sangham and the Sree Narayana Paripalana Yogam were established with two distinct objectives, were they not?

[GV1:P0521] Guru: Yes, it became clear that Narayana Guru's ideals would not be implemented through the SNDP. That is when he did this. During this time, he was also a patient. On that route, he went to Madras for Dr. Pandala's treatment. When he returned from there, the Ezhava elites welcomed him at the Kollam boat jetty, brought him to the place where Neela Hotel stands today, where he stayed and once again reminded them of the community's affairs. Saying, "Alright, let it be. I am coming to Sivagiri," he sent them back. When he reached Sivagiri again, three days before the Swami's Samadhi, the community leaders arrived once more. They spread out a will for him to sign. At that time, it was customary to support and raise the Swami, who was bedridden with severe illness. He suddenly sprang up and indignantly asked the visitors, "We made this through sorcery and medicine, right? Won't you even let me lie down?" In his agitation, he stood up, and a clock donated by someone immediately fell over and shattered. At that moment, the leaders left. His Samadhi took place on the third day. For his forty-first-day memorial ceremony (Nalpathukuli), these community leaders arrived at Sivagiri with a stay order, and not only did the ceremony not take place, but they were not even allowed to serve cooked food there. It had to be served across the paddy field. Following that, a legal case continued for ten years between the Sree Narayana Dharma Sangham and the Sree Narayana Dharma Paripalana Yogam. On that occasion, as the case was progressing in favor of the SNDP, in order to destroy the records showing that the Sree Narayana Dharma Sangham was established, two almirahs were lifted from Sivagiri, brought to a rock at the place where the watcher Kunjiraman lived on the southern side of the Sivagiri school, and burned. Thus, after the case dragged on for ten years, when a Receiver was appointed, while sorrowfully searching through various records, a copy signed by him stating 'I have resigned from the SNDP in thought, word, and deed' was found. It was produced in the bench of Sankarasubba Iyer, who was a High Court judge at the time. Through that, the verdict came in favor of Sivagiri and against the SNDP. At the time of the Swami's Samadhi, the Dharma Sangham, which was only a year old, could not reach its required functional capacity. Consequently, the Sangham was unable to properly manage its ideals. The ascetics who came later did not work focusing on the Swami's ideals either. Because this word became a monopoly of the Ezhavas, ascetics from other communities could not join it. As a result, because the community, lacking sufficient experience and tradition, did not know how to respect ascetics, many quarrels and disputes occurred. Through the passage of time, it has become as if it is the property of one community. Now it is impossible to correct it.

[GV1:P0522] Question: So, even while he was alive, the Guru had to endure a great deal of suffering, didn't he?

[GV1:P0523] Guru: Absolutely. There are records showing that not only this community but other communities as well harassed him, starting from the time they uprooted the casuarina tree at Aruvippuram and chased him away from there. I am not discussing that now. From what has been said so far, haven't you understood what they have transformed the Guru's ideals they adopted into? Similarly, the Nair community has turned Chattampi Swami into the property of the Nair community. While the Swami was alive, he wrote and published a book titled *Vedadhikara Nirupanam*. The Nair community did not want it then. Today, as it has more or less come into practical experience, they want it. In the same way, Sri Sankaracharya was also built up by Vedic orthodoxy. They hid the Guru who established Advaita behind it. Therefore, without knowing the facts, there are quite a few people today who say that it was Sankaracharya who brought about the caste system. Haven't you understood from this? That is, the community itself is devouring these ideals and preserving them for their own exploitation to bring out something else. Following this, even the politics up to this day is aimlessly wandering without foundation, craving for something unknown.

[GV1:P0524] Guruvani

GURUVANIKAL · February 1980 · Volume 1
Malayalam source paragraphs GV1:P0525 to GV1:P0564

[GV1:P0525] February 1980

[GV1:P0526] Question: What is the purpose of this Kumbha Mela? It is not our custom to worship gods and goddesses. Then with what intention is the Kumbha Mela conducted?

[GV1:P0527] Guruji: It is called Kumbha Mela; it is not called Kumbhabhishekam, is it?

[GV1:P0528] Question: No. We often hear the term Kumbha Mela in temples. I am asking assuming it is similar to that.

[GV1:P0529] Guruji: This is not like that. You will understand it naturally when you become familiar with it. Nevertheless, since you asked, I will tell you. I was trained and brought to realization among those who believe in these gods and goddesses. You clearly know that experiential nature exists here, don't you?

[GV1:P0530] Question: I know. I do not have much knowledge about that experiential nature. I do not know whether it is an experience derived from gods and goddesses or an experience from the Guru lineage.

[GV1:P0531] Guruji: I had one or two experiences before leaving home. After leaving home, I had a visionary experience in Aluva. That too was not complete. Following that, I came to Sivagiri because of that experience. I had two or four experiences at Aruvippuram. After that, until the age of twenty-seven and a half, I had no notable experiences. However, following that, I found a Guru, and in connection with that, although there was no order, discipline, or method, the experience had to be truly realized. Thus, it was first experienced on the veranda of the Thuckalay Munsiff Court. It was after two and a half years that I was able to experience it extensively in the right path. By then, it had been a year since I had moved away from Sivagiri. Initially, I saw the aforementioned gods, goddesses, and evil spirits, and believed in them itself. Thus, I was able to see with my physical eyes gods and goddesses, the subordinate gods and goddesses associated with them, and subsequently evil spirits, and even the subtle forces of this world.

[GV1:P0532] Question: How can you reflect in this world that you saw this as the truth?

[GV1:P0533] Guru: Why do you ask like this? Are you not seeing it here now? You hear it being said that the children here have this vision, and through them, certain disease traits, things that doctors cannot diagnose, they subtly discover and declare that it happened for a specific reason—that you have this particular trait, or your house has it, or your inauspicious time is such and such. Have you been able to see that they believe it to be true?

[GV1:P0534] Question: Yes, I have. I understood that it was true in my own case, didn't I?

[GV1:P0535] Guruji: Then why did you ask how this will be reflected among the people?

[GV1:P0536] Question: I had not thought this far.

[GV1:P0537] Guruji: Following this, I will answer what you asked. Thus, I have been able to convince not only gods and goddesses but also the sages who believed in gods and goddesses and their lineage.

[GV1:P0538] Question: After that, what is the reason for saying that the worship of gods and goddesses is wrong and abandoning it?

[GV1:P0539] Guruji: I did not say it is wrong. I did not say that gods and goddesses do not exist. I only said that today, a form of worship suitable for these times is needed.

[GV1:P0540] Question: By "these times," you meant the Kali Yuga, didn't you?

[GV1:P0541] Guruji: Yes. Haven't you heard through some Puranas that gods and goddesses have no place in Kali Yuga, and that they too will take birth in Kali Yuga to attain liberation?

[GV1:P0542] Question: Yes. So, we should understand from what you said that even gods and goddesses have births.

[GV1:P0543] Guruji: It is not that you should understand what I said. The previous authors of the Puranas, as well as the authors of the Upanishads, are seen recording about their births through some histories. For example, we have heard about the story of *Parayi Petta Panthirukulam*. The great figures in it are Nandanar, Pakkanar, Thiruvalluvar, Naranathu Bhranthan, Vayillakunnilappan, and Avvaiyar. In times like these when all this has even come out as cinema, what is the difficulty for us to know?

[GV1:P0544] Question: We clearly understood what you said. We understood that there is birth, that even gods and goddesses can only exist accordingly, and that beyond this, there exists divine power, God, and Brahman.

[GV1:P0545] Guruji: Yes, so you completely believe this now, don't you?

[GV1:P0546] Question: Yes, I believe it.

[GV1:P0547] Guruji: During the time these experiences were occurring, several people approached me with faith; some viewed me in the tradition of a Guru and began having experiences themselves. As these experiences commenced, they started sensing not only deities but also a whole lineage of Gurus within themselves. After about three years had passed in this manner, we began to notice some minor errors—errors even in the visions they were experiencing.

[GV1:P0548] To eliminate those errors, we engaged in divine worship to the best of our abilities. Furthermore, since God had granted us the opportunity to meet each of those Gurus and express our grievances, we conducted all possible trials and experiments within our capacity at that time. None of these efforts yielded any fruitful results. The struggle itself became the only outcome.

[GV1:P0549] During that period, I was in Varkala. At that time, some of the very individuals who had encountered these experiences began speaking ill of me, completely disregarding their own experiences. Through them, this attitude permeated among the locals, leading to numerous defamatory campaigns and various attempts to obstruct our path. Suffice it to say that we somehow barely managed to escape from this predicament.

[GV1:P0550] Question: Why is it that despite having such a progression of experiences, such adversities came to pass?

[GV1:P0551] Guruji: It is precisely for you to understand this in detail that I began speaking in this manner. A testament to this can be found in the story where Gandharvas and Kinnaras came to disrupt Vashistha's yagna and subsequently halted it, following which Vishwamitra brought Sri Rama and Lakshmana, stationed them as guards with the king's permission, drove the disruptors away, and completed the yagna.

[GV1:P0552] Question: Yes.

[GV1:P0553] Guru: History states that many great souls have been made to experience similar situations.

[GV1:P0554] Question: What is the reason for experiencing it this way?

[GV1:P0555] Guruji: This is not the era of deities. When we worship them and reach a state of fruition, some pure souls—not everyone, but as hundreds of thousands and millions of devotees pass by—some emerge like Vyasa and Vashistha. The attempt is to obstruct them. Similarly, anyone who ascends to that level will be obstructed.

[GV1:P0556] Since it is not their era, if a human being manages to ascend through the righteous path, the deities create these entanglements in this state to prevent the individual from suddenly surpassing the realm of the deities and ascending directly to the state of the Supreme God.

[GV1:P0557] Question: Was it in that state that they brought disrepute to you at Varkala and attempted to obstruct the righteous path?

[GV1:P0558] Guru: Yes, it was then that I received a notification, not from these deities but from some light, to leave that place and come sit here. That is how I came to be here.

[GV1:P0559] Thus, nine months after arriving here, I was able to receive a correction for this and overcome this state. Through that correction, we were made to perform what was called a completion twenty-seven times. We only understood that a stage had been crossed. We did not comprehend what it was. For the twenty-eighth time, we were asked to conduct a prayer, calling it a completion. We conducted the prayer. On the ninth day after starting that prayer, we were told to place a Kalasham. Placing the Kalasham, an order was given to perform rituals in specific ways for seven days. We did so. An instruction was given to take the Kalasham and perform it in specific ways. That was also done. The reason for this Kumbhamela was received through a revelation on that day.

[GV1:P0560] This will be beneficial annually for believers and faithful vow-makers. For both children and adults, to address any illness or to achieve any other objective, conveying a prayer—or performing it with all kinds of traditional instrumental music—can be undertaken by those making vows.

[GV1:P0561] The revelation stated that it would serve as both a festive event and a means to fulfill the objectives of the believers. It declared that this would become immensely significant in the world. The Kumbhamela is conducted exactly as received in the revelation regarding this movement.

[GV1:P0562] Question: So you are saying that this is in accordance with the divine will.

[GV1:P0563] Guruji: Yes, this is the divine will. The revelation states that it will grow larger as time passes, and in due course, it will manifest as the greatest meritorious act in the world. This is the brief overview of it.

[GV1:P0564] Guruvani
