[GV1:P0565] November 1980

[GV1:P0566] Question: Now, through what do you intend to establish this?

[GV1:P0567] Guru: I told you earlier itself, that this must be established through a Guru.

[GV1:P0568] Question: I understood that. You yourself say that it should not be through a Guru who lacks experience.

[GV1:P0569] Guru: Merely having experience is not enough. There are certain states and paths in this. A Guru who has not reached at least the seventh state through that path cannot establish and bring this to perfection.

[GV1:P0570] Question: Then how do you currently opine that this can be brought about?

[GV1:P0571] Guru: For that, we have words regarding the states that were directly communicated to us from the light itself. It is my absolute conviction that it can be brought about in that manner.

[GV1:P0572] Question: Could you please tell us a little about that?

[GV1:P0573] Guru: That is not something that can be simply told. However, I cannot help but say a little. Everything else will be revealed to the public by those who believe in this after my time. For now, I will tell you just a little for your understanding. When I speak, you will only understand if I explain from its original nature. Therefore, I will tell it that way. I will recall and talk about the place and house where I was born.

[GV1:P0574] Recalling the place and house where I was born, I had a family lacking in knowledge and a mother lacking in knowledge. I have no memory of seeing my father. He had passed away. I know from the locals that my father was a great devotee. My mother was someone without devotion. My maternal grandfather's family was also the same. From a very young age, I was aware of certain experiences. I did not mention them at home. I did not even tell my mother. There is a family temple at home. The divine worship of the people in this house meant going to the temple once or twice a month, that's it. My maternal grandmother used to take me to that temple. Once there, after the prayers were over, I would not feel like leaving.

[GV1:P0575] One day, after the prayers, when my grandmother held my hand and stepped onto the path, I was about to say that I am not coming. It was then that a voice came from there. I do not know from where. My assumption is that the Goddess spoke. The voice was like this: 'These people are fools and savages. Do not speak to them about this matter.' Thus, I would not do any such things while they were watching or listening. Nor did I inform them.

[GV1:P0576] During all that time, as far back as I can remember, I could see a form inside my chest. It is densely filled in there. It is from that form that the words emerge. I thought that all people had this. My body is like a microphone. I know that this lasted until I was about nine years old. Later, it disappeared. It was only after that I played or conversed. Until then, I wouldn't speak. Not because I didn't know how to. Assuming it was because my tongue couldn't twist properly, the family used to offer vows and rituals. Due to this, I couldn't even attend school at that age. Until about twelve years of age, I went to a traditional village school (Ashan Pallikkoodam) and acquired a basic education.

[GV1:P0577] I spent two years at the place where my mother was married for the second time. There, my stepfather used to drink and cause quarrels. Thus, within those two years, I internally felt an end to the life there. Since the desire to go to some ashram was within me, I wore a garland around my neck under the pretext of going to Palani.

[GV1:P0578] One day at dusk, my stepfather came home drunk, made excessive noise, and used inappropriate words. Because of that, I went and slept on the veranda of a nearby Bhajan Mutt. The next morning, I woke up, went to the teacher who taught me the alphabet, and told him that I wanted to go to an ashram. The teacher thought for a while, came with me, and enquired about where an ashram could be found. We met a person. He said that there is the ashram of Agamananda Swami in Kalady, but he didn't know if they had the practice of taking in and teaching children there. Regardless, the teacher took me there itself.

[GV1:P0579] Upon arriving there, I was informed that they were not enrolling children for education at that time due to a lack of facilities. Consequently, I walked from there and reached the Aluva bus stand by dusk. Hearing two individuals, who were oiled and ready, conversing about bathing at the ashram ghat, I followed them. Upon seeing the place, it indeed appeared to be an ashram. The head of the Sivagiri Mutt was present there on that day. I approached him and explained my situation. He replied, "Alright, let the morning come; go and sit over there for now."

[GV1:P0580] The following morning, he himself asked me to stay there. He then called the local secretary and entrusted me to his care. From that day forward, my life in the ashram continued there without interruption for two years. Subsequently, my life associated with Sivagiri extended for seventeen years, both at the main Sivagiri center and its branches. During this period, many things that people perceive as negative attributes came upon me without my awareness. I had committed no wrong to warrant this. I had to endure profound sorrow because of it. Having lived for so long without attaining any spiritual realization, my desire to find an enlightened soul intensified immensely. Fortuitously, that situation enabled me to find a Guru.

[GV1:P0581] Through him, I attained spiritual realization within two and a half years. Thus, two more years were spent residing in Sivagiri and its affiliated branches. In the interim, I faced significant opposition from my co-residents. They would initiate conflicts by levelling baseless accusations against me, of which I was entirely ignorant. I was compelled to endure such adversities in various forms while at Aruvippuram. I eventually relocated from there and returned to Sivagiri.

[GV1:P0582] Despite possessing this spiritual experience, my lack of formal education presented a significant hardship, as I was unable to read and comprehend other matters. Although they attempted to educate me on several occasions, an inherent inability to learn prevented me from acquiring literacy by any means. Upon my return to Sivagiri, I grew weary of an existence fraught with these deficiencies. Surrendering all the keys to the authorities, I resolved to seek out my Guru and reside with him. I informed him that I had grown exhausted of my life at Sivagiri, had relinquished the keys to the management, and had thus returned. The Guru remained silent for a considerable time before placing one and a quarter rupees in my hand. He then instructed me, "You must return to Sivagiri this very instant. There is no one present there. In those days, a sum of six annas would afford a meal at the Grand Hotel in Thampanoor. You should dine there and proceed to Varkala."

[GV1:P0583] I perceived this directive as exceedingly distressing. The predicament arose from the fact that I had already surrendered the keys and departed with the declaration that I would not return. However, guided by the conviction that a Guru's command must never be disobeyed, I resolved that I would only embark on any further journey after first returning there. The thought of my household also crossed my mind. They suffered from a distinct lack of cultural refinement. My guardians were descendants of those who had led an unrefined existence in the past. Consequently, the prospect of returning home felt utterly abhorrent to my way of life.

[GV1:P0584] Regardless, I decided to first proceed to Sivagiri before venturing anywhere else. Thus, I arrived there. Upon hearing the sound of my washing my hands and feet, Swami Kaivalyananda, who was serving as the treasurer at the time, called out, "Karunakaran, please come here for a moment."

[GV1:P0585] He informed me, "The Samadhi shrine has not yet been opened. Go, open it, light the lamp, perform the necessary duties, and return." Accordingly, I fulfilled the required tasks. At night, after our meal of gruel, he summoned me to sit at the pavilion in front of the Sharada Mutt and advised, "Do you understand? When you departed, there were many people here. Now, it is deserted. It has become a deplorable state of affairs. When individuals who have dedicated themselves through hardships, such as yourself, leave, this is the inevitable outcome. Many arrive here for various disparate reasons. None of them truly lead a life of spiritual contemplation. You must not depart in this manner again. Is this clear to you now? Therefore, you must never harbor such intentions or leave in the future."

[GV1:P0586] He narrated all his experiences following his participation in the Vaikom Satyagraha and meticulously detailed the tenets of the Sivagiri way of life, omitting nothing. Consequently, I firmly resolved not to leave Sivagiri again. Despite all these subsequent events, what captivated me the most was my Guru's prescient declaration that Sivagiri was deserted and all activities had ground to a halt. From that day onward, my reverence and devotion toward the Guru deepened profoundly, cementing my conviction that his commands must remain inviolable. Thus, as some more time passed, the Guru who had imparted these teachings to me arrived, sat near the Sivagiri culvert, and summoned me.

[GV1:P0587] He informed me, "You will soon experience a transition from this place, but do not depart abruptly," and promptly placed a one-rupee coin in my hand. True to his word, the prophecy materialized, and I was subsequently relocated from Sivagiri. Regardless, witnessing the fulfillment of his assurance instilled in me an even greater measure of faith and unwavering resolve. I knew I had to remain there until his return. He was on a journey, and seeking him out would be a futile endeavor. Following my relocation from Sivagiri, an individual named Gangadharan Muthalali, who harbored a personal fondness for me, facilitated the construction of a modest hut, where I subsequently took up residence. Even after more than six months had elapsed, the Guru remained entirely untraceable. There was a specific location near the beach where he occasionally stayed. Upon investigating that area, I eventually found him there. He remarked to me, "You have not yet attained spiritual realization, have you? You may depart only after that realization has been awakened within you."

[GV1:P0588] Consequently, I resided with him at the coastal area for an extended period. From there, he took me along to Thuckalay. During the daylight hours, we would wander through various mountainous terrains, marshlands, and forests. As the Thuckalay court convened and adjourned, he would frequent the court premises. I remained entirely oblivious to the purpose of these actions. The Guru would proclaim to the disciples congregated there, "Do you know him? Do you realize who he is?" Having seated me beside him, he would shower me with profound adulation, declaring, "He is an exalted soul. You fail to comprehend his true stature."

[GV1:P0589] I am well aware that he spoke such words extensively. However, I remained entirely detached from his assertions. A lingering curiosity did persist within me regarding his motive for bestowing such immense praise.

[GV1:P0590] Thus, on the fourth day at three in the morning, while nine of us were lying in a row, I suddenly experienced a sensation as though the entire world was collapsing and my body was being crushed into the size of a mustard seed. The Guru struck me lightly and inquired, "Are you frightened, child?" I replied, "My inner being is not afraid." "Ah ٹ ! You are saved."

[GV1:P0591] However, I lacked the sense to walk on the road. I could see vehicles coming, but I did not know to move aside. I had the traits of a madman at that time. He called one of his disciples, a man named Parameswaran Pillai, and said, "You must take leave for a few days and look after him." Thus, he took leave and took care of me. During the daytime, he would take me to all the holy places around there. When we went there, I could see all the conceptual deities and gods present there. There is a hill called 'Kattuva Sahib Mala' there. One has to pass the Padmanabhapuram Palace to go there. On the way, we rested at two places. There is a conceptual entity called Kalliyankattu Neeli there. Upon reaching there, the Guru made us all sit down and asked us to meditate. While I was meditating, Parameswaran Pillai called the Guru and said, "Swami, she has come!" "Tell her to go," the Guru replied. When I woke up from meditation, I understood. They were talking about the entity called Neeli. Then he asked me, "Did you see anything?"

[GV1:P0592] "No," I replied.

[GV1:P0593] "Alright, nothing with a demonic form will come before you. That is good. I need to make him do a task now."

[GV1:P0594] I did not understand what it was. Then, he praised me quite a bit and started walking along the way. He asked me to pick up a tile seen on the road. I picked it up. After walking a while, we saw a fairly decent temple with an outer wall where daily worship was held. The time must have been around three o'clock. The Guru sat near that temple. He made all of us sit down as well.

[GV1:P0595] "Open the temple and show everything to him alone," the Guru instructed. The sanctum sanctorum was locked. The rest were a few idols cast within the compound wall. Ablutions had been performed, flower garlands had been offered, and worship had been conducted on all the idols. When I returned, the Guru asked.

[GV1:P0596] "Did you see everything?"

[GV1:P0597] "I saw."

[GV1:P0598] "It is a clean place, isn't it?"

[GV1:P0599] "Yes."

[GV1:P0600] "There are few such clean places in Tamil Nadu, right?"

[GV1:P0601] "Yes."

[GV1:P0602] "Did you like everything?"

[GV1:P0603] "I liked it,"

[GV1:P0604] I replied. He got up from there and said,

[GV1:P0605] "Go inside, spit thoroughly on this idol, and come back."

[GV1:P0606] I felt a little hesitant and troubled. I am a Hindu believer, and moreover, how could I spit on this, which I had worshipped since childhood? However, the Guru's word could not be disobeyed. He asked me to step on its feet and the idol's chest. I obeyed that too.

[GV1:P0607] "Bring that tile here; take it, urinate in it, and bring it back," he said. I did so.

[GV1:P0608] "Pour a little of it on the crown of all these idols"—I did that too. After that, I had a fear inside me. I was afraid of whether I could do such a thing in the realm of faith. Then he came back, sat down, and gave us all an explanation about all this. It pertained to the details regarding the remnants of the ascetics, the remnants of what was offered to the deity, and what humans use. All these entities were suffering here. He convinced us that all of them had become eligible for liberation from this day onwards.

[GV1:P0609] We walked again and reached Kattuva Sahib Mala. We had visions there. He provided descriptions about it. We consumed the fruits and water we had brought with us and descended. Throughout this time, he explained the stories of the ascetics and their greatness to us. It was then that I realized there was a large part of what we had merely heard that was yet to be fully known. After returning, before coming back from the road, he stripped me of the shirt and dhoti I was wearing, handed me a piece of torn cloth, and asked me to wear it. After I wore it, he gave me a slap and told me to run.

[GV1:P0610] Saying "Where am I to go?" I ran.

[GV1:P0611] The experiences encountered on that journey were profound. In places like Suchindram and Kanyakumari, I had indescribable experiences. By this point, I developed an obstinate desire to reach the Guru as quickly as possible. I arrived. On my way, I received money for clothes without asking anyone. Moreover, I had attained profound internal experiences that could not be expressed to anyone. Upon hearing all this, he embraced me, wept, and bestowed a blessing, saying, "Now you may go anywhere, you will get everything you need." Immediately, I became adamant about going to Thiruvananthapuram. I boarded a train from Thiruvananthapuram to Varkala. He went to Vallakkadavu.

[GV1:P0612] Subsequently, for six and a half years, many such experiences were observed and corrected. After five and a half years, those who approached me began to have certain experiences. Thus, after seven years and three months (on the 1st day of the month of Vrischikam), three individuals arrived as if they were coming for morning prayers after a bath.

[GV1:P0613] Within that month itself, a sudden popularity surged among the people, reaching a level where hundreds of individuals were arriving daily. They began coming and reporting that they experienced relief simply by mentioning their ailments and leaving. I did not do anything in particular; I only made mental resolves for them. After seven months, the men and women who came began to experience a phenomenon of having visions. It was experienced by about fifty people to an extent recognizable as visions. However, they did not know how to correct it or guide it properly. Nevertheless, they began to attain such a state. They would say that all the matters they came with intentions for were being fulfilled. I did not do anything specifically.

[GV1:P0614] It continued in that manner for about three years. People developed a great deal of love and respect. During this time, one woman and two men emerged and began handling other matters themselves. The woman and one man were older, and the other was a child. After proceeding like that for a while, things would work out sometimes and fail at other times. After a while, I had a feeling that they had made mistakes, and I beat and reprimanded them extensively. None of this yielded any results. Time and again, things failed to work out, and difficulties kept escalating. Various types of difficulties began to emerge in different ways. Previously, if it was said that an issue would be resolved in a certain number of days, it would have been resolved ten days prior. Later on, even after the specified date passed, the illness could be seen partially lingering. Gradually, it reached a state where three-quarters of the time, things did not work out. For all this, I would reprimand them.

[GV1:P0615] During those times, an inexplicable slight hostility began to spread among those who came. The construction of Varkala College was completed. Classes also commenced. When boys went in groups, it was common for them to tease the girls. When they arrived there, these girls would go inside. Perhaps from hearing what was said to many while standing there, some felt an affinity towards this and made it a habit to receive prasadam. Many boys also came. Among them, those who walked around passing comments at girls noticed certain changes in the girls' behavior when they came there, leading the boys to feel that this was a deception or sorcery. As this spread in the college, it gained a facility to spread simultaneously to all the market shops and about four thousand homes. Along with this, some changes and behaviors that deviated from the same faith were observed in the children who had visions. Thus, an earnest investigation began to find out what this was. How could one know? Our Hindu rituals begin by standing in the position of the Trinity. Despite doing all the necessary work through this, I struggled without gaining liberation from it. Consequently, I had to face difficulties in that state for about a year. The children with these visions themselves continued to experience tremendous hardships. Finally, a disembodied voice was heard saying that two people should not sit together in a manner visible to others. Following that, we remained withdrawn for another two months. Again, the same message came: you must not sit like this.

[GV1:P0616] Today, in the place known as Santhigiri Ashram in Pothencode, a small hut-like structure was built for an ashram. A person was appointed to light a lamp there. When another intimation was received, feeling it was no longer appropriate to stay here, I moved there. In those days, it was not a place where people would frequent. One could stay peacefully. About seven months passed like that. During this time, there is a cave in Melkadakkavoor in Vakkom where Narayana Guru had sat. Its owner came and said that it was in a dilapidated state and asked if something should be done. I said, "Light a lamp. Let six months pass." After six months, people living even four miles away could see a great light emerging from that cave. Following this incident, the owner said it should be converted into a place of worship. While its construction was going on, the intimation to move to Pothencode was received. Along with it, a couple of words were given: "You should chant this. Chant and become strong." Two lines were given for two people. Before completing this, while sitting at Kadakkavoor railway station at dawn to go to Chirayinkeezhu with Kadalikkad Gopalan Master, some boys returning from a festival came that way. Some of them booed and made noises, and when I held on and got into the train, someone came, struck me a blow, grabbed me by the towel, and dragged me. However, on that day, I had suffered a lapse in memory. The words received through the divine voice had instructed me not to step outside for three days. For the first two days, I did not step outside. On that day, forgetting this, I went out. It was three days after this that I happened to come here, based on the intimation not to stay in a place where two people gather. When I left Varkala and came here, a rumor was spread that boys who were hostile to me had beaten and chased me away. When I was not seen, people believed it. They were never convinced of the truth either. Nine months after coming here, a word was received from the light that anything should be done only after two and a half years. However, after nine months, an intimation was received from the Trinity and the Rishis under the Trinity stating that treatment for illnesses could be done. It was started. The results started appearing double than before. Suddenly, a situation arose where about three hundred people would come and go daily. Within three weeks, the situation was such that sixty patients could lie inside and get cured. There were no buildings or anything else here then. The patients and visitors used to lie on the bare grass. They were exposed to both dew and sun alike. Out of dedication, they disregarded all this. Suddenly, like before, it became difficult to conclude all this within three months.

[GV1:P0617] In the meantime, an intimation was received to chant the name that was given to us earlier. When that name was prayed and resolutions were made with it, all the undertaken diseases were cured. Again, an intimation came to remain motionless for three and a half years. In accordance with this intimation, I remained silent. I was informed to undertake a journey, and I travelled. There were four of us at that time. We also took a child along. It is known that this child had received a vision earlier. We stayed here for a few days. Until then, none of those who were communicating through visions were taken along. The reason for not taking them was the feeling that, like before, some errors were occurring due to the obstruction of certain Devas. Meanwhile, it became evident that what was coming from these Devas was wrong. A feeling arose that this was no longer needed! What is received from the Light is sufficient. I firmly decided not to accept anything of this sort. This was also spoken through a divine voice. Finally, a correction was received over three weeks in the nature of a vision of Krishna. That has remained true in experience to this day. Before reaching all the temples during the journey, this ten-year-old child would visibly receive the deities and signs present there. Thus, we went up to Madras. We accomplished more than intended within three months and returned. Along with returning like that, the location for the Kallar ashram was found and it was established. Many things happening today were foretold right there. Since it is impossible to reveal any of that now, it is not being done.

[GV1:P0618] After that, it is understood that the intimation received from 1973 to 1979 is almost entirely filled with truth and greatness. It can be stated here that a few things in that intimation need to be clarified for this human world. There are two paths for the worship practices of Hindus. One is the path of Devas and Devis (deities) and the other is the path of the lineage of Rishis. The status of Devas and Devis belongs to the Treta and Dwapara Yugas, and the path of the Guru is for humans to experience and exhaust through births all the mistakes they have committed in various periods and attain liberation. The other is that the souls who have lived with the path of merging with God, having taken birth in this Kali Yuga, standing as a Guru to human beings and indeed all living creatures engulfed in Kali, will grant liberation to those who need it; and other pious souls will get rebirth in the approaching Satya Yuga, living on earth like Devas, attaining the fulfillment of birth in a way that allows change according to other yugas—it can be understood that this is the path maintained by the Guru lineage according to the law of Manu.

[GV1:P0619] Therefore, the future intention for the remaining period of Kali Yuga is to advise humans according to the directions of the Gurus belonging to this Manu lineage, convince them about the luminous matters beyond this Trinity system, and guide them on that path to liberation or transform them into souls eligible for the positions of the aforementioned Acharyas. What has been said is only a few brief portions of the intimation received from 1973 to 1979. The parts of karma performed accordingly and the experiential parts realized through it will be discussed later. Those are matters with certain directions and intentions. They cannot be stated hastily like this.

[GV1:P0620] Guruvani

GURUVANIKAL · February 1981 · Volume 1

[GV1:P0621] February 1981

[GV1:P0622] Question: You had mentioned earlier that it could be stated with a directive. I am interested to know what that is.

[GV1:P0623] Guru: During the experiences of the past sixteen years, certain directives have become our own. Moreover, certain past events have come and gone according to the times. We must lay down the directive by truly accepting all of them, not by opposing and defeating them. But the familiarity to understand that must reach the people. The main role in that has come to the ascetics (Sanyasis) themselves. The Dwapara Yuga and Treta Yuga, two completed yugas, were useful for some time in knowing the past, present, and future through direct perceptions and inferences.

[GV1:P0624] Question: You mentioned direct perceptions and inferences. I do not understand the intention behind it.

[GV1:P0625] Guru: We are not speaking of the direct perceptions and inferences spoken by a materialist. Deva, Devi, Guru - when saying Guru, there are four types of Gurus: Brahmavit, Brahmavaryan, Brahmavarishtan, Brahmavareeshtan. When speaking of the era of Devas and Devis, it only means the Treta and Dwapara Yugas. Two: The people who worshipped Devas and Devis performed certain miraculous feats (siddhis) and magical acts. They did all this by satisfying the Devas and Devis with mantras and tantras. The application of siddhis has been carried out in all periods. Even today, some ascetics and yogis continue to do so. One should not assume this is the ultimate truth. We must gain the knowledge that the lives of these Devas and Devis continue to exist with awareness throughout their time.

[GV1:P0626] Question: How can we acquire this knowledge?

[GV1:P0627] Guru: This knowledge is acquired when a Guru transcends the status of Devas and Devis and realizes the glory of the divine presence. A Guru can advise on this only when knowledge about the universe is attained. Under a Deva, there are also Rishis and ascetics. They have a shorter lifespan than this Deva. That being the case, in one sense, they have stated that Shiva and Mahavishnu are complete. They gave a name and showed some calculations. That is their logic.

[GV1:P0628] However, descending from the Trimurti system, all religious followers possess certain attributes conceptualized as sub-deities. Muslims refer to them as Jinns and Christians as angels. The determination of this time period is obtained when tracing the lineage of Manu. The period of a Manu is calculated as seventy-one *Chaturyugas*. One *Chaturyuga* is twelve thousand divine years. A divine year equals three hundred and sixty-five and a quarter human years. One divine year constitutes a single day for a deity. Calculated thus, how many lifetimes would human beings require to comprehend this? Even when a human dies and becomes a *Pitru* (ancestral spirit), our month equates to a single day for them. For *Yakshas*, *Gandharvas*, and *Kinnaras*, the time span is even greater. We must comprehend at least a portion of such calculations through direct inference. It has been stated that the era of a Manu spans seventy-one *Chaturyugas*. When a single *Chaturyuga* comprises twelve thousand divine years, one can deduce the magnitude of seventy-one *Chaturyugas*. We have not yet completed recording the chronological calculation of deities for a single *Chaturyuga*. That in itself is the predicament. How can one chronicle a calculation of such immense duration?

[GV1:P0629] If we fail to evaluate Manu at this juncture, we will be confounded once more. We ourselves have been unable to comprehend the history of the Manus. Consequently, oblivious to the narrative of the Manus, what can we, leading mere century-long lives, possibly comprehend? Our scholarly pursuit has already been diverted from this trajectory to another. The very mathematics has vanished from such matters. Judging by the nature of the calculations detailed in our *Bhagavata*, Europeans still have a considerably long way to go in catching up.

[GV1:P0630] The reason for this lies in their calculation of minutes. To arrive at a single minute, we would have to compute extensively. It is stated that a time measurement is assigned to the fraction of a moment it takes for a robust young man, forcefully thrusting a sharp stylus, to pierce through one tender bael leaf and strike another placed immediately beneath it. I am aware that preceptors in traditional village schools used to teach such calculations. They were referred to as *munthiri* calculations, *maahani* calculations, and the like. It is taught that one thousand *maahani* equals 62.5. I have transcribed such calculations onto palm leaves. In those days, regardless of the complexity of the calculation, one merely had to learn and recite it within five minutes. Today, attempting such calculations without mechanical assistance would require countless iterations of multiplication and division.

[GV1:P0631] When the *Gita* speaks of *pratyakshavaham dharmam*, it means that the deity, goddess, or guru we envision manifests directly to prescribe specific *dharmas* (duties). *Pratyakshavaham dharmam* implies that such manifestation encompasses the past, present, and future timelines of a life. Thus, it should be understood that just as humans have spoken of the three tenses, the calculations pertaining to everything from deities to the Earth, the nine planets, and the twelve zodiac signs can be obtained through this direct perception. If we preserve the knowledge obtained in this manner, it becomes clear to us. The life of Sri Krishna itself further substantiates this example. Arjuna—who stood on the battlefield paralyzed by fear, casting away his bow and arrows, declaring he wished to gain nothing by slaying his uncles, grandfathers, and preceptors—failed to comprehend when Krishna told him, "You kill no one, cause no one to be killed; the soul cannot be destroyed," so the narrative goes. Krishna repeatedly advised him. When that counsel proved fruitless, he summoned Arjuna: "Do you believe in me?" "Yes, I always believe in you." "Then why do you fail to understand despite my repeated explanations?" Arjuna then replied to Krishna, "My only fear concerns the act of killing them." "Very well, do one thing. Try to envision me. What was I prior to this era? Were you alive then or not? If so, who were you? Who were your uncles and preceptors back then? Who were you? Observe what you were doing." Looking thus, with the eyes of wisdom, he saw who they all were and who Krishna was back then. In this manner, God clarifies that we ourselves possess a state providing evidence of our manifold attributes. We have numerous other proofs as well. Great sages have authored treatises—such as Agastya's seven thousand and Bhogar's one thousand. It is said they would look at a plant and ask, "What are you good for?" This signifies that they looked at the plant with divine contemplation. The divine illumination residing there bestowed the knowledge of its medicinal properties. Because they meticulously recorded this, preparing a formulation based on those calculations yields results even today. They did not make discoveries through laboratory testing as is done today. Back then, they discovered everything without the use of machinery. Today, we find it impossible to live without mechanical equipment. Viewed in this light, to this day, no errors have ever originated from these great masters.

[GV1:P0632] A question might naturally arise: how then did this Vedic authority reach its current state? The present era speaks of the deities' calculations. However, the calculations of the Vedas and Upanishads speak solely of illumination. Similarly, we have received various revelations over the past sixteen and a half years. Fully comprehending and applying this knowledge will take ages. When utilized according to these revelations, the present-day Trimurti system—namely the Vaishnava, Shakta, and Shaiva traditions of worship—must attain completion through the path of the Guru and the lineage of Manu. It represents an experiential possibility resulting from the integration of the gross, subtle, effect, and cause states for both men and women, young and old alike.

[GV1:P0633] Guruvani

[GV1:P0634] March 1981

[GV1:P0635] Question: Does "experiential possibility" imply that we must harmonize all past events to foster a specific disposition?

[GV1:P0636] Guru: To speak more precisely, there is no need to state that we must foster it. Everything unfolds according to time. Furthermore, it would be more accurate to say that much gets distorted due to our ignorance. The only flaw herein stems from the deficiencies accumulated because we are unable to act appropriately at the right juncture.

[GV1:P0637] Observe the sheer ignorance prevailing in places we herald as progressive. We encounter numerous newspaper reports indicating a significant belief in witchcraft in contemporary times, to the extent that even in America, there is an apprehension of sorcery. Similarly, amidst us who proclaim our culture to be the greatest, what sort of Vedic behaviors are on display? Disgraceful practices, such as inquiring whether one should demonstrate their prowess while in a state of trance, are taking place here.

[GV1:P0638] Even for individuals who feel ashamed to declare "I am a believer," their own families will not permit them to disavow it. Or if they are permitted, the neighbors will end up ostracizing them; such is the situation. Otherwise, the presence of believers mirrors the epidemic of modern politics. Within a single household, one might be a devotee of Vishnu, another of Shiva, a third of Subrahmanya, and a fourth of Kali—each worshipping their chosen deity under the conviction that theirs is supreme. Hearing them speak, we too might feel they are correct. Is it not correct? It is indeed correct. However, this escalates and transforms into the language of the "ego."

[GV1:P0639] In this world, everything that comes into being and perishes, starting from a single grain of sand, possesses its own distinct completeness. One can perceive that this world is sustained by the support of that completeness. Viewed from this perspective, it is evident that even completeness cannot endure without the support of another completeness. We mutually support each other without even comprehending this completeness, thus feeling a sense of grandeur akin to a frog in a well. While navigating life in this world with this understanding, one fundamentally requires something to stand firm upon.

[GV1:P0640] The truth is that if our actions towards it are unified into one, they encompass everything. Otherwise, it will become so void that we will feel entirely incapable of having accomplished anything. Step aside into it for a moment. Then, the recurring anomalies in actions performed at another time for the sake of wholeness will appear as a substantial aggregation. Our current endeavor can merely reduce its magnitude; however, if anyone believes it can be entirely eradicated from this world, such a notion is akin to nihilism.

[GV1:P0641] Therefore, our only recourse is to act while praying for the wisdom to align our spontaneous intellect and capabilities with the divine will, standing closely behind it. For this, the words that convey this divine decree to us serve as our foundation. Upon deep contemplation, we realize that our existential state lacks even the significance of a mere atom. In this atmosphere, if one gazes into this mirage, countless atoms can be observed flickering in and out of existence within the circumference of a single coin. It suffices to consider ourselves merely as one among such atoms. One must not assume a state of absolute nothingness. Doing so would lead to complete voidness.

[GV1:P0642] When it is understood that billions of such atoms mutually interpenetrate and that this penetrative quality pervades everywhere akin to a gas, one should immediately reflect upon whether the nature of our mind is not analogous to this. In such a gaseous state, the mind will completely permeate our desires, exactly like a gas. We must comprehend that this mechanism remains identical, regardless of whether the desire is virtuous or malevolent.

[GV1:P0643] Certain ascetics serve as exemplars of this phenomenon. Placing their faith in the ritualistic nature of particular deities, they elevate and worship them as the Supreme God. Consequently, this transforms into a form of worship dictated by their individual desires. As the number of adherents engaging in this worship multiplies, some develop an inclination to exhibit their prowess. This leads to the urge to exercise mystical powers (*Siddhis*). The application of such powers may be intended to attract crowds or to serve selfish motives. Regardless of the intent, the ultimate objective remains the fulfillment of desire. Moreover, an individual's desire has the potential to inflict instantaneous harm upon many.

[GV1:P0644] Since the epoch of creation, the world has continually existed as an amalgamation of virtues and vices. Therefore, it is only after thoroughly contemplating and comprehending the true nature of ourselves—who are a composite of good and evil—along with others like us, and the world itself, that one should endeavor to manifest miracles, and indeed, the greatest of miracles. Otherwise, one would be compelled to perpetually perform miracles merely to mitigate the destruction engendered by these very manifestations.

[GV1:P0645] Consequently, the actions performed by both individuals up to that point are rendered futile. It implies that while one created, the other destroyed. Ultimately, neither party is able to achieve anything. This is precisely how those who identify as ascetics act and ultimately face defeat.

[GV1:P0646] Question: Are you referring specifically to mystical powers (*Siddhis*)?

[GV1:P0647] Guru: I am not merely referring to mystical powers, but rather encompassing all aspects of action. None of these ascetics committed these acts with the explicit desire to become wicked. They simply slipped in their actions. If one lacks the innate disposition to act with their mind focused upon the divine presence and aimed at the divine will, this flaw will subtly overtake us without our awareness. It is this specific detriment that afflicts us as we continuously engage in numerous external and internal actions.

[GV1:P0648] Question: In your opinion, what must be done to avert this?

[GV1:P0649] Guru: The directive to avert it is inherently contained within those very words. Did you not notice it? A devotee inherently possesses a distinct qualitative excellence in their disposition. For a yogi, it manifests through the science of yoga. For a person of action (*karmi*), it emerges through their deeds. The seeker of knowledge (*jnani*) possesses it innately. Even though the essence remains the same, the devotee possesses the effortlessness to act with a sense of total surrender; the yogi harbors the mindset that their achievements stem from yogic prowess; whereas the *karmi* holds the attitude of "behold the deed I have accomplished." The *jnani*, however, is capable of recognizing that everyone's actions are correct from their respective standpoints, and can establish that they themselves are the embodiment of that very truth. Experience has proven that only the *jnani* and the devotee can attain this effortlessly.

[GV1:P0650] Question: May we consider this as a self-realized experience?

[GV1:P0651] Guru: You may. However, while considering it as such, one must not deviate from the philosophical discipline by adopting an attitude of "that is their experience, and this is my experience."

[GV1:P0652] Question: What is the reason for saying so?

[GV1:P0653] Guru: Because the devotee, the *jnani*, and the yogi all possess a *sattvic* (pure) nature, they will acknowledge it. Yet, accompanying this is something known as *sattvic* ego. One unknowingly takes pride, assuming that the actions they have performed possess considerable superiority. This tendency has thus emerged and afflicted everyone.

[GV1:P0654] There is evidence that this is ingrained in all of us. There is a tendency in us to say, "It is somewhat acceptable." We also do not say it is completely unacceptable. We use this same expression even for the very best. This flaw primarily occurs in the most intelligent individuals. If it can infiltrate the intellectual, how can we be certain it will not infiltrate us? It will certainly infiltrate us as well. To prevent its entry, the devotee develops an attitude of absolute surrender toward the Guru, recognizing that the previously mentioned path is the sole recourse. The *jnani*, observing the goodness that everything is functioning correctly in its respective place, consistently anchors their sacred actions solely in virtue, and accomplishes them in an ordinary manner without being overwhelmed by the force of that virtue.

[GV1:P0655] Question: I still wish to hear further elucidation on the exact nature of what you are implying through all of this.

[GV1:P0656] Guru: I will have to reiterate what has already been said. Nevertheless, I shall explain it in slightly more detail. In this current *Kali Yuga*, we can only speak by observing its weight and magnitude. Therefore, it can be clarified better only if articulated with that at the forefront. What is your current understanding of the term *Kali*?

[GV1:P0657] Question: It is perceived that *Kali* has deeply entrenched itself within people and everything else. The prevailing belief is that, unable to perform righteous deeds, the innate goodness of humanity will be entirely annihilated.

[GV1:P0658] Guru: That is incorrect. We ourselves assert that we have arrived on this earth in accordance with the results of our past actions (*karma*). If that is the case, does it not imply that the fruits of actions performed incrementally in the *Treta Yuga* and *Dvapara Yuga* will manifest in this *Kali Yuga*?

[GV1:P0659] Question: It will manifest.

[GV1:P0660] Guru: If it is to manifest, shouldn't the virtues cultivated during those eras also manifest?

[GV1:P0661] Question: The virtues must manifest as well.

[GV1:P0662] Guru: If so, isn't acting in the fourth era while evaluating the virtues and vices of the preceding three eras conceived as a state of absorption (*layanathmakam*), where one reaches a state of liberation—devoid of both positive and negative attributes—achieved through the fruits of actions executed with a perfectly balanced understanding of the weight of merits and demerits?

[GV1:P0663] Question: Yes, it is exactly like that. Then, is it your proposition that this era is capable of fully grasping and retaining virtue?

[GV1:P0664] Guru: Yes, certainly. No other three eras offer the opportunity quite like this *Kali Yuga*, where one can strive, perform any action through hardship, and bring it to the forefront. Or even if they do, it is exceedingly delayed. This is precisely why even our ancestral sages desired to be born in the *Kali Yuga* to attain liberation.

[GV1:P0665] Question: Having listened to what you have said thus far, it is to be understood that, by evaluating everything that has transpired until today, an attempt is being made to rectify past anomalies by establishing a system as suited to the times as possible, shaping the forthcoming state of affairs, and bringing it to the forefront, is it not?

[GV1:P0666] Guru: That is precisely the objective. That is also the knowledge we have received. It would require an extensive period to completely implement and consolidate the knowledge we have documented over many days.

[GV1:P0667] In that systemic arrangement, when observing the characteristics of ashrams that have existed until now, our ashram exhibits certain distinctions. Thus far, the practice has been to strictly follow the predecessors and tread the exact path they have shown. All of this needs to be systematized—not partially, but entirely. That is to say, according to Hindu jurisprudence, we have now been entrusted with these three types of worship modalities. To unify the scenario of establishing "one" in the place of all three, one must first comprehend the matter and believe in it. It is only after believing that one will be able to put it into practice.

[GV1:P0668] There are some people for whom outdated methods of worship are ingrained in their flesh, blood, and marrow, clinging tightly to their lives. As soon as faith is first established in this, the concepts of ancestors and the concepts of God they have worshipped thus far should be unified, and with the power they have worshipped, they must be brought into the divine light. Then, in that place, the faith in the Guru must be firmly established again. They must be convinced and believe in what that Guru is. Thus, they must learn to worship with the concept that the Guru is God. Such is the fundamental principle of the Hindu. That is why it begins with 'Gurur Brahma' and concludes with 'Sakshat Para Brahma'. Only if such knowledge is acquired can it be conveyed to the common people.

[GV1:P0669] Therefore, one must know the qualities that this Guru, who is the Supreme Brahman, should possess. He must treat both the wicked and the virtuous equally. He will try to bring the wicked to the right path by afflicting and inflicting pain through their own actions. However, what is shown to the virtuous is also the same. There is only a slight difference. That difference is that even if there are many faults in the actions of the wicked, he will forgive them and let them be. He will not try too hard to correct them. But in the case of the virtuous, he will control them very strictly. If they do not listen when controlled, he will let them go. Why is that? If they deviate even slightly from the path they have ascended, that slight deviation will cause a profound gap within them. If such a gap occurs, it cannot be bridged in that lifetime.

[GV1:P0670] It is keeping that memory in mind that Gurus develop an attitude that even if someone does not become right, it does not matter, let them go. If it is a wicked person, they will think let him fall a bit and then rise up. That is why, in a Guru-disciple relationship understood in this manner, disciples take care not to give room for even a single contradictory word. A Guru lineage that begins to turn in this way will face stages of enduring numerous hardships. Because the course of that lineage seems contrary to what people are accustomed to. For example, if one observes carefully, one can see what kind of revolution occurred when attempts were made to change each existing thing.

[GV1:P0671] If one happens to read at least once the sorrowful truth experienced by the recently emerged Christianity and Buddhism, along with their lineages, it is easy to understand what the people who experienced that pain and their Guru lineages went through. It is because they went through such hardships that their sacrifices have to be valued. Looking at the era we live in today, unless we proceed with a bit more strength and propriety, it will not be possible to bring people to the right path.

[GV1:P0672] Every individual standing involved in the path we intend should assume themselves to be resolute in purpose and that they are the strongest and most appropriate person on this path. Whoever they may be and in whichever path they may live, they must live focusing on that Guru's path. Only if we fully internalize such an ideal can we serve this and create precedents. Otherwise, out of desire or base enmity, one might create a rift and move away.

[GV1:P0673] For that, first truly study this ideal and draw strength from it. Having gained strength, act moderately and come forward through intellectual prowess to advance. It is imperative that every individual possesses all appropriate compromises, outpourings of love, and a wealth of sacrifice. Only such lineages have been able to come forward to date. All those who step into this must be courageous and possess the capable nature to reconcile even those who are estranged through love. If this happens, we can all see a good tomorrow as divinely conceived. This is how our Guru lineage should set its goals.

[GV1:P0674] Especially householders (Grihasthas) should be the ones to become acquainted with this and come forward. Men and women must join together and perform only actions that mutually accommodate each other with love and respect in all endeavors. Thus, the home will attain a place of unity. Through that love, the lineage of offspring will be good, and in imparting the necessary knowledge to the children in that lineage, two or three other conditions will also have to be adopted.

[GV1:P0675] In this regard, one should not consider which caste, which religion, or which class someone belongs to in the Guru lineage. Regardless of how they are, let there be unity. What is achieved through that unity is that they are all like members of one family. Through that, find occupation and create a unified form. Through this, there will be a peace for their life's hardships. The lineage of self-education will become theirs. That culture will be cultivated to a level befitting the lineage. Thus, when their organizational nature becomes one, their sense of unity will also become one. Even if we gather everything for this, there is another nature we must strongly know.

[GV1:P0676] This nature called Guru must be one in whom all the special powers of the divine system have occurred. It is not for us to imitate the path of the gods and goddesses. Without recognizing them and correcting the destruction, one cannot be brought before a Guru. The people must be completely corrected and brought back along the path traditionally taken by our predecessors, the Devas and Rishis themselves. Furthermore, one must have held both the system of Devendra and the position of the lord of the Ganas. They must be ones who have experienced what is called the presence of Ishwara, the presence of God, and the presence of Brahman. Only such a Guru can bring these ideals together.

[GV1:P0677] Question: Hearing what you just said, one must recognize and correct everything from ghosts to Yakshas, Gandharvas, Kinnaras, and the city of Vetalas. What is the way for us to know and correct this here?

[GV1:P0678] Guru: There, it is enough if you accept the word of the Guru exactly as it is. You do not need to correct it. The Guru is one who has borne all of this, right? It is sufficient just not to violate the words of the Guru. Then you can ascend without error.

[GV1:P0679] If one intends to act like the Guru after the Guru's time, one must observe and correct this, learn all of it while the Guru is still present, and stand with wisdom. Otherwise, that movement will stagger for a while after the Guru's time. Then it will cease to exist.

[GV1:P0681] April 1981

[GV1:P0682] Question: So, could that be the reason why most institutions established in this way are seen stagnating after the founder's time?

[GV1:P0683] Guru: Not only because of that. While that person is alive, there are certain things that need to be completely finished. It has to be corrected and completed through experience. Even if known, it becomes difficult to complete them. The reason is that all the human beings living with him are those who have thought and lived contrarily. Then, some differences seen are several poems by those who are called scholars. Thus, experiential matters cannot be imparted through a scholarly nature.

[GV1:P0684] What is called scholarship is like polishing. It is just like building with bricks and painting it white. If those who lived in a well-painted, good building are taken and made to live in a hut, one will see a scene where they cannot even turn around due to disgust and mess. They will not have the knowledge that the mansion originated from a hut like this. It is difficult to see a conscious effort to make the relief of sorrow in between a reality and to maintain the tradition through that karmic power succeed with everything falling into place.

[GV1:P0685] One who brings success in such a manner will have to experience sorrow like Jesus, the Prophet, and Guru Nanak. Contemporaries witnessing all this might see nothing right but only faults in front of them; upon seeing all this, some might decide to remain silent. Some will work a little and stop. Seeing such things, quite a few will withdraw, saying, 'Didn't you see so-and-so acting and getting ruined?' When hearing what those without this inclination say, assuming it to be right, everything gets pushed into despair.

[GV1:P0686] Question: You mentioned some states from the city of Vetalas to the world of Devas. There is a desire to know how that can be explained as well.

[GV1:P0687] *Continued from the previous issue

[GV1:P0688] Guru: It is difficult to comprehend that precisely. This is because only the masters who are born in accordance with the times will attain this completely. Others might attain it to a certain extent, but they will never grasp its complete dimensions. The knowledge required to observe and act from the very origin of the universe cannot be simply transformed into exceptional intellect. Even if one observes it, they will not obtain all the favorable circumstances required to execute and fulfill it. What else can be done then? One can only stop right there, isn't it?

[GV1:P0689] Once the realm of Vethala (Vethalanagaram) is crossed, a somewhat worthy state is achieved in the subsequent stages. That is, the departure towards the state of deities. That state will be seen as completely radiant. What one immediately receives is an easy path within the Trimurti system. The reason for attaining this is the positive things received as a rest from what happened prior to it. Before successfully crossing the realm of Vethala, we will have to experience and realize numerous sorrowful truths. The stones and thorns placed by God for this purpose are our contemporary human beings and even other creatures in this earthly world.

[GV1:P0690] The only difference between them and him lies in good thoughts and good deeds. Everything else is exactly the same. He will experience all the powers of that demon through his contemporary humans. They will view him as Hiranyakashipu. Words cannot express the difficulty in rectifying this widespread distress, which is as incompatible as milk and horse gram. However, attaining a position in this state of ascending to the deities serves as an interval of relief. To all other believers, he will be perceived just like the Trimurtis. Having seen this much, one cannot be faulted for unknowingly becoming arrogant, feeling, "I have become everything." However, neither this experienced individual nor the society that accepted him in a mimicking manner upon seeing his qualifications will be able to realize that all this merely demonstrates the cyclical and repetitive nature of the heavenly world.

[GV1:P0691] What happens here is neither anyone's fault nor merit. It is a place where such things naturally occur. If one looks at what the Puranas say about Kailasa, one can see what kind of luxurious traits and antics are described! You will understand that when you read the Shiva Purana. There are other Puranas that speak about the Vaishnavas. If you read about that, it is even grander. Thus, if you examine each Purana, you will find that the essential matters occupy only a very small portion of them. Transcending all this and bringing it to a resolution—as proclaimed by the Puranas themselves—takes multiple lifetimes. In our experience, this is also largely true. Overcoming all these means that a soul, which has been led purely and holily through lifetimes, will eventually reside in certain divine realms. Sometimes we hear the names of stars, don't we? Like the Shukra star, Velli star (Venus), and Arundhati star. There are many such stars, both large and small. There are those that are much larger than the Earth and those that are much smaller. It may not be possible to meticulously comprehend and analyze all of these.

[GV1:P0692] Question: What should we understand from your words about what needs to be done here next?

[GV1:P0693] Guru: Haven't you understood from what has been said so far? Isn't it clear that these celestial spheres stand beyond nine realms, similar to Earth? Beyond knowing about these star systems and all this, there is a higher state. Only then can this be known. Even at the very first stage of this Trimurti system, one is seeing and experiencing almost up to the state of Godhead. Do you think it is possible to experience, realize, and describe this, or to accomplish and conclude any one of these tasks?

[GV1:P0694] Question: From what I have heard, I can understand that it is indeed difficult.

[GV1:P0695] Guru: When it is this difficult to repeatedly accomplish even good things, imagine the magnitude of difficulty in knowing and realizing the qualities contradictory to everything we mentioned earlier. When he begins to repeatedly realize this, all his contemporary people who respected him and considered him good—even those who sang his praises until then—will look at him with disdain. They will act with enmity, torment him in every possible way, and drag him down, piling misery upon him. Eventually, only a cluster of these heaps will be seen. If one carefully examines history, one can see numerous great men who, despite working for the good, were transformed into something worse than beasts. One need not even look at history. Can't we see it if we look at the contemporary nature of today?

[GV1:P0696] Question: Yes, we can see that.

[GV1:P0697] Guru: Do you know how all of that is seen through us?

[GV1:P0698] Question: I have understood it. But it is not clear how exactly it happens.

[GV1:P0699] Guru: Currently, aren't you seeing a lot in the papers regarding various believers, rationalists, different godmen (Bawas), and the evaluations of scholars? Haven't you understood what all this implies? It means that no one can truly recognize anyone else. Just like in the past, each person is slipping from one state of blindness into another even now.

[GV1:P0700] Question: Then, in your opinion, how should this be corrected?

[GV1:P0701] Guru: Here, what is needed now is not correction, but realization. Will anyone among those mentioned admit that they are flawed? If anyone in the world says that one particular group among them is bad or anything of the sort, they will all gang up and resort to untoward actions. Each of the godmen is clever. The college professors and principals here are all qualified for their respective positions. The religious scholars and authors of the Puranas here are also qualified. Then there is a specific section of people who believe that only the Vedas and Upanishads are right. What they say is above all this. And then there are the rationalists and salvation-seekers, who act as if they have mixed all this up and swallowed it whole. Does someone who knows a little bit and tries to speak have any standing? There is a venomous breed of wasps. It would be fortunate if all of these people don't act like them, spreading toxicity and finishing him off right here.

[GV1:P0702] However, one cannot say that all this is wrong. It must be called right. If one discerns all this at a glance, the subjects appear in a way that suggests the right is slightly more prevalent. When examining the Puranas and stories, these godmen, such gurus, rationalists, and salvation-seekers are souls who have been repeatedly born and died over countless ages. If we observe closely, we can see whether they are the ones who have returned repeatedly in this era. Behind this is another group that pretends everything happens through them. All this is the growth of science. Can we, who experience and understand it to a large extent, say it is wrong? Similarly, if time moves forward a little, they will have to admit that a lot of this is flawed.

[GV1:P0703] For example, by the time the medicines discovered, tested, and released through laboratories are used on the public, they begin to declare them as flawed. Thus, they have reached a stage where they do not hesitate to declare things as right or wrong every second. Another group is standing firm here, ready to repeatedly assert that all this is correct. Recently, with the fall of Skylab, a lot of panic spread across the world, and numerous opinions regarding this have surfaced among the people.

[GV1:P0704] Shouldn't we understand that all this is causing some kind of disruption and that a danger lurks behind it? We are already experiencing the reality that numerous toxic gases have spread in the atmosphere, affecting humans and all living beings, causing various diseases. One must suspect whether purity of character itself has become akin to some sort of machine. It is bound to happen that way. Because, there is no doubt that consuming plants and food materials grown under the influence of these gases will affect not only our bodies but our intellect as well.

[GV1:P0705] We have overt empirical evidence laid out before us to substantiate this. The artists in our midst are virtually incapable of writing or performing unless they consume a specific kind of intoxicant. Once a small quantity of it is ingested, melodies flow spontaneously. Dance movements may ensue, whether they align with classical aesthetics or not. They attempt to compensate for bodily grace at least through exaggerated contortions. As this tendency proliferated, it eventually permeated even the ranks of healthcare professionals; consequently, if patients were to awaken suddenly from an unconscious state and behold these individuals—whose appearances make it indiscernible whether they should be regarded as doctors or the deity of death—they might instantly succumb to sheer terror. Perhaps this explains why certain patients die immediately upon regaining consciousness post-surgery. This remains our only logical conjecture. Those lying sedated under the influence of narcotics are essentially lying frozen in the proximity of death.

[GV1:P0706] Deep within the patient's psyche, the preconceived mythological narratives concerning the God of Death would instantly rush to the forefront. Consequently, their breath would cease. A minority devoid of such preconceptions might somehow survive. By the same token, the ominous formations emanating from these toxic gases might congregate in certain regions of this atmosphere. Once congregated, they possess the potential to precipitate any magnitude of catastrophe from the skies. It is entirely superfluous to state what might transpire thereafter!

[GV1:P0707] Question: You articulated earlier that certain individuals are forcefully stepping forward to assert that everything is absolutely correct. I have not entirely comprehended the meaning of that statement.

[GV1:P0708] Guru: In our society, a fervent race for education is perpetually disseminating among both the impoverished and the affluent classes. Generally, the progeny of the highly affluent do not engage in rigorous academic pursuits. They acquire degrees by leveraging financial power or through other means; ultimately, their primary destination is the political arena. They envision themselves as leaders. Automobiles and airplanes are placed at their absolute disposal without them even demanding it. Observing such privileges induces a state of euphoria that leaves individuals completely ungrounded. For whom does this happen? The descendants of the profoundly impoverished—those who lack adequate sustenance and clothing—also grasp the edge of politics under the influence of this euphoric illusion. They aspire to become leaders. The superficial rhetoric they have heard and witnessed metamorphoses into their ideological principles. Observing these dynamics, a select few individuals recognize this as an opportune mechanism and swiftly infiltrate the political sphere. Upon their arrival, they manipulate the masses by validating their actions as absolutely correct, eventually ascending to become the leaders of the existing leadership. Consequently, by asserting claims ranging from the trivial to the monumental, they reduce the populace to mere peripheral sentinels and commence their governance. This specific faction epitomizes the ultimate embodiment of those who actively rationalize these systemic anomalies as fundamentally correct. Viewed from this perspective, does it not become evident that our pervasive toxic influences have extinguished the vital consciousness within all living entities? Contemplating this paradigm, one is left with no alternative but to assert that all of this is absolutely correct.

[GV1:P0709] Question: If all of this is deemed absolutely correct, what then is the implication for how we are supposed to navigate this?

[GV1:P0710] Guru: The question is indeed valid. I am inclined to believe that your comprehension of this matter is akin to asserting that a tortoise possesses the fur of a camel.

[GV1:P0711] Question: It is nothing of that sort. I posed the question merely to attain clarity. I have exhausted myself reading the Puranas and the Upanishads. I have yet to ascertain where the foundational crux of this actually lies.

[GV1:P0712] Guru: I have repeatedly elucidated this to you in the past. One of the profoundly informative forms, born periodically in accordance with the Yugas, transformed into enlightened sages through their supreme sacrifice and divine grace. Posthumously, for the life forces radiating from various sacred planets and stellar constellations, only those sons who are born by divine providence—guided by the disembodied celestial voice that reminds them of the luminous verses of the Gita, the Upanishads, and the Vedic proclamations—can accomplish this through divine grace alone. These profound truths cannot be acquired merely through instruction, regardless of whether one is categorized as a scholar, a layman, or an intellectual. These revelations remain entirely inaccessible to both the rationalist and the mere seeker of salvation. Therefore, let us conclude these particular segments here. Expounding further will only transcend your comprehension.
