[GV1:P0714] May 1981

[GV1:P0715] Question: You had previously indicated that Krishna is the incarnate deity of a specific Yuga!

[GV1:P0716] Guru: That is correct. The era of Krishna signifies the commencement of one Yuga and the culmination of another. However, prior to deliberating upon Krishna, certain other matters necessitate clarification. Numerous great souls were born prior to Krishna and conducted themselves in accordance with the prevailing Yuga. Yet, even before that, certain systemic anomalies persisted. A Shudra sage was assassinated with an arrow. Concurrently, the rigid caste system, internal sub-castes, and a monarchical regime that systematically deprived specific populations even of basic literacy were forcefully instituted.

[GV1:P0717] Under the dominion of a single monarch, one specific group of subjects was permitted to acquire literacy, whereas another group was strictly prohibited from doing so. How did such a paradigm come into existence? Consequently, it is unequivocally clear that these structural anomalies existed long before. The reality of diverse categories of subjects existing under a single monarch is the direct consequence of strategic political maneuvers, whereby a certain demographic was systematically ostracized and expelled to seize control of the governing apparatus. Those who complied were granted everything, while the dissenters were brutally subjugated and driven away. If observed meticulously, one can discern the remnants of such exclusionary tactics in contemporary administrative structures even today.

[GV1:P0718] It is observable that the scholars who authored the history of Kerala during the period of India's independence conspicuously omitted prominent leaders. If such historiographical distortions occur in the present era, one can only hypothesize the magnitude of manipulations orchestrated by the governing bodies of antiquity. During that epoch, an absolute decree was established forbidding a Shudra from listening to the Vedas. It was precisely for this reason that the Shudra sage was systematically denied the fundamental right to pursue asceticism. If subjects residing under a sovereign's rule are utterly deprived of their right to perform penance and worship the divine, one cannot even fathom the depths of degradation they would invariably descend into. This is the calculated handiwork perpetrated by the adherents of such exclusionary religious paradigms. We must critically analyze the multitude of malicious intentions they deliberately executed. We are already cognizant of historical narratives that are not too distant in the past. Have we not recently witnessed the actions of the Pakistani administration as well?

[GV1:P0719] *Continued from the previous issue

[GV1:P0720] What all transpirations occurred when Marthanda Varma assumed control of our Travancore monarchy? Men were systematically annihilated, and women were captured and forcibly handed over to the fisherfolk. Consequently, as they fled to various kingdoms in desperation, it is documented that they sought refuge in regions such as Karunagappally, Karthikappally, and Vaikom. Their inherent aristocratic dignity and aesthetic grace remain undiminished even today. The lineage of Chempil Arayan, renowned for the traditional snake boats, continues to live with immense respectability. One can also observe Brahmins and others partaking in meals while seated in distinctly separate rows. When such overwhelming evidence remains tangibly present, there is absolutely no doubt that history has been fundamentally distorted. In such oppressive circumstances, as a direct consequence of internalizing a corrupted culture devoid of any authoritative access to the Vedas, none of the individuals from the Shudra caste downwards have been able to achieve genuine emancipation or rectitude.

[GV1:P0721] Since the other two Yugas (Treta Yuga and Dwapara Yuga) constituted the epoch of the Devas, it was entirely feasible to conceptualize the deity and perform divine worship. The fourth Yuga constitutes the ultimate seat of authority for all of this. If the other three Yugas have sequentially progressed in strict accordance with their specific Yuga Dharma, and if one possesses faith in that cosmic order, is it not an absolute certainty that the fourth Yuga must execute its own inherent Dharma? If the Puranas emphatically celebrate that gods and goddesses hold no designated position within the Dharma of the fourth Yuga, is it not an absolute imperative that this cosmic mandate be actualized? Stating that Shudras shall wield governance during the Kali Yuga is not merely a concept to be comprehended; one must inevitably concede when it is asserted that the profound authority over the Vedas also fundamentally belongs to them. Furthermore, by meticulously hoarding these privileges and subjecting us to the indignities of polyandrous alliances devoid of recognized paternity, we have been systematically reduced to our current deplorable state. Delving further into this matter will necessitate extensive discourse. Is it not unequivocally evident that by monopolizing such authoritative domains, the marginalized subjects at the absolute bottom of the hierarchy were systematically disenfranchised and displaced?

[GV1:P0722] There has been a change since the time of Krishna. As mentioned earlier, Krishna's period is at the end of one yuga and the beginning of another. That is, at the end of Dvapara and the beginning of Kali Yuga. We celebrate Onam here, don't we? It is grandly celebrated in Kerala. When a good royal administration existed here, they concocted stories of God appearing and coming here, along with tales of sages, passing them around to create a logical justification. We are taught fabricated stories that someone was pushed into the netherworld just by the touch of a foot. We have also enjoyed listening to them. Certainly, that noble king who ruled well was loved by the people. Therefore, doesn't this prove that the intelligent Brahmin fabricated a story to show that even God is hostile to someone who does good, killed him, seized that royal court, and then made the one who wrote stories for the king at that time create this mockery?

[GV1:P0723] Looking at it this way, one can see such an appearance of God in the house of the King of Pandalam as well. God appears and does what is necessary only when calamities befall the women in the king's house. Looking at the history they have written, it seems that God does not appear to any poor people in our homes. Mahabali, who belonged to the Asura race, was stomped upon; as soon as he was touched, he went to the netherworld. That is how God comes to touch. Thus, as soon as a woman in the king's house got a headache, Mahavishnu and Shiva set out together. When they arrived here, since the woman was unwell, both of them engaged in absurdity, and immediately [the offspring] fell out by splitting the thigh. It was not even a direct birth. Immediately, he mounted a leopard and went into the forest. He caught and tied up a leopard, brought it back, milked it endlessly, and cured the disease. There was a time here when royal administration and the worship of God were conducted through such absurdities. Since the people were illiterate, it was not difficult to weave these stories and make them believe them.

[GV1:P0724] There is evidence for this. There is a history of Ayyappan coming and staying in an Ezhava family in the Cheerappanchira house in Cherthala and teaching Kalaripayattu there. During that time, he also gave advice to a girl there. After that, he went from there to a place called Kanjiramattom Mosque. There he taught Kalaripayattu to Muslims and gave advice to a Muslim youth. At the same time, he went and stayed at the place where the Arthunkal Church is situated today, and facilitated various benefits for many people there. It can be seen that Christians still preserve its memory today. Anyone can be convinced of these facts by going to these places and investigating.

[GV1:P0725] After that, he went to Kanjirappally via Kottayam. It was a place where a group of Brahmins lived at that time. All these Brahmins together took Ayyappan to the King of Pandalam. Upon going there, seeing that he was brilliant and an ascetic, he was made to stay there and entrusted with the responsibility of teaching Kalaripayattu. On that occasion, Ayyappan heard the stories of Vavar, Kochukadutha, and Valiyakkadutha. Thus, one day when Ayyappan went to see the hill, he met Vavar, Kochukadutha, and Valiyakkadutha and gave them advice.

[GV1:P0726] Prior to that, there was a temple there consecrated by a Brahmachari from the royal family. A trench was dug to stay upon arriving there, and a temple was built in the middle of it. To see this, he took them along and went to the place of the Sastha idol, which was a conceptual consecration. The Brahmachari from the royal family - named Hariharan - consecrated it with the conception that his family should become like the Buddha's family in the future, and attained Samadhi right there. An idol of Ganapathi was consecrated over the Samadhi. It was during this time that this Ayyappan arrived and performed penance.

[GV1:P0727] Ayyappan gained power by performing penance over this consecration and Samadhi. Then Kochukadutha, Valiyakkadutha, and Vavar all came down to the king. They had taken control of all the properties there. When the king inquired how to get this back, Ayyappan agreed to sort it out by talking to them. Because Ayyappan was convinced that they would listen if he spoke, as they were his disciples. Thus, the king's men, Vavar, and Ayyappan came to an agreement, and they surrendered the forest wealth. They were also given some land.

[GV1:P0728] In this, Vavar emerged prominent. In the settlement, a condition was placed that one should go to see Ayyappan's Samadhi place only after seeing Vavar's Samadhi place. That is how the 'Saranam' chanting originated, which perpetuates the memory of Kochukadutha, Valiyakkadutha, and Vavar.

[GV1:P0729] Through penance, Ayyappan became greater than this Hariharan and the conceptual consecration. Thus, it could be seen that Sabari stood as a support and shade for this Ayyappan. There is a custom where all first-time Ayyappan devotees take an arrow from Vavar's Samadhi place and place it at the spot of the Saramkuthi banyan tree. That banyan tree is not there today. The one that stood very large was destroyed. Since it is the place where Sabari performed penance, ghee and coconut are offered there. It can still be seen like a homa kunda today. Ayyappan attained Samadhi at the temple precincts. The girl from Cheerappanchira, to whom Ayyappan had given advice during his lifetime, went and met another disciple, the Thangal of Kanjiramattom, and the two of them met Vavar, and everyone together went to Ayyappan. They left that girl there and returned. The temple known today as Malikappuram is where this girl stayed and was interred in Samadhi.

[GV1:P0730] The aforementioned Thangal is the one who attained Samadhi at Kanjiramattom. Today, the family members of this Thangal are traditionally known as the Thangals of Kanjiramattom. Muslims are well aware that the Thangal who attained Samadhi at the Kanjiramattom Mosque is a disciple of Ayyappan. At the Kanjiramattom Mosque, the flag hoisting is on the first of Makaram. At the same time, the doors of Ayyappan's shrine are closed after the lamp lighting on that day. After a very long case in the name of the girl from Cheerappanchira, the High Court granted the right to fire ceremonial shots. The upper-caste hegemony seized that as well again. Stating that such a right should not belong to a household like this and that it is inferior, they filed a case in the court. The right to fire shots was canceled. This was done by the Devaswom Board. This is a recent example of upper-caste hegemony.

[GV1:P0731] Who is this Ayyappan? A boy belonging to a carpenter family in the Palakkad district in North Malabar. His father and mother died when he was three years old. Many households adopted and raised him. Eventually, he learned Kalaripayattu and other things, the martial arts deities appeared, and through that, he almost attained Siddhi. All these things happened while he set out on an ascetic path. This is the history of Ayyappan. (Have you heard the Saranam chanting in the name of this Ayyappan? They will not lie. But they will show a trick - they call out 'Harihara Sutan Ayyanayyappaswami'. It means that Ayyappan, who was Ayyan, became Ayyappaswami. Hariharan is the Brahmachari from the royal family, the Sastha, the conceptual consecration that was there.) If this can be distorted and done like this, isn't it the truth that the poets of that time distorted history and handled it in this way? Isn't it proven that such histories were distorted carefully so that their hegemony would not be lost? Most of the poets of that time belonged to Brahmin families and were authorities in the royal family. The other illiterate people - growing like wild grass - do they know this? From so much evidence existing like this, isn't it understood what all destructions this Varnasrama Dharma has caused?

[GV1:P0732] Question: Where did you get this much history from?

[GV1:P0733] Guru: This history is not just this. There is a lot. That cannot be said. It was just indicated for the knowledge of the people. I have said, haven't I - that many things have been told through philosophical visions, which cannot be revealed now. I have also said that after my time, if there are people who believe in this, let them reveal it.

GURUVANIKAL · June 1981 · Volume 1

[GV1:P0735] June 1981

[GV1:P0736] Question: You started talking about Sree Krishna earlier and stopped, didn't you? I am interested to know what that is.

[GV1:P0737] Guru: According to the laws of Manu, five gurus emerge during a single epoch (*Yuga*). When two epochs are combined, eleven gurus appear. Sri Krishna is the eleventh guru in the combined span of the *Treta Yuga* and *Dvapara Yuga*.

[GV1:P0738] Question: Is it not the case that Sri Krishna is traditionally referred to as a deity (*Deva*)?

[GV1:P0739] Guru: Generally, conferring the status of a deity was the prevailing practice. Elevating him to the status of a deity was a necessity for the survival of the Brahmins. They perpetually maintained a specific form of worship exclusively for themselves. They remain the sole officiants of rituals in any temple. Furthermore, they reserve certain specialized rituals strictly for their own households. Consider the great Lord Venkateshwara—the idol lacks a distinct nose and eyes. The adorning of sacred ornaments and the complete coating with sandalwood paste (*muzhukkappu*) are conducted in a highly specialized manner. A figure is drawn by concealing the facial features such as the eyes.

[GV1:P0740] Appropriating anything of value as their own was an integral part of their strategy. They have consistently preserved this approach throughout history. Even today, regardless of the political party or organization one examines, they can be found positioning themselves as the authoritative figures over any non-caste-based entity. They operate as the dominant elites in society, securing a position that sustains their influence. Following the lifetimes of the gurus from the *Parayi Petta Panthirukulam*, they authored verses retrospectively assimilating these figures into the Brahmin fold. Historical records indicate that during the lifetimes of these gurus, there was a profound reluctance to either associate with them or to accord any canonical status to their poetic works.

[GV1:P0741] * Continued from the previous issue

[GV1:P0742] Historical accounts suggest that even prior to Sri Krishna's birth, anticipating the emergence of such a profound force, efforts were made to thwart it. Eventually, they themselves developed the conviction that Sri Krishna was perfected by his very birth. It was also established that he was a profoundly wise being. When his preeminence became evident through his birth and maturation, they began to disseminate writings that, while perhaps not overtly abusive in tone, subtly undermined him through the citation of specific narratives. The advent of Sri Krishna provided the world with a magnificent figure who upheld the highest standards of morality and sanctity within the prevailing socio-cultural system of that era. He accomplished this by assimilating all the pre-existing virtues, honoring and cementing them, thereby fulfilling the ultimate purpose of his incarnation. A singular incident narrated in the epic account of the eighteen-day war serves as conclusive evidence for this. Since he aligned himself with truth, it is evident that he possessed absolute clarity regarding the purpose of his mission. He relinquished his entire army and armaments to the Kauravas, choosing to stand entirely alone alongside Arjuna. Assuming the role of Arjuna's aide, he guided him through profound discourse and impelled him to wage the war. Had he been a mere deity, he would have directly engaged in the conflict himself. To a guru, all individuals are fundamentally equal; however, desiring the ultimate victory of truth, a guru invariably aligns with it.

[GV1:P0743] Following the advent of Krishna, they invoke names such as Krishna, Kalki, and Janardhana. These concepts have largely transformed into subsequent interpolations within the Hindu tradition. There have been concerted efforts to deify figures like Sri Ramakrishna, Sri Narayana Guru, and various eminent personalities from North India as divine incarnations (*Avataras*). A similar narrative is propagated by some concerning Chattampi Swami. Nevertheless, one might plausibly contend that the manifestation of the Kalki *Avatara* has already occurred. Elements such as the sword and shield are notably prominent within the lineage of Guru Nanak. Aside from the traditions of Christianity and Islam, they represent a distinct lineage adhering strictly to the structural discipline of a guru tradition or prophethood. Mainstream orthodoxy refuses to acknowledge this, dismissing it on the grounds that it effectively established a separate religion. Regardless of these contentions, it remains an undeniable historical reality that this phenomenon occurred within India itself.

[GV1:P0744] Many religions, such as Jainism and Buddhism, have originated in India. Among them, they are reluctant even to admit that this occurred in India. The reason for this is that it possesses a character distinct from Hinduism. Even upon joining the military, they have been granted the right to retain their traditional headgear and swords. Although they depicted Krishna as a deity and added many other elements while writing his story, they circulated a mere fabricated myth among the common people—the myth of him being the husband of sixteen thousand and eight women.

[GV1:P0745] If such a narrative is presented to the common masses, how would these innocent people perceive this individual? Those with limited knowledge will merely remain entangled within this orchestrated scheme, unsure of what to do. For them to acquire knowledge, all aspects of wisdom have been compiled and restricted to the recitation of the *Gita*. Others are strictly forbidden from even viewing it. They have guarded the Vedas in a similar manner, and the same applies to the Upanishads.

[GV1:P0746] Question: There is no prohibition against reading the *Gita*, is there?

[GV1:P0747] Guru: There is no explicit prohibition against reading it. However, you are aware that those in the lower strata of society were historically denied even the right to basic literacy. In a context where even basic literacy was denied to a *Shudra*, perhaps only one in a hundred thousand people from other communities would have possessed knowledge of epics like the *Mahabharata* and the *Ramayana*, or profound texts like the *Gita*.

[GV1:P0748] Today, the general assumption is that everyone is familiar with the *Gita*. But how many people actually read the *Gita*? A few individuals might attend and listen to discourses on the *Gita* where they are held, and that is the extent of it. One should reflect on how extensively the Sanskrit *Gita* has been mastered in languages like Malayalam, Tamil, Telugu, or Tulu. It has gained some traction in Hindi, primarily due to the lack of significant differences in the script.

[GV1:P0749] If one observes closely, they will realize whether such widespread propagation of the *Gita* existed prior to the last sixty years. However, until recently, there was widespread familiarity with texts like the *Narayaneeyam*. That is no longer the case; the *Gita* has now been brought to the forefront. What was the underlying motive behind circulating a degrading fabrication among the poor regarding a great personality who possessed the rights to such a monumental text? It should not be naively dismissed as an act done out of ignorance. This remains one of the most monumental farces perpetrated through the cunning manipulation of knowledge.

[GV1:P0750] Certain historical accounts state that Krishna married eight women. That might also have been due to the societal conditions of that era, which dictated that unmarried girls should not interact too closely with men. Similarly, the history of the Prophet mentions that he married ten women. This is why they are referred to as the luminaries of their respective epochs. Whatever is required for that epoch, be it good or bad, they must demonstrate it before their departure. It is for this precise reason that such marriages were demonstrated. Krishna was one who attained eight such states. Similarly, it is stated that the Prophet had to marry to fulfill this specific state. This is an act compelled by nature itself—perhaps implying that they had a specific cosmic mandate to fulfill. Merely because such a perspective exists in Islam, a local *beedi* roller or a fishmonger attempts to equate himself with the Prophet and marries ten times. Similarly, citing the example of Panchali, people in southern Travancore can be seen marrying up to five times. They fail to emulate or even glance at any of the other profound actions demonstrated by these great figures.

[GV1:P0751] This group of people has not displayed even the slightest inclination to contemplate why these great figures acted in such ways. Whether dealing with a king or a divine incarnation, unless the label of 'Brahminism' is attached to them, some form of deceit will inevitably be concealed within their historical narratives. The narrative surrounding Maveli serves as a prime example of this. By examining the extensive efforts made to confer *Kshatriya* status upon rulers from other castes at this end of the country, one can comprehend the extent of the manipulations they have orchestrated. To prevent the loss of their divine status, they intellectually engineered structures like the *Amarakosha*, beginning with 'Amara Nirjara Deva', completely consolidating their narrative. They even managed to subtly integrate texts like the *Siddharoopam*, which cost a mere eight *kashu* in Travancore at the time, into this grand scheme. Consequently, irrespective of the context, anyone operating within this linguistic framework is inextricably bound to the concept of the deity.

[GV1:P0752] In order to prevent the loss of such Vedic authority, the *Varnashrama Dharma* has been preserved to this day. The *Gita* itself states that in the *Kali Yuga*, there will be an intermingling of castes (*Sankara*). Why, then, should one adhere to the *Varnashrama Dharma* today? Today, poetry is hybridized. When even a plant growing in the courtyard is experienced as a hybrid, what exactly are we trying to achieve with this *Varnashrama Dharma*? If one examines this meticulously, the trajectory up to the present day demonstrates that throughout the extensive duration of this *Kali Yuga*, the lifespans of all human beings will be guided toward an ultimate reality where only liberation (*Mukti*) and the divine (*Deva*) hold authority.

[GV1:P0753] Question: What did you mean by stating "only liberation and the divine"?

[GV1:P0754] Guru: That is to say, it has been elucidated thus far that those who follow the absolute Guru lineage attain liberation, whereas those who follow alternative paths are granted multiple incarnations, elevating them at least to the stature of a deity. As an illustration of this, even if the realization that human rights are universal for all individuals has not been entirely achieved, the conviction has been firmly established.

[GV1:P0755] It has become government legislation that education is accessible to all human beings. The government has facilitated this by providing financial assistance. Consequently, there is no doubt that over time, all forms of knowledge will become universally accessible. Once knowledge, wealth, and intellectual awakening have been comprehensively attained, humanity will reflect, "Despite possessing all these, a state of tranquil peace has not been achieved; let us investigate this." Once knowledge, wealth, and intellect are equitably attained, human endeavor will be directed toward peace. There is absolute certainty that they will attain and perfect it unconsciously. Should these aspirations remain unfulfilled over ten or twelve generations, the world may descend into profound chaos in ten to two hundred years. If such a state of stagnation occurs, nature might manifest an opportunity, akin to the immediate influx of water following the introduction of salt, resulting in the birth of exalted souls capable of inherently transforming the situation. Hoping that, instead of compelling such an intervention through divine glory, all sections of our society may be inspired to utilize our endowed intellect and capabilities to earnestly comprehend and act in accordance with the divine will, I shall conclude for the present.

[GV1:P0757] July 1981

[GV1:P0758] Question: From what you have just concluded, it would appear to those with some intellect that this is being stated with immense resentment.

[GV1:P0759] Guru: There is resentment, unequivocally. Would I appreciate my contemporaries deteriorating in any manner? If I possessed a home and a family, would I remain a passive observer if they committed an error? I would endeavor to rectify it to the best of my abilities. If there were a mother, a sister, or close relatives, and it was understood that their actions were detrimental to them, to me, and to the populace, I would alter it. Currently, none of that exists. Presently, devotion to God is not juxtaposed with malevolence. It aligns with benevolence and the elements that sustain it. Consequently, one naturally gravitates toward realms where goodness prevails.

[GV1:P0760] Simultaneously, is it feasible to comprehensively reprimand those who exhibit malevolence? A peculiar perversion that diverts everyone toward malevolence is permeating us. It is observable in everyone, irrespective of distinctions such as scholar or ignoramus, ascetic or yogi, sage, devotee, or man of action.

[GV1:P0761] Just because it is the truth, is it possible to approach everyone and state it directly? Even if articulated, there would scarcely be anyone to heed it. Observing certain things induces agony. Observing others evokes sympathy. There are numerous instances where one is distressed by the sheer obstinacy of certain individuals. In the context of enduring such agony over an extended period by witnessing myriad such occurrences, all these individuals possess distinct capabilities within this world. None of them were deficient in exercising their intellect. If, by divine grace, their intellect could be redirected even marginally toward a virtuous path, is it possible to articulate the immense asset it would be, not solely for us, but for the entire world? Is not the existence of such souls in this world a profound truth that perpetually disseminates eternal peace?

[GV1:P0762] Individuals who harbor the notion that it is sufficient for themselves or for you need not entertain such thoughts. There are countless multitudes in the world. Would it not suffice for ten or twenty-five of them? The nature of devotion to God, or God's love, cannot be comprehensively delineated in any measure. Consequently, the capabilities born of such love manifest in myriad forms. Love resides in everyone. Elevating that love to the pinnacle of its realization can only be accomplished through unceasing vigilance. I do not believe there exists anything comparable to that divine love. It might be owing to the fact that I have become such a believer that these sentiments have emerged. Otherwise, it is my conviction that my words would never exhibit a vindictive nature toward anyone. Perceiving everything through the love that constitutes true knowledge, resolving the deficiencies of existence through actions rooted in that knowledge, acquiring merit in its stead, and ultimately transcending both merit and demerit—if there is an 'I', I perceive it merely as one among billions of offspring, one among billions of living entities. All of this is encompassed within Your glory; You are the truth and the untruth of the world; You Yourself are Sat, Chit, and Ananda—I have merely articulated words aspiring to merge into that state. My sole aspiration is that God may bless all His children to attain this.

[GV1:P0763] Question: The world today appears to be in a precipitous rush with such a revolutionary disposition. What might be the underlying cause? Wherever one observes, religiously and politically, there is a conspicuous absence of tranquility, and actions seem to have devolved into a state of profound uncertainty.

[GV1:P0764] Guru: We should lament only if the populace had not evolved into this state. Observing the progression and regression of the world, this is absolutely imperative for the present epoch. If we remain complacent, assuming that what has been discovered thus far holds some validity, it will prove more detrimental than the preceding conditions. If we concede that what existed previously was valid to an extent, it would culminate in a trajectory that plunges the entire world into obscurity. This is because, oppressed by the tyranny of monarchies, feudal hegemonies, and tenant servitude, caste and religion intensified to their utmost extremes, rendering life entirely bestial. Thus, an ideological quest for liberty fostered a political tension here. None of these aforementioned political enthusiasts emerged by discovering a traditional foundation and seeking to sustain it. Their selflessness, born of witnessing the myriad afflictions and losses of the people, engendered a desire to enact some form of liberation. That is the zenith of their capabilities. Within that paradigm of thought, they progressed—stumbling and recovering—achieving some commendable outcomes while inadvertently precipitating subsequent chaos.

[GV1:P0765] This is an absolute distortion unconsciously assimilated within them, fueled by their egoistic assertions of supremacy, comprising a faction that rejects everything unequivocally and another that accepts everything indiscriminately. When disparate types of leaders were embraced within this matrix, numerous followers blindly enlisted and began unconsciously spouting ideologies. They are ostensibly valorous individuals who remain utterly ignorant of the essence of sacrifice or its fundamental nature.

[GV1:P0766] There is a contingent of individuals who endorse them—destitute people lacking both education and wealth. They implicitly believe whatever is articulated by those they harbor affection for. By aggregating all such vulnerable individuals, a numerical dominance is manufactured. Observing this, the leaders who initially instigated the movement reigned as idealists and leaders for a significant duration. Embellishments and altercations continue to proliferate, creating the illusion that this constitutes the absolute reality of the world. This is the unbridled manifestation of the resentment against the tyranny of the feudal lords and tenants we alluded to earlier. Such distortions will inevitably permeate this process. It is inconsequential. In that frenetic race, even if contemporaries advocate for righteousness, it may not be implemented. Because in an unrestrained surge, this too shall dissipate. Such a pursuit is merely akin to arriving at the seashore and reveling in the sight of the horizon. A state of stagnation will inevitably ensue. A predicament will befall them wherein they can neither retreat nor maneuver from their current position.

[GV1:P0767] Such a juncture will precipitate a phase that rectifies the world's antecedent deficiencies. Thus, as a consequence of this multifaceted and suffocating chaotic trajectory, analogous to the populace heaving a sigh of relief, the temporal manifestation of divine will shall promptly arrive at that precise moment. Then, these aberrations will autonomously recede or be eradicated from religious leaders and mass leaders. Much like the dissolution of numerous monarchies and feudal regimes, it will transpire imperceptibly. Concurrently, an embodiment of the divine will shall emerge. Subsequently, a period characterized by conflicts and disputes over its respective ideologies will persist. For a duration, an intense fervor to implement it will be exhibited. Akin to insatiable desires, it will necessitate a considerable epoch to achieve consummation. When it is thus realized over an extended period, the intrinsic worth of this era will be unequivocally affirmed.

[GV1:P0768] Question: Does this period refer to the Kali Yuga?

[GV1:P0769] Guru: Yes, it refers to the Kali Yuga.

[GV1:P0770] Question: Then, what is meant by this Kali?

[GV1:P0772] Question: Certainly, goodness. What is the reason for calling it absolute goodness?

[GV1:P0773] Guru: That has already been stated. As you know, Kali Yuga is the end of the Chatur Yuga. The early period of Kali is an evaluation of the good and evil of the other three past eras. Moreover, it could be that this evaluation is reached over ten or twenty-five thousand years.

[GV1:P0774] Question: Does this evaluation refer to previous births?

[GV1:P0775] Guru: Absolutely, it does.

[GV1:P0776] Question: Then we can firmly believe that there are numerous births, right?

[GV1:P0777] Guru: Yes, you can believe exactly that.

[GV1:P0778] Question: How can this be made believable to the people?

[GV1:P0780] Question: Then how is this fully implemented?

Thus, I am telling you in the light of experience that this will be brought to a good path. It will also attain a complete form, just like what exists politically and religiously now. Consequently, in humans who discover this, honesty, humility, and the competence to practice them will reach their full potential. It will be utilized for the peace and survival of humanity. However, that will last for a long time. The era known as Satya Yuga will be shifted to the next Chatur Yuga.

[GV1:P0782] Question: The essence of what you are saying is that it will grow in this manner and complete the era of each Manu, isn't it?

[GV1:P0786] Question: Although everyone here talks about progress today, it is shown that there is no progress even in their names. A sweeping term like 'Harijans'. [GV1:P0790] Among the Ezhavas of the south, four illams (lineages) are mentioned: Mootillam, Choyillam, Pallichayillam, and Mayyanattillam. Even these so-called high communities have not been able to play any significant role here.

[GV1:P0792] The reason for this is that the government, consciously or unconsciously, in every sector under the name of democracy, has established that education and wealth can belong to everyone, and that a position in the government can belong to anyone. Isn't it clear that this marginalization occurred because the governments in their respective times viewed people with different perspectives? Similarly, today the government gives equal freedom everywhere to the backward Christians and Harijans. Moreover, it provides all the necessary financial assistance for them. At this rate, if we look back after eighty years, the upcoming eighty years will bring them to the level of those who are called the greatest prominent communities today. There is no doubt. Therefore, in any era, there is no doubt that people will be marginalized or prosper depending on the manner in which the state handles and leads them.

[GV1:P0793] However, due to the magnitude of time or for some other reason, Islam has incurred certain shortcomings. They will do many things to show greatness through their rule. Because of that zeal, the stories most commonly seen in Arabian history are those of imprisoning one's father and ruling by oneself. A proof of this is Pakistan and Bangladesh. Even though the Prophet was accepted as a messenger, there is a history of even his children being murdered. It is not customary to kill the priestly class. Yet, we see it being done. Because of the Prophet's steadfastness, wealth and popularity came to them. Now, they are unable to adapt and practice it properly according to the times. If merely one thousand five hundred years of the Prophet's era have been made like this, we see an inextricable knot when we consider what the countless historical treasures of the Hindus are, which cannot even be fully enumerated.

[GV1:P0794] Therefore, even if the question you asked is correct now, it must be inferred that some children of God would have been born among that group as well to remove their marginalization. [GV1:P0796] It should not be inferred from this that the intention is to condemn them or to banish them in order to move forward. We must also believe that it is perhaps by divine design that they attained certain positions of status, and that through their cunning intellect, they have been able to control and govern the masses to this day. However, we can affirm with confidence that the wise will not reject this era—an era most conducive for them to unite with all human beings, exercising compassion while remaining steadfast in the philosophical principles of Sanatana. This can be achieved if even these capable and cunning individuals strive to impart cooperation and good sense to others in accordance with the present times, thereby demonstrating the unity of human society. Let us conclude this with a prayer that the greatest good sense may prevail.

[GV1:P0798] September 1981

[GV1:P0799] Birthday Message

[GV1:P0800] Disciple: What prompted you to take up ashram life?

[GV1:P0801] Guru: An inherent inclination that unknowingly existed before merely found an opportunity to manifest itself more clearly, that is all.

[GV1:P0802] Disciple: What was that opportunity?

[GV1:P0803] Guru: It was the ignorance within the household. What I mean by ignorance is—my stepfather, the absence of a father—because of that, we were at the place where my mother was married a second time. There, my stepfather would drink, and quarrels surrounding that were a regular occurrence. This was the cause for the motivation.

[GV1:P0804] Disciple: You considered this as an opportunity?

[GV1:P0805] Guru: Yes, this came as an opportunity.

[GV1:P0806] Disciple: After this opportunity arose, towards what did that initial inclination of yours turn?

[GV1:P0807] Guru: This inclination further sharpened the aspect of devotion. Thus, although the desire for an ashram life was within me for two years, since I was in an environment where I did not know how to go about it, I felt like going to Palani. For that purpose, I undertook vows and walked around with a garland around my neck like others do. After two years passed like this, everyone started asking why I was not going. I replied that I would go when the time comes, and that extending the duration of the vows would not cause any harm.

[GV1:P0808] Disciple: Was it after going to Palani that you reached this state?

[GV1:P0809] Guru: I did not go to Palani. I went to the ashram itself. One day, due to a quarrel with my stepfather, I spent that night in a bhajan mutt there. The next morning, I went to the guru who had taught me the alphabet and requested him to take me and enroll me in some ashram. He fulfilled that desire.

[GV1:P0810] Disciple: In which ashram did he enroll you?

[GV1:P0811] Guru: Initially, it was in Kalady. Since things were not right there, I came straight to Aluva and reached the Aluva Advaita Ashram.

[GV1:P0812] Disciple: What was your age at that time?

[GV1:P0813] Guru: Fourteen years old.

[GV1:P0814] Disciple: At that age, when you raised such a request to him, he took you straight to an ashram without saying anything else, didn't he!

[GV1:P0815] Guru: He already knew more information about me beforehand. It was with this understanding that he did this.

[GV1:P0816] Disciple: His name?

[GV1:P0817] Guru: Kumara Pillai.

[GV1:P0818] Disciple: Whose was the ashram where he first took you?

[GV1:P0819] Guru: Agamananda Swami's - Sri Ramakrishna Mission.

[GV1:P0820] Disciple: Was it with the intention of leading a monastic life that you started the ashram life even then?

[GV1:P0821] Guru: Certainly.

[GV1:P0822] Disciple: In that regard, I have a desire to know about each experiential realm of the life you have had since then, that is, about each experience of the monastic life.

[GV1:P0823] Guru: I came to the Aluva Advaita Ashram and spent two years there. After that, I was invited to Sivagiri. I came to Sivagiri and spent quite some time in the branches of Sivagiri. After spending four continuous years in Sivagiri itself, they sent me to various institutions. I also spent a considerable time taking charge of those institutions. Altogether, seventeen years were spent in Sivagiri and its affiliated branches.

[GV1:P0824] Disciple: In spiritual matters, there is a tradition of initiating one into the monastic life, that is, giving spiritual instruction (upadesha). Did you receive that from Sivagiri itself?

[GV1:P0825] Guru: No. There is such a practice in Sivagiri. They usually do it at the time of bestowing the saffron robes. Until then, many live there under the boundary of being a brahmachari. However, I had felt earlier that an instruction devoid of spiritual experience was unnecessary. Therefore, I did not receive instruction from them.

[GV1:P0826] Disciple: You deliberately refrained from receiving it.

[GV1:P0827] Guru: Yes.

[GV1:P0828] Disciple: Then, during which period and from whom did you receive the instruction?

[GV1:P0829] Guru: During my time spent at Sivagiri and its branches, while at Aruvippuram, I developed a strong, indescribable desire to find a guru possessing true experiential merit. While I was pondering how to attain this, a person named Vijayan (from Karinkulam), who was a disciple of a wandering ascetic known as Pathani Swami, spent a night with me. The next morning, saying, "You are quite good, I will show you a Swami," he took me along. We went towards the beach. Reaching the beach, we walked from Vallakkadavu to Poonthura. While returning and arriving amidst the thickets on the western side of Beemapally, he was there.

[GV1:P0830] He did not have the appearance I had imagined. A very large, dark figure. With a very long beard and wide, staring eyes, his physique evoked a formidable disposition. He was wearing a piece of a sack. It was getting close to dusk. Therefore, I did not approach him. When Vijayan went and sat to speak with him, I heard him say in Tamil that he did not know me. Saying "Alright, let it be morning," he let it go. That night, we slept at Beemapally. The next day, very early in the morning, while I was bathing, he came down that way. Seeing me walking like that, he called out and imparted the instruction to me right there and then.

[GV1:P0831] Disciple: You mentioned that you received the instruction; within how much time after that did you have the spiritual experience?

[GV1:P0832] Guru: It was two and a half years after receiving the instruction that this realization occurred. Prior to that, I happened to receive a vision. In a very clear manner.

[GV1:P0833] Disciple: What was thatٹ

[GV1:P0834] Guru: That was—during the time I resided at Aruvippuram, there was an occasion when I was mentally and physically exhausted. The mental exhaustion was partly due to certain difficulties from the administration. Another was the distress of not attaining this, of seeking for the sake of spiritual matters and not attaining it; the body wearing out with daily fever. Waking up at four o'clock every day was a routine. One day when I woke up, I felt dizzy and fell, hitting the wall. It was six o'clock when I managed to get up from there.

[GV1:P0835] That day, there was such an exhaustion of the mind. The body gave out too. And the purpose for which I came was not fulfilled. What would this life be? Thinking like this, I felt that I did not come desiring any of this. If the body goes, let it go. What is there to think more about it? When I felt that way, a sort of courage came over me, and I quickly performed the daily routines. There is a full-length portrait of Narayana Guru Swami in a room of that southern building. After sitting there and performing prayers and pujas, I immediately felt that I should go to the place where he meditated. Going there, I made a firm resolve that day to climb this hill for forty-one days and see what happens, and thus I kept going for forty-one days. On the fortieth day, upon reaching there and looking up from the rock, I suddenly saw a halo, much like the halo of the moon. And within it, a face. That face was unfamiliar to me. Since I was unfamiliar with what it was, a sudden shudder went through my body. And I climbed down.

[GV1:P0836] That evening, I went to Neyyattinkara to fetch oil for the temple. While there, another acquaintance invited me into a coffee shop. As I was drinking coffee, I looked up and saw a portrait of the very figure I had seen earlier. Upon inquiring whose portrait it was, I was told that it was Rishi Sai Baba. I resolved then that if I ever were to build a humble dwelling, I would enshrine this portrait there first.

[GV1:P0837] My experience with my Guru was thus—without my speaking another word, and without his saying anything further, I received his spiritual initiation.

[GV1:P0838] Disciple: I fail to comprehend that. What does it mean to receive initiation without either party exchanging a word?

[GV1:P0839] Guru: The purpose of my visit was stated in a single word. He also posed a question in a few words: 'For what purpose have you come?' I replied, 'For whatever may bring peace to my soul.' These were the only words exchanged. Embracing me with tears, he declared, 'You are the rightful heir.' He then wrote down the initiation. Without uttering another syllable, he instructed, 'Very well, take this and continue to utilize it in this manner.' They were two mantras. 'Within three months of utilizing this mantra, two signs will manifest. They will appear in a dream. You must return here then.' Accordingly, the signs appeared, and I returned. The Guru stated that everything was present, yet there would be a considerable delay. It was only after approximately two and a half years that a continuous series of experiences commenced.

[GV1:P0840] Disciple: Could you perhaps elaborate on those experiences in a manner that we might comprehend?

[GV1:P0841] Guru: Merely recounting the experience to you will not render it comprehensible. This experience entails the manifestation before us of a light or form that we had not anticipated. It must not be a projection of our intentions. That is its underlying truth. If it were anticipated, would it not merely be a materialization aligned with one's own thoughts?

[GV1:P0842] Disciple: Indeed, it would imply that it arose in accordance with one's imagination.

[GV1:P0843] Guru: Is it not correct to say it manifested from his imagination? Did he not possess such an imagination? He certainly did—regarding God,ٹ he will only receive what is conducive to his mental transformation at that particular moment. However, that is not the case. From its primordial form, it must manifest beginning from whatever he initially experienced, in accordance with the evolution of the soul that has been instrumental throughout his successive incarnations.

[GV1:P0844] Disciple: It must emerge from the earliest stage, that is, from the very inception of the soul.

[GV1:P0845] Guru: Affirmative. It must manifest in accordance with the meritorious deeds of the soul's primal incarnation. Therefore, it ought not to manifest in this manner. It should not appear in the form currently venerated, nor in forms that have passed, nor in those anticipated in the future; rather, it dawns within him in accordance with the destiny of that specific incarnation. It is utterly impossible to articulate this in words. One can only rely upon what has been seen and heard.

[GV1:P0846] Disciple: Indeed.

[GV1:P0847] Guru: Consequently, what will you comprehend from this? You shall comprehend nothing. I might claim to have seen Shiva, to have seen Vishnu, to have witnessed myriad other entities, to have beheld the entirety of nature, and to have observed numerous forms that have manifested within nature unto this day. However, none of this will foster any true comprehension. Merely uttering the words jaggery, sugar, clarified butter, and honey, and attempting to taste them—will that yield any sweetness?

[GV1:P0848] Disciple: No.

[GV1:P0849] Guru: Even licking the written words will impart no sweetness. It must be properly cultivated and refined. Such refinement can only be achieved by each individual themselves. It cannot be cultivated through any other means whatsoever.

[GV1:P0850] Disciple: We earnestly desire to hear through which stages and by overcoming what obstacles you have attained your current state, presented in a manner that provides us with an understanding of the unique characteristics inherent to each realm of these experiences.

[GV1:P0851] Guru: As I have previously recounted to you, a form of which I had neither heard nor possessed prior knowledge manifested before me. Prior to that, for seventeen years, I offered worship at the samadhi of Narayana Guru and at the site of his consecration. I derived no such spiritual experience from that practice. [GV1:P0865] Guru: Until then, Arjuna held the belief that the deities, ascetics, and sages as per the scriptures, as well as the associated gurus and uncles who were their followers, were all to be respected. Arjuna had within him something capable of removing all of this in an instant to reveal his inherent nature, yet he remained in a state where he could not understand or act upon it. The merit of a guru lies in correcting this. History says that Arjuna was with Krishna for about fifty years. Yet, it is said that Arjuna still doubted Krishna and questioned him again. Finally, sitting on that battlefield, he asked - "Do you believe me?" "I certainly believe you," said Arjuna. "Then why are you not doing what I say?" "I will not do such things. It is not in accordance with Dharma." - How can one say "I believe you" and "it is not in accordance with Dharma" at the same time? "I certainly believe you. But citing this moral condition, it is not right to kill uncles, others, and gurus. Therefore, I will not do it," he said.

[GV1:P0866] "Let that be, you know me." "I know." "Why did I come? See why you have come now." This means he is speaking of his wisdom. We call it vision (Darshan) here. Arjuna could also receive it, just like these children receive it. Sitting there, he looked. He showed that he had come to reclaim the state of this era. "Alright, do you believe that?" "I believe."

[GV1:P0867] "Alright, then we must see in what all stages we both have taken this human birth since the beginning." [GV1:P1074] The Muslims are not like that. They merely handled a religious system. And then, applied some brute force. They too managed to secure a certain hold in this manner. Therefore, no matter how enlightened they become through education and wealth, or how long they are seasoned in administration, they have not reached the path of Sanatana Dharma—an enlightened state combining orderliness, cleanliness aligned with Hindu Dharma, and a pure lifestyle blended with humility. To bring about a special character suited to this Kali Yuga by combining what is in other religions as well, all religious followers and all religious scholars must unite and evaluate the hybrid era of the author of the Gita. [GV1:P1079] Disciple: Is it in the sense of 'what is to come' that you inform us by saying certain things involving the twelve zodiac signs, nine planets, and twenty-seven stars, and make us understand a method that demonstrates that practical nature?

[GV1:P1080] Guru: Yes. Unless a path of action is implemented by evaluating these three periods, it is not possible to see unity in any other way or to experience in the future the actions done for the good of human society. For this, evaluating the cause, effect, macro, and micro aspects, removing its flaws to that extent can only become possible for our survival, which we preserved earlier, if it reaches up to four or five generations as a systematic progression of a lineage. The summary of the above is that it will not be possible for anyone other than the children who come by the grace of God.

[GV1:P1081] Disciple: Does this mean that all the religious cultures and administrative cultures that have come down through the ages until today should blend together as one, and its own path of practice should come forward as the core, form, fulfillment, and action in the value of human sacrifice?

[GV1:P1082] Guru: Yes. We must certainly understand that only if it happens this way can human effort be evaluated in submission to the divine will, value be assigned to the sacrifice that operates and culminates through it, and the peace and harmony of all of us who worked together in its goodness be realized. I conclude with a prayer that the divine resolve (Brahman's will) may bless us for this.

[GV1:P1085] Disciple: Kerala politics, or Indian politics, or world politics - do you have anything to say about this?

Such people certainly cannot think about the consequences or make a decision and implement it after thinking. If he also gets a gratuity, will he be able to study and improve in this world? What will happen to his children? It is certain that his children will never study. Thus, the intention will complete the old ways too. The trick is that what is older than the old has been completed. Then, we must believe that what is thought of as politics existed here for some time. There is a memory that the light of the predominance of its sacrifice began to be seen from 1944 to 1948. After that, it continued until about 1960 in the name of that weight. [GV1:P1093] Disciple: What do you mean by minor things?

What we need is to understand what endures among the people currently involved in all these things, and how they should be able to endure in the future. What we need now is to lovingly bring about a sense of unity regarding everything among the people, as mentioned earlier. However, unity in love can only be brought about through a certain kind of fear. Cultivate that fear as if it were towards God, a father, or a mother. Cultivate love and respect. Regardless of what the children of Bharat are involved in, attempt to create a way of life, at least in Bharat, that serves as a model for the world. If today's castes or religions can create various political groups, the believers here who think, learn, and teach should stand together to form a national organization, recognizing that believers are one, irrespective of religion and caste. Religious leaders should not be included in this. They should only provide guidance. As Mahatmaji said, one should not desire to cling to it, but merely achieve the objective. Thus, when believers also become those who fear out of love, they will have to respect each other through mutual love. We cannot sustain anything without such love and respect. It seems that on Indian soil, the concept of love is used like a gas. An example of this is communists going out at night to create problems. If a wife and children go to the temple together and someone questions it, they say it was done for their sake. This might be done because they cannot entirely deny a matter that is deeply ingrained in the people. It should be exactly like that. Otherwise, the dynamic between the capitalist and the worker, as well as the attitude of posing as a leader, will inadvertently change. [GV1:P1095] Disciple: Are you certain that such a thing will happen?

[GV1:P1097] Disciple: So, based on what we have heard from you, do you have anything further to inform us regarding any doubtful aspects of this solar system, which consists of nine planets, twelve zodiac signs, and twenty-seven stars?

[GV1:P1098] Guru: Yes. As mentioned earlier, this is the era of the seventh Manu. This means that half the time since the origin of the world has passed. It has yet to function for another half of its time. We must believe that there are an unknown number of solar systems in this universe.

[GV1:P1099] Disciple: Do you have any absolute proof for that?

[GV1:P1100] Guru: Yes. One hundred and four solar systems have been observed. Ours is a medium-sized solar system among them. There are stellar constellations seen between them. These stellar spheres are realms where the aforementioned virtuous souls reside. Divine creation has endowed each solar system with a unique nature.

[GV1:P1101] Disciple: Do you believe that any other solar system is more powerful than this one?

[GV1:P1102] Guru: There are numerous other solar systems of greater size and special power. It cannot be said that they are exactly like this one. There are also solar systems with entirely different characteristics compared to this one. Everything in nature undergoes change. A cluster of ten solar systems forms one measurement unit. Thus, there are many stellar spheres that control the existence of the solar system. Those stellar spheres observe and sustain all of this.

[GV1:P1103] Disciple: Why did you say that?

[GV1:P1104] Guru: Just as there is a gravitational field of attraction between this earth and the solar system, there is an attractive force between these stars as well. Accordingly, based on the virtues and sins of a particular solar system, each sphere within the solar system may draw closer to another, or to a stellar sphere.

[GV1:P1105] Disciple: What could be the reason for such drawing closer?

[GV1:P1106] Guru: I mentioned earlier that a human being has only two things to do once born in this world: virtuous deeds and sinful deeds. The result of the sinful or virtuous forces we accumulate as we are born, die, and exist in this world—as its weight increases, it may draw closer to the solar sphere or any other sphere for either destruction or survival. If that drawing closer leads to destruction, fire might erupt due to air pressure itself, causing it to melt and collapse. Alternatively, extreme cold might arise, leading to a state where nothing can survive. Or, everything could be entirely upended, resulting in either complete destruction or partial survival. Conversely, if it draws closer to a stellar sphere that has accumulated virtues, it might cause some destruction but then function in a good state again.

[GV1:P1107] Disciple: In that case, can we know or guess whether it is a region that has committed sins?

[GV1:P1108] Guru: Virtue and sin are not what we merely intend them to be. They are the experiences that befall us if we do not act according to the righteous order ordained by Brahman. We should not assume that we possess the knowledge to understand this and act accordingly.

[GV1:P1109] Disciple: If so, then how do we distinguish between good and bad?

[GV1:P1110] Guru: God has given us a medium to distinguish them. That is the Manus who have passed before us and their lineage. We can only accomplish our actions in accordance with that. If we fail to act accordingly, such things may happen.

[GV1:P1111] Disciple: In that case, if a celestial body undergoes any destruction, will it cause the destruction of this solar system itself?

[GV1:P1112] Guru: No. That will not happen. It may be destroyed or grow due to the pressure of air, water, or other solid substances. Only its physical form will change; its ethereal nature cannot be altered. The change in that ethereal nature occurs just as the specific eras of each Manu change.

[GV1:P1113] Disciple: Are you saying that this solar system will undergo a change only after the era of the Manus is completely over?

[GV1:P1114] Guru: Yes, it is precisely so. Only at such a time will a change occur to it. Otherwise, the calculations would have to be radically altered, not just from this world, but from many worlds. Therefore, God will not do such a thing.

[GV1:P1115] Disciple: So, you mentioned earlier that there are some spheres that are more powerful than this, right?

[GV1:P1116] Guru: Yes, there are. There are certain spheres capable of magnetically attracting not just our actions, but our very earth itself.

[GV1:P1117] Disciple: In that case, a situation could arise where the earth is destroyed or something else happens to it.

[GV1:P1130] January 1982

[GV1:P1131] Many variations occur in the evolution of faith and trust. Starting with the trust we have in our parents, we maintain different forms of trust in our children, family members, neighbors, and even the animals we rear. How many attitudinal shifts occur within this? If we reflect upon whether we have perfected this, we realize that we have not been able to achieve absolute trust in any of the aforementioned. Even concerning a mere garment, our trust in it lasts only as long as its utility. Thus, trust has its limits. Initially, there is a conviction that one cannot survive even for a moment apart from one's father or mother. However, this later shifts towards one's spouse and children. When some people place their faith in alcohol, they forget everything else.

[GV1:P1132] Above all this lies faith in God. This ranges from deities like Madan, Kali, Bhadra, and Chathan, all the way up to the Guru. Love is deeply intertwined with faith. A father's love for his children resides profoundly in his heart; it is invisible to others. The trust and love a woman feels for her husband differ from what she feels for her father. A mother's love is of an entirely different nature. Even if she lacks formal knowledge, she harbors immense love for her children within. Love is glorious. In today's times, even the love between siblings has its limits. How can we sustain this love beyond these boundaries? Nurturing any of these forms of love is easier said than done. Putting it into practice is where the difficulty lies.

[GV1:P1133] At the very least, we must preserve the depth of this love. This love is the result of humanity's boundless endeavors over countless ages. Today, we acquire a piece of clothing effortlessly. But what was our condition before its invention? Similarly, to bring each subject to our knowledge, our ancestors or we ourselves must have struggled through lifetimes. To prevent this love from breaking apart here and there, the parents are the first ones who can impart teachings. It is the parents who initially teach a child to bow before a lamp or a stone. Even without the child's conscious awareness, the glory of love blossoms within. The child then begins to express the same back to them. Unknowingly, knowledge awakens within the child.

[GV1:P1134] We roll the dung of the cow we rear and envision Lord Ganesha in it. Why? That is a form of faith. How did faith develop in this foul-smelling substance? A person without faith might find this ridiculous. How much must our ancestors have struggled to instill love within us even for cow dung? After bowing before the cow dung, people began shaping idols to solidify their faith. Even an onlooker would unknowingly bow down in reverence. When Tamils sculpt an idol of God, it often has a mustache. Both the one who sculpted it and the one who worships it do so with God in their thoughts.

[GV1:P1135] Some people remain neutral, not denying anything, thinking they do not know whether all these exist or not, and that it is all just people's beliefs. Such a person lives with understanding. Christians, Muslims, and Buddhists all establish their own respective constructs and attempt to instill faith in people. How can this faith be sustained in life? How can it be imparted to those around us? We are able to exert our own will by forgetting both those whom we nurture and those who nurture us. How is this possible?

[GV1:P1136] Consider what happens if the source of love flows elsewhere. What is the implication if it is said that a woman with four children eloped with another man? This can only be changed by your own mind. This is a path of washing away other vile thoughts by firmly establishing faith and love. Those of you who desire this should contemplate how to gather the strength for it.

[GV1:P1137] This is a subject where knowledge must be imparted without making a distinction between men and women. Just as those who teach in primary classes that the sun rises in the east later explain the reality as the students grow older, Vedic scholars will also reverse the order of worship. By fostering something called faith, they bring you to a certain stage, then detach that faith from one object and direct it towards reality. Gunangudi Masthan is an example of this. He says that there is no use in merely murmuring mantras. He says this only after reaching that elevated state. However, until then, they were the ones who taught people to murmur mantras.

[GV1:P1138] The majority of believers are those who desire to work towards an entirely better tomorrow through some form of disciplined practice or their faith. What was described above is a characteristic of that faith crumbling when it could not be sustained. What you can gain from this description is the insight to observe a certain state of the world. Only a Guru can provide that insight. Those belonging to the Trimurti tradition can perceive and accomplish things to some extent. That is what has been proclaimed in our Puranas and Vedas.

[GV1:P1139] However, beyond this, we can perceive it scientifically. When any science reaches a certain limit, it becomes impossible for them to handle it. The reason is that they understand all this by keenly observing nature. If a disturbance occurs in that nature, it will all come to an end. The evolution of the mind is not like that. It is a purity of nature that surpasses even the physical world. It is something acquired through life. We can perceive for ourselves how many lifetimes we have had. Even among those present here, there are quite a few who have carefully realized this truth. However, they have not been able to bring it forth into action. Yet, these believers are experiencing it. Why are they unable to bring it forth? How is it that we fail to attain its glory? If we indeed prepare ourselves to closely understand this glory, certain karmic courses will obstruct us. It will hinder us in life, not just in one way, but in every possible way. When one begins to act with a degree of sacrifice, some kind of shortcoming will inevitably attach itself to them. It will also cause them to act aimlessly.

[GV1:P1140] Both men and women will experience this. It is difficult for a person to understand this without the assistance of a Guru. There are numerous such subjects. It takes quite some time just to comprehend all of this. To impart this understanding, there must be a lineage of perfected Gurus who have regulated themselves through their own actions. When speaking of these Gurus, we typically only encounter those who fall under the Trimurti, those whose reach extends merely up to Vethala Nagaram, or, at best, Gurus who stand at the level of the Trimurti.

[GV1:P1141] Beyond this, there are *Kalanthara Gurus* (Gurus transcending time). This is said to be the lineage of Manu. You might ask why the lineage of Manu is being discussed again after stating that it had committed an error. Just because Manu erred, it cannot be deduced that it was not the era of Manu. A flaw in the lineage of a Manu cannot overturn this epoch. The errors that occurred over eons can only be rectified. The era of Manu cannot be falsified. Fourteen Manus were born and upheld its glory. It will be managed through them alone. However, since an error occurred in between, it is revealed that without granting complete autonomy to this, it will be fulfilled through a Guru who embodies it. This revelation is not something we can obtain simply by demanding it. Nor is it something we can bear in any manner. By divine decree and the design of Brahman, it arrives through the destined path. Beyond this, we have no further knowledge to impart.

[GV1:P1142] Guruvani

GURUVANIKAL · February 1982 · Volume 1

[GV1:P1143] February 1982

[GV1:P1144] Our lineage has become entirely ignorant of such matters. The reason is the flaw in the *Trimurti* system and the Vedic decree of untouchability towards the Shudra. As the Shudra was relegated to a very low status, the ignorance of our lineage increased significantly. The Shudra exists in our homes, in the homes of Vaishyas, Kshatriyas, and Brahmins. However, this Shudra is rarely discussed here. To maintain class consciousness, every caste today asserts its class identity. A situation has arisen where people are unwilling to accept someone as a Guru or acknowledge their Guru-hood unless they belong to their specific caste. As evidence of this, starting from Adi Shankaracharya, there are individuals who mention the names of various Mahatmas and speak of them grandiloquently, while calamities continue to befall not just Kerala, but the entirety of India. If asked how many people actually internalize and act upon these teachings, the narrative changes entirely. The auspicious acts of India were accomplished by numerous such Gurus. Let it be remembered that a distinctive power is constantly observing and studying us.

[GV1:P1145] Although God has nothing to learn, He watches how our actions unfold and how the actions of the soul translate into *Karma*. The actions and lineage of Manu serve as an example of this. A society that functions within its respective eras and experiences deprivation manages to survive without completely succumbing to it, exhibiting a certain degree of wealth, intellect, and capability, and thereby passes through life acquiring some fortune. It is easy to observe and understand these matters. What we are practicing now is an easier path to this. That easier path has been bestowed upon us by God Himself.

[GV1:P1146] Gurus are of four categories: *Brahmavit*, *Brahmavaryan*, *Brahmavarishtan*, and *Brahmavareeshtan*. Among these four Gurus, the *Brahmavits* hold the status of the *Trimurtis*. The *Brahmavareeshtan* holds the status of a Rishi. Only two of these Gurus actively engage with the world. The rest do not participate extensively, nor are they accessible to you. This is because they do not descend frequently to act in the worldly realm. They merely speak of what they observe as they pass by. It is difficult for you even to approach and see them. Even if you do see them, you would lack the intellect to comprehend what they say. Although their practical engagement is minimal, their knowledge is profoundly exalted. They merely set forth demonstrating the humility born of love. By internalizing them

[GV1:P1147] *Continuation of the month of January

[GV1:P1148] you will not be able to function. This is not because they lack love, or because you lack love for them. Moreover, there is no provision to accept two Gurus. The Guru will impart advice or guidance to only a select few. Nothing else will be obtained. Whatever you receive comes solely from the *Brahmavit* and *Brahmavaryan* Gurus. Beyond these four categories, there are other Gurus. They are born in accordance with the times. God Himself ordains their birth through a special decree. Certain Gurus born without inherent supernatural powers (*Siddhi*) are examples of this.

[GV1:P1149] Ramananda Swami is the Guru of Kabir Das. Based on the *Bhaktavijayam* and the Puranas, the soul of Kabir Das is understood to be that of a *Brahmarshi*. Kabir Das was not born of a womb (*Yoniputra*). His birth occurred under extraordinary circumstances. It is not something that can be easily explained and comprehended here. It is said that the *Trimurtis* requested Kabir Das to be born in a specific manner. Only then could they have him act according to their intentions. At that point, Kabir Das informed the *Trimurtis* that he could not be born of a womb. He agreed to incarnate only after they promised to facilitate his birth through an alternative means. We are listening to the history of such a great soul. However, what that great soul speaks about the world, the Guru, and the lineage encompasses vast and profound domains. It is then that we truly comprehend the greatness of the Gurus.

[GV1:P1150] In South India, obtaining Gurus of such magnificence has been exceedingly rare. Even if such an occurrence were to happen, our inclination is merely to subordinate them to a deity rather than preserving their legacy in accordance with their greatness. The reason for this is the advent of Shudra governance here. By 'Shudra' here, it refers to the class-Shudra (*Varga-shudra*), not the caste-Shudra. This Shudra was compelled to do everything. Among us, excluding the Brahmin, Kshatriya, and Vaishya, all others are considered Shudras. By establishing governance through the class-Shudra, diverse types of subjects came under the rule of a single monarch. This implies that the king lacked discernment. The one called a king attained power through brute force, not by legitimately occupying the position of a Kshatriya. There is historical evidence for this. The history of Travancore itself serves as an example. The *Ettuveettil Pillamar*, Marthanda Varma, and the *Ettara Yogam* were all members belonging to the Shudra category. Following this, women were adopted from a Kshatriya household. This Kshatriya family was the Mavelikkara family. These are all historical facts. We have not had the opportunity to reflect upon this.

[GV1:P1151] Extremely arduous labor was extracted from the Shudra. History from a thousand years ago does not indicate the existence of caste here. The caste system seen today has emerged merely within the last millennium. Prior to that, the only castes were the aforementioned four foundational classes (*Varnas*).

[GV1:P1152] You will understand the greatness of the Guru only when you comprehend the blunder we have committed. Upon coming to South India, the very concept of the Guru faded away. Apart from offering verbal praises, you have never had the administrative experience of respecting and obeying a Guru. You are also ignorant of your own domestic traditions. This lack of knowledge caused the position of the Guru to degrade so drastically. Due to the absence of a Guru tradition (*Guru Sampradaya*), we have encountered numerous afflictions.

[GV1:P1153] What is the reason the people in South India lacked a complete Guru tradition? The era during which we treated each other as untouchable castes upon sight was not insignificant. That is where you committed your first error. That is what brought a king here. Subjects raised in such a country were prohibited from acquiring education. They were not allowed to handle wealth. The state administration was never intended for those devoid of education and wealth. Thus, they were trampled and suppressed. Those who ruled with tyranny, eating and drinking whatever they could extract, along with a few corrupt officials who thrived on bribes, created a new class. This class was forced to perform all kinds of labor. Due to harsh and menial labor, a community grew in utter ignorance, much like wild grass. Meanwhile, a few within this system sat back and enjoyed luxuries.

[GV1:P1154] Under the cover of such comforts, the local rulers acquired the power to do anything and destroy anything. The king also needed their power. They were given positions of honor. You do not need to know any of the Vedas, Shastras, or Upanishads behind this. If you go out at dawn and work until dusk, you will get a measure (idangazhi) of paddy. The work is for an idangazhi of paddy. Not even for an idangazhi of rice. Out of this idangazhi of paddy, a little is given to the shop to buy salt or chili. The rest is parboiled, pounded, cooked, and consumed to pass the time. Today you might say it is starvation. No. How long ago did the habit of wearing good clothes come about? In those days, none of the workers could afford a dhoti costing more than ten chakras. Even on a taluk basis, you might find about ten such houses. There would certainly be no more than that.

[GV1:P1155] How can we acquire any kind of knowledge while leading such a life? Instead of leading a life endowed with such knowledge, our inability to attain it is due to the grand schemes of the kings. It is impossible even to count the rich people who showed a kind of perversity, stretching their legs to immerse themselves in all the worldly pleasures, making the poor work to help them and destroying them through labor, and those who tolerated these debaucheries to lead an opportunistic life by exploiting them.

[GV1:P1156] When transitioning from the rule of the Ettuveetil Pillamars to the reign of Marthanda Varma, Marthanda Varma's own history states that he beheaded those who applied intellect, logic, and knowledge. Because if they lived, his own head would not remain. The administrative histories before us show that the women of these Ettuveetil Pillamars were captured and married off to fishermen, while the men were beheaded. The government was the 'Ponnu Thampuran' (the golden king). It is said that the Ponnu Thampuran ruled and washed away everything here. Who was washed away? The poor - they were washed away as he pleased. Anyone of some standing was beaten to death. The others were ruled using brute force, much like the British administration did, and through this rule, they became the masters.

[GV1:P1157] The British struck with the butt of their guns. Then it was set right. When this happened, the followers of Vedic rituals and the godfathers here stepped down and started offering enchanted flowers. They chanted mantras after praying for many days. When those who had said they could just pluck and throw them away realized that the butt of the gun would hit their own backs, they cleverly became their slaves. Not only did they become slaves, but they also betrayed the country to them. Gradually, it became about paying tribute. There are records that the king here paid eight lakhs as tribute in those days. Yet, the royal rule continued like an empty shell. We can understand without asking anyone that the people who lived under this rule had no awareness or discretion about good and evil. In this context, demanding "we want freedom, we want freedom," a struggle was waged as a challenge against the British for about a couple of hundred years, and freedom was attained.
