[GV1:P1273] April 1983

[GV1:P1274] Where does human life originate? Where does it culminate? What must one acquire through human life? Or, what level of understanding had we reached before commencing this life? What level of understanding have we reached today? First, conceptualize and comprehend this knowledge. If one lacks the capacity to do so, one must find a capable person (a Guru), stand behind him, observe, familiarize oneself, and seek to understand.

[GV1:P1275] When attempting to find such a person, one must discern whether he is a Yogi, a Karmi, a Jnani, or a Bhakta. Those seeking his acquaintance must understand this before approaching him. The one thus found must be devoted and capable of destroying his own *karma*. When we speak of *karma*, the *karma* accumulated across countless lifetimes spanning multiple reincarnations up to this day remains inextricably entangled and stagnant within this soul. The Guru we seek must be someone capable of taking upon himself the *karma* of those who approach him, utilizing his own actions, intellect, and the power of penance. We may not be able to accept this readily. This is because today we stand before those who preach and practice the ideology of absolute egalitarianism. That mindset has penetrated us, and we too have become a part of it. Rather, one must prepare for this path by observing and learning from the life of an individual who has attained a distinct persona—one who has realized the destined source of existence, acted upon it, facilitated action in others, and acquired blessedness through a life lived in surrender to it.

[GV1:P1276] If we observe our society today, we often see the highly educated incapable of accomplishing any meaningful work, while those with no formal education operate at a very high level. This depends on the *karmic* capacity of each individual. Similarly, we see individuals who have transitioned from running a small betel leaf shop to a wholesale business, as well as those who are incapable of running even a betel leaf shop or rolling a single beedi. What we witness there is the purity of *karma* formed by the alignment of his fortune, blessedness, and aptitude for action. Those who acquire such *karmic* capacity eventually become public leaders and administrators. For example, if there is an era where someone who merely acts in movies can take over governance, all this is possible. You know who rules today. That is a distinct characteristic of *Kali Yuga*. Even though he wandered into cinema due to a diversion in his path, he reached the seat of governance through his *karmic* capacity and intellectual power. Whether rightly or wrongly, he is also able to control a considerable number of people. Yogis are also capable of this.

[GV1:P1277] But there is a Karma Yoga that discerns who the preceptor is, who the disciple is, who the subject is, and who the ruler is. If one does not perceive the collective totality from the standpoint of that Karma Yoga, it will collapse like the Western concept of the collective and, in the frenzied dance of distortion, proceed along a path that destroys both the people and oneself. Today, they have reached that stage. Seeing this, we too are leaping into it. Today, we are like dog feces wrapped in silk and labeled as a pot of nectar. What resides within us is the rampant play of distortion and the frenzied dance of the grotesque. However, if one realizes that within us lies a precious gem, and within that, a pot of nectar, no one will throw dog feces into it. But instead of dog feces wrapped in silk, we must truly have that precious gem and the pot of nectar within us.

[GV1:P1278] Karma is what you cultivate for this purpose. Behold the difference between following a blessed soul whose life is enriched by the performance of that Karma, and following one who dances grotesquely, reinforcing collectivism! A body or action nurtured in that distorted nature can achieve nothing here. Nor can it discover anything. They will only depart from here after destroying what has been discovered, turning it into a legacy of distortion, and sowing destruction. What is needed here is a mother to envision this and a father to observe and act with restraint. For this, each of you must be prepared to begin a new life. What is required here is a Karma Yogi who absorbs only the good on that path of life, eliminates the bad, and bestows a creative life that ascends once again to that exalted position. You must not deviate until you assign this its true worth and stature, enrich your Karma, attain eligibility, and integrate it as a collective totality, much like oil permeating within. You must initiate such a life. You cannot achieve this except through a life that imbibes and assimilates its primordial and ultimate values, blending it into the purity of character like the oil that fills every sesame seed, and elevating it to a state of blessedness. Your Karma must be dedicated to that purpose.

[GV1:P1279] Understanding this, we must be able to fulfill Dharma, attain liberation through action (Karma Nivritti), and completely eradicate destruction in order to lead our lives to the realization of their ultimate goal. For this, God has given us intellect and a suitable nature. We have been provided with paths of action suitable for all states of health. The era of lacking food and clothing, and not knowing how to use them, has passed; today, having taught us how to refine and utilize food and clothing and how to lead our lives, God is guiding us towards a path that redirects our intellect toward spiritual contemplation and secures the right to the liberation of the soul. At that time, both punishment and protection will come equally from the same source. If one considers that as a hunt, the purpose will not be served. No practitioner of Karma who fails to understand that by accepting that punishment, they are embracing another spiritually fruitful action can achieve anything here. There is no meaning in your saying that you will accomplish everything through this Karma without understanding this.

[GV1:P1280] The aforementioned Yoga and the path of Dharma constitute a way of performing Karma with a sense of dedication, without abandoning adherence to righteousness. No one should utter even a single word aimed at destroying that path. If that happens, it will forever lead you to ruin. When you look at it, it might seem like a temporary deception or a betrayal. But it will manifest somewhere and emerge as a means of exhausting one's Karma (Karma Nivritti). That will harm you; you will also have to suffer. Therefore, instead of turning towards that destruction, you must work for the spiritual welfare of your life or soul.

[GV1:P1281] Therefore, you must conduct yourselves with at least the sense of dedication that our present actions, thoughts, and humility should all harmoniously blend together to build a better tomorrow, so that virtuous progeny, endowed with humility, purity of action, and constant vigilance, may emerge as a foundational support for the world. That should be your goal. Instead of idly talking about Vedanta and the like, wasting time without achieving the goal, leading a foolish life, and corrupting Karma, you must pray that our lineage is spared from such Sanyasa, Karma, or Yoga, or even any act resembling the nature of one fallen from Yoga (Yoga Bhrashta). You must pray for all good qualities and virtues to be present for all people yet to be born and the great souls yet to come, and perform your duties with the dedication that this goodness should benefit the world, the nation, each individual among us, and every blade of grass. Only then will we reach our intended destination.

[GV1:P1283] May 1983

[GV1:P1284] Our present endeavor is for the negative actions and positive actions to come together, leading to the destruction of the negative actions, and reflecting as positive actions through divine grace. For this endeavor, it is essential that we know certain things. Weighing the rights and wrongs that have come and gone here over time, we must consider whatever we have practiced, how that practice will reflect within us in the future, and how that reflection should benefit the land and the nation. We must first practice and understand that beneficial manner ourselves, and only after acquiring the capability to execute it without flaws will the world be able to accept it. Only if we conduct ourselves with this conviction can we bring it to reality. For this, we must believe that a foundational sense of duty, which ought to have been instilled in us, has indeed been instilled within us. The reason for this is that over many past periods, spiritual experiences occurred here without our knowledge. Through them, certain words and actions were imparted, and it is in the light of those words and actions that we conduct ourselves today. We received that word only after the complete operational capacity of this world was revealed to us. After revealing it, it was shown over several periods how rights and wrongs occurred in this manner, and what else remains for us to do. First, one thing is shown. Then, it will be shown in another aspect. Only after being shown in this manner multiple times have we been able to comprehend it in a systematic order.

[GV1:P1285] That systematic order, to our knowledge, is the Trinity (Trimurti) system—the one that exists among us and is known to us. In this Trinity system, what was first shown were the flaws that occurred in every action performed by the Shakta, Shaiva, and Vaishnava sects. We did not understand why these flawed aspects were being shown. Later, the positive aspects were also shown. It was shown in which era the application of this virtue was required. How did it come into operation? Why did it go wrong? At that time, a distant vision also emerged. It was the lineage of Manu that created the primordial operational capacity for all of this. Thus, it was realized that this lineage had been able to manage and bring it forward properly. Therefore, the lineage appears to have descended in a very worthy manner. It has come like a lineage that we cannot even imagine today. First, the birth of a Guru belonging to this lineage of Manu.

[GV1:P1286] The knowledge of it that has been imparted to us is that nine spheres were created through the power of that penance, and upon those nine spheres, twelve zodiac signs were created, and subsequently, through twenty-seven constellations, its karmic results were manifested. How far-sightedly it was managed for this purpose! What tremendous fruits of effort those great souls must have experienced for this! Today, there is no need for us to dwell on any of this. We are born in the result of that Karma. However, due to our own actions, certain flaws have befallen us.

[GV1:P1287] The flaw being referred to is that, initially, an unorganized path emerged in the lineage of Manu. The beginning implies that this occurred during the third Chaturyuga (four-age cycle) of the seventh Manu. The seventh Manu—according to the knowledge obtained from the Bhagavata and other sources—is named Vaivasvata Manu. It was in his third Chaturyuga that this error occurred. If one contemplates them, it becomes evident that everything happened through them. The wise men of that era, wherever they looked, could see that karma originated through them. Wherever one looks, only the lineage of Manu is visible. Manu himself has transformed into God. There was deep contemplation regarding this. Upon observation, it is seen that even the repetitive capacity of this sphere has manifested through them.

[GV1:P1288] What is that? They are the ones who performed the karma (actions). Thus, they possess authority over it. As they became the authorities of that karma, an arrogance inadvertently grew within them. It is something that happens to us as well. If we accomplish any small task, we tend to feel that we have achieved something monumental. This feeling can manifest in anyone—whether they are householders, ascetics, workers, yogis, wise men, or devotees.

[GV1:P1289] A devotee—when goodness is perceived in his perfected nature, he may think that he has attained near completeness. What might have occurred would merely be the manifestation of some minor deity or goddess. However, the matter he envisioned materialized. He could not see beyond that. We possess the familiarity of assuming that if a deity is manifested, everything is achieved. If, behind this, a situation arises involving Vedic authority or a state where even learning alphabets is forbidden, it leads further into wilderness. We have encountered many such experiences. Yet, no one knows the reason for pointing out the flaw in this lineage of Manu. That is why we remain ignorant about Manu. It has even been asked why others could not attain this knowledge. The reason is that over many periods and many births—when we say many periods and births, one birth might occur four or five times in a single yuga. Thus, they were born, raised, and died across countless yugas. It is said that the karmic potential within this remained confined to this soul. The prolonged activity of this soul was in a state of doing what is instructed and doing nothing beyond that. There are many such great souls. But they are brought forth only as needed. By divine will, that soul has been set aside and kept at a distance. They were given what was necessary. That falls under God's necessity and duty. Whether we call it God or Brahman, assign it any name. If it brings forth such a specific creation, there is a forethought to it. That forethought is what has transpired. This is one such soul within it. It was stated that it has been brought forth according to my intention, and it will function solely according to my intention. Therefore, the karma occurring according to this intention is not ours, but God's. So, this was merely explained to us. It did not come through our own realization. It was indeed completed over several eras. When asked in which eras this error occurred, it was in Manu's third Chaturyuga—the third Chaturyuga of Vaivasvata Manu—that this error emerged. They became arrogant with the notion of 'I'. Why did such arrogance arise? That course of karma is observed in these spheres. That course of karma is seen in the zodiac signs. That course of karma is evident in the twenty-seven stars. No human can be born outside those stars. Not even a blade of grass can sprout. Then this karma becomes theirs. The consequences of the karmic power seen in it, whether good or bad, will be seen as their own. Then whom should they respect?

[GV1:P1290] This is how an ascetic felt the urge to proclaim "Aham Brahmasmi" (I am Brahman). The capability to assert "I am Brahman" spontaneously developed within them. However, it is flawed; one should not declare oneself to be Brahman. From that point, this lineage of Manu shifted entirely. Yet, they forgot the matters concerning Manu himself. It is said that having forgotten, three more Chaturyugas merely passed in such narrations—the people existed aimlessly. Again, in the seventh Chaturyuga, the Trimurti system emerged. They too examined these texts, completely altered the lineage of Manu, and established the Trimurti system by strengthening it. Thus, all calculations were converted into those of Brahma, Vishnu, and Maheshwara. By only changing the calculations, they established that all creation occurs through this. However, there is a divine resolve for this to happen. When this emerged, their preference shifted toward the state of comfort. The position of a deity is exceedingly comfortable. The Trimurti system is celebrated by them with great joy. But it exists only up to the realm of the Devas (Devaloka). This group did not, nor do they, make an effort capable of proceeding beyond that to the realm of Brahman (Brahmaloka). This was fulfilled by this Trimurti system itself. Or rather, reaching the divine presence was accomplished by the eleventh Chaturyuga. It is stated that a Chaturyuga comprises twelve thousand divine years. How many of our years would these twelve thousand divine years amount to? That is, one divine year equals three hundred and sixty-five of our years. Such twelve thousand divine years make one Chaturyuga. Thus, it was completed from the seventh to the eleventh Chaturyuga. That is to say, this Trimurti system—observe the extent of preparations made during this period, fulfilling the lineage of Manu or the lineage of the Trimurtis according to that Brahmic resolve. Consequently, their specific course of karma emerged; the karmic course of the Trimurtis.

[GV1:P1292] June 1983

[GV1:P1293] When brought up to the Chaturyuga, they do not move forward. They learn from the stories written thus far up to the heavenly realm (Swargaloka), celebrate that alone, walk exactly through that, and will not change. From that day onwards, for God or for Brahman, a lineage must emerge again in accordance with that Brahmic resolve. But how will it come to be? Only those born and raised here with intelligence and capability will reach this path. When moving along this path, those standing on the route taken by their ancestors can only proceed by looking at the concepts written down as yoga, karma, jnana, and bhakti. Thus, one's time will pass simply by studying the manifestation of a deity or their mantric and tantric instruments. He will not be able to advance beyond that. After this, another person attempts the journey, and his situation remains the same. It is said that many such instances were observed. Therefore, the time and state capable of stirring and clarifying this will arrive only in the Kali Yuga. This is because everything else has transpired according to destiny. Denying that, the Kali Yuga is an era where all of these can be suppressed, activated, and united into one. For this purpose, Kali is chosen repeatedly. In such a Kali Yuga, numerous such great souls appeared. That is why some great souls have mentioned in the Puranas and elsewhere: "I must take a birth in the Kali Yuga just to witness the manifestation of Kali, and the Lord must permit it."

[GV1:P1294] What is this Kali—do they not know it? They do know. It is because they are experiencing it. That is the essence of what was said. Thus, many of them took birth in our present Kali Yuga itself. An example of this is the vision Suma received at the ashram in Kallar. A lotus was shown with two thousand four hundred and forty-four petals; when asked how it was counted, it was explained—each petal fell off one by one. When asked what they were, it was said that each represented a Mahatma (great soul). Nothing else was said. It stopped at that much on that day. The following year, an explanation for this was given here. Until then, each event had been unfolding. I am summarizing it. Giving the explanation, it was stated that the Mahatmas seen that day are to take birth and work within our lineage. The first Mahatmas were unable to function within it. They went and referred to the ancient texts. If one refers to those texts, they would revert to the old ways. Because of such an error, it is said that many were born without knowledge, wealth, or enlightenment. Examples of this are Parayi Petta Panthirukulam, Jesus, and the Prophet. Everything they have said in this manner is completely the opposite. They have spoken contrary to these Trimurtis (the Trinity). We did not have the practice to examine what this was. When we take the old texts, we go back into that. That is not needed. Gunangudi Masthan, who came in recent times, had asked, "Will a planted stone speak?" Though various great souls came and spoke for us, we lacked the wisdom to grasp it. However, apart from these Trimurti traditions, because the two great figures who appeared in Western countries came as prophets in a minor capacity and conveyed the exact words they received, they gained significant prominence. They came and ruled here as well. Both these groups ruled our India, which is known as a spiritual nation. Yet, our religious consciousness did not even allow us to ponder the reason why those ordinary people came here and did all this.

[GV1:P1295] Looking at it from this perspective, from how far away we have received this! These two thousand four hundred and forty-four Mahatmas are yet to come and function. This is the first lineage of its kind. You will not find any other familiarity to recover for this. We cannot learn it by looking into those ancient texts. The texts are flawed. These are texts that have originated from prior experiences. It is in this context that ascetics had to employ occult powers (siddhis). Ascetics should not use occult powers. If they do, they will incur their own karma. If they function with humility for the public good and spiritual purity, the weight of their karmic progression should naturally transfer to the life forces merged in the world or the atmosphere, leading them to that ultimate goal. This must be their karma. That has been our principle since ancient times. But having been caught up in this—under this deity—by giving the deity the right to do many things, who knows what that deity has done! It is said that by standing as a god to humans, they would exhibit many mischievous deeds. That was given from Brahman. To remove that, after making a mistake themselves, they must realize it, act again to rectify that error, and humans must rise above the deity. That is the true karma. What we have been told today is a part of such karma. How should that come about?

[GV1:P1296] Certain aspects of your past lives and the devotion you practiced with dedication during those times will merge within your life, bringing about certain feelings and changes. But if you wish to act with a sense of dedication toward the Guru, you must remove the latent tendencies (vasanas) before you. You have a tendency to rationalize and speak without dedication. You do not possess the consciousness to do anything on your own. Yet, you will act upon it bearing witness to your past experiences. If we proceed like this, what will happen to us? We are not to merely quote an ancient text and move on. However, this does not mean we should completely avoid mentioning the texts. What we have to learn from them is this—there have been many errors and many correct actions in the karmic path of the world. What is the reason for this? The karma of a Sage (Rishi) and the karma of the Wise (Jnani)—here, the Rishi and the Jnani have arrived at the same karma. But what distinguishes the Rishi? They have functioned across various levels. If we do not understand the karma of the Rishi, we might think, "Someone else did this in that position, so we can do it too." But we are not of that lineage; that lineage has committed many errors. If we undertake that karma, we will incur harm from it. Therefore, we should not practice it. Moreover, a complete karma intended for our own lineage has not yet come into this. Now, we have a karmic path that we must perform ourselves and fulfill for tomorrow. How will we take it up? We have no experience, no capability, no wisdom—then what is it? It is an acceptance. Without violating that acceptance—we have been taught that "the word is truth." We must believe the word of a great soul. When we apply, understand, and act upon that word, it will become the truth. Then we will feel a deeper reverence. It transforms into the Guru, then into truth, and then into God. Thus, the Guru transforms into God and into Brahman. This is the karmic path we are meant to practice. Now, rather than standing apart as individuals, if you were all born together in this atmosphere, everyone has a rightful share in this karmic progression. It is said that even if we are born as a blade of grass, it is part of this karmic progression. So, what must we, who are bound by this karmic progression, practice and realize? What are the errors pointed out in this? The Guru may commit that error. Only then can that error be rectified. Everyone has committed errors. One progresses by working through those errors. Otherwise, if you operate solely through correctness, you will have to flee when you encounter the operational capacity of both right and wrong combined. Think of the blunders the Guru who first bore this has committed in their life! After returning from a long period of making mistakes, they instruct you, "Do this." When a mistake occurs after doing it, they correct it by saying, "You must do that only after doing this"—do it. It is by believing the word in this manner that they have become Rishis. Then you must accept the word the Rishi speaks. They know that if this is not done in a particular area, this person's karma will not be resolved. They will make you do it. Performing that karma, they might wander and struggle, and perhaps their very life will be thrown into turmoil. It will feel as if the life they had built up to that point is completely battered, like beating clothes on a rock in the water until everything falls apart, when experiencing this beating. This beating is meant to remove the fish bones and impurities stuck to it. They will batter it away just like that. They will wash and straighten out life, but they will not let it tear apart. Even if it tears somewhere, it will be stitched back together. Whatever flaws exist in human life are what get washed. It is washed using the words of the Guru. You might think, "The Guru made me do a mistake." He does not know what this mistake is. He cannot be rectified without this washing. Everyone says, "I was made to perform the wrong karma; I was not given the most correct karma to perform." It cannot happen any other way. He must first err. He must learn from this error. Otherwise, the karmic trajectory within him must be eradicated through that error. Then, the mistakes of the karmas he committed in his previous births will be resolved when he performs this. Once this is accomplished, he will either be guided forward, or he will walk forward on his own.

[GV1:P1298] July 1983

[GV1:P1299] Some people will come here and ask if they can do something according to their own ideas. I will say, do it if you can. The Guru should only think that much. They themselves must observe and state that it has such and such flaws. God has bestowed them with intelligence as well. They should reflect on it a little. They must become capable of correcting it themselves. That is why they are made to do this. Is it enough to simply sit with folded hands claiming one is obeying words? If someone is told to go and dig, they won't be instructed to dig only in this specific square or at this specific mark. They must clear the area and cultivate it themselves. If something is lacking, they will only be advised occasionally to do it in a certain way. They must do it themselves and gain experience. Consider any profession in the same way. Suppose someone is studying medicine now. A procedure will be demonstrated once. Then they have to perform it using their own reasoning. Look at weaving itself. Each person must rectify their own shortcomings. Similarly with cooking. They will learn to prepare another dish on their own. All these are mastered through practice over time. Likewise, when we take up something new, our own karma (action) must come into play. We must observe where the trajectory of karma, undertaken with the four aspects of karma, yoga, jnana, and bhakti, is applicable in the gross, the subtle, the effect, and the cause. This exists even in the demonic realm. If a sanyasi insists that he will only travel in pure places or sleep only in odorless places, he will attain none of this. While in the avadhuta state, sanyasis wander and travel in this manner. They will sleep wherever they find a spot. Sometimes it will be in a cemetery. Sometimes in a drain. It could be on a shop verandah, on the seashore, or under a tree. Sometimes in various temples. Resting here and there, he is taking upon himself his karma. It is by completing such a course of karma that they return as a yogi.

[GV1:P1300] That course of karma is necessary for both men and women. It is not sufficient if only one person completes it. Thus, a two-fold course of karma—a course of karma where man and woman can work together—must be completed. The course of karma from a small child to one hundred and twenty-five years of age, completed in each lifetime, is entirely discovered through the subtle power of the Guru; by studying its nature and understanding in what manner they should be guided to perform karma, conversely, each individual must be corrected by assigning them different kinds of karma. But one may ask, aren't they all human beings? What one person does is not what another does. Thus, it is pervasive in the total karma of the world. It is infused as vasana (latent tendency) like oil in sesame seeds. To activate this—the dryness of a sesame seed is not that of a coconut, the dryness of a coconut is not that of a marotti seed; thus, if you observe the nature of the oil, there are manifold kinds of karma within it. That oil must be extracted, right? Then one must know how to apply it. You must be able to integrate such things into your life through karma. At the same time, it can be washed and purified through that karma. The completion of karma and washing it pure can occur simultaneously. We ourselves lay the foundation for what is past, what exists today, and what is yet to come. Humans should repeatedly perform such a course of karma. Only then can we offer it as our own. That is why it is advised not to falter when you do something. Those with profound vision have understood this. Jesus is the greatest figure in terms of sacrifice. Not in terms of state. Of all who have descended to this earth to date, Jesus is the one observed with the most profound sacrifice and love.

[GV1:P1301] Question: (To the children with vision) What did Jesus tell

[GV1:P1302] you?

[GV1:P1303] Answer: Children, he said with tears in his eyes that you should not make mistakes.

[GV1:P1304] He said that this is the greatest fortune.

[GV1:P1305] Question: What did Vivekananda say?

[GV1:P1306] Answer: I did not have the fortune to find such a Guru.

[GV1:P1307] If I had received such an opportunity, I would have conquered the world and offered it at the Guru's feet.

[GV1:P1308] Guru: Thus, these three have received it in three different

[GV1:P1309] ways. Until now, it has not been possible for various Mahatmas to arrive and establish such a Guru lineage.

[GV1:P1310] Question: Has any Mahatma or Guru portrayed this

[GV1:P1311] incorrectly?

[GV1:P1312] Answer: No.

[GV1:P1313] Question: Approximately how many Gurus will appear?

[GV1:P1314] Answer: Thousands of Gurus have been seen.

[GV1:P1315] Guru: Not merely one or two Gurus. For us, the existence of the Devas is not just a myth.

[GV1:P1316] Crores of Devas can be witnessed. What do we comprehend from this? (To an experienced householder disciple) Tell us what you witnessed when you visited Guruvayur. (He was previously a non-believer).

[GV1:P1317] Householder Disciple: Standing in Guruvayur gazing at the idol, during the worship

[GV1:P1318] I saw Guruvayurappan in the form of the Guru.

[GV1:P1319] Guru: You saw the Guru there, didn't you? If you see the Guru in Krishna's idol,

[GV1:P1320] what would you infer? Or if you perceive Krishna in the Guru's heart, what should you infer?

[GV1:P1321] Householder Disciple: I was able to perceive that divine consciousness, worshipped even by Krishna, in the form of the Guru.

[GV1:P1322] Guru: Arjuna had lived with Krishna for fifty years. Sometimes, Arjuna was even convinced that he and the Guru had taken numerous births together prior to this. Yet, he was unable to act with firm resolve until then. He faltered at the moment of the war. How could he kill all of them, bound by human reasoning? "I cannot kill!" he said. But Krishna insisted that he must. Despite being told repeatedly, he refused to comply. Then, he was asked to reflect and comprehend it. Such a directive can only be given to someone who already possessed vision. He was asked to look into the purpose of his arrival. He looked. Then, he grasped the reason for his existence. He asked no further questions. He immediately bowed in reverence and commenced the war. Despite possessing so much familiarity and knowledge, he was unable to understand and act initially. Living as contemporaries carries such a limitation. It can happen to anyone. After all, they eat, sleep, play, and laugh together. Consequently, the true nature of this was understood only later. Once he understood, he acted. Meanwhile, the *Gita* is narrated through Sanjaya. Because Dhritarashtra was blind, Sanjaya described it to him through divine vision. It is said that Sage Agastya himself went and advised him, "You must not do this. Do not send them to war; everything will be destroyed." When he did not comply, he was told, "See for yourself—I shall grant you vision." This implies bestowing wisdom. "Acquire it. You can witness your own birth, Krishna's birth, Duryodhana's birth, and so on. Upon seeing that, appoint them for this," he said. However, Dhritarashtra declined it. "Then listen to this; this young boy will tell you," Krishna stated. Thus, with Sanjaya seated beside him, the events of the battlefield were narrated. This is what the *Gita* refers to as *Sanjaya Uvacha* (Sanjaya said). It is only after all these events unfolded that the purpose of Krishna's arrival, the arrival of the hundred men (Kauravas), and Arjuna's arrival were understood. But there is no point in discussing it after the fact. If the people had understood it then, this war and these events would not have been necessary. Why was such a situation created? It is for us to study history. Causing such a great soul to be born among the Shudras was intended to bring the era of the Shudra to the forefront. Is it not evident that this endeavor has been ongoing since the time of Krishna? Even before the onset of the Kali Yuga, a Guru was brought forth and provided. This recurring history was explained in detail through two individuals. By causing Krishna and Arjuna to be born as mediums, that entire karmic process was brought to light. There is an instance where Arjuna, an individual capable of anything, ultimately failed. Arjuna inquired of Krishna why that was so. It marked the beginning of Kali. Stating, "Let us now embrace renunciation (*Sannyasa*)," Krishna and his lineage renounced the world. This is history. The trajectory of karma up to that point was demonstrated. Once Kali begins, neither the deity nor the Guru of the previous eras holds a place. That is the essence of *Sambhavami Yuge Yuge* (I manifest from age to age). To bring this karmic trajectory to the forefront, every aspect concerning Krishna will be visible until the end of this Kali era. It has been demonstrated how Krishna arrived and functioned, and how the Guru arrived and functioned. Yet, the tragedy is that we fail to understand. Ultimately, didn't Krishna himself have to instruct him to realize who he was? It is by guiding us in this manner that everything has been accomplished. Kali began. It has been proven once again that whatever actions one performs in any birth, there are consequences to be faced. Krishna, seated beneath a tree in the forest, was shot and killed by a hunter's arrow. Whosoever it may be, the accumulated course of karma must be experienced and exhausted. It was proven that no matter how many births one takes, this consequence will follow. It is said that his body was consumed in the fire of yoga (*Yogagni*). Even such a great soul could not alter his own karmic trajectory. What multitude of such karmic trajectories must reside within you! This is why it is advised not to apply your mere intellect to this; if the intellect is not aligned with the good and applied, it will lead to errors. You must not employ your own logic or the logic of the state. This is highly perilous. The democracy seen today will plunge you into chaos. It is neither of these; rather, by attributing supreme greatness to the Guru's word, you must harmonize yourself with that greatness, act, and transform into it. That is the profound familiarity known as Guru and disciple.

[GV1:P1323] Guruvani

[GV1:P1324] Birthday Message

[GV1:P1325] September 1983

[GV1:P1326] The world today is engaged in a conflict without a clear adversary. Knowledge battles knowledge, wealth battles wealth, and authority battles authority. It is everyone's belief that this struggle is for the sake of progress. Today, this phenomenon is most prominently observed in India. Gradually, this conflict is escalating to the extent of a father against his son, a son against his father, and a mother against her daughter. The assumption is that this is done with pure intentions.

[GV1:P1327] The *Puranas*, epics, and religious scholars document that this phenomenon is not confined to the present day but existed in previous epochs (*Yugas*) as well. Among religious scholars, both those with spiritual experience and those without have engaged in this equally. Experience, in this context, refers to divine experience. There are also experiences rooted in faith and those rooted in action (*Karma*). Upon comprehensive examination, it becomes apparent that they have acted in a manner that makes everything appear correct. What remains incomprehensible is the ultimate objective they seek to conquer. What is it that they intend to sustain? It can be observed that they have upheld truth, righteousness (*Dharma*), kindness, and compassion to the best of their respective understanding. Those who have operated at the forefront of this endeavor are the Gurus, prophets, and scholars. Following them are the adherents of the four paths: *Yoga*, *Karma*, *Bhakti* (devotion), and *Jnana* (knowledge). There is no one who operates outside these four paradigms. A question may then arise: why specifically highlight the followers of these four paths? The answer is that each one of us is encompassed within these four paths. However, the majority of the populace remains ignorant of the true nature of their actions.

[GV1:P1328] It was mentioned earlier that this dynamic existed in preceding epochs as well. However, the majority have failed to comprehend that these occurrences manifested during the transitional phases—the conclusion of one epoch and the commencement of another. Driven by a universal desire for transformation, they implemented their ideologies. Today, those transformations have fully materialized. It must be deduced that they lacked the foresight to precisely delineate how one ought to function until a specific period. We continue to operate today in the same manner as previous epochs did. Yet, a doubt arises as to whether due consideration has been given to the specific requirements of the current epoch. Indeed, it is no longer a mere doubt but an established reality. There is no need to look far for evidence. Individuals are actively manifesting this within their respective spheres of action and reveling in it.

[GV1:P1329] This is rooted in the premise that India stands at the vanguard of action (*Karma*) and righteousness (*Dharma*). A resolute dedication to action, functioning upon this foundation, has flourished here. Concepts such as religious tolerance, alongside all analogous principles, are encompassed within this. However, a profound ignorance regarding when, where, and how to apply these principles has afflicted all our adherents. Furthermore, it is India that finds itself entirely incapable of eradicating this ignorance. It is not difficult to deduce that other nations have managed to overcome this to some extent, aided by the grace of certain prophets and various astute intellects. This is because, within the framework of the Trinity (*Trimurti*), the *Shakta*, the *Shaiva*, and the *Vaishnava* traditions are each regarded as paramount within Hindu *Dharma*. None is deemed inferior to the others. Furthermore, they have all invariably remembered to strive toward the realization of non-duality (*Advaita*). In this pursuit, both the learned scholars and the unlettered masses demonstrate equal proficiency.

[GV1:P1330] Why does such a situation arise? The adherents of the Gurus from those respective eras constitute the grave underlying context that has plagued India. There is a vociferous, collective demand that this paradigm must be altered. Yet, no one possesses the slightest comprehension of what should replace it. Because each *Shaiva* and *Shakta* faction has introduced its own particular dogmatism, individuals have consequently become entrenched in their respective ideological trenches. The fundamental conviction of those traversing these paths seems to be merely collecting and showcasing the stones, thorns, and sheer disorientation they encounter within those trenches.

[GV1:P1331] However, remaining detached from all of this, without anyone to forge, open, or facilitate a path for them, there exists a group of people who simply wandered arbitrarily along their course. They constitute the Shudra class. For generations, they have been bereft of the knowledge required for their own upliftment. Yet, this Shudra class remains oblivious to the fact that this is an era in which the Divine is bestowing grace upon them. Kerala serves as a definitive illustration of this phenomenon. In Kerala, up until a certain historical juncture, even the monarch belonged to the Shudra class. Historical records attest that the administration of Marthanda Varma and his successors, as well as the preceding reign of Cheraman Perumal, transpired here. Similarly, evidence indicates that individuals belonging to this Shudra class exercised sovereignty across various regions of India. The fisherwoman referenced in the narrative of Sri Ramakrishna has been historically substantiated as a woman of royal lineage. The undeniable truth, however, is that we have failed to unequivocally comprehend and articulate these historical realities.

[GV1:P1332] It is worth reflecting that although many Gurus emerged in India, their followers were unable to practice, sustain, or even preserve a single word of their teachings. Here, the Shaiva, Shakta, and Vaishnava traditions have never failed to shower accusations like a volley of arrows on the Gurus who spoke the truth and on their followers. Caught in this trap, it is usual for these Gurus and their followers to drown over time.

[GV1:P1333] To some extent, it is the Westerners and the Arabs who have escaped from this. However, their time has also passed. It is good that they are also thinking in tune with the times. A great opportunity has arrived for the people of India as a whole to think in accordance with the times. Although we received such opportunities many times in the past, we were unable to bear them. At least now, we must be able to bear it and spread it to the world. This should be our determination. We must reflect deeply on why Buddhism had to be exiled from here and how we should utilize that lesson. Similarly, the Parayi Petta Panthirukulam has proven its steadfastness in action. Basaveshwara, who came in the recent past, was a steadfast man of action despite being a Shaivite. So was Narayana Guru.

[GV1:P1334] All these are being twisted and taken back to the Shakta, Shaiva, and Vaishnava traditions. We are unable to accept any matters suitable for the times. There is evidence that the aforementioned three forms of worship were practiced all over the world. The sacrificial altar which prides itself as self-existent ٹ that is, during the time of Moses, when he saved everyone, helped them cross the river, and taught them everything, among that, when he asked his followers to raise their hands, it became clear that one person could only raise it below the elbow. This was precisely because the face of a bull was held under the armpit. It is seen from the story that he cursed them on that day.

[GV1:P1335] Whatever it may be, what we have gained today from Indian stories is a lot of blessings and curses from gods and goddesses. Today, every person who practices Shakta, Shaiva, and Vaishnava as the right path has become a slave and a yes-man to those who accepted a prophet, yet they have not forgotten to claim that Advaita is supreme. Belonging to a tradition that is unable to think up to the level of cause and effect and take what is needed, and being under the Gurus who act proudly as followers of an assembly of scholars, we are still falling into the same old trench today. Out of lack of prior experience, and because governance and education were far away from them, the Shudras, who flew across freely like birds—neither human nor animal—and walked without digging pits where it lay open, had to accept the slavery of the Western and Eastern intellectuals in the work they did by pretending to be upper caste with what they got. Those eloquent speakers who talk about the universe-embracing Advaita, who belong to both the lower and upper castes and have no hesitation in saying that Dharma has decayed and Adharma is being practiced, are yearning for the dress and language of the white man.

[GV1:P1336] To transform this situation, let us all forget the discriminatory mindset of being a Shakta, a Shaiva, or a Vaishnava, forget religious hatred, and find out the easiest way to accomplish what we need to do in the Dharma of this age called Kali. For this, let the existing wise men*, scholars, religious leaders, and the intellectuals in today's political rat race, without bargaining with each other, think if there is anything we can do in the Dharma of Kali. I use this auspicious day to wish for an opportunity to think and make others think in a way that is useful to all the people of the world, that this twentieth century or the followers of the Gurus who lived then have contributed, as the first step of this Kalidharma, by combining action and righteousness and bearing witness in that compassionate Brahman.

[GV1:P1337] *Those who have the inner eye of wisdom by the grace of God.

[GV1:P1343] October 1983

[GV1:P1344] How have we brought about the value of human life? We have been entrusted with the task of correcting this value from the wrong path and bringing it back to the right path. First, we must learn how to perform this duty. That is what was meant earlier when it was said that we are starting at the very beginning. What has been done now is the beginning of every part. You must not make mistakes in such a beginning. If a mistake is made, it will also become subject to divine punishment.

[GV1:P1345] You are merely rolling things around in your intellect without understanding any of this. Intellect should not be used in such a manner. Mistakes will occur. Whether right or wrong, things must be reported to the Guru exactly as they are. It was mentioned earlier that the Guru might even ask one to commit a mistake. Why is this so? To dislodge a karma that has become firmly rooted through errors, the disciple himself must be made to commit a mistake. For this purpose, the Guru, knowingly or unknowingly, may utter a word that leads to that mistake. Then the disciple will be shaken, thinking, "Alas! I have done this," and subsequently correct it by reversing the action. For instance, it is like something revolving from one to another. What if one fails to rotate? Both (right and wrong) must inevitably rotate.

[GV1:P1346] You should at least understand this much before initiating the karma. Otherwise, the karma will not be perfected. There are those who argue, "That is wrong; if he is a Guru, would he do such a thing or make someone do it?" It is unknown what knowledge prompts them to speak in this manner. Their understanding remains at such a rudimentary level. The objective is to teach the disciple the subtle aspects of the committed error and the reasons behind its occurrence, thereby correcting him. Only then does he attain perfection in it.

[GV1:P1347] What we require today is to identify where our karma has gone wrong, where our ancestors have erred, and what must be done to prevent future generations from making mistakes—these constitute our objectives. When correcting the mistakes that have occurred in karma, we must endure significant hardships. Thus, the karma is redirected into an entirely different course.

[GV1:P1348] It is impossible not to make mistakes; errors will happen. Only if a mistake occurs in karma can it be corrected. Therefore, there is no need to fear when a mistake happens. However, one should not intentionally commit errors. It does not mean that since mistakes do not matter, one can allow them to happen. If there is even the slightest speck of doubt in our conscious mind, we must halt right there. Further action should only be taken after seeking clarification. Otherwise, it will lead to an error, necessitating a backward journey to rectify it. That situation should be avoided.

[GV1:P1349] When we examine the lives of Vyasa, Vasishta, and Viswamitra, we observe that they committed numerous mistakes and subsequently corrected them. Countless errors can be seen in their lives. Why has this been demonstrated? Could they not have proceeded without making mistakes? If we consider all the Gurus, we can observe this pattern. Therefore, understanding this, we must purify our karma. In this manner, we must advance by questioning, discussing, and acting upon every single aspect. This is what we are required to do now.

GURUVANIKAL · November & December 1983 · Volume 1
Malayalam source paragraphs GV1:P1351 to GV1:P1365

[GV1:P1351] November & December 1983

[GV1:P1352] When we begin to learn and teach each aspect of our lives for the first time, we must comprehend its inherent difficulties through experience or through life itself. When it is said that one must know through life, it implies that knowledge is essential for our individual lives or for the existence of every subject.

[GV1:P1353] In today's circumstances, where everything is available, we forget even to contemplate the state of the era when people did not know how to cook food or weave clothes. Initially starting with leaves, they progressed to tree bark, and subsequently invented clothing. How much hardship and sacrifice must have been behind the invention of alphabets and medicines for diseases! In the beginning, humanity suffered from diseases for an extended period before discovering medicinal remedies. Countless lives must have been lost in the process of testing them. Even today, the discovery of medicines continues. In this manner, we continue to discover various things.

[GV1:P1354] From that time until today, as each new development emerges, we refine it under the guise of 'modernization'. Thus, using our intellect, we prepare whatever is necessary for this life in myriad ways. If we reflect upon the aforementioned hardships, everything we witness today is the culmination of immense suffering endured in the past. Similarly, we initiated practices of worship. In the beginning, we possessed no such knowledge. Thunder, lightning, rain, the sun, the moon, and the stars were all marvels to the people of that era. This gradual sense of wonder transformed into worship, and eventually, the concept of God unknowingly permeated human consciousness.

[GV1:P1355] Primarily, all living beings desire food. Following that comes the need for clothing, and then the management of bodily pain and diseases—surpassing each of these stages, we have now arrived at the era of nuclear science. Science will undoubtedly make many more discoveries. However, all of these are merely for material existence. Similarly, a substantial effort is required to cultivate our inner consciousness. Beyond all these factors, there is a profound element behind humanity acquiring such capabilities and intellect. We must recognize that.

[GV1:P1356] An unseen regulatory power is controlling not just us, but the entire universe. After contemplating this for ages, intellectual individuals began to worship it in a manner that seemed appropriate to them at the time. Subsequently, guided by their prevailing intellect, they might have retreated to isolated places and engaged in practices akin to penance or meditation. This could have been performed on a seashore, beneath a tree, on a mountain, or in any solitary location they could find. Later, they practiced this in various forms, such as collective hymns, songs, and chants.

[GV1:P1357] Among those who practiced in this manner, certain great souls began to have specific experiences. They reported seeing a particular color, a flash of lightning, a circular light in a certain location, a beam of light resembling that from a torch, or a radiance akin to the rising sun or moon. Such experiences have been described in various ways. Following these visions, they repeatedly beheld a human form.

[GV1:P1358] Attributing various interpretations and characteristics to that human form, they progressively taught society to worship and promote worship in its current state. When referring to the current state, idol worship holds primary significance. There are those who argue that there is no substance in this, claiming it is merely an entanglement rooted in human thought processes. Be that as it may. Regardless, we must entrust someone as a witness for every painful circumstance we endure.

[GV1:P1359] During childhood, parents are the most significant figures. As individuals mature, they develop the understanding that there are figures greater than their parents in the world. As more time passes, they realize the existence of a governing authority above them, and ultimately, a God who transcends everything. Consequently, as we undertake various practices to comprehend the glory of this God, we may receive revelations in forms other than the previously mentioned luminous apparitions. Certain great souls possess words of correction for this. It is through such processes that we too have been corrected and guided.

[GV1:P1360] Evaluating each of these aspects, we do not have to suffer even a fraction of the hardships endured by our predecessors. Considering the magnitude of their sacrifices, they suffered immensely on our behalf. However, we have lacked the vision or the conscious effort to evaluate and appreciate these contributions. Nor are we developing such an awareness. Perhaps a few individuals might be doing so, and society reaps the benefits. Thus, when we examine every matter, it becomes evident that we must fulfill our individual roles as well as the roles of every individual within our society.

[GV1:P1361] This knowledge consists of understanding what we must do in this regard. Every branch of knowledge must be practiced, experienced, and understood; its deficiencies must be eliminated, and it must be demonstrated—as an individual—in a manner that is beneficial and accessible to humanity. For this, a person is required. You may call him a Guru or by any other name. The nomenclature does not matter. It is sufficient that we acquire the knowledge.

[GV1:P1362] Ever since the inception of the world, humanity has possessed this spirit of inquiry. Within this realm of inquiry, there are those who remain completely ignorant. Furthermore, there are individuals incapable of acting with the requisite knowledge for it. Such an ability is inherently attained only through birth. For instance, a plant grows and blossoms solely because it possesses life. Subsequently, that life-force transitions into various other organisms, then evolves into reptiles and animals, ultimately culminating in the human form. Humans thus acquired intellect and cognitive discernment. We have progressed to our current state through the harmonious interplay of this intellectual brilliance and inherent tendencies.

[GV1:P1363] We must believe that all this is either a divine play or the glory of God meant to be revealed to us. Understanding this, why have we gathered here today? What is our duty? Who should we become tomorrow? Our ancestors are the ones who provided each of us with the guidance to contemplate such questions and pursue that path of inquiry. What is the era we are living in now? Our current quest is to determine how to proceed in accordance with these times. The present era is *Kali Yuga*. Prior to this, three eras—*Satya Yuga*, *Treta Yuga*, and *Dvapara Yuga*—have passed. It is the knowledge that existed in the *Treta Yuga* that we have been slowly unearthing and comprehending piece by piece. When *Dvapara Yuga* arrived, it evolved into a state of knowledge where we could explicitly experience it and facilitate its experience for others. In *Kali Yuga*, the knowledge we must henceforth apply and realize is that which allows us to discern its right and wrong, thereby embarking once again towards the *Satya Yuga*. We must be endowed with the fortune and knowledge that amalgamate the residual wisdom of the Gurus who appeared across various epochs with the divine grace that illuminates through our present endeavors.

[GV1:P1364] Does everyone attain this fortune? No. Divine grace exists, but that specific fortune is not always received. Today, it is said that Westerners are at the forefront of discoveries. Yet, wherever one goes in their lands, one can find both the ignorant and the knowledgeable. Refined knowledge exists everywhere and at all times. However, the reason for all this, as stated by our religious followers or spiritual Gurus, is that what has presently manifested is the innate derivation of that life-force, shaped by the accumulated *karmic* tendencies of one's birth and upbringing. It is this life-force that operates in such a manner within our bodies. This is precisely why the true nature of that divine grace cannot be fully comprehended. Nevertheless, there are indeed those who fully comprehend it and act upon that realization; we currently fall into this latter category.

[GV1:P1365] Guru Vani

GURUVANIKAL · January & February 1984 · Volume 1
Malayalam source paragraphs GV1:P1366 to GV1:P1386

[GV1:P1366] January & February 1984

[GV1:P1367] In the primordial era of ignorance, humanity acted in a beastly and demonic manner, appropriate to those times. That state has evolved, and today it has reached the visible position of *Dharma* (righteousness). The current condition in *Kali Yuga* is one where an individual contemplates the nature of this luminous entity rooted in philosophical discipline, and wonders how to integrate oneself into it. This state is replete with all attributes. The world functions perpetually in such a way that both good and evil are thoroughly churned and clarified, enabling us to extract its ultimate essence.

[GV1:P1368] The endeavor is to imbue ourselves with this functional capacity, impart it to our children, and elevate it traditionally through generations. God reveals this to us so that it may operate in the most optimal manner. How does this occur? For instance, various imaginations and perceptions spontaneously arise in our minds without our conscious knowledge. When terms like *Bhakti* (devotion), *Yoga*, *Jnana* (knowledge), or *Karma* (action) are mentioned, a corresponding imagery forms in the mind. Little children have a specific perception when they see their father, whereas adults have a different one. The same applies when seeing a mother. Thus, the perception towards individual persons varies uniquely among different people. Similarly, a painter and a singer possess distinct forms of imagination. How did this imagination emerge in the human mind? The imagery that arises corresponds to each individual's inherent tendencies (*vasana*). It is the intrinsic inclination of one's own life-force. What happens is the continuous amplification of this tendency. It is a profound secret residing within us, often without our awareness.

[GV1:P1369] Consequently, various forms of perceptions arise—similarly, a specific disposition is developed towards God. After contemplating various matters in the mind, the perception that ultimately reaches us is an amalgamation of beauty, humility, truth, tolerance, and merit. It emerges spontaneously from within ourselves. This is an assimilation intrinsic to the evolutionary nature of the mind. It can only be realized through experience and cannot be adequately expressed through words.

[GV1:P1370] *Bhakti* (devotion) is a dimension akin to a magnificent mountain of love. It is fundamentally a path of love. That love is the perception of a profound glory in everything one beholds. It is a state of mind where an involuntary reverence for all things emerges from within us. Children naturally develop an affinity for toys or tasty items. As age advances, this affection undergoes a twofold transformation: one aligns with earnestness and dutiful action (*karma*), and the other with emotionality. This is something each of you has experientially realized. However, it is impossible to articulate exactly how this transpires.

[GV1:P1371] Through these continuous transformations, it is only when we encounter a great soul—or a philosophical thought associated with them—in whom the underlying realities of humility, truth, and sacrifice function in perfect unison, that we comprehend the true weight of this devotion. It is an exceedingly magnificent glory. We are currently situated within it. Standing in this position, our reflection should be: 'I must integrate this into my life-force, cultivate it incrementally, and act in a manner that benefits my colleagues, home, society, and nation.' Some individuals observe, understand, and merely move on. Others are different; they endure any sacrifice and exert relentless effort for the welfare of others. Everyone is human. For some, merely witnessing all this provokes anger. For others, there is an element of selfishness in their affection. Or alternatively, they possess an ignorance that prevents them from recognizing and respecting whatever actions others undertake. Thus, we have deficiencies in every aspect. True cultural refinement (*samskara*) can only be achieved by rectifying all of these flaws. To accomplish this, we must step into a public sphere, carefully observe every action there, discern the inherent good and evil within them, and ultimately arrive at the path where further sacrifices must be made. Ascend in this manner and set forth upon the sacrifice of instilling the excellence of this greatness into every individual among us. It is through such selfless individuals that we have gained so much familiarity and knowledge today.

[GV1:P1372] How shall this be acquired hereafter? Through whom shall it be acquired? We all possess knowledge and the desire to acquire all this. However, when it comes to the point of execution, there are numerous obstacles—we may find ourselves incapable, or if we attempt it, the actions may lack mutual coherence, rendering us unable to accomplish the task successfully. We must eliminate these impediments and forge ahead. We should advance in a specific direction only after meticulously consolidating our thoughts on what must be done to achieve this.

[GV1:P1373] For instance, Hindus initially establish a *Bhajana Matham*—a designated place for devotional worship. Following that, a Temple is built, and subsequently, an *Ashram*. Similarly, for Christians, it begins with a chapel for the month of devotion, then a Church, and finally the establishment of a Metropolitanate. For Muslims, the progression follows the order of *Thaikkavu* (prayer hall), Mosque, and finally Mecca. This is the progressive structure all these wise predecessors have established. Through this, they have been transmitting distinct levels of knowledge. It has been integrated with each respective religion in this manner. What is the significance of this integration? Through lived experience, they have harmoniously blended spiritual and material aspects, linking them together like a chain. Otherwise, the individual would stray from the path.

[GV1:P1374] This, however, is distinct from that. Here, both discipline and salvation are surrendered at a single focal point, and from there, each aspect is gradually reclaimed. That is the fundamental nature of love inherent in the Guru-disciple relationship. My savior and my disciplinarian are one and the same entity. In a way, it is akin to a monarchy; however, it is intrinsically different. It is a process of learning through life itself. In every individual's life, the Guru prompts them to perform specific actions, and through the disciple's affectionate reverence and loving respect, this essence is gathered purely, cleansed with humility, and imbued with an indescribable, fortuitous love. Consequently, there is no state unacquainted with glory in that realm. It is by embodying this profound glory that each of us must perform our actions.

[GV1:P1375] The sanctity of the titles of father, mother, and siblings exists only because we bestow it upon them. The status that we have instituted for God is quite similar. When we take up water to drink, we often close our eyes for a brief moment. Some individuals do this when they lift a spade to dig, pick up their tools of trade, or take a pen in hand. It is not that they revere these objects as God. However, unconsciously, there exists a certain sanctity associated with them. It is merely a demonstration of this inherent sanctity.

[GV1:P1376] There is a general assumption that drivers, boatmen, and mahouts possess no reverence for anything. Yet, a driver will close his eyes for a moment to display that reverence right before taking hold of the steering wheel. As for the mahout, he too pauses for a moment before picking up the goad. Why is this so? He knows the beast could trample him to death or gore him. Therefore, upon taking up the goad, he inwardly prays that the animal remains docile at its sight. The same applies to a boatman. A mere glimpse of dark clouds gathering in the sky is enough to evoke intense anxiety within him. A person soaring through the heavens may mistakenly consider himself as free as a bird. However, once on board, it is solely his unwavering focus that ultimately guides him to his destination. Observing these instances, one must recognize where such mindfulness is required in life. The primary duty of a Guru is to cultivate this profound sense of mindfulness within an individual. You must comprehend all these aspects. Irrespective of our path, it is impossible to navigate life without this fundamental attentiveness.

[GV1:P1377] We are presently standing on a narrow path of knowledge. We are merely beginning to enact one part of it. Therefore, the first lesson to learn is how to cultivate innate human love. We are accustomed to perceiving love both with and without an exclusionary mindset. We must diligently learn how this love should manifest in various contexts. Regardless of whether we are scholars or unlettered individuals, we can only progress in this world by imparting this love. By perceiving the sanctity of that love in everything, we must stand firm and begin to study it. Through that study, we must examine each subject and bring it to the forefront of our lives. This remains our ultimate objective.

[GV1:P1378] Guruvani

[GV1:P1379] March 1984

[GV1:P1380] Navigating our life is, in a way, relatively effortless. To illustrate, when a first-grade student observes a fourth-grade student studying, it appears as an overwhelming burden to the former. Nothing seems clear to him at that stage. However, upon reaching the fourth grade himself, he learns playfully. This is because he has already grasped the most effective methods to facilitate his learning process. We approach every subject in a similar manner. Once we acquire that intuitive aptitude for learning, everything else becomes trivial. Conversely, if an individual lacks any exposure to such concepts and has never even attempted to seek that knowledge, they will initially comprehend nothing. Furthermore, when they finally begin to understand, the mind feels heavily burdened, causing an urge to retreat from it entirely. Many among us suffer from this tendency to flee when confronted with something inherently good. This stems from our lack of habituation in witnessing, listening to, and familiarizing ourselves with virtuous matters.

[GV1:P1381] A system known as *Shudranyayam* (the logic of the Shudras) once emerged amidst us. There was an era when a Shudra was prohibited from doing practically anything. They were not allowed to touch, listen, or approach others; if they were to perform any task, they were expected to complete it and immediately run away—this was what they had taught us. Such an oppressive culture prevailed in our society during that period. Subsequently, an opportunity presented itself to the Shudra. This chance materialized in the fourth phase.

[GV1:P1382] It has been 5000 years since the birth of Sree Krishna. During these 5000 years, we have not been able to articulate and realize the true role of the Shudra. By bringing forth great souls into this world, God continuously educates us through their exemplary lives. However, to closely observe and learn from their lives, we require a certain degree of wisdom. It is perhaps due to a deficiency in this wisdom that we have failed to accomplish this.

[GV1:P1383] The Vaishya can conduct himself rather gracefully. Nevertheless, he has been unable to internalize and act upon this higher wisdom. The Marwaris and Gujaratis of Northern India serve as a prime example of this. They are at the forefront not only in generating wealth and sustaining their lives but also in undertaking philanthropic endeavors for various causes. They often execute these acts of charity with immense grandeur. Such behavior is rarely observed among us, as we are unaccustomed to it. When they offer *Gurudakshina*, it is of the highest standard. They continually desire to contribute as much as possible. However, they are equally ruthless in accumulating wealth, harboring no hesitation in adopting any means necessary to acquire it. Ultimately, they gather these riches, only to give them away charitably with the other hand.

[GV1:P1384] Even though kings belonging to the Shudra caste ruled here, it proved futile for us. During the reign of a Shudra, we ought to have attained complete freedom. It was either by divine intervention or a stroke of fortune that administrative power fell into the hands of the Shudras. However, instead of utilizing it for the greater good of the populace, they manipulated it in a manner that exclusively benefited their own kin. They segregated society into various classes and castes, eventually leading to a situation where one Shudra could not even walk in the territory ruled by another Shudra. Consequently, the ruling Shudra began oppressing the other Shudras under the guise of caste divisions. Armed with the scepter of authority, they were prepared to crush anyone who stood in their way. As a direct result of this, they now stand utterly ruined and dismantled. We have failed to perceive this reality. The rest of the Shudras degenerated into a marginalized class devoid of even the right to walk on public roads. It was a dark era when they lacked the fundamental rights to adequate food and clothing. Their garments had to remain strictly above the knee; such was the draconian law. If an official arrived to collect taxes while the head of the household was having a meal, the homeowner had to shout out from his place, stating, "Your humble servant is sitting here drinking a little rice gruel." They were compelled to speak in such a subservient manner. According to the law, when girls attained puberty, four *chakrams* had to be paid to the authorities. Similarly, women were strictly prohibited from covering their breasts. A breast tax, known as *Mulakkaram*, was imposed upon them for this very reason. Failure to pay this tax would result in the authorities confiscating all the decent household goods. Once, when officials visited a house to commit such atrocities, a woman residing there was overcome with unbearable anguish. She placed a fresh plantain leaf before the official, severed the very body parts upon which the tax was levied, and offered them on it. This horrific incident took place in the Cherthala taluk. Even today, recounting this event evokes a profound sense of disgust and horror.

[GV1:P1385] It is only after enduring such an oppressive era that we have arrived at our present state. Thus, the administration of that specific class of Shudras—who subjected us to myriad forms of suffering and actively sought to demean us—has finally been eradicated from this land. Today, even their own descendants cannot justify those past actions. They have evolved to a significantly higher moral standing. That is indeed a blessing. Consequently, we can console ourselves with the hope that some goodness will prevail when they ascend to positions of power.

[GV1:P1386] Guruvani
