[GV1:P1575] January 1986

[GV1:P1576] Yagas and yajnas have been initiated to celebrate and bring our Vedic sciences to the forefront. 'Chandika Yajna'—the very mention of the word Chandika makes its nature clear. By conducting this yajna and convincing us of many things, they turn us into its worshippers. Then comes the Soma Yaga. Through this, they intend origin, dissolution, and destruction. It is claimed that prosperity will increase. The prosperity of the offspring is not their goal. They are exhilarating people by saying many other things. It is said that its benefits will last for ten years. By saying so, they make a person perform the act of pleasing the deity for those ten years and keep him tethered to it. Again, linking to it, each yajna is introduced. When doing so, the lineage of offspring falling into this inclination will naturally increase. They are doing it very intelligently. Thus, if his *sattvic* nature is directed towards the deity, since it is an era where the deity has no place, he too will perish like the deity. Observe the sharpness of their intellect! He will assume the authority of a bunch of rabid, ruined people like this. He will perish. Even so, let his foot remain on top. He will also get the reputation of having done all good deeds. At the same time, the poor ignorant Shudras will fight and die. They know how to completely destroy the Shudra class in this manner. It is the result of forgetting the thought of God. They will also prattle that it is the result of not decorating the temple grandly. You must think deeply about this. As long as you do not think, you will not be able to accomplish anything here.

[GV1:P1577] Recently a yajna was held, wasn't it? What is it? Atirudra Yajna. What is achieved by this? What prosperity do we get? Taking a Shiva Purana story from the Treta Yuga, bringing it into the form of a yajna, and bestowing this yajna. Even though they have imparted this masquerade among you who live in such a civilized world, you do not understand. You gained nothing from diplomacy. What you received was only the stratagem, 'Let us fight tomorrow, today we are friends.' At first, knowledge was not obtained. What was received through the alphabet and education is this culture. Thus it became a situation of 'neither did it come from the south, nor did it fall into the trap.' Now if we speak about renunciation (*sannyasa*), nothing has been gained so far. The old history has collapsed. The idol being rebuilt must be rebuilt once more. We received no knowledge beyond this. Meanwhile, some *sannyasins* and prophets appeared here. They have all been driven away from here. In Kerala itself, many great men came saying, 'Brahman alone is truth' (Alathur Brahmanandan, Shivayogi, etc.). The vast majority of people here are ignorant of such things. If told like this, how will they transmit it? Shivananda, Kanhangad Ramananda; many such people have come to Kerala. But some of them just went towards the deity. Then, if we are to say someone actually highlighted this in relation to Kerala, it is Sree Narayana Guru and Chattampi Swamikal. The community in which Chattampi Swamikal was born did not need him even a bit back then. Narayana Guru was brought and born amidst a most ignorant society. None of the capitalists of that time, who paid a tax of five rupees, respected him then. You must possess the knowledge to evaluate all this and act accordingly.

[GV1:P1578] Guruvani

[GV1:P1579] March 1986

[GV1:P1580] Not only is there no knowledge about the path of self-realization (*Atmajnana*), there is not even a notion of it. What exists is merely the knowledge of some chaotic events that occurred either religiously or based on caste and class. However, with the vision that all this should change, by divine decree, everyone from Sree Krishna to the recently arrived Gurus have come as prophets, guides, and visionaries. But because we have not received the knowledge to understand these visionaries, we do not know what their visions are, what their lineage is, or what will happen to the world through them. They demonstrated many things. But we again evaluate them by tying them down under a god or goddess, viewing them as miraculous powers emerging from that. A lack of knowledge about the path of *karma* and the failure to receive guidance for a pure life. We have received a kind of knowledge that makes life itself go in vain. Not only have we not been able to achieve anything through this, but we are also playing around on the path of blunder.

[GV1:P1581] We must be able to bring about a change from this. This is a path that the divine will (*Brahmanischaya*) itself has shown for us. We can do whatever is possible by us in this regard. Looking at the size of the individual, the home, and this world, I have become nothing. I have not even become an instrument. But without a conviction that I must be able to do it and that I can, whatever you hear or know will either be destroyed by despair, bring about destruction through violence, or plunge you into futility due to the arrogance of possessing profound thoughtfulness. If any such situation arises, it is impossible for you to recover. This is the flaw that has persisted to date.

[GV1:P1582] Bringing about a change from this is possible only if we work with utmost dedication. This work means instilling goodness in whichever parts of our mind have functional capacity. Evil is what causes destruction. The means to sustain this must exist in our imagination. That is not a small matter. What is meant by the imagination to sustain it is—when one begins to draw a picture, it is depicted according to the mental prowess of the person illustrating it. It will be as beautiful as the way people imagine that picture. When some people imagine it, it does not turn out right. That is called their mental refinement. Or let it be called culture.

[GV1:P1583] Similarly, we have no knowledge about the cause of origin or its destructive cause. However, by visualizing it through imagination and with the intellect serving as an aid, it is being transformed into action. Thus, this imagination is primarily about depicting the purity of the mind of the person visualizing it, or its inherent sacred state. Therefore, if we are to attain that sacred state, we must first possess humility. This special imaginative faculty that can reside in humility grows in this manner. The attitude that nurtures this, whether in the little children accompanying us, in adults, or in elderly great souls—they are all shaping this mind. But it is pointless to visualize something without keeping any of this in mind. We must have the awareness that we need to raise children with such imagination, and we must possess the sense of responsibility to nurture any child who wishes to grow in that imagination. Then, once that child grows up in that manner, the child itself will know that they are nothing else. Having reached a nature of becoming nothing, if there is any truth beyond this, the child develops the consciousness that they have a duty and obligation to provide guidance to reach there. Be it a boy or a girl, it should be so. Without such an understanding, we cannot grow. We will become exhausted. Seeing everyone's actions, one might feel, "I cannot do anything amidst this vile behavior, I cannot even get a drop of love, there is no action left here anymore to live, nurture, and learn," and out of such despair, one might sink to the very bottom. This is not right. One should not reach a path of such despair. It will disappoint us and drag others down as well. We should not fall into such matters.

[GV1:P1584] For this, what I state first is the knowledge out of respect for the things we have received—ensure what we are capable of adopting. Along with that, after understanding who we are, we must understand what our lineage is. We must establish a true realization within ourselves: "What ability do I have? Nothing at all. Yet, through this special imagination, I can advance by informing, knowing, and acting." This is the primary duty. For this, a state of pure life must emerge within us, and we have not been given any other nature but to demonstrate it through our own lives. Nor is it possible to have one in the future. Now, evaluating the truth that has been imparted, our actions should reach the children in all corners of this world so that they can attain the merit of this action. One must always be vigilant to acquire a fortune that is a blend of the determination to deliver it, that detachment, honesty, humility, and merit. Fix this much firmly in yourselves first. It is your ignorance to think that Vivekananda or people like him did not take that path. Because they did not come for that purpose. They have come for the attainment of life that many people like you desired. They might not need to work for their lives like someone sitting hunched over with crossed legs tied in a string. Their actions may have nurtured the land, the nation, and the world. That will lead to the Satya Yuga. Because we do not attempt to grow like this, we end up adopting the justification given by someone who examines the pages of history. They would be offering it carrying an imitative nature of their scholarship. We cannot grow by utilizing that.

[GV1:P1585] For instance, let us consider the scholars who have studied Sanskrit. It is unheard of that they ever agreed on anything. Bringing in fishermen who languished as mere destitutes without literacy, making them do all this, taking on his attire and language, they nurtured them by giving them something true. He takes what he sees day by day, packs it, and consumes it as he goes. Someone wrote a shloka here and sent it across. If a reply shloka was not received, they were ready to slaughter him right then—such was the method of our ancestors. This was pointed out not to declare whether they were bad or good. We just need to observe this. What has benefited us now is the alphabet of the Westerner, isn't it? Since we recognized and respected it, even though they came to plunder and destroy us, they gave us a language and turned us into merchants. Shouldn't we respect this? Respecting the merchant in the place of a merchant, we must live as an owner ourselves. If we speak Vedanta, none of this will be effective. What is required here is knowledge. If the end of the Veda is not marked, will our affairs proceed here? That is not what I am stating. Good, not bad, fine, we respected all that. But whatever is necessary for the daily conduct here today—we must accomplish that. What follows is wisdom. That will arrive on its own. So, the objective is to perceive our own flaws. Then identify where we went wrong, was it from our father, our wife, or our husband?

[GV1:P1586] We have two paths to escape from this. One is the path of the Devas, and the other is the path of the Rishis. This path of the Devas was appropriate in the Treta Yuga and the Dwapara Yuga. Today is Kali Yuga. In Kali Yuga, even this Deva must take birth as a human. He is an intelligent human being. That intellect belongs to the Deva. His life is that magnificent. It is beneficial if we catch and eradicate this distortion of life. Today, if you affectionately keep close the children whom you consider useless and ask them if what they did was wrong, ninety-eight out of a hundred will agree. Once the mistake is admitted, it can be rectified effortlessly. There is no need to doubt that. Why? Nature is favorable to us. Those who practiced kingship back then have all been ousted. Those who were practicing Vedic rites became Tantrics. Now, it is not the Vedic path that is being practiced. It is Tantra. Tantra, Yantra, Mantra—didn't you comprehend that this is a trick? Now he has departed. The Vaishya and the Shudra together acquired merit through action. Earning fortune through merit, he has been compelled to seek the path to liberation. That is the era we are in. Why doubt here? You should be capable of this. It is sufficient if you do not keep looking at the old things. I am not stating that the old should be completely discarded. Observe the mistake as it is and accept that mistake as ours. Otherwise, do not assume it can be altered. Then, if we just correct that mistake, it will attain purity by the third generation.

[GV1:P1587] Guruvani

[GV1:P1588] April 1986

[GV1:P1589] Since the dawn of creation, among the humans born and raised in this world, some give thought to life and leave behind a record according to their knowledge. Some live doing nothing, lacking the knowledge to do so. Only when countless people pass by in such a manner does someone make such a record. Among them, some emerge artistically. Arts can be seen making the effort needed to reach completion by incorporating various means. Such arts themselves have been attributed to the name of God, shaping the knowledge about it into various art forms—thus attempting to replicate life itself. The history of numerous great souls has been replicated in this manner. In this, the majority of artists are those who employ intellect and logic. There are artists who sing, enjoy the moment, and let it pass. Some are contemplative, possessing the endurance to last for ten, three hundred, or four hundred years, having attained karma through faith in God. Over such a long period, the practice seen among people today is writing poetry by reflecting on the acceptance or rejection of this. If numerous people over such a long period come and handle things in this manner, it will reach an extent beyond our imagination regarding how many absurdities and profound truths have accumulated within it. Meanwhile, after all these individuals depart from earthly existence, having attained the results of good and bad karma, they become subtle bodies in the realms of ancestors (Pitriloka) and gods (Devaloka); thus, belonging to this solar and interstellar division, according to the results of constellations and planetary positions, each of these individual souls (Jivatmas) remains in the atmosphere indefinitely, and it must be observed how they act during the events of birth and death pertaining to their own families and other families. How can we, who blindly believe that this courageous execution of karma entering not only humans but all living beings is ordained by fate and willed by God, obtain a correction from this? From here, cursing birth itself, they vanish from the face of this earth.

[GV1:P1590] Guruvani

[GV1:P1591] May 1986

[GV1:P1592] Among those existing within the solar and interstellar division—ranging from demons to Yakshas, Gandharvas, Kinnaras—up to the dwellers of the realm of gods—down to human beings who, according to Hindu tenets, come from the ancient lineage of Manu—as these beings who stand as masters of karma, with or without faith, are born, the truth of life, which is referred to as family dosha or karma dosha acquired through the tendencies belonging to their respective religions or rituals, and the good and bad karma involving discord and unrighteous living within it, cannot be truly valued and understood by everyone in relation to their own lives. If one carefully observes these learned men who are known as the greatest intellectuals, scholars, or logicians, they can be seen at a dead end, enduring the misfortune of being unable to string together their own lives multiple times and preserve it as a model. The offspring involved in this and a few people who accept them have prospered through karma as inhabitants of the earth. The secret of life of such prosperity is experienced in such a way that not even a single individual who led this aforementioned life could make his followers accept it, or find satisfaction in his own life through a belief, and this is also evident in the soul that remains as his subtle body. Look entirely at the lives of great men who desired sacrifice through life, prosperity through karma, and sustenance through dharma. Recognize these as the most crucial chapters in human life and act accordingly. It can be seen that some rare individualities among the Jivatmas involved in this, who act as mediums and are known as dwellers of heaven, whose good and bad karmas can be understood and acted upon, lived in this physical world itself, demonstrated a life for the benefit of others, and then departed from this earthly existence.

[GV1:P1595] * Continuation of the April issue

[GV1:P1596] Question: In the past, it is said in the Puranas and elsewhere that great things were accomplished by manifesting the gods, isn't it?

[GV1:P1597] Answer: That is more or less true. Because the knowledge, qualification, and intellect of the writers are mixed into it, errors will occur in the Puranas. Those who study such errors, consider them as truth, and practice them will also suffer the same folly. They commit worse mistakes than atheists. Their souls will have to struggle immensely to attain salvation.

[GV1:P1598] Question: What do you say is the reason for that?

[GV1:P1599] Answer: Because this soul acts and learns in this manner, remaining somewhat aware and unaware of the fruition of its actions, it may happen that they cannot live respecting anyone during their lifetime. The reason for this is the arrogance that they are the ones who have experienced and known certain things. Beyond that, it is their unwillingness to see anyone else.

[GV1:P1600] With this, all of their actions will begin to go wrong. Thus, they will lead a life that ordinary people cannot endure. They will be unable to speak respectfully of highly spiritually faithful people. They will even reject them. Many such people can be seen in various places during the exact same time period. Upon leaving their physical body, their souls will remain embedded in the atmosphere. They will not get a rebirth quickly. Standing there, they will gather souls lower than themselves alongside them. Thus, they will become a group. They will torment ordinary people and mislead highly devoted individuals.

[GV1:P1602] July 1986

[GV1:P1603] Kerala is a small state today. Although known to many in its novelty, believe that novelty is a purity of antiquity. What is considered this purity consists of the ideas and aspirations of great souls who have taken multiple births. They have not forgotten to demonstrate their courageous actions through these ideas. Certain individuals, standing isolated, deceived the people by manipulating these widespread ideas and aspirations into a deceptive web, much like a mechanical and cunning Chanakya-style administration. We have been convinced numerous times that the conditions where most of those who earnestly tried to awaken from this and failed, occurred during their own lifetimes. Poets and artists have been trapped and troubled by this. Having read all this and attained scholarship, some learned men and critics have set out to show that the asset of this came through them. Quoting their aphorisms, they try to bring them to the forefront by saying, 'Haven't you seen what so-and-so said?' Instead of hastily tying their intellect with the intellect of those ancients and declaring 'Here I am at the forefront', if they use the intellect and firmness bestowed upon them by God to independently reflect, understand the dangers that have occurred to date, point them out, and write at least a few words as their contribution to remind the masses about that karmic proficiency in a manner suitable for today's times, they can attain courage. Otherwise, caught in the cunning tricks that make one believe these are words from the lineage of Manu, mixing Brahminhood and the state of Brahman, stepping down to replicate it in the state of Shudras and Chandalas, suppressing praise, condemnation, Gita, Yoga, and karma, displaying a long list of dharma to conceal reality, and wrapping it in old, fabricated tales of karma, it will end up like a pot of nectar overflowing resembling dog excrement wrapped in exquisite silk through the perspective of objects that are impure offerings. I only wish that they can contemplate what is required to move away from the footprints of this deceit.

[GV1:P1604] Guruvani

[GV1:P1605] Birthday Message and My Experience

============================================================

GURUVANIKAL · September 1986 · Volume 1
Malayalam source paragraphs GV1:P1606 to GV1:P1645
English line for line; each paragraph carries its Malayalam source number.

[GV1:P1606] September 1986

[GV1:P1607] Question: I often visit many ashrams. Similarly, I came here too. I have heard many people saying various things. I have a doubt.

[GV1:P1608] Guru: Listen to what I am going to say. Then the doubt will be cleared.

[GV1:P1609] Question: I have worked in many ashrams and institutions. What I see here is a method different from those. That itself is my doubt.

[GV1:P1610] Guru: That is not your doubt. It is indeed the truth.

[GV1:P1611] Question: That is what I need to know.

[GV1:P1612] Guru: That knowledge cannot be obtained just by being told; it must be known through belief over a period of time. The Trimurti system and the Shaiva, Shaktheya, and Vaishnava methods of worship seen today have not only misled the people but also impoverished and alienated Bharath (India) itself. Even today, we accept the rule of others and call it our own.

[GV1:P1613] Question: Why did you say it belongs to others?

[GV1:P1614] Guru: The English language is not ours. The attire is not ours. In short, everything is an imitation. We have lost everything of our own. Exhausted as we are, we have not yet been able to see this as the truth. As a result of arguments between early priests and kings, the Puranas were rewritten by a few immigrant scholars known as Brahmins, altering the knowledge that was in the hands of the kings. When further arguments arose through that, the Upanishads were created. They contain little reality. A few poems written by scholars and the realities written by the wise are mixed together in them. Initially, there were only the Dasha Upanishads (ten Upanishads). That became eighteen, then one hundred and eight. Now they are countless. The same goes for the Gita. Initially, there were only three hundred shlokas (verses). The rest were added over time according to the circumstances.

[GV1:P1615] Question: How did you get this evidence?

[GV1:P1616] Guru: Haven't you understood that this evidence is a vision (darshan)?

[GV1:P1617] Question: You yourself say that visions can contain falsehoods.

[GV1:P1618] Guru: I told you, I got this when I tried to correct that.

[GV1:P1619] Question: How do you handle this knowledge?

[GV1:P1620] Guru: There is a command to carry this knowledge forward like a Guru-disciple relationship. That is the path being followed now.

[GV1:P1621] Question: Another doubt. It is about this Akhandanama (continuous chanting) which is chanted using your own name.

[GV1:P1622] Guru: It is not an Akhandanama. It is a mantra. If needed, it can also be a stotra (hymn). In that sense, it can be called an Akhandanama. While receiving visions, two disciples received these lines as an ethereal voice (ashariri). 'You must strengthen this by chanting it. You will need it someday'—they came and told me that they received it this way. I did not let them do it then. The reason being, my name was in it. But those who received it used to chant it without my knowledge. The reason for that was they had received an ethereal voice saying, 'If you do not strengthen this by chanting, danger will befall you.'

[GV1:P1623] Question: There is no way they could chant it without Swami knowing, right?

[GV1:P1624] Guru: They would chant it loudly when I was not around. When I was present, they would do it mentally. Because of that, I was spared.

[GV1:P1625] Question: Could you explain a bit about that?

[GV1:P1626] Guru: It should not be explained. I can say a few things. I mentioned earlier that our attire and language are not ours. We had to adopt them because there was a lack of knowledge and action in our country. A person without knowledge cannot expand any action, can they?

[GV1:P1627] Disciple: How can you say there is no knowledge—isn't our land the one with all the knowledge?

[GV1:P1628] Guru: Then why did we take what belongs to others?

[GV1:P1629] Question: In the past, we had universities like Nalanda and Takshashila, didn't we?

[GV1:P1630] Guru: I too am saying that they existed. That language disappeared from among us because our merit (punya) diminished. When our merit diminished, we had to become slaves to the infiltration of others. They had knowledge and capability. A language like Hindi or Pali existed here. I do not know if it came about as a mixture of everything. As a renewal of that, Sanskrit was introduced. Through Sanskrit, the Puranas, Upanishads, and Vedas were written. In them, they wrote 'Amaranirjjaradeva' and turned the Brahmin into a god. Consequently, the vast majority of people came to be known as Asuras. Through some of them, the Shaktheya system was developed. Through some others, Shaivism was developed. And through yet others, Vaishnavism was developed. None of this is bad. Each is better than the other. How will you find out which of these is right and which is wrong?

[GV1:P1631] Question: It cannot be found out.

[GV1:P1632] Guru: That is the exact experience I had. It led me astray to a great extent. For us who are living, learning about the past is fine, but it is not something to be practiced in this era. Knowing that, what is needed is the sense of dharma to unite and work for the present time. Assimilating the bygone Vedic dharmas and karmas, mixing them in the Puranas, giving undue importance to gods and goddesses, and thereby diluting human potential—this is the result of poets and artists working together. This led to a surrender to miracles, the occult powers derived from miracles, and all kinds of activities taking refuge in them. I am a person who has experienced and known such surrenders. Bearing witness to the direct inferences I had and have experienced through that, I tell you—I am trying to present myself before you to instill courage in you, the courageous souls who have attained a truly worthy birth. May you be convinced.

[GV1:P1633] Perceptual inferences (*Pratyakshanumanangal*) refer to our ancestral beliefs and their guiding principles. Direct perception (*Pratyaksham*) is a part of this. The disembodied voice, the stream of light—the only witness to recognizing them is the grace-filled, luminous streak of compassion. What and how to testify to it is solidified over time by the experiential record of that moment. There is a reason for saying 'over time'. Otherwise, a Guru is needed to explain it in that very moment. If lacking complete qualification, not only will the Guru be unable to do so, but the disciple will also fall into disarray. Because of this, many people wander astray and reach danger zones. There is evidence that they have suffered thus. Our nation was full of goodness and had reached great heights in all respects. All forms of nature here are favorable for the way of life. Nature and its elements intertwine, and humans experience its complete bliss. Other countries have not received such favorable nature. They have climates that are partially favorable, partially unfavorable, and even uninhabitable. Mahabali, the Asura emperor, is proof that our land was completely filled with goodness, blending devotion and humility, and possessed a governance system that imparted a good method of protecting the weak. The hypocritical policy that branded one who does not consume *Sura* (liquor) as an Asura insulted noble kings, transformed the one who consumes Sura into a Deva, overturned knowledge through Homa (fire rituals) and Tantric practices, diverted Dharma from virtue towards Adharma, manifested this course of action here, redirected all charities to Brahmins, thereby fostering Adharma and causing the loss of the people's merit. In the Kali Yuga, this Dharma is an absolutely harsh Adharma. The Vedic system, which did not even hesitate to write down '*Pratyakshavaham Dharmam*' by portraying all the virtuous souls as Asuras and Asura lineages while realizing the one who poured Sura as a Deva, fabricated the Puranas and Vedas and became the authority of the Upanishads. Consequently, the Asuras degraded into a state without literacy, not even feeling that the land and country belonged to them. Then, divine worship became trances, lamps, ululations, and joyous shouts at the edge of the forest, along with the consecration of ancestors under the shade of trees. Over the years, this tutelary deity system evolved into global worship. It includes Yantramoorthi, Tantramoorthi, Yogeeshwaran, Marutha, Kali, Kooli, and even the Brahmarakshas who protects Brahman. If needed, it becomes Dakshinamoorthi. Once it becomes Dakshinamoorthi, it is a wait to consecrate Uttaramoorthi. The boons received by Bhasmasura are a deception created by writing such stories. Just like the verse in the Gita, '*Pratyakshavaham Dharmam*', I too could see everything directly. Not only did it become direct, but I also received the word, and through it, illnesses were cured. Not in a trivial way—a patient treated in Singapore for eight years was cured in forty-one days. A patient in a family where the father, daughter, and daughter-in-law were doctors was cured. Their names are not disclosed as they might feel slighted. Only holy ash (Bhasma) and holy water (Theertha) were given. Even bladder cancer of that nature has been cured. Similarly, there are many direct experiences considered as spiritual realization. It was then that terrifying forms of tutelary deities and gods appeared ceremoniously with salutations in an instant, informing through those with visions that performing certain methods would yield quicker results, and we acted accordingly. After a month of this, the influx of people increased exponentially. During that time, all this began to fall apart. Not only that, all the people who had loved until then resorted to abuse, fighting, and quarrels. It was only after about seven and a half years that a correction was received for this.

[GV1:P1634] During this period, an opportunity arose to uplift the place currently known as Guruvihar in Melkadakkavoor. Its rightful heirs—Sharada, Bhargavi, Lalitha, Bhargavi's husband Gopalan Master, and son Ramadas—all arrived at Varkala Santhigiri to resolve their family curse. They inquired about this. The descriptions were explained to them. Among them, madness and incurable diseases were persisting. When asked among that group, "A curse of Narayana Guru is seen. How did that happen?", they told the truth.

[GV1:P1635] "There were two mothers in our group. One of them had hurt Narayana Guru. One was favorable to the Swami. We four are the children belonging to one of those branches. We had an unmarried uncle. He and the Swami were close friends. In those days, the Swami was known as Nanu Ashan. The Swami used to come and go at Kuzhivila. An artificial cave was created there. It had enough space to accommodate a table, a chair, and a sofa. One day, when the Swami arrived, the sofa and chair on which the Swami used to lie had been chopped up and thrown into the nearby deep water. This was done by the mother and her accomplices who disliked the Swami. The mirror was thrown on the floor and shattered. The heartbroken uncle said to the Swami, 'It is no longer suitable for us to sit here, let's go.' Then, he took the Swami to the house of their relative, Mundayil Kunjikrishnan Chattampi in Varkala. Walking from there through the Thoduve bridge along the canal, he sat under a jackfruit tree and worked towards what is today's Sivagiri." All this was narrated by the late Gopalan Master. He was an Anchal Master; the father of Ramadas, who is currently the Junior Health Inspector at Anchuthengu. Only a small remnant of that dilapidated artificial cave had survived. He sorrowfully told me that women now use the spot to sit out of the sun and beat coconut husks, and children use it for defecation and urination.

[GV1:P1636] Then, what I felt like saying was this: "It doesn't matter, lean some long palm fronds against it, tie palm leaves to it, clean the place, and light a lamp there for six months. Then you will have some experience. After that, we can do what is necessary." Accordingly, they cleaned it and did what was required. Before the completion of six months, it was time for the Sivagiri pilgrimage. At 4:00 AM, while the milkman living there was milking the cow, light reflected on the vessel, and when he turned to look, a ball-like light was rising from the cave, from the spot where the lamp was lit. When it rose and ascended upward, dogs, cats, and cows in nearby houses created a commotion, and cows broke their ropes; this incident was experienced within a four-mile radius. This can be understood by asking the locals there.

[GV1:P1637] After this, as per my suggestion that it could be renovated, they repaired it, resumed the rituals, and began to see results, at which point the old adversaries reared their heads again. When I went there, a quarrel took place. While Gopalan Master and I were hastily boarding the train from Kadakkavoor railway station, a member of this family came, struck me, snatched away my towel, and left.

[GV1:P1638] Today, they are averse to recounting this history of Guru Vihar because I am its primary agent. Even now, madness and other incurable diseases continue to haunt that family, and these afflictions have not been completely eradicated. This serves as evidential proof that if spiritually blind souls lacking ancestral purity remain within a family merely to conceal the truth, that family can never be truly reformed. Consequently, those who sincerely desire reformation will be unable to attain it through their own efforts, and others will be ready to misinterpret the situation. The opponents concealed the truth, relayed false information to Chirayinkeezhu Ramakrishnan, and consequently had him write about Guru Vihar in a distorted manner. As I have stated earlier, it took me seven and a half years to discover the underlying cause of this opposition, and it took another seven years to rectify it. What I am addressing today through my own experience is the profound realization gained from that rectification. I have consequently discerned how this Trinity system originated, what anomalies exist within it, what befell the lineage of Manu, and why the memory of Manu has vanished from the hearts of the people. I shall not expound upon these matters at present.

[GV1:P1639] Question: It is said that Manu is the son of Brahma, is it not?

[GV1:P1640] Guru: That is exactly what I said has been corrected. It will take a considerable amount of time for you to be convinced of it. After you read some literature and become somewhat convinced, I shall explain it to you. It is a spiritual revelation, after all! Did you not observe that the very people who were granted the experience eventually harbored enmity toward me? To understand this to some extent, read the section titled '*Daivachinthanam*' authored by Narayana Guru. Subsequently, read the *Guru Gita*. It contains the spiritual instructions imparted by Lord Shiva to Goddess Parvathi. Let at least some of your doubts be resolved through that text. The remainder will naturally follow through direct experience. This Kaliyuga possesses a highly unique characteristic. We have been conditioned to believe that Kali is inherently evil. Satyayuga, Tretayuga, Dwaparayuga, and Kaliyuga—these four epochs collectively constitute a Chaturyuga. All human beings born in the fourth quarter of this Chaturyuga—Brahmins, Kshatriyas, Vaishyas, and Shudras—must experience both good and evil equally and attain liberation in their progressive journey toward the ultimate truth. This principle is not stated differently for anyone. The Brahmin, whose supremacy was established by the Brahminical religion through Vedic tenets and Tantric practices, holds no legitimate place here. The Kshatriyas, who executed royal governance utilizing their education, wealth, and enlightenment, also have no place. If the era of the Devas was culminated through magical and Tantric methodologies during the Tretayuga and Dwaparayuga, the epoch of Kali must be fulfilled through profound penance (Tapas) and supreme wisdom (Jnana). Penance, in this context, is the formidable ascetic power attained through righteous action; it is not acquired by retreating into a forest. That comprehensive action—action encompassing all dimensions such as thought, word, and deed—will systematically engender both fundamental purity and supreme sanctity. Through this transformative process, spiritual merit (Punya) will invariably manifest as an inherent trait. Undoubtedly, when one accrues spiritual merit, divine fortune will perpetually accompany it. It is proclaimed that this very fortune can empower one to claim the right to ultimate liberation (Mukti). One may designate it as 'Yoga' if so desired. This is precisely the doctrine articulated in the *Bhagavad Gita*. Act by thoroughly assimilating the profound words of the Supreme Soul Sri Krishna: "Buddhyayukto Yoga balena" (Act with the formidable power of Yoga seamlessly united with the intellect). This will subsequently pave the definitive way for liberation. This is the paramount Dharma of Kali. It is fundamentally because the Tantric dominance of the Brahmin and the sovereign administrative rule of the Kshatriya have been irrevocably dismantled that the priestly scholars deceptively propagate the notion that Kaliyuga is entirely worthless. That is not the factual truth. On this auspicious day, I am formally recording these profound words for you, seamlessly incorporating my own spiritual experience.

[GV1:P1641] I am reminding you once again to ensure the absolute culmination of the essential duties that were previously brought to your attention and which you have only partially executed. Everyone must undoubtedly remember how we desperately wandered in search of drinking water two years ago. There were even individuals who deeply pondered whether Kerala would perish entirely due to a devastating drought unprecedented in recent times. During that critical period, prayer assemblies were conducted continuously from Santhigiri across various locations, actively involving both believers and non-believers. You are thoroughly convinced that everything stated back then was the absolute truth. In the geological history of this Earth, which remains a relatively small sphere revolving within the orbital path of the solar system, India, situated prominently along the equator, inherently possesses an almost temperate climatic system. I am articulating this without forgetting the empirical fact that extreme heat and cold are occasionally experienced in certain regions here as well. However, when objectively compared to other nations, we primarily experience a highly temperate climate. This is exceptionally true concerning Kerala. We are all thoroughly cognizant of the historical condition wherein Kerala was virtually a terrestrial paradise when compared to states like Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, and Madhya Pradesh. Yet today, systematically reversing that idyllic state, various specific committees and assemblies have been strategically established here to firmly entrench Tantric practices and the orthodox Brahminical religion, functioning in a destructive manner that eradicates intrinsic spiritual merit and leads the very nation toward its ruin. You are well aware that as a direct historical consequence of their past actions, immediately subsequent to the onset of Kaliyuga, our nation was tragically lost into the subjugating hands of numerous foreign invaders. The frenzied oracles of Tantric practices are once again aggressively roaring with rhythmic percussion, dance, and song, deliberately obscuring the grim historical reality that we not only lost India's vast economic wealth but were also stripped of our indigenous modes of worship, traditional attire, and native language, thereby being universally reduced to abject slavery. Alongside this chaotic scenario, several individuals superficially labeling themselves as believers and non-believers are wandering aimlessly in utter intellectual confusion. Those who ostentatiously claim to be non-believers have readily adopted the alien attire and language of foreigners, overflowing with the arrogant delusion that the absolute core of all knowledge resides exclusively within them; they have tragically transformed into sterile intellects, much like the barren arrogance of a mature yet entirely leafless tree. Nothing whatsoever emanates from their literary endeavors except a profoundly putrid stench. The piercing arrows of so-called 'modernity' have been conveniently provided to them as ideological weapons for this destructive purpose. They completely fail to realize that they and this aggressively roaring mob of pseudo-believers are not two distinct entities, but fundamentally one and the same. It is merely akin to the myriad waves of the ocean roaring and crashing individually. Every single wave violently strikes the shore driven by the forceful ego of asserting its own supremacy. The exhausted and systematically impoverished masses, who innocently believe all this spectacle to be the ultimate truth, must consciously avoid falling into these deceptive traps and losing their spiritual bearing; instead, they must meticulously investigate and comprehend the inherent Dharma of this specific era. As long as we physically exist on this earth, if consuming food and drinking water is an absolute biological necessity for us, we must concurrently cultivate profound spiritual merit in a harmonious manner that does not violate or alter the fundamental, immutable laws of nature. In this noble pursuit, all human beings are fundamentally equal. There is absolutely no distinction between the erudite scholar and the unlettered commoner. There is no discriminatory differentiation between a Kshatriya and a Vaishya.

[GV1:P1642] From the Santhigiri Ashram, you have been repeatedly and emphatically reminded of this in the following manner. In this earthly realm, the present epoch is unequivocally the Kaliyuga. The Satyayuga, Tretayuga, and Dwaparayuga each possessed their own distinct and specific Dharmas. During those respective historical periods, those designated principles were duly and systematically executed. If such was indeed the historical precedent, we must firmly and logically believe that Kaliyuga also possesses a specific, inherent Dharma. What was scripturally documented in the specific context of Devas and Devis has already been comprehensively practiced until the historical culmination of the Dwaparayuga. The Supreme Soul Sri Krishna has conclusively proven this fundamental truth, visibly demonstrating it by appropriately acting and facilitating designated actions. Critically examine the eminent Yugapurushas (epochal spiritual figures) who have emerged since that era. In the Western nations, numerous divine mandates have been successfully established through the profound ministries of Jesus, Moses, and the Prophet. Concurrently, within that same historical timeframe in our own land, from Sri Krishna to Buddha, Vardhamana Mahavira, Dayananda Saraswati, the profound preceptors belonging to the illustrious lineage of the *Parayi Petta Panthirukulam*, countless solitary Mahatmas, and within Kerala itself, spiritual luminaries like Sri Narayana Guru, Chattampi Swamikal, and Sri Shankaracharya—all these great souls have unequivocally and repeatedly exhorted us to live harmoniously and fraternally like the children of a single father; deeply contemplate upon the absurdities and contradictions we are currently perpetrating in the sacred presence of their monumental spiritual legacies.

[GV1:P1643] I am reminding you once again. If we are to successfully avoid wandering endlessly in a desperate search for essential drinking water and food, we must sincerely and exclusively engage in monotheistic prayer directed solely to the One Supreme God, rather than blindly and futilely chasing after numerous demigods and subordinate deities. It is precisely to impart this profound realization that these great souls have been prominently highlighted. We are not intellectually bankrupt people who fail to comprehend any of this. Instead of finding false, momentary solace in witnessing aimlessly wandering spectacles—such as the bizarre ritualistic aberrations in Tamil Nadu, the extreme worship practices resembling cannibalistic savagery in Rajasthan, or the demonic, self-destructive savagery of leaping into blazing fire pits in Lanka—we must consciously awaken with rational wisdom and spiritual clarity. By artificially categorizing spiritual paths into Mahayana and Hinayana, we must decisively and permanently escape from the deceptive, binding strings of the regressive Tantric practices that have once again thrust us downward into a lesser spiritual trajectory. Emphasizing once again the undeniable and absolute truth that the 'Path of the Guru' (Gurumargam) is unconditionally essential for this ultimate salvation, I solemnly dedicate these words to you.

[GV1:P1644] Your Swami,

[GV1:P1645] Guruvani

[GV1:P1646] October 1986

[GV1:P1647] Today, the actions we perform concerning the concept of God are typically conceptualized through various forms and attributes. However, some individuals differ, often perceiving this in an illusory manner. Others conceptualize the divine nature as absolute nothingness, without any specific objective, yet omnipresent and pervading everything. Humanity was created by endowing it with form, expression, and action. Consequently, a person's conceptualizations and emotional expressions develop in alignment with their mental maturation. Through such conceptual frameworks, great souls have emerged and departed in accordance with the *Yuga Dharma* (the duty of the epoch). It is customary for us to regard the extraordinary power associated with their concepts as the very concept of God. This subsequently transitions into a form of worship. Initially, we lacked the capacity to worship or even conceive of such a phenomenon. There existed such an era. After all, in the beginning, humanity experienced a primitive state, incapable of cooking food or wearing clothes. Later, through the progressive development of the human intellect, and by imparting expression, form, and love, those actions were cultivated. The spiritual power of such souls has flourished and exists today. This is precisely how every object we currently utilize was conceptualized. Following this conceptualization, humanity learned the appropriate and inappropriate applications of these creations. Thus, through the continuous discernment of the good, we comprehended the nature of life's actions.

[GV1:P1648] Since today is the atomic age, you can understand this in every way. Today, there is a course of action to examine and know what exists on earth, in the sky, and in other celestial bodies. We happened to be born, grow up, and experience this in such an era. If we had lived ten or two hundred years ago, we would not have been able to use or even imagine these motor services and other vehicles that we see today and use daily. Similarly, electricity, as seen today, could not have been conceived in those times. Today, so many things have been invented for human comfort. Whether sitting at home or anywhere else, events happening in every corner of the world are visualized and seen in the same form, expression, and emotion as if they were happening right here. This is the merit of our times. This is *Kali*. Therefore, it is impossible to describe what can be achieved when the *Kali Yuga* progresses further. This demonstrates the magnitude of human invention. At the same time, it was somewhat similar in the ancient times of the Devas, only their methods were different. It is said that they chanted mantras to release weapons and suspended things in the atmosphere through sheer willpower. Such things have occurred since time immemorial. However, we should not assume that this happened to everyone at all times. Back then, things could only happen that way. Consequently, the human mind was directed toward that path, and that path was continuously strengthened. Strengthening through mantras, strengthening through form and expression—all these were brought into action. Through the same imagination, it remains effective in the atmosphere, within us, and in each of the celestial spheres, proportional to the magnitude of that concept. However, as time progressed, we have grown into the knowledge to think, make others think, learn, and teach beyond those ancient methods.

[GV1:P1649] Today, we are situated within the *dharma* and *karma* of the *Kali Yuga*. We have attained things easily today. Those who lived two hundred years ago could not have even dreamed of any of this in reality. We are strengthened in such an action. However, in the *dharma* of *Kali*, there is something we need to attain profoundly. We must realize it through self-actualization. Just like our concepts and actions, a concept and action specific to this *Kali Yuga* must exist in the world. What are they? We must continuously perform virtue-dense actions through conceptual manifestation, eliminating the negative aspects of the past, elevating them to higher planes, and establishing them in the world as a domain of action (*karma kanda*) on our behalf. For this purpose, we have received guidance through divine revelations and spiritual visions. Having been blessed to partake in this monumental task, we must possess the absolute certainty that we can accomplish this—which represents the highest of merits, the greatest of actions, and the pinnacle of wisdom. If we, who are entirely convinced of this truth, treat this matter trivially while being recipients of the era's potential, it would be a profound disrespect toward the Divine. It would also befall us as one of the greatest sins. Therefore, regardless of whether we are sick or healthy, young or old, or whoever we may be, it makes no difference in this regard. This is an action that affords us the opportunity to perceive everything as one. Saying that everything is one does not imply that all human beings are identical. However, in terms of merits and demerits, there will be minor variations according to their individual abilities, tastes, and colors. The eligibility for experience will be more or less the same. Medicine may act quickly for some, while for others, it may not. It will succeed or fail depending on one's inherent karmic tendencies. Similarly, someone may be able to make inventions swiftly, while others can understand things immediately upon hearing them. Someone else might be able to manifest something into action merely by visualizing it from afar. Such variations exist. This is the truth. Therefore, one should not claim, "Only what I have seen is right," or "Only what you have seen is right." What everyone has perceived is indeed correct. It is a state of awareness cultivated by performing actions while rooted in one's respective imagination. However, a shortcoming has occurred among our ancestors. A habit has developed where past eras are pushed back, and only those past times are acknowledged. That is insufficient for us. We must give importance to the era we are living in, highlight past actions, undertake what can be practiced from them, preserve their goodness, discard the evil if it must be discarded, halt what needs to be halted in its proper place, and harmonize the conceptual methodology, action, and wisdom required for this world.

[GV1:P1650] Guru Vani

GURUVANIKAL · November 1986 · Volume 1
Malayalam source paragraphs GV1:P1651 to GV1:P1661

[GV1:P1651] November 1986

[GV1:P1652] Initially, there was only a very small hut in Santhigiri. A hut just about my height. Only if one stood exactly in the middle would their head not hit the roof. In every stage of growth, we must be able to reflect from the very beginning. What myriad hardships were overcome since those days to reach this point? Within a year, we managed to build a small prayer room in place of that little hut. It was only after seven years and four months that people began arriving, recognizing it as a place of worship. Today, it has reached this state. You must realize how much hardship brimmed with the profound response of goodness within this journey. You must understand that whenever goodness is about to occur, it is preceded by an element of evil. From that time until today, this has been my experience. If the impending goodness is monumental, it will be preceded by a situation where people collectively criticize or speak ill. If it is minor, it will be some other situation that causes mental anguish. If it is even smaller, at least a little child will cause us some pain. Something of that nature must occur. That is the reaction of goodness. However, ordinary people believe that sorrow should never befall them. We even have a system for that—offerings (*nercha*). If they hear that going to a particular place will ward off sorrow, they will rush there. Yet, we do not visit such sacred places merely to prevent sorrow. It is to inquire and understand our joys and sorrows, to discover what solutions exist for them, and to explore the possibilities within our lives to alter the state of our soul. It is to recognize the potential disruptions that may arise from our course of action, to work through them, and to attain the opportunity to become the true masters of our own *karma*.

[GV1:P1653] In the karma of gods and goddesses, they revel in numerous joys and sorrows, immerse themselves in it, and are then forced to take birth again. However, this is not what is said about human beings. But it is the singing of praises and rituals of the gods and goddesses that you have learned. You sing praises to the gods and consider it to be everything. This is similar to some emotional people who love someone deeply and then stand ready to hang themselves. If asked why, even they would not know. Similarly, when these special praises, with their repetitive power, reach our karma, it becomes equivalent to hanging our lives. However, they have stated in one word—in the Satya Yuga, penance is required; in the Treta and Dvapara Yugas, manifesting the deity and offering praise; and in the Kali Yuga, chanting of names. They haven't specified whose name. Therefore, even in the Kali Yuga, we merely chant the root mantras (moola mantras). Scholars have written that salvation (Sayoojyam) can be attained through this. By bestowing all forms of mastery upon the gods and making us worship them, they are kept pleased. The enlightened ones stand above this and speak of the Upanishads. There are Upanishads written by scholars. In them, depicting such descriptions, those who consumed liquor (Sura) from the enlightened kings of that time were preserved as Devas (gods). Thus, those who consumed the liquor and meat offered to the gods became Suras. Those who did not became Asuras. The people who are categorized as Asuras belong to the Shudra class. This Shudra class constitutes about eighty percent. All of them might turn into Asuras. You yourself should ponder the reason for this.

[GV1:P1654] This Shudra class encountered a peril in the beginning. It can be untied if one tries, but as long as it remains untied, it continues to be an affliction. This is expressed in a verse in the Bhagavata.

[GV1:P1655] Karma acts as bonds for a person.

[GV1:P1656] Liberation certainly comes only when the bonds are severed ٹ

[GV1:P1657] So, even if you have wondered what the method to untie the knots is, you have not been able to untie them so far. That is the greatest of the perils that befell the Shudra class. Praises were written in such a way that it seemed violence and mischief were the virtues of the Kshatriyas, thus instilling cruelty in them and making them great. All forms of growth have been denied to the Shudra class. If any mistake occurs in that, it is enough to give alms to the Brahmin. Furthermore, they taught that if a Brahmin curses someone to death, that too is a blessing. Cursing meant beating to death. How many such stories do we have? Initially, when I said this, those who portrayed it as deliberately spoken to malign the Brahmins are with me today. Today, they are somewhat convinced. I did not say this after studying history. I said it after observing and understanding the ancestors of each class and caste. It is upon seeing that I called it an affliction that one does not know how to untie.

[GV1:P1658] There were no Brahmins in India. Those who were here were the Konkanis. They are still docile people. (I do not forget the fact that some are ready to become violent under the RSS). They were meritorious people who treated snakes and cows alike and lived without hurting anyone. You must understand that a lineage with such merit perished in this manner. The Aryans drove away this Brahmin community, which maintained honesty, from here by copying various intellectual systems. Then they created their own language, their own order of worship, and became gods themselves. That is the trick of the Aryan.

[GV1:P1659] Some of those who were driven away returned. They can be seen in many parts of Kerala. But today, they have no hold anywhere. If anything is fabricated anywhere, it is the tantric knowledge of the old Aryans. Realizing that this fate befell them because they accepted Tantra and Vedic rituals, they have not yet been able to retreat from it. Although an acharya named Madhwa came among them, he led them back to the old ways. You should not assume it is dishonesty. It is honesty. Only by asking that very power of light what went wrong with us will there be a correction for it. That was also difficult to get at that time. Because Madhwacharya had some scholarship, he did not move in that direction. Thus, Madhwa is the acharya who wrote Dvaita as Advaita and asserted that one can attain Advaita from this Dvaita. Consequently, that lineage reached a state where there was neither Dvaita nor Advaita. Worship reverted to those old tantras. Thus, that lineage declined.

[GV1:P1660] We too must be careful not to make a similar mistake. I am not speaking of Advaita here. I am speaking about the purity of karma. You should not eliminate karma by conflating it with Advaita.

[GV1:P1661] Guruvani

GURUVANIKAL · December 1986 · Volume 1
Malayalam source paragraphs GV1:P1662 to GV1:P1676

[GV1:P1662] December 1986

[GV1:P1663] Question: In the Varnasrama Dharma of Brahmins, Kshatriyas, Vaishyas, and Shudras, the author of the Gita himself has pointed out that Kali is the era of the Shudra, the fourth stage. To bring them to the path of karma, that is, to unite and uplift the Shudra (the ignorant), what should be done, Guru?

[GV1:P1664] Answer: A people can only be united under a single ideology! And that too, only an ideology in accordance with the Yuga Dharma.

[GV1:P1665] Question: Given that only an ideology mature enough to sever the roots of beliefs deeply embedded in the framework of old habits and rules can sprout a change in the hearts of the people in accordance with the dharma of Kali, who will be the authority of that supremely noble ideology, Guru?

[GV1:P1666] Answer: Haven't you seen that the Treta and Dvapara Yugas have proven that the Yugacharya will be the authority of the Yuga Dharma? Kali also has such authorities.

[GV1:P1667] Question: How can that great soul be found, Guru?

[GV1:P1668] Answer: When karma is increased and merit is attained, that path will become clear.

[GV1:P1669] Question: For those engaged in industry and commerce for their daily livelihood, by what virtuous deed will they attain it?

[GV1:P1670] Answer: When the Western policy of destroying nations and draining wealth through industry and commerce is abandoned, both will be purified.

[GV1:P1671] Question: How can ordinary individuals achieve this?

[GV1:P1672] Answer: First, each individual must maintain purity and moderation in their own thoughts and actions. Goddess Lakshmi and Goddess Saraswati were the sources of wealth. The lineage of acharyas, who had nothing, acquired wealth through their own karma and meditation. Each individual must take a firm vow that we should be able to become a generation capable of passing it on to the next generation. His education and culture began with the acharya. Even his letters began with the acharya's first letter, and he should be able to live a life of dedication.

[GV1:P1673] Man's karma and dharma constitute his greatness. It should be the acharya who makes the people perform karma and gets it done. Even prompting thoughts about the goal of human birth stems from the acharya's adherence to ideals.

[GV1:P1674] The systems of justice conceived by human intellect are not sufficient to sustain human dharma. People do not even think about the necessity of writhing and twisting, claiming it to be devotion. They do not consider the basis for dismissing something by saying, 'This is Kali.' Today's order, discipline, civilization, and intellect are not those of the olden times. Man can only be guided through methods suited to the times. The culture with its ancient heritage is becoming unknown to today's generation. We are the remnants of having lived as slaves due to a lack of wealth and knowledge, devoid of freedom and culture. Many acharyas came and tried to change this. They failed. The Shudra culture extinguished the ignorant people's inclination to embrace the acharya. When wealth and position came, the Shudra became arrogant. Arrogance destroyed the clan. Even the Brahmins of India fell under the spell of the Westerner's whiteness—possessing a Vedic demeanor but the karma of a Shudra.

[GV1:P1675] The people stood in wonder before the demon-dancers, much like a job-seeker before a palmist. Scholars focused only on making shelves, buying books, reading, and filling them up. No one could save the people from this. Only an enlightened Acharya can save them. One can live in accordance with Dharma only when they are able to internalize the Acharya. Only through that can virtuous deeds be performed.

[GV1:P1676] Guru Vani

Malayalam source paragraphs GV1:P1677 to GV1:P1684

[GV1:P1677] January 1987

[GV1:P1678] Many of you are engaged in ashram duties here. However, you have a lack of experience in such activities. We can only act according to the karmic path laid down by our ancestors or contemporaries. Irrespective of the era, we only inherit a few tendencies of our ancestors, our own tendencies, and the knowledge of our contemporaries, whether they are scholars or ordinary folks. The world has a peculiar characteristic today. We can instantly know events happening in any corner of the world through the media. That wasn't the case before. Many events would occur within a five-mile radius that we wouldn't even know about. That does not happen now. However, things happening in remote villages are still often unknown. Even though such awareness has grown significantly within us, we have not completely succeeded. Along with that, each of us needs to grow culturally as well.

[GV1:P1679] There is a kind of knowledge that comes from observing and doing everything. We can only attain that knowledge to a certain extent. To impart knowledge to us, there are various systems like the Bhajana Mutt system, the temple system, and the ashram system. What we receive from all sides is knowledge. The knowledge belonging to the Bhajana Mutt is not what the temple system holds. The ashram system is not the knowledge of the temple system. Only the ashram system will move us towards true knowledge. Until then, they make us believe by preaching the grand aspects of the karma system, convincing us that everything is achieved through those rituals. Massive lies. In Hindu logic and Vedic authority, there are many fire rituals (*havanas*) like *Tila Havanam*, *Mrityunjayam*, *Shuddhi Havanam*, and *Kshetra Pindam*. Then, they attain *Mantra Siddhi* (mastery of mantras). *Mantra Siddhi* is later converted into *Deva Siddhi* (divine attainment). Only after going through this does one realize that none of this is true knowledge (*Jnana*). It is for the sake of true knowledge that one enters an ashram.

[GV1:P1680] For a wise person (*Jnani*), there is no *Karma Kanda* (section on rituals); there is only *Jnana Kanda* (section on knowledge). *Jnana Kanda* can only be obtained from an ashram. A sannyasin or a Vedic scholar wandering in Vedic rituals will not attain it. The ashram is meant to impart this understanding and to practice and internalize it. We have never had such knowledge. We have only acquired knowledge about the blazing miracles that cause overwhelming excitement by witnessing this *Siddhi* (occult power) system. It is exactly as scholars have written it down. We have heard that in Vashistha's ashram, there was a cow that granted whatever was asked of it. We do not realize that all this came from the poet's imagination. We just swallowed it as it is. We completely believed the story of Kanva's ashram and Shakuntala, as well as the miracle-filled history of Buddha. These stories have only managed to corrupt us, not improve us. When ordinary people narrate, sing, and play out these things, it becomes like a *Thiruvathirakali* (a traditional dance). After watching it for a while, one gets bored of all the games. How many such fabricated tales have they made us believe! The *Devadasi* system itself is an example of this. How much ignorance exists in the *Devadasi* system. We are the culmination of such ignorance. We just do not understand that.

[GV1:P1681] The ashram system does not talk about any of these things. It is the realm of spiritual experience (*Anubhuti*). Gods, goddesses, the sages under them, and the wise men standing alongside them will all come before this true *Jnani*. Before the *Jnani*, all of them are merely subordinates. Subordinate means they have absolutely nothing to give to this individual. In front of that person, they possess a much lower level of operational capability. None of the things related to the temple system or similar practices can be performed before this *Jnani*. It is when this happens that we understand reality. So, it is not easy for this knowledge to be transferred to us. Why? We are the remnants of the karma performed by our ancestors. Secondly, that path of karma is commonly practiced among us today. Therefore, we cannot stay away from it. Our belief systems have become like that. Moreover, looking at the world at large, the followers of various gurus and prophets have become corrupted in different ways by misusing their intellect and power. This even spread as a distortion within governments. Thus, religious systems have turned into statecraft and a trick to win in it. All concepts became like that. We do not realize that we are destroying ourselves in this manner. A change must be brought about from this.

[GV1:P1682] It was mentioned earlier that the ashram is the realm of spiritual experience. When you count from demons to gods, and from gods to sages one by one, you realize that their knowledge is limited to a certain extent. Haven't you heard a short poem? It might not have been written with full understanding. Or perhaps it was: *'When you cross the six steps and reach there, you can see Lord Shiva.'* What do you understand from this? The meaning everyone gathers is that Shiva can only be seen after crossing six steps. It actually means that if you cross the six steps, you can see what Shiva possesses and what he does not. It means one can understand that Shiva is limited to this much. Before someone who has crossed five and a half steps, Shiva has nothing to do. Devendra will not approach one who has crossed six steps. Devendra is the lord of all these gods, yet even he won't come. Then comes the state leading to the divine presence. None of these exist there. There is only the gross, the subtle, the effect, and the cause. Then there is the concept of a sage who transcends even that. Haven't you heard, *'Sankalpa mathrena Parameshwara'* (The Supreme Lord exists merely by thought/will)? This is not easily understood. It is impossible to know who transcends this. It is also difficult to cross this state. According to the dharma of the *Yugas*, we cannot cross it in the *Treta Yuga* or *Dvapara Yuga*. That is because those eras belong to the gods. When that time passes, even these gods must take birth as humans and attain liberation. That is what the Puranas celebrate, after all. So, we have taken birth in such a time. That is why it is said that the sages pleaded, 'Please allow us to witness Kali (Yuga).' It means they desired a birth in the Kali Yuga, hoping that at least then, by being at the Lord's feet, it wouldn't be bad if they were saved and liberated.

[GV1:P1683] Thus, without this familiarity, you will not be able to achieve this. It is for this reason you are advised to behave in accordance with the ashram's nature. It is the task of transforming a human into a god, into a sage, and guiding them to the path of liberation. First, solidify your belief system. The worship we perform today—realize that the gods and goddesses are limited to what they are. Then, embrace a form of worship in accordance with the dharma of the Yuga.

[GV1:P1684] Guru Vani

[GV1:P1685] February 1987

[GV1:P1686] After material and spiritual explorations, humans select certain sanctuaries and, according to their intellect or divine will, glorify them as holy lands, turning them into a distinct arena. These sanctuaries are viewed as holy lands where many go and perform penance according to their intellect, abilities, and capacity, and where the fruits of that penance endure for a long time. We must be very careful before setting out to such sanctuaries. That was the discipline in ancient times. Now, we see a decline in such discipline. Some might still go that way. As far as we are concerned, most people do not pay attention to this. The power of penance accumulated over countless ages, along with the struggles and steadfastness in duty of countless people, resides in the aforementioned places. Very few people think that we should be able to experience any one of these realms and possess the proficiency in action required to understand its authenticity.

[GV1:P1687] Even after the passage of ages and through immense effort, attaining an awareness of at least one epoch (yuga) is exceedingly difficult. This is because we have not lived our lives with such mindful vigilance. Furthermore, we have not acquired a sense of righteousness corresponding to the epochal duty (yuga dharma). We merely lived according to what we saw. Even among us, there is a section of people who somehow speak, act, live, and let others live to some extent. However, we must possess the wisdom—at least through careful observation—to understand the nature of the ascetic power of the great souls who have traversed across ages. The principal aspect of this pilgrimage must be undertaken in this manner.

[GV1:P1688] We undertake pilgrimages in various ways. Depending on our own sincerity towards it, we often go alone; sometimes, people travel in groups out of a desire to elevate their lives. For some, this is a path of escape. The belief underlying that desire is that their body will no longer recover in any way. Others, despite earning, giving, and receiving abundantly, perceive a certain emptiness in their existence—they set out seeking how this occurred and what caused it. Apart from these, individuals who have sought merit through virtuous deeds journey with a fervent determination to fulfill their lives, or to do and inspire others to do at least a fraction of what they can for the people, contemporaries, and future generations in the concept of God. But we are entirely ignorant of all this. We are unaware that such a realm of spiritual wealth exists and that we have a role to play in this scheme of action. We do all these things without knowing why.

[GV1:P1689] Irrespective of what we do among these, or even if one becomes a perfect ascetic, we are all destined to leave this bodily cage. When we depart from this cage, we do not pause to reflect on what fortune we managed to accumulate within it, what our meritorious deeds were, and what constitutes them. Even if we do think about it, we limit it to a brief reflection. What is the part we can play in this scheme of action? We should become an asset of wealth for ourselves, or for ten, a hundred, or a thousand people. What are the qualifications we need for this? We have never thought in this manner either.

[GV1:P1690] The effort cultivated over numerous ages in accordance with the epochal duty is an endeavor that began from a time when one did not even know how to wear clothes, or how to seek them—or even when one could not contemplate whether clothes were needed or not. That has evolved through food, clothing, and civilization, leading us to reach various states today. Even the material and the spiritual domains have emerged through refinement. This material and spiritual are not two different entities. They are one and the same. They are categorized into two merely for the sake of differentiation through nomenclature, to attain certain realizations.

[GV1:P1691] This very material body serves as the foundation for the spiritual as well. The foundation of the spiritual comes to us, knowingly or unknowingly. Having profoundly contemplated over ages on what occurred in the material realm, what occurred in the spiritual realm, or if something did occur, what is to be derived from it, certain great souls firmly resolved to fulfill their lives and do everything possible to bring about peace and harmony beneficial to the world. A fragment of the ascetic practices they conceived, acted upon, and realized exists in these places. It is for this reason that we select such holy sanctuaries and undertake pilgrimages.

[GV1:P1692] In ancient times, there were individuals who investigated all this and undertook journeys with purity of action. Such rare individuals exist even today. There are those who reside permanently in various places such as Kashi, Rameswaram, Ayodhya, and Vrindavan. These permanent residents are to be considered merely like the numerous crocodiles present in Kashi. Nothing more has emerged from it. However, only a person who contemplates this can reclaim the knowledge of its meritorious essence, and thereby, acquiring courage in action, become one among the countless people who earn it for the sake of humanity, all living beings, and contemporaries.

[GV1:P1693] Guruvani

[GV1:P1694] March 1987

[GV1:P1695] Thus, after wandering around and passing a considerable amount of time, such a soul—some of them—returns for eternity. Thus, someone whom we call a prophet, a deity, or a guru emerges once in an era, in a manner that they cannot even be considered one in a million. That is what is meant by a prophet or a guru.

[GV1:P1696] Everyone can be a guru. Fathers, mothers, husbands, wives, and children are everywhere! Therefore, everyone is a guru, right! Not in that sense. It is a soul that returns after contemplating and recognizing this, having diligently executed the scheme of action in that ascetic power for a long time, and then surrendering. Whatever this returning soul does, people turn out in two ways to either accept or abuse him. There is a kind of people who agree to whatever is said. They are completely useless. There is another group—the impotent ones. Today, they perform actions with stubbornness. They perform actions with immense stubbornness and clamor. Among these, only a very few honor the truth. Perhaps one in ten million people might emerge as virtuous. Most of the aforementioned people would be there to abuse and assault him. It is such people who are born and die among us. However, there is a small section that differs from this. They can be called by any name, whether a devotee, an active worker, or a wise person. We perform our actions by being part of this. When performing actions as part of this, what all thoughts should we possess?

[GV1:P1697] What have we and our ancestors accomplished? What actions have they performed for this world? We turn to this path to learn this. This is a story unknown to most people. When we turn to this path, there is a medium to focus the attention of those with experience—for instance, householders with a minor level of experience, even if they are not spiritualists. There are a few men and women here with vision. There is also a circumstance to learn many things through them. There is a medium to focus their attention too. They must also have a resolve. During my life, during the life of my society, what am I witnessing? What am I hearing? What is my duty towards them? Numerous people like me have been born, lived, died, and perished; what is this provision I have received? For what purpose is what I have seen and what God has shown me? A medium that aids in reflecting upon these. Having instilled monotheistic belief and brought it to you, God is establishing a stage in this medium through you that is capable of bringing change to the people of the world themselves.

[GV1:P1698] In that position, if you act in a manner that evades the duty of seeking action through purity of mind, word, and deed, there are certain dangers. Those with experience must be very careful; the matters stated in this* must be very carefully noted. What all is transpiring in this world? Have you not seen that there are inner-dwellers (antaryamis) and the special qualities mentioned about them in it?
