[GV1:P1701] During a pilgrimage, just as our mind becomes corrupt, they** will enter. Just as it becomes good, they will also enter. When performing actions without being either of the two, one will go there.

[GV1:P1702] Only God is above this. Each one of us needs to see something. When we speak of a guru lineage, when travelling with gurus, when praying and imagining along with the person who prays considering them as a guru, this will enter according to our strength, our line of thought, our karma, and our thinking habits. You do not know this. It can enter even without this. You should be careful at such times. Most of you will not be able to handle this. The reason for not being able to is our own ignorance. We belong to the Shudra class, don't we! Even if it is today's Brahmins, they too know nothing. Other than knowing some mantras and tantras, some properties of yantras, and some rituals, they stop when it comes to the path of manifest dharma. There, they change to a state of not knowing anything.

[GV1:P1703] These inner dwellers, who exist in this atmosphere in microscopic form and have the ability to do anything anywhere and go anywhere, have the karmic capacity to do and make others do everything. That is why the Prophet said that this world is ruled by Jinn. In their language, they are called Jinn, Hindus call them Brahmarakshasas, and Christians call them saints and angels. It is in this position that you are going with the guru.

[GV1:P1704] You need to have caution when going with a holy soul. This holy soul brings benefits and leads to attaining liberation up to the position of karma. To go beyond this, a truth must be carried. Without a guru lineage, one cannot go there; no matter how truthfully it is done - where to? One cannot go past that state. For example - suppose we go to a place looking for a great person. We do not know this person directly. We do not know anyone there either. If we ask, they won't let us in. In this situation, wouldn't we just get stuck there? Similarly, in this position, there is a block. Without knowing the way. There is no one there to inquire and find out. There is no one there to find. There is no one to tell us either. There will come a state, a plight, where we have to go and knock there. The magnitude of this plight will cause us to wander there and become nothing. That is what the path of the guru is for. The guru will bring the quality of our life to whatever position it stands in and keep it there. How much? To get a certificate from the government, a certain qualification is required, isn't it? There is such a government there. This government according to the law will be a power. That power will not let us pass. Such powers are turning us hither and thither. Those authorized for that are standing there.

[GV1:P1705] If people with corrupted minds during self-reflection go and handle things there, it will take advantage of that convenience and get inside. And then mislead this person. At the same time, what if it is merit that is found? It will enter looking at that context too. Just a slight slump is enough, it will enter then. That is its job. There are many such tricksters in the atmosphere. It will make us into its nature. Then it won't let go of it either.

[GV1:P1706] Billions of such indwelling entities densely populate the atmosphere. They enter us from the atmosphere at the velocity of wind. In the presence of a Guru, billions of these souls (jeevatmas) arrive, depart, and linger there. Having arrived, they stand observing closely at the threshold of merit and sin. Whatever actions you perform at this juncture, they will enter you assuming that very nature. While in the presence of the Guru, if your disposition is contrary to the Guru, they enter in that state, and if contrary to the Guru's ideology, they enter in that respective state during that time. Alternatively, if your disposition is aligned with something else, they enter bearing that ideology, and if it stems from an act of defiance, they permeate as a defiant ideology. Subsequently, it becomes impossible for them to attain goodness. You must be mindful of this during that time. Once it permeates, you will be unable to progress further. If you do not remain highly vigilant and aware while engaged in this action, it would be tantamount to inviting one's own destruction. It becomes exceedingly distorted. The majority of you are unaware of this.

[GV1:P1707] An example of this was observed during our previous journey*—these were experiences of indescribable helplessness. This is evident through experience. Similarly, regardless of your endeavors, such occurrences do not manifest at all times or in everyone. These souls arrive with the conviction that they will attain something through spiritual merit (atma-sukrutham).

[GV1:P1708] Conversely, when you embark on an endeavor for the sake of karma, what myriad virtues might you acquire unawares? You might elevate the people themselves, or transcend the prevailing impurities of character. Failing that, you might at least tread a path that imparts goodness even through a single word. That higher functioning aspect might transition toward goodness through us. Our vital force (jeevan) is the master of such a conscientious act. The vital force maintains such vigilance. Consequently, the mind gravitates toward whatever captures its focus.

[GV1:P1710] May 1987

[GV1:P1711] Therefore, when undertaking a pilgrimage, one must be cognizant of these matters. Otherwise, you are merely travelling aimlessly. People do not engage in these acts with such understanding. The prevailing belief is that one will acquire the merit to transform one's very vital force. Simultaneously, an equal measure of the opposite effect may also manifest. This is a profound knowledge capable of transforming anything through affectionate care. We are entering into that realm of knowledge. For that, one must continuously strive. Thus, ten pilgrimages; ten holy visits. Through such a progression, the complete realization of this knowledge dawns upon us. This knowledge becomes the catalyst for our wisdom and power of penance (tapobalam). If necessary, it transforms into the very power of penance itself. This is the ultimate objective of such journeys. One must remember that we are dealing with matters of such profound knowledge and merit.

[GV1:P1712] During our travels, we often visit the birthplace and the place of Samadhi of an individual endowed with the power of penance. A place where numerous ascetics resided—Rishikesh is the central location where countless sages sat and performed penance. A place where so many holy souls performed austerities—if we visit such a location, we can witness the immense penance-power of those great souls. We can behold the tapobalam of holy souls who performed penance in multitudes. This is true vision (darshan). You are able to experience this only because there is at least one experienced disciple accompanying you. We undertake this by preparing ourselves for the karma of performing and facilitating meritorious deeds, understanding this to be a Guru lineage. Regardless of who it is, since it is founded on love, it must be executed with absolute vigor. While sitting and observing in various places, one can witness numerous good and evil spirits, deities, Yakshas, Gandharvas, and Kinnaras. Through the power of our intentional prayer (sankalpa prarthana), they too acquire merit. We were able to witness this during our previous visit. As they depart having attained merit, billions of evil spirits are annihilated by our intentional prayer, and through our prayer that such karmic residue should not remain in that space, it is destroyed, allowing merit to spontaneously manifest there. We are embarking on a karma laden with such manifold virtues.

[GV1:P1713] People accomplish this by travelling to places like Rishikesh, Ayodhya, Badrinath, and Vrindavan, wearing a single piece of cloth, living in isolation, and performing rigorous penance. When Sivananda of Rishikesh obtained his M.A. degree, he suddenly felt a profound detachment. He declared that the paper in his hand was utterly useless, not even fit to scoop bran for eating. Thus, he discarded it, saying he did not need it. He was a Marwari. Discarding even this certificate, he went to Rishikesh. Upon reaching there, he performed penance in the only manner he knew—for that was all he knew. Consequently, he was able to achieve something monumental. He did not embrace what could be termed a traditional caste-based asceticism. For seven rupees, they would build a green hut with a porch and a room, constructed using materials cut from the forest. Along with it, a few other things would be tied together. It would merely provide shelter from rain, wind, and sun. That was all. Constructing this, he sat there and chanted the 'Hare Rama Hare Krishna' mantra. This is the very practice carried forward by the modern 'Hare Rama Hare Krishna' movement. 'Hare Rama Hare Krishna' is a phrase originating from the Narada Upanishad. He sat there and chanted for twelve years. Eventually, he had a few spiritual experiences. That is how it expanded. 'Sivananda of Rishikesh' is the name of the ashram there. Around three hundred people reside there. Similar to Rishikesh, there are various other ashrams like Kailas Ashram. References in 'Daiva Chinthanam' stating that experienced individuals exist even today are alluding to such instances.

[GV1:P1714] We have this in our experience. Having witnessed such resolve as that of Sivananda, what should you, with all this experience, aspire to become? You are individuals following an ideology. You must adopt that ideology with profound interest and pay careful attention to how it should manifest in your karma and dharma. Devoid of immense knowledge, ideology, and karmic merit, you are the ones who must demonstrate that you possess the capability to actualize this ideology. It should at least serve to alleviate this state of helplessness. You must maintain the awareness that you are embarking to undertake a karma far more righteous than visiting other pilgrimage centers, along with the unwavering resolve to successfully actualize it.

[GV1:P1715] As we travel to various places, we encounter numerous ascetics (sadhus). Upon seeing these sadhus, we feel joy towards them, and they towards us. But what do we have to offer? Love. What kind of love is that? On what criterion shall love be given? How will I execute it? Why have I arrived here? Why did God bring me here? One must possess at least the resolve to contemplate such profound questions. They too are human beings, just like us. They also love us. We reciprocate, thus mutually sharing love. Numerous destitute individuals come forward, displaying affection and fondness towards us. Within these poor souls too resides a vital force exactly like ours. Why does he exhibit this? Why does he display such resolve? One must ponder upon these matters before departing from that place.

[GV1:P1716] All the flaws within me must be eradicated. No evil should take its place! One must at least impart goodness! Otherwise, what is the purpose of going for this? What is the point of going merely like Kuttiyali going to Kollam? Therefore, we must possess a certain resolve—"I will attain it". What kind of resolve do we require? What is primarily needed is a walking staff. A sankalpa (firm intention). If the staff of sankalpa breaks, does anything remain? The staff must not break. Our walking staff must not break. If it breaks, all is lost. Everything is gone. We have kept everything propped up upon this sankalpa. In the past, some people used to say—"All that was gained ended up on the stick." Is this that kind of walking staff? This walking staff must never be discarded. Leaning upon something, we stand upon the foundation of an ideology. If we are to become advocates of such sacrificial karma, what level of sacrifice do we require? What hardships must we endure? What karmic qualifications must we possess? Exploring all these is the very purpose of this journey.

[GV1:P1718] June 1987

[GV1:P1719] There exists a lack of familiarity among us regarding the reclamation of the *Trimurti* and *Rishi* traditions. We predominantly presume that *Rishi*s are merely worshippers of deities. We too subscribe to this same belief. Have we not relegated our women even to the level of servitude? We have become so debilitated by blind faith that we remain ignorant of this reality. How can we, operating under the misconception that this approach will benefit our nation, redirect it towards an alternative path? How can we transform individuals who harbor such convictions? You yourselves possess an intuition that this is insufficient. But how can it be transformed? Do you not require a definitive approach for that? It is due to our lack of inherent aptitude that we have failed to assimilate this.

[GV1:P1720] Many individuals have emerged among us. These include both those who exhibited mystical powers and those who did not. The majority comprise individuals who demonstrate occult powers invoking deities; those who prophesy through trance and frantic movements. Our prevailing notion is that blessings and curses are the only outcomes we can attain as rewards. Have we not been indoctrinated to believe that a mere vision of God is sufficient, signifying ultimate fulfillment? Is that not the rationale behind recounting the divine visions of Poonthanam and Bhattathiri? Even if one were to experience thousands of such visions, they hold no substantial value. This is because such phenomena can contribute nothing to the pursuit of Self-knowledge (*Atmavidya*). I am conveying a realization I attained during a period of profound distress. I was instructed to discard all these practices and proceed in a specific manner. It was only subsequent to acting upon that guidance that I attained salvation.

[GV1:P1721] If the *Treta Yuga* and *Dvapara Yuga* existed before the advent of the *Kali Yuga*, does not the *Kali Yuga* have its own *Dharma*? If *Satya Yuga*, *Treta Yuga*, and *Dvapara Yuga* possess it, *Kali Yuga* must also have a *Dharma*! How, then, do we practice the *Dharma* specific to *Kali Yuga*? Our flaw lies in not discovering the path and acting upon it with love and sacrifice. It is not about claiming to have discovered it and sitting somewhere for five or ten years. We have not learned how to impart this to our children through sacrifice. We remain contented with blessings, curses, vows, and ritual offerings.

[GV1:P1722] Experience is what is required first. If someone discovers it, we must hold onto that discovery and progress. It may not be possible for everyone to discover the truth. Such a path does not reach us. This is due to the historical errors of the *Shudra* class from time immemorial. Should not this error be rectified, thereby generating merit, leading to fortune, and ultimately culminating in fruition? Do you assume this can merely be plucked effortlessly? This realization must manifest within us. This is its designated path. It cannot be attained by citing any other justification. Furthermore, it cannot materialize except through you, the householders. Regarding the roles of wife, husband, and children, as long as self-knowledge does not awaken within them, what is the meaning in labeling their children as bad if they grow up aimlessly? We are unable to take this up with absolute determination. This must somehow be integrated into our being.

[GV1:P1723] There are two paths - the *Rishi* path should be understood as the path of sacrifice. Instead, one should not adopt the mystical paths of deities or the paths of ascetics who perform miracles. What is to be done with that? Do not try to alter it yourselves. The individual you accept must possess the capability to transform it. Otherwise, it will be like holding the leg of someone who is hanging onto a palm frond. One must grasp it with conviction. One must be convinced that this person is experienced. There is no use in saying things like 'I saw Sri Krishna' or 'I saw all the deities'. This is not spiritual truth. All this may be true on one level. But it is not spirituality. Why did I say that? Did I not tell you earlier that I traversed the path where all this was seen and guided? This is not suitable ٹ. And then I stated that it became correct only after I took an alternative route and reclaimed it, did I not? That is the path of sacrifice. This is the *Rishi* path. This *Rishi*, this guiding force is not subordinate to any god, goddess, or the trinity known as Brahma, Vishnu, and Maheshwara; they are referred to as the *Kalantara Guru* (Guru across time). They highlight the rights and wrongs that occur over time and make us the inheritors of it. Thus, are you not the rightful heirs? Through your life, you are conveying this to your wife and children. It is that wife and children who will accomplish something meaningful for this world.

[GV1:P1724] Who all emerge from your household? Have not all the paths that exist—be it that of the *Yogi*, the *Karmi*, the *Jnani*, or the *Bhakta*—originated from the hands of this householder (*Grihastha*)? Once goodness emanates from them, is there a need for another individual to come and do something for this land or country? This path is not in our hands; we claim we lost everything because 'they' invaded or 'others' invaded—but who paved the way for 'them' and 'others' to invade? Was it not our own ancestors? Because they invaded, we at least attained literacy. Otherwise, even this would not have happened. Having understood at least this much, you must develop a steadfast determination for this cause.

[GV1:P1725] Today, there are more than a hundred families capable of speaking the truth openly. There are householders who can even explain what these Trimurti are and what is within them. There are indeed people who can explain who a *Jnani* (the enlightened) is and what the greatness of the Gurus is.

[GV1:P1726] Today is Kali Yuga. Kali has a specific dharma. Can we, who are born in Kali Yuga, live by abandoning it? We must adopt an approach wherein we accomplish everything while remaining within Kali. Do our own people not say so? In Kali Yuga, the chanting of the Lord's name (*Namajapa*) is sufficient. Whose name? What kind of name? They do not know how to answer this. If we consider the current practices, have they not chanted millions of times? Are they not chanting billions of times? And what is the result? Whoever embodies fortune in Kali Yuga; there is another expression for it — having done all these...

[GV1:P1727] Residing at the foot of a tree, performing penance,

[GV1:P1728] One must dedicate their idol in the service of the sages.

[GV1:P1729] In such service to the sages, it means that one should minister to them and follow their path. If we do this, it will bear fruit. We might lack self-realization. That does not matter. We must at least be capable of doing this.

[GV1:P1730] Birthday Message

GURUVANIKAL · August 1987 · Volume 1
Malayalam source paragraphs GV1:P1731 to GV1:P1748

[GV1:P1731] August 1987

[GV1:P1732] Ever since the publication of the Santhigiri magazine commenced, it has been customary to include a column titled 'Birthday Message', based on my experiences and perspectives, in the special editions released under the name of an annual issue or a birthday issue. Similarly, a doubt arises in me whether this note, provided in the special edition intended to be released this time, also entails a critical tone. The reason for this is the two facets that emerge from life: one good, the other bad. Or rather, sin and virtue. Sins are of many kinds; virtues are of many kinds. Likewise, when speaking variously of realization, vision, empirical narrative, life memoir, and life struggle, one's own knowledge and erudition are also incorporated. Erudition is sometimes referred to as knowledge and wisdom. However, no one should doubt that true erudition is spoken of in relation to the *Jnanis* (enlightened beings). But these *Jnanis* themselves are of many types: the *Karmi* (man of action), the *Yogi*, the *Jnani*, and the *Bhakta* (devotee) — it is through these four paths that one acquires a tradition of wisdom commensurate with their knowledge.

[GV1:P1733] For example, a believer and devotee realizes one of the chosen deities in the tradition of *Ishta Devata* (tutelary deity), such as *Pey*, *Marutha*, *Mantramurthi*, or *Yogeeshwaran*. What is meant by realization is the truth—encompassing the gross, the subtle, the effect, and the cause—that can be perceived even by his physical eyes. When he presents this courageously, with love, out of an affinity towards humanity, and compassionately to the best of his ability, people use the word *Siddhi* (attainment/supernatural power) to describe it. If necessary, this can be termed a form of wisdom. A little further ahead is the Vedic approach, represented by the Vedantin or the *Karmi*.

[GV1:P1734] The *Karmi*, having realized each deity through *Mantra Siddhi*, also desires to stand at the forefront of public service with this attained charm, employing mantras, tantras, and yantras. On the other hand, the *Yogi* attains miraculous powers in the science of Yoga by testifying to the six *Chakras* (vital centers). It can be seen that Gorakshan, the practitioner of mystical powers who is believed to have reached the pinnacle of *Siddhi* and is immortalized in stories even today, attempted to surpass Vagbhata, the sage of the heart mentioned in Ayurvedic science. However, the Ayurvedic scientist, the sage of the heart, instructed how and where to use everything from cumin, mustard, and turmeric to *Kurunthotti* (Sida cordifolia), *Thamizhaama* (Boerhavia diffusa), banana stem, ash gourd, and *Paalmudukkan* tuber. Without the aid of modern laboratory equipment, maintaining precise weights and measures, he expounded the truth on how single herbs like *Aanachuvadi* are effective for various diseases. He guided how even a young child could prepare herbal decoctions (*Kashayam*) with minimal additives, advising without causing any harm to our physiology, and laying down rules so that these remedies can be utilized as long as humanity exists. Concurrently, the aforementioned Gorakshan is also a *Jnani*.

[GV1:P1735] From this, we understand that there are various types of *Yogis* and *Karmis*. However, let us now try to observe a true *Jnani*. Among the names of such *Jnanis*, we intend to look back at a few—like Shankaracharya. To make us understand, four words have been used for four types of *Jnanis*: *Brahmavit*, *Brahmavaryan*, *Brahmavarishtan*, and *Brahmavareeshtan*. It is impossible to distinctly show in which all states the acquisition of wisdom occurs just through the word *Brahmavit*. Disentangling the terms *Brahmavaryan*, *Brahmavarishtan*, and *Brahmavareeshtan* is indeed impossible. We must respect the words of Kumaran Asan, who was able to honor all these at least to some extent through his erudition. The ability to articulate this must have stemmed from the assurance provided by the proximity of Sree Narayana Guru. Otherwise, one would not be able to say it out of fear. His lines, stating that "Yakshis and demons are gods to them" and "they have long built fortresses with Smritis," alongside the lines "Change the rules yourselves, or else / they will change you," further strengthen this sentiment, clearly demonstrating the agony in his heart.

[GV1:P1736] Because the aforementioned *Varnashrama Dharma*, which emerged from an upper-class mentality, was interpreted erroneously, we must not forget the role played by the literate scholars here, who devoted their logic, intellect, time, and eras—giving their all through their erudite path—to enlighten or uplift the masses.

[GV1:P1737] However, a true *Jnani* sees none of these; yet, they see everything. Let us look at what that *Jnani* attempted to make us do. To impart love when we see each other, they accustomed us to the gesture of *Namaskara* (greeting) with an *Anjali mudra* (folded hands), conveying utmost grace and facial dignity. This is not difficult for any layman or scholar to follow. It can indicate whatever humility one possesses. Even if there is ego, it would seem to disappear somewhere and stand isolated. The karma is realized in such a way that even the most ignorant person can be elevated to the status of a *Jnani*. At the same time, without forgetting the *Jnani*, the scholar, and the *Yogi*, they have been respected without ever losing the purity of the attempt to realize them by assigning each their respective position. Yet, one must doubt whether this *Jnani* views the scholar's application of terms like *Mithya* (illusion) or *Maya* (delusion) in the exact same manner. The reason is that, having reached a state of respecting everything, this *Jnani*, out of love—to use the words of Sree Narayana Guru or Chattampi Swami, "counting one by one, until the meaning is exhausted"—attempts to polish and refine even the fluctuations of the subtle-sighted ones starting from that point; this aspect constitutes the *Yugantara Dharma* (the dharma of the transition of epochs). Included in this are the calculations of the fourteen Manus and the count of the *Jnanis* who are to appear in a *Manvantara*. It is not merely destroying these calculations; the aforementioned scholarly arrogance or ignorance is clearing a path for eternal destruction in a way that destroys our very religious consciousness. As a result, we have become so deteriorated that we cannot recognize ourselves, isolated from each other, and devoid of religious consciousness due to discovering God and subsequently dividing into classes. Therefore, a permanent state of perpetual distancing, preventing us from uniting, has taken deep root in an insurmountable manner. Consequently, the people here have grown day by day, as if on chemical fertilizers, realizing themselves as pests of destruction; with minds fiercer than Bhadrakali and degenerating into vulgarity through alcoholism, they have become enslaved to the art and prowess of Western culture, ready to assume ownership of what is celebrated as education. This has become the domain of a competitive karma that the Brahmin, Vaishya, and Shudra—who claim to be the Vedic scholars and *Jnanis* here—are eager to collectively accept. Having evolved to this extent, we have been able to reclaim ownership of an administration that owes allegiance to no one.

[GV1:P1738] The householders (*Grihasthashramis*) who stand at the forefront of this, through their modernization, scholarship, knowledge, wealth, and authority, have taken all the aforementioned ignorance upon their heads and become the masters of the aforementioned actions. Do we, who are so eager to create everything from the nursery education they have started to postgraduate study centers after graduation, even remember this? It is worth pondering whether the householders belonging to this division of action, or the aforementioned degree holders or postgraduates, have been able to even glance into the lives of the wise sages who sacrificed their lifespans and bodies to serve the people by aptly placing and operating everything in its proper place. Western culture has stepped in, girding its loins with the determination of the previously mentioned Bhadrakali, to keep us as a group of ignorant people trying to bury forever these truths and dharmas envisioned by the sages so that the thoughts, words, and deeds of every Indian could work in harmony. What we see today, right from the nursery level, is a culture that turns children into possessors of an education that makes them ignorant of who their parents are, only to eventually create old-age homes to hide them away in some corner. If the administration falls into his hands, he will protect the people by inventing not just Star Wars but many other things. Is it not essential for the people of India and all the cultural center trainers who try to impart this to think whether they want to raise their children like this? Do not try to make yourselves incompetent! I offer this before you with the request that you give importance to my repeated pleas.

[GV1:P1739] I see that even those who have cooperated with me in daily life for twenty or thirty years still have minor doubts and find themselves in the unfortunate position of being unable to explain this matter to another person. However, among Hindus—from temple dwellers to Shudras—we have a medium adopted to understand God. Using that as a medium, an advertisement was placed in two newspapers at a cost, along with an astrologer's planetary chart. It was explicitly stated in the astrological query (*Prashnaroodha*) itself that this has not been attained by the lineage of Acharyas until today, that liberation is being granted as requested by the deities, and that the impurity of that very astrologer's family temple has been removed. Once again, those belonging to the temple dwellers and temple believers have sent me several letters in a way that shows they have understood nothing. Who knows what they understood about that astrological query! In that advertisement itself, it was specifically written that they should come to the ashram to find out. Instead, they wrote letters. And the others did not understand anything either. It is with all this in mind that I have written such a message. I wish for you to read and understand this patiently.

[GV1:P1740] May this auspicious day bring goodness to you.

[GV1:P1741] Yours, Swami

[GV1:P1742] Guruvani

[GV1:P1743] September 1987

[GV1:P1744] You people of Palakkad do not have a small life. You have a certain dignity. Even today, you are truly dignified. Why is that? Because they work hard and live off their earnings without harming anyone else. Such a large community exists in this region. However, minor ignorances have occurred. That happens, aren't we humans? Except for what has come from holding the flags of today's politics or imitating various other things, you are worthy - more than anyone elseٹ . You possess honesty. These ruined Namboothiris - though they are useless in some aspects, they are good in others. The entire land currently in the hands of the Shudra class was once theirs. Even today, if one of them is called up in a case and asked, they will not lie. If asked why this is not yours, they will simply say that the possession rights belong to the others. But if it were our people, they would try to lie a little. Despite having such honesty, they were ruined. Why did they lose their Vedic and administrative authority? At the same time, despite being very low religiously, the Shudra has come to the forefront. Even after all this, why doesn't your self-awareness emerge?

[GV1:P1745] It is not just the glory of the era. We don't get that understanding. We only get what our parents showed us. Isn't it through them that our life itself moves forward? Did we have Vedic authority or scholarly expertise? Then how did we come forward? Be it through some imitation or anything else, when we get it, do we have the sense to stubbornly develop it? How many great souls were born here for us? The Parayi Petta Panthirukulam, the eighteen Siddhars - they were born among these Dravidians. Buddha explained what this is for, and told us to do so-and-so. We couldn't take up a path that was told to us like this for ourselves - even today we can't! Recently in Kerala itself, Sankaracharya, Sree Narayana Guru, and Chattampi Swami came. What have we done? Haven't we divided ourselves in the name of caste, confined it within the caste, put it inside a fence, and poured water? Then what is the meaning of saying we didn't get it? Whatever we get, we must grab it quickly. Isn't this because we lack the stubbornness and zeal to have it?

[GV1:P1746] Despite having administrative and Vedic authority, how did they lose it? It was not discarded by simply stating it was unwanted, was it? You yourselves are aware that there were eighteen *Agraharams* (Brahmin settlements) here. Why do you not consider how these were lost? The fourth quarter is the era of the Shudras. It is not their era. Why are we unable to claim it? We are standing in a lineage where our tradition has ruined us. That is the reason. For example, when mentioning the Palakkad region, you yourselves are aware. You know that there is a practice of consecrating and worshipping (*Vacharadhana*), do you not? We handle this in various ways. Is there not a system in our land of consecrating and worshipping even *Karinkuttichathan*? If this *Karinkuttichathan* becomes our deity, who will we become? Suppose a sorcerer in our family consecrated this; where will this sorcerer stand when he dies? If this ancestor goes astray, who will we, born in that lineage (*Rashi*), become? Then, is there any doubt that our deity and our object of worship—all these aforementioned things—have led us astray? An example of this is that all these Brahmins have reached their current state today. We never performed more than them, did we! We only did trivial things using all this. At the same time, they would step out of the house only after strictly following the procedures using this. What has become of them today? Some may say it is because they performed it incorrectly. Did everyone perform it incorrectly?

[GV1:P1747] What you call imitation is indeed correct. If it were not for this attire and language of the British today, would we have been able to obtain even a single penny from the government? So, we have no attire, no language; are we merely the ones who came to claim ownership of the attire and language of those who belonged to a wretched system? Despite facing such a predicament, why can we not change away from it?

[GV1:P1749] October 1987

[GV1:P1750] I shall recount an experience of mine to you.* There is a difficulty in deceiving you by telling this. That is why I am speaking to you in this manner. If told in any other way, you will not be able to accept it. Several people have come to me. There are a few who have known me since childhood. I was a believer in God. I only knew that. I knew nothing else.

[GV1:P1751] I lived at home until the age of ten or fourteen. I had to commit a deception to leave home. I also knew that it was the only way to leave home. Is there not a custom among us to go to Palani? Stating that a garland and a vow were required for it, I wore them. Thus, I left under the pretext of going to Palani. I went straight to the ashrams. I engaged in various positions within the ashrams. I found no satisfaction from any of this.

[GV1:P1752] My entire desire was to attain a spiritual realization (*Anubhuthi*). It is the Sri Ramakrishna Mission and the Sri Narayana Mission that stand strengthened in Kerala today. I am well-acquainted with both of these. Then there are the lineages of Madhva and Sri Shankara—they do not prove to be of much use to the Shudra class in that manner. Because caste and such are still deeply entrenched there. Therefore, there is no salvation there. Near the very house where I was born, there is an ashram belonging to the Sri Ramakrishna Mission. I was associated with it as well. Apart from that, I spent seventeen years associated with the Sri Narayana Mission and its other temples. Not only was I associated, but I also handled several matters within its administration.

[GV1:P1753] They had arranged the rituals of worship and all other regulations. Whatever this may be, to speak of a realization from this—there was a realization lasting two days. Other than that, there was nothing. Thus, with the desire for a Guru, if I learned that an individual resided anywhere, I would leave the ashram citing some excuse. I would go and observe there. In this manner, I regularly visited a person who sat like an *Avadhuta* for ten years, going there one day a month. I would go stating that I needed to visit one of the ashram's branches. I would go there just for the namesake. Then, during the night, I would sit with this person the whole time. This person lay on the sand at the beach. Despite going for ten years, I gained nothing from this person. It was not because he did not know how to speak; rather, he simply did not speak.

[GV1:P1754] While things were thus, I found a monk through another person. He understood me as soon as I arrived. Yet, he said nothing. He said, "Let it be tomorrow." When I went the next day, he asked, "You are the person who came yesterday, aren't you?" This man also lay on the sand and in the bushes. "Why have you come?" he asked me. I replied in a single word. Saying, "You are the rightful inheritor," he embraced me and wept. He wrote down a mantra for me and said, "You must keep using this. Then realization will occur. You must come here when that happens."

[GV1:P1755] The experience came. I went. Everything is there. But it will take a very long time. I understood nothing. Even after two and a half years, there was no result. Meanwhile, difficulties, hardships, and tribulations were pouring in. I never did anything to warrant that. After this, whatever the experience was, it remained unclear. Aside from it being proven true, I do not know what it is like or how it is.

[GV1:P1756] You will only understand if it is stated as it is. If said in any other way, it will not be clear to you. Therefore, I only recounted my experience. You should pay attention to at least that.

[GV1:P1757] He himself had a desire to grant me a realization somehow. He would say it whenever we met. One day, a situation arose where I had to leave Sivagiri itself. I had not committed any mistake to warrant that either.

[GV1:P1758] Before that, he had shared a word with me. While wandering as an *Avadhuta*, he came there. One day, after the puja was completed, as I came out carrying the offering plate (*thattam*), a person acquainted with me came and said that a Swami was standing there inquiring about me. I immediately handed over the plate and went. He instantly said: "I am going on a journey from here. There is a change for you from here. You must not leave without seeing me."

[GV1:P1759] To leave after saying this out of nowhere! I could not believe it. Because I had been rendering service for so long. And not by taking a single penny. I had been there for such a long time. How could I leave from there? Even if asked to leave, would I muster the courage to go?

[GV1:P1761] November 1987

[GV1:P1762] When left with no other choice*, I moved away, built a hut, and stayed there for seven years and four months. In the fourth month, on the first day of the *Vrischikam* month, seven people arrived. They came carrying all kinds of food items in their hands. They said, "We are observing a vow here today." Based on what they went and told others, eight to ten people arrived the next day. In this manner, within that month itself, the situation became such that nearly a hundred people were arriving daily. They claimed that their diseases and troubles would be cured. This was the knowledge gained from what they said. Furthermore, peace was also visible in all those who came. After continuing like this for about two and a half years, it ceased to yield results.

[GV1:P1763] The spiritual experience occurred at the Thuckalay Munsiff Court. It took approximately three years to complete. All the demons associated with the completion of the Trimurti system—whatever names are spoken—they are all present. What we have heard of in this world is very little. What comes before us is in the crores. All these do indeed exist. But what spiritual strength will this impart to us? Apart from obtaining a result when offering certain vows and oblations, when one transforms into a human being with spiritual experiences, what realization is gained from it? For its spiritual peace. This became clear to me. It is said in the Gita itself—Dharma is that which is directly perceivable, is it not! Standing materialized and imparting knowledge, and having received guidance in such a manner, I became convinced that this is the truth. After becoming convinced, the question arose as to how to manage this. When it was managed, it was completely fruitful. Not a single syllable failed to bear fruit. This was effective for hundreds of people. It was not managed by me alone. Regarding the ailments, those that were given up by the Medical College came and were completely cured. Even bladder cancer was cured. If this is spoken of, people will naturally come! Following this, it became ineffective. People suddenly began to hurl abuses. There was no information as to what it was. Investigations were made through all possible means of inquiry. It did not become clear. At that time, a word was received. The two lines currently chanted, "Om Sri Karunakaraguru Parabrahmanane Namaha / Om Sri Karunakaraguru Satyapradaya Namaha" were stated, and it was said: "You must chant this and strengthen yourself. Otherwise, harm will befall you." It was not understood. My name comes within this. Because the name appeared, I told the children who received it not to chant it. Since they had received it through revelation, they would chant it without my knowledge—without making a sound.

[GV1:P1764] After three years, there was a relocation from this place to another place—the place currently occupied. It was only after being told three times not to stay here that the move there occurred. It was instructed that one should not reside there in a manner visible to two people. Today, there is nothing there. It has simply become barren land. It lies like a withered, grass-covered expanse on the sloped area of the hill.

[GV1:P1765] A few days after arriving here, a large number of people started coming. Normally, such gatherings do not occur at Hindu places of worship. But this was indeed a massive crowd. People just began arriving in that manner. Suddenly, it reverted to the old state. The reason for this was unknown. What was instructed had not been violated. It was said that an error had occurred. If an error had occurred, why could it not be pointed out? The number of people who arrived was overwhelmingly large. If necessary, it was enough to cause harm to the Ashram itself. There were prominent merchants. There were those who came from high social standings.

[GV1:P1766] They were residing on this rocky ground, enduring the dew, rain, sun, and wind. It was for their ailments to be cured. There were no other buildings anywhere here. There was something akin to a small marquee. How many could sleep inside it? Yet, all of them kept coming like this. However, they had faith in me—in this work of mine. Regardless, I told them one thing: I will only come out after understanding this. You must take care of these patients. There were mentally ill individuals, those with stomach pain, and those with various types of diseases. Having said this, I went inside and sat down. All these patients became violently agitated. Those with stomach pain started screaming terribly. The mentally ill, since there were no trees here, went to climb and hang themselves on the trees in the adjacent property. In this manner, some fifty or sixty individuals became agitated in this state. Those who ran away were chased down and brought back.

[GV1:P1767] That evening at five o'clock, an announcement was made that food should not be consumed. It was said that even water should not be drunk. There were two merchants. Saying, "Now water cannot be drunk, such a rule has come," they went to the well, drew water, and drank it. Five minutes later, they vomited. What they vomited was poison—like something mixed with green color being poured out. Swelling also developed. When two others went outside, they received two blows—from where, it was unknown. Terrified, everyone remained inside. This was the incident of that day.

[GV1:P1768] That evening, permission was given to consume food. The announcement came: "I will come when it is five minutes to six o'clock. You must all be ready for prayer." It was done accordingly. On that very day, three patients were instructed to act in a specific manner. They were cured. Thus, within fifteen days, all these ailments were completely cured.

[GV1:P1769] Then, a journey was instructed. Among the journeys undertaken in that manner, one proceeded up to Chidambaram, the largest temple in South India, but it was not continued thereafter. Walking continuously from Kanyakumari through this region, Chidambaram was reached. Even after arriving there, there was nothing to impart. It was decided, "I will not go anywhere anymore."

[GV1:P1770] Guruvani

[GV1:P1771] December 1987

[GV1:P1772] There was an occasion of becoming bewildered after receiving visions. An astrological consultation was conducted to find out why such bewilderment was occurring, and it was found that while standing under the deity, only that much could be done. A visit was made to the astrologer, along with Parameswaran Pillai. There was a belief that some particular state of affairs had taken hold, and that it would change.

[GV1:P1773] The visit to the astrologer was made yielding to compulsion. The astrologer cast one or two zodiacal signs. The Bhrigu Samhita is used to ascertain the astrological calculations based on the zodiac. The Bhrigu Samhita is recorded in the form of a dialogue between a Guru and a disciple. According to it, what was seen was that he is a celibate, a perfect individual. A mistake caused by a woman in some past life is what is reflecting now.

[GV1:P1774] The experience was also the same—because of this woman, there were constant quarrels and commotions. It was believed that this was indeed true. The Bhrigu Samhita was not read completely. Only an approximation had been read. Therefore, the remaining part could not be understood. It stated in it that nothing should be done for two years. For these two and a half years, nothing was done. After that, it was impossible to stay there. It became necessary to leave that place.

[GV1:P1775] It was from there that the residence at Santhigiri in Pothencode began. Nine months after coming and residing there, this became clear again. Instruction was given to act. It was done. When it was done, bewilderment ensued. Even then, this woman was present. She would speak falsely through visions. She would tell lies in the manner of the most deceitful ascetic. How did this girl, who was only about nineteen or twenty years old, obtain this deceitful secret? There must be some deceit within her. Otherwise, there is no need for her to say this. I am a person who has travelled with an ascetic who had attained numerous avadhuta states. How did she acquire this falsehood that I cannot even conceive of? It could not be grasped. She was laying a snare and encircling. I distanced myself without falling into her trap, like iron and butter. I was very cautious.

[GV1:P1776] That was the truth. It took another four years for that to become clear. All this time, she was also following behind. A falsehood that she was Madurai Meenakshi. The parents said that she had a disease associated with the worship of Madurai Meenakshi. It was with the plea to save her somehow that she was brought. But she had come to kill. Taking me along to her house in Chirayinkeezhu, she claimed that the heat of the homam performed there still remained. That the heat of a homam performed eight or ten generations ago still remained!

[GV1:P1777] Upon reflection, what was revealed was a Brahmin woman. When trying to catch her, she would hide behind someone. She was the one who instructed to place the Rudraksha. When asked what kind of Rudraksha should be placed, she told us to ask the disciples. We asked. Then it was said that an old man and an old woman reside to the southeast of the Changanassery market, and that it could be obtained if we went there. We took the car and went. Approaching the Vazhappally temple, we saw a Vedic priest (*Vaidikavadhyar*). When asked, he said there was such a house. Without seeing him, this could not have been known. He showed the way. We proceeded accordingly, and after travelling a distance, the person who had the vision suddenly asked to stop the vehicle. The instruction regarding that woman was that a person with a dark mark on the tip of the nose could be seen, and if asked, he would know. When asked, he showed us the house. [GV1:P1823] How did the precise determination of the Kali Yuga become impossible?

[GV1:P1824] Long before the advent of Hinduism, the Earth had already undergone the transition of twenty-five *Chaturyugas*. One might ask whether *Chaturyugas* existed prior to these twenty-five *Chaturyugas*. They indeed did. That was the *Chaturyuga* system observed in the Manu tradition. It is divinely ordained.

[GV1:P1825] An inadvertent error has precipitated prolonged calamities. This devastation escalated and ultimately destroyed the cyclical resilience inherent in the concepts of 'Bharatiya', 'Hindu', and 'Sanatana'. These adversities were dormant only during the first three *Chaturyugas* of the current *Manvantara* (Vaivasvata Manvantara). To rectify this error, a new mandate emerged in the fourth *Chaturyuga*. That is, the corrective action commenced from the seventh *Chaturyuga*. By the eleventh *Chaturyuga* of this *Manvantara*, the Trinity system (*Trimurti Sampradaya*) was completely formalized.

[GV1:P1826] The lineage of Manu was flawless. Until today, numerous attempts have been made in various guises to rectify the inadvertent error. It did not succeed. Furthermore, it paved the way for numerous imaginative speculations. With the influx of these speculative fantasies, the functional capacity required for accurate chronological determination was lost. The Trinity system (*Trimurti Sampradaya*) was meticulously managed through the tenth *Chaturyuga* of this *Manvantara*—utilizing yoga, law, and the calculation of the six foundational chakras (*Adharas*). Yet, the lost capacity for action could not be reclaimed.

[GV1:P1827] Of the nine realms (*Navamandalas*) described, seven possess form. The remaining two exist in a manner capable of centralizing form. It constitutes a cyclical phenomenon entangled with Rahu, Ketu, and Saturn. When the prescribed duties associated with the seven heavens representing the seven realms were established, the Satya Yuga progressed truthfully. However, the majesty of nature, which shared dominion over the remaining three epochs, altered its temporal course. This deviation gave rise to the ideological propagation characterizing Kali Yuga as a period of absolute destruction. This propagating argument continues to persist even today. That is well-known to everyone. The multitude of speculative narratives already constructed through the refined language (Sanskrit) is innumerable. A perilous trap, wherein the capacity for action could not align with Dharma across various instances, paved the way for the very destruction of time. Consequently, Kali became categorized as an epochal duty defined by destruction.

[GV1:P1828] We cannot progress by denying what actually exists. The operational capacity we have internalized thus far is the cumulative anomaly of the twenty-one *Chaturyugas* that have transpired. It has become so entangled that no one can grasp it anywhere. Consequently, both the learned and the unlearned have drowned alike, losing all chronological accuracy. Crores of great souls who emerged to operate for brief periods have sunk in the uncertainty of this epoch. As Hinduism was formalized in this manner, the *Sanatana* essence was lost. As a result of concluding without knowing where to begin, an ignorance arose in the writings praising the six-faced god (Kartikeya)—claiming that when asked the meaning of *Omkara*, the face of wisdom was pinched off due to ignorance. On a path traversed in such a manner, Kali reached a position bereft of Dharma; Kali became synonymous with destruction.

[GV1:P1829] We must specifically comprehend the Dharma of Kali. However, the evaluation of a transitional state—which lost its entire functional capacity due to the perpetual categorization of Kali as an era of absolute destruction, staggering in an arena devoid of Dharma—is what annihilated the Dharma of Kali. [GV1:P1835] Know What the Truth Is

[GV1:P1836] (When the biography of the Guru, titled "Through the Karmic Realm of Sacrifice" prepared by the lineage of disciples, was read aloud, for its completion,

[GV1:P1837] the words spoken by the Guru)

[GV1:P1838] What we have observed thus far is a prevailing resolve to instantly destroy the life of a great soul the moment they are born, regardless of whether the household is worthy or not. Therefore, this birth is kept concealed as the Brahman itself. Doctrinal theories insist that a great soul must be born as an emperor of emperors. However, when questioned about the logical justification of such a doctrine, we mostly encounter a karmic inadequacy that leaves one speechless.

[GV1:P1839] Numerous great souls have emerged since Sree Krishna. All of them arrived with the advent of another doctrine. In short, Vyasa, numerous prophets born as world teachers, and the similarly originated *Parayi Petta Panthirukulam* (the twelve tribes born to the Pariah woman) have defined this emergence. When studying the theological doctrines constructed by the Hindu *dharma* to confine everything within the divine tradition, one perceives an illusion as if a method of deception was bestowed by God Himself. What kind of an event was the very birth of Krishna?

[GV1:P1840] Before the birth of Krishna, the seven children born to that mother were beaten to death. The eighth one could not be caught, and therefore, was not killed. The story-weavers claim that even though Putana was sent for this purpose, she was destroyed. Looked at from this perspective, whether born as a supreme emperor or in a cow shed, whether born in a hut or a palace without distinction, the karmic saga endured by these great souls has been sung by poets in rhetorical embellishments, disconnected entirely from their actual lives.

[GV1:P1841] If one examines the great souls who arrived after Sree Krishna, it is evident that their very lives have been toyed with. The profound ignorance of the scholar who presents this as a unique narrative is not insignificant. When viewed through the lens of the epochal *dharma*, their lives have been so excessively eulogized that the truth is obscured, making it impossible to establish historical chronology. This becomes clear upon examining the long list of poetic imaginations adorned with both praise and condemnation. The foremost example of this is the life of Sree Krishna himself.

[GV1:P1842] Concealing the evidence that Sree Krishna arrived as a Guru, millions of stories have been woven portraying him as a deity. By transforming Krishna into a god and preserving the Gopis as *devadasis* (servants of god) in a manner that eradicates his identity as a Guru, reality has been obfuscated through the acquired, *dharma*-less tales born from the rhetorical flair of eminent poets, thereby displacing *dharma* and squandering *karma*. In order to fabricate the narrative that Vyasa lived contemporaneously with Krishna, Vyasa was specially bestowed with the appellation 'Krishna Dwaipayana'.

[GV1:P1843] Dwaraka submerged. When Arjuna, following Krishna's instructions, gathered everyone and departed from there, forest bandits looted everything from him. It is recorded that they slaughtered many and spared Arjuna. At that juncture, Vyasa is reported to have said: you were able to utilize the boons of the gods, along with the bow and arrows obtained from them, only while the Lord was present. Now, let us proceed to embrace asceticism. It is a known fact to all that these events are said to have occurred in the region where Gujarat is currently situated.

[GV1:P1844] Observing from then until now, the births of all great souls following Krishna's era resemble hidden arrows. Because Buddha was born into a royal lineage, he remained silent without doing anything initially. Eventually, when he became a Bodhisattva, he was killed by being fed pork. Similarly, it is said that Jyothiramalinga departed in his physical body, leaving only a lamp behind. Those who wrote the story of Rama many epochs ago state that he abandoned his physical body in the river, while poetic imagination suggests he was taken away in a chariot to some unknown realm. The story of attaining *Jalasamadhi* (merging with water) is also told regarding Ramatirtha.

[GV1:P1845] Thus, whoever became a Shudra by birth and a Dvija (twice-born) by action, all of them have been destroyed in this manner, even reducing them to mere poets. What exactly is the history of Kabirdas? Even though it was conveniently written that he was a disciple of Swami Ramadas, no one knows what purpose that suffering served. Here too, they have been defeated by fabricated narratives. What was Kabir's devotion to his Guru? "Even if all the trees that have grown strong to date and those yet to come in the world were made into pens, and all the oceans into ink, writing with them would still leave the Guru's greatness inexhaustible"—this was Kabir's devotion to his Guru.

[GV1:P1846] When examining the historical presence of great souls, the exceedingly rare stories written about them have subjected them to the karmic flaw of miracles, completely destroying all their experiential truths in an ocean without water (making them incomprehensible). We must carefully discern the underlying motive behind writing and preserving the stories of Moses, Buddha, Jesus, and the Prophet, who came after Krishna. It is these fabricated miraculous deeds that the poor intellectuals have been manipulated to propagate. When speaking of realization or philosophical vision, apart from being recorded as the light of the world, the embodiment of light, or an abundance of sermons, there too, it is the gods who have been glorified.

[GV1:P1847] The truth regarding the births of Moses and Jesus has been veiled in a way that renders it unrecognizable. Even the portion assigning the karmic purpose to recount Jesus's sacrifice has been distorted. If there is evidence for the claims that the Prophet who came after Jesus was chased away by the people, that the mountain was set on fire, that upon the fire extinguishing he descended and ate roasted leather, and that he proclaimed 'Alas, it is the Jinn who rule the world'—then why has the exact location of that great man's resting place (Samadhi) not been fully revealed? In reality, upon witnessing the demonic power of these Jinn, he simply sat down in that very graveyard. Once seated in one place, natural bodily excretions would be evident for seven or eight days. Eventually, his existence concluded there. In spite of all this, where was that profound sorrow taken and appeased? Without even establishing that historical truth to serve as a reminder, today they attempt to express devotion in a language far more severe than the Hindus. Having ostensibly bestowed sanctity upon that great man's life through such a path of devotion, the realms of sacrifice have been preserved as lands of miracles, in a manner that makes it impossible for us to comprehend or collectively preserve them.

[GV1:P1848] What will become of our children who inherit such karmic flaws?

[GV1:P1849] From Lord Krishna to the present day, no one has been spared. After the time of the great souls, who can resolve the karmic affliction that preserves them merely as miraculous phenomena? Is this not the wicked obsession of demonic forces that refuse to embrace the karma of this land of sacrifice?

[GV1:P1850] The miraculously decisive dharma, which demonstrates the boundless excellence of yoga and karma by categorizing them into Yoga, Bhakti, Karma, and Jnana, has been attempted to be depicted through Lord Krishna and Swami Vivekananda. What can be done about the so-called champions of dharma who cause intellectual decay by engaging in arguments in the names of Sri Shankara, Chattampi Swami, and Narayana Guru, who were born in Kerala? They have reduced the people to mere puppets and thrust them under a veil of blindness. Hatred based on caste, religion, and class has grown within them to such an extent that even God's forgiveness would be inadequate.

[GV1:P1851] The blue sky is a colorless color that transcends the seven realms known as the realms of knowledge (Jnanabhumika) or ignorance. Today's path of action has been reached through the advancement of science, which has documented the theoretical trajectories of the nine planets in a language accessible to both scholars and laymen. Science has become fragmented, reaching a stage where it can neither be fully quantified nor defined. Modern aeronautical science is in this state. Scientists must contemplate whether we truly need these discoveries, given such names, which possess the potential to destroy the entire earth like the acts of lunatics. What is achieved by measuring the size and weight of every planet? What branch of wisdom is going to emanate from that? What else can be derived from it, other than the path of action that turns a goat into a dog, as the ancients used to say? Having traveled in a manner that never attains true consciousness in life, wearing absurd disguises, abandoning the language of true scholarly eminence, and fostering a culture dressed in ambiguous forms that serves up intellect-killing actions—what can be said to these utter fools? We have nothing to do with such baseless tales that cultivate this kind of absurd humor. We also know that this is a failure of our daily lives. Do we not need at least one good vision...?

[GV1:P1852] Will a realm of action (karmabhumika) emerge if the karma to be realized through life is lost by merely singing, speaking, and writing about it excessively? Is there anything else to this beyond an intellect that obeys or forces obedience through rules? Are all these spectacles we see merely stages for the play of good and evil, where the words of God are intellectualized? Who does not know that this nurtures and corrupts the multitudes of people who do not know how to behave, realizing that all this is a consequence of the errors of the Yugadharma (the dharma of the age)?

[GV1:P1853] Who does not know that only what the courts construct by swearing in the name of God will prevail? What has the legacy of those ignorant creators made of us—these wretched human figures they have created, who behave like war-mongering beasts, trying to choose good and evil through figures like brigadiers? It is by making us believe that this is global governance that dharma is being presented to us. I ask you again, what else is there in the world other than each person bearing the burden of sins, born from the errors of the Yugadharma, according to their own capacity and strength? Understand this dynamically and reflect!
