[GV1:P1952] August 1988

[GV1:P1953] To rectify the errors that emerged in the novelty of antiquity and the antiquity of novelty, numerous great souls have incarnated on earth across various eras, known by different names such as prophets and avatars. It is evident that they all functioned in accordance with their respective times. When speaking of time, life itself constitutes a temporal span even for an ant. Similarly, for the animal kingdom, life is a dimension of time. This principle applies to everything from a mere blade of grass to the sprawling banyan tree, which achieves the absolute fullness of life within its species. The ancients utilize the banyan tree metaphorically in this exact sense. The fundamental reason for their growth is the presence of life. Contingent upon the variations of space and time, the cycle of growth, sustenance, and destruction is inherent not only in human beings but across all living creatures. Intelligence, too, manifests with distinct variations among them. What is the cause of this?

[GV1:P1954] Plants and trees are uprooted prematurely, and human beings face untimely demise. Those who perish in wars, those who lie waiting for death, and those who end their lives by hanging are all included in this paradigm. This encompasses those who believe that all these possess life, those who believe in the existence or non-existence of the power of sin, the intelligent and the unintelligent, the scientific scholars who consider themselves to have attained the pinnacle of intellect, and above all, the path of action, agency, and execution that operates without instruments or mediums—not merely on this earth but across the nine celestial spheres—directing the essence of the atomic life of the *Panchakoshas* (five sheaths), which has evolved through the five elements and is channeled into the five senses, configuring its distinct nature.

[GV1:P1955] When knowledge becomes subjugated to the lower nature,

[GV1:P1956] A fraction of a second feels like a thousand years.

[GV1:P1957] As stated by Narayana Guru, there can be no doubt for scientific or biological theorists that science would require thousands of years to thoroughly evaluate the virtues and vices of life encompassed within the evolutionary theory of the *Panchakoshas* of life. The process by which such an expansive operation of life creates wonders before humanity, most visibly through the earth, the sun, and the moon, is evident even to the most ignorant. Through the passage of eras, one can deduce that everyone—from demons who possess a subtle understanding of the potential of action extending to *Moola Ganapathi*, the lord of the foundational forces spanning from the elemental entities to the stellar constellations, to the *Vethalas*, the indwelling demigods who have attained the celestial realms, and even up to the holy Trinity (*Trimurti*)—is equally subject to pleasure and sorrow.

[GV1:P1958] The time referred to here is not the time mentioned earlier. The culmination of time occurs in terms of *Manvantaras*. The epoch of one *Manu* is documented as consisting of seventy-one *Chaturyugas*. The seventh *Manvantara* among these is the *Vaivasvata Manvantara*. We are currently in *Kali*, the fourth quarter of its twenty-eighth *Chaturyuga*. The *Dharma* (duty/righteousness) of the *Kaliyuga*, which is considered the fourth quarter (the others being *Satyayuga*, *Tretayuga*, and *Dvaparayuga*), is to contemplate and evaluate the virtues and sins accumulated through the actions of the preceding two *Yugas*, and to execute the actions as ordained by that divine (*Brahman*) resolve. This has been incorporated into the designated karma of the *Shudra* class. The term '*Shudra* class' denotes the ignorant, the despised, the lowly, and the caste-fanatics extending down to the *Chandala*. There was a system of karma that regulated even food consumption. The trajectory of karma that resulted in the categorization of emperors, kings, and Brahmins as the rulers not just of India but of the world, was a modern diversion of this. Although it is stated that the potent trajectory of all these karmas is destined to fall upon the *Shudra*, it is not easy to evaluate and articulate the ignorance that ensues when knowledge and capability fall into the hands of the world's *Chandalas*, who do not even understand for whom this is intended.

[GV1:P1959] This is because, when it fell into the hands of the ignorant *Shudra* class, and the context of the coming together of the Dravidian and the Aryan arose, bringing with it a succession of wars, victories, and defeats akin to karmic prowess, it is not difficult to observe that both the Dravidian and the Aryan equally harmonized their dedication, reliance, karma, and dharma—not merely in India but globally—to attain the true deity of fortune through the traditional system of divine worship. It has been proven that the most suitable lineage for this is the *Shudra* class. A proof of this lies in the divine voice (*Ashariri*) that occurred even prior to Sri Krishna's birth, warning that despite giving birth to him, he should not rule as a subordinate to the emperor. Since the king of that time could not be made to declare this, Krishna demonstrated it through his actions by slaying him and assuming the role of the rightful heir. It is in the sense that Krishna, who stood at the absolute forefront of divine status, embodied every deity, sage, ascetic, active participant, devotee, and prophet who had appeared until then, that the phrase "*Yatra Yatra Yogeshvara Krishna*" is uttered. In the visionary doctrine known as *Yugadharma*, asserting a prominent position, Sri Krishna profoundly and authoritatively expounded upon the duties of the age through the eighteen chapters of the *Gita*, while preceptors, gods, and sages provided an intimation of the future.

[GV1:P1960] Numerous prophets, gurus, and the lineage of the *Parayi Petta Panthirukulam* who came thereafter have vindicated this. It is evident that figures from the more recent past, such as Sri Shankara, Narayana Guru, and Chattampi Swami, emerged with distinct ideological missions. Whether they successfully achieved them or not is beside the point. Sri Shankara propounded Advaita, Madhvacharya advocated Dvaita, and Thiruvalluvar poetically championed the concept of 'One Caste, One Race, One God.' Chattampi Swami authored and completed the *Vedadhikara Nirupanam* to dismantle the ritualistic sections (*Karmakanda*) of the Vedic religion. Narayana Guru functioned practically, striving to elevate humanity through action.

[GV1:P1961] The dharma referred to here is the *Dharma* of the *Kaliyuga*. Whether a *Chandala*, a Brahmin, or anyone in between, the *Shudra* has advanced by acting in a way that makes him forget his own karma, merit, and prowess, which are essential for humans, as well as for the departed sages and gods, to attain liberation and virtue. The ultimate reward for a god or a sage thus far has been liberation. In order for this very same outcome to be realized for the entire *Shudra* class, an act in accordance with divine providence is outlined below. It proclaims a truth that is indispensable not just for a householder, but for absolutely everyone.

[GV1:P1962] The rationalist and the salvation-seeker, stricken by paralysis, are swaying unconsciously after consuming poisonous liquor to the brim. Each of us is a human being embodying moral decay, trying to pose as a scientist or a research scholar. This is because they are petty creatures who mix up the scientific and the unscientific without hesitation, eager to denounce each of the aforementioned. Today's rational beings, operating without distinction between the scholar and the ignorant, losing both *karma* and *dharma*, are like plants uprooted from a gymnasium. Consequently, the scholar, the ignorant, and everyone else caught between them are eradicating their lifespans within this vortex. To escape from this, I am utilizing this occasion to inform you of a clear and resolute matter.

[GV1:P1963] Discovered through states described as ethereal, manifest, and luminous, a path of karmic resolution is taking place here. This path enables one to act and cause others to act benevolently for all living beings in the world, while seeking the cessation of sorrow in my twenty-nine years of life. The *Guru Margam* (Path of the Guru) advised at Santhigiri is the greatest path of resolution, which, through a life of obedience according to the divine will (*Brahmanishchayam*), removes sorrow, brings merit through action, and carefully preserves *dharma* as its foundation. This *dharmic* life, which must be acquired with vigilance, is meant to reach not just humans but all living beings, by making each person enact the chapters of *dharma* that span from the atom to the infinite in the universe, thereby realizing it within oneself. It not only allows us to preserve it in our actions by theorizing the evolutionary paths of the solar system that we previously pervaded, but it has also become capable of achieving the complete realization of the lineage. Its detailed explanation is not to be publicized but only spoken of in person. Informing you that the medium that helps all people, forgetting caste or religion, to arrive at the singular doctrine of humanity is something you can trust and inspire trust in, and wishing you eternal peace so that this auspicious day may benefit you by enabling you to progress through it and, if necessary, making yourself worthy of liberation,

[GV1:P1964] Your Swami

[GV1:P1965] Birthday Message - An Appendix

============================================================

GURUVANIKAL · August 1988 · Volume 1
Malayalam source paragraphs GV1:P1966 to GV1:P2285
English line for line; each paragraph carries its Malayalam source number.

[GV1:P1966] August 1988

[GV1:P1967] Disciple: What can we, who have no knowledge about such a profound subject,

[GV1:P1968] understand? How can we understand?

[GV1:P1969] Guru: The fact that such a matter exists in the world is known at least to a few among the Hindus.

[GV1:P1970] It has been spoken about a little at a time, on multiple occasions, by various people.

[GV1:P1971] Disciple: Who are they?

[GV1:P1972] Guru: Sri Krishna is the one who comes foremost.

[GV1:P1973] Disciple: What the Guru just said is not entirely clear. It would be helpful if you could

[GV1:P1974] elaborate on it.

[GV1:P1975] Guru: The first evidence is indeed that even before Sri Krishna's birth, Kamsa received

[GV1:P1976] a notification in accordance with the divine will. Along with that, Kamsa felt inclined to deny it because the royal authority of the *Shudra* class lacked humility. Wherever the *Shudra* class has attained royal power, it has been like that.

[GV1:P1977] Disciple: Knowing that he would lose his life upon hearing the ethereal voice, wasn't Kamsa's action a primitive aggression for survival,

[GV1:P1978] rather than a mere denial?

[GV1:P1979] Guru: Once it is seen as divine will, how can it be an aggression for survival?

[GV1:P1980] What Kamsa displayed was something inherent in the oppressive nature of royal authority. The arrogance of not knowing what constitutes the gentle or the virtuous. That is the ignorance of the *Shudra*. Later, Buddhism emerged. It was the *Shudra* class within it who completely denied it with the help of the Brahmins.

[GV1:P1981] During Sri Krishna's time, the state administration was in the hands of the *Shudra*, wasn't it? Even within Sri Krishna's Yadava clan, the lack of humility and wisdom to respect the gentle and the virtuous later surfaced. Isn't making Samba dress as a woman and incurring the sage's curse evidence of this? With that, didn't the Yadava clan fight among themselves and perish?

[GV1:P1982] Wherever you go, you can see that the *Shudra* remains the same even today. Even though Sri Krishna came as such a great personality in the past, and granted that the Brahmins or all these *varnas* glorify Sri Krishna—don't we have good evidence that they still could not truly respect him?

[GV1:P1983] Disciple: Could you elaborate a bit more on the evidence that they did not respect

[GV1:P1984] him?

[GV1:P1985] Guru: Without accepting Sri Krishna's words that those who worship the ancestors go to the ancestral realm, those who worship the deities

[GV1:P1986] go to the realm of deities, and those who worship me will attain me, the Vedic religion was re-established in Sri Krishna temples. Imposing a Vaishnava nature on Sri Krishna, the Vedic religion, which did not hesitate to draw a sacred thread around Sri Krishna's neck, performed all sorts of mockeries here! Can't you guess? As for the clan in which Sri Krishna was born, even though Sri Krishna became a king, they still remain in the status of Harijans today. They have not been able to respect that clan either. In South India, so many people belonging to the Harijan or *Shudra* class held administrative power. Cheraman Perumal was one such person. Pulayanarkotta stands as evidence for that.

[GV1:P1987] I have heard that a fisherwoman whose illness Sri Ramakrishna cured was a woman of royal stature. This woman was a devotee of Kodungallur. Unable to enter temples in Bengal, she came here to Kodungallur. Here, the idol could be seen up close. One day, the Goddess showed her in a dream: "Why do you come here; can't you place me there?" Thus, she immediately had a form of Bhadra sculpted. After it was sculpted, she realized that a Brahmin had to consecrate it, not her. So, she kept the sculpted form safely in a box. She had another dream, instructing her to have Sri Ramakrishna Deva perform the consecration.

[GV1:P1988] This woman fell ill. Her husband was a Brahmin. If a royal woman dies, a Brahmin cannot remain there. Hence, he met Sri Ramakrishna and expressed his sorrow. Within a few days, she recovered. She had vomiting and diarrhea. The Swami caught it. He was bedridden for three months. When such great historical truths exist, why are you asking all this? There would be so many similar things to say.

[GV1:P1989] Disciple: Are you saying it is because of an inability to respect Buddha

[GV1:P1990] ?

[GV1:P1991] Guru: It is not about the inability to respect Buddha. Because he was a king,

[GV1:P1992] everyone accepted him. For instance, Emperor Ashoka allowed his own children to work for the cause. With that, it became the norm that celibates (*Brahmacharis*) could operate anywhere. Buddhism spread in India and abroad. For about eight hundred years, Buddhism remained in power. The followers of the Vedic religion waited. For convenience, some *Shudra Brahmacharis* in Buddhism abandoned their celibacy. Consequently, not only did the people turn against them, but the Kshatriyas and the Brahmins who aligned with them collaborated to use the *Shudra* class itself to beat and drive away Buddhism.

[GV1:P1993] Once the Buddhists retreated, bad rumors spread about them. Many Buddhists were indeed killed. Moreover, in their places of worship, instead of the eulogies of Buddha, they consecrated Bhadrakali and created rituals like *Vela*, *Padayani*, and *Poora-idi*. Don't you know about the offering called *Poora-idi*, where young maidens carry *Thalappoli* around the temple, and they set up mortars and pestles, pound turmeric and charcoal together, and scatter everything around amidst frantic dancing, drumbeats (*chenda*), and a demonic atmosphere? All of these were implemented here by the rulers who came after Shankaracharya.

[GV1:P1994] Disciple: Before Shankaracharya?

[GV1:P1995] Guru: I mentioned earlier that Buddhism existed here for eight hundred years.

[GV1:P1996] Remains of Buddhist *viharas* glorifying the attributes of Buddha have been excavated from many places in Kerala itself. When faced with opposition, those among the followers of Buddha who had wealth, capacity, and resources fled to countries like Ceylon and China.

[GV1:P1997] Then some physicians remained here. The reason is that a physician cannot be created overnight, right? There were also a few administrative personnel. The Ezhavas or Chekavars were the military commanders here, the administrators of that time. Later, untouchability and caste discrimination were introduced and implemented here in order to destroy them.

[GV1:P1998] Disciple: It is said that Shankaracharya created the caste system, right?

[GV1:P1999] Guru: Shankaracharya had to collude in this and do many things.

[GV1:P2000] It was done to prevent the remaining people from being beaten to death. Advaita was introduced with the concept that all should live as the children of one father. However, it was not implemented because it was impossible to step down into the impurity and work. The followers have written extensively to make it appear that the *Varna Dharmas* were prescribed by Sankaracharya. Adi Shankara did not do that.

[GV1:P2001] Disciple: Can it be said that all this was ordained by God?

[GV1:P2002] Guru: No, it was not ordained by God. When there was a lack of people with administrative or martial capabilities, they created untouchability by making the Shudra class fight among themselves.

[GV1:P2003] Disciple: In places like Kannur, Thalassery, and Kozhikode, the Brahmins who embraced Buddhism

[GV1:P2004] were ostracized and degraded. The degraded Brahmins are the Thiyyas. This is what Kerala history states. Is this what the Guru is also saying?

[GV1:P2005] Guru: Exactly that. Later, when the Malabar rebellion occurred, the thugs prepared to harass the Thiyyas. Again, a number of people belonging to their community fled to Coorg. Many men were hacked to death. It was mostly the women who fled.

[GV1:P2006] Thus, the Ezhavas were degraded in every way and transformed into an untouchable caste. Some were included in the Harijan category. The rest became the poor, the farmers, and the physician families. Out of necessity. Those who faced such severe untouchability, those without formal knowledge, became physicians. Sanskrit became their own—how did the Sanskrit of the Brahmins reach those who were considered unapproachable and untouchable? Reading history reveals that physicians emerged among the Nairs only within the last three hundred years. The Nair community itself did not exist. The scholars later wrote and created sixty-four sub-sects within the Nairs themselves. Aren't Valappat Maman Vaidyar and Kakkanat Vaidyar, who came from the Ezhava tradition, renowned? How did this happen?

[GV1:P2007] Disciple: In the olden days, the appellation Harijan did not exist, did it, Guru?

[GV1:P2008] Wasn't it Gandhi who popularized such an appellation?

[GV1:P2009] Guru: Harijan means belonging to Vishnu or belonging to God, doesn't it?

[GV1:P2010] In that sense, weren't those in Krishna's lineage at that time the people of Hari themselves? Weren't the people of Hari left unrespected even then?

[GV1:P2011] Disciple: Wasn't it in the name of Rama that Gandhi surrendered himself and performed his actions?

[GV1:P2012] Guru: Gandhi held firmly to the name of Rama and the concept of Ramarajya.

[GV1:P2013] That was a mistake made by Gandhi. Are not Rama and Ramarajya, which became obsolete due to the Yugadharma (the duty of the age), belonging to the Treta Yuga? As a result of going after worship, Gandhi's mission remained unfulfilled. His organization did not listen to his words. Despite being such a sacrificial figure, not only did India fail to respect or obey that man's words, but he was also shot dead. And that too was done by a Brahmin. If Mahatmaji had been a Brahmin, perhaps he would not have been shot. Is not this much evidence enough to completely expose the statesmanship here?

[GV1:P2014] Disciple: For a moral culture to emerge in a manner suited to the times,

[GV1:P2015] what should be done?

[GV1:P2016] Guru: What must be done has come through Sri Krishna and Buddha.

[GV1:P2017] It has also come through the Parayi petta panthirukulam (the twelve clans born to the Pariah woman). The eighteen Siddhars belonged to all clans, starting from Brahmin, Kshatriya, and Vaishya. Was it not Thiruvalluvar, who said 'Ondre Kulam Oruvane Devan' (One caste, one clan), who belonged to them? The *Thirukkural* of such a Thiruvalluvar stands very strongly as the core of Vedanta. It is also a part of knowledge. With the scholars' method of closing their eyes and creating darkness, isn't all this equivalent to having gone into the dustbin?

[GV1:P2018] In libraries in America and Europe, the Gita, the Bible, and the Quran may hold the first position. Does that mean that Christians in Britain and America as a whole will accept the Quran or the Hindus? Will they obey?

[GV1:P2019] Disciple: Are you suggesting that the public generally enjoys the Gita and the Thirukkural

[GV1:P2020] merely as literary forms?

[GV1:P2021] Guru: What is the doubt in that?

[GV1:P2022] Disciple: Can you suggest a path that can be

[GV1:P2023] followed by humanity as a whole?

[GV1:P2024] Guru: Are not the things that existed in the past

[GV1:P2025] applicable to humanity?

[GV1:P2026] Disciple: Distinct from them, do you have anything to suggest that does not lead to religious hatred

[GV1:P2027] and makes human cooperation more evident?

[GV1:P2028] Guru: In principle, there is something to suggest. If we do not discard it

[GV1:P2029] as we did in the past, an authoritative step towards permanent existence for the entire world is being implemented through our current ideology. Our beginning is from where Narayana Guru, Buddha, and Krishna left off.

[GV1:P2030] Disciple: How is that? I do not understand.

[GV1:P2031] Guru: The Supreme Soul Sri Krishna came and demonstrated something through His actions

[GV1:P2032] before leaving. He demonstrated the matters of the Devas (gods) and the Pitrus (ancestors) and assumed agency for it Himself. That is why it was said, 'Mamekam sharanam vraja' (Surrender to Me alone). He removed the scholars and court poets of that time, as well as Bhishma—who was an expert in archery and attained the bed of arrows—and Drona from this world, and re-established the government itself. He Himself proved that sages and the enlightened are its guides.

[GV1:P2033] The enlightened ones do the very same subject that the sages perfect. They implement it in its entirety. That is why Vyasa, in the language of realization, said, 'Yatra Yogeshwarah Krishnah' (Wherever is Krishna, the Lord of Yoga). The perfect evidence for this is that Krishna took birth as an enlightened being Himself. Another proof is crossing all the states of the Devas, attaining the presence of Ishwara, and stepping into the presence of Brahman. That is the eighth state.

[GV1:P2034] Having understood all this and established the administration, Krishna tells Arjuna that, since the Yadavas themselves ignored the sages, Dwarka itself would sink due to that sinful power. Not only could they not be saved, but they were also going into renunciation. It proves that the Dharma of Kali had begun there. The truth is that, because the birth happened in the Dvapara Yuga, despite doing everything, it could not be completed.

[GV1:P2035] Respecting this, Buddha, who studied all texts, stopped everything else and tried to awaken people by making them chant only 'Buddham Sharanam Gachchami'. It must be an enforcement of the very same thing that the great Thiruvalluvar stated. Sankaracharya, who was elevated in Satva, realized that his caste would not change merely through the study of Puranas and epics. There is a story told about this. It is said that Parvati, in the guise of a Pariah girl, lay on the road wailing, and when he shouted 'Hoy Hoy' to avoid untouchability, the poor woman lamented, 'Son, if you, who are pious and wise, do this, will others touch me? Therefore, lift me from the path and lay me aside.' And accordingly, he moved her. When the frail, bone-like woman felt very heavy, he thought about the reason right there. The story goes that when he recognized her as Parvati, he saw that beauty and wrote the *Soundarya Lahari*. That must be regarding spiritual enlightenment, which is why it is written that when he shouted 'Hoy Hoy', she retorted asking whether it was the body or the soul that should move away. Writers might have fabricated him as an Advaitin. In spirituality, there is only one argument. It might have been done for the survival of the Vaidikas, to satisfy through court poetry, and to maintain the hegemony of the Brahmins. In doing so, the truth might have been forgotten. Human, after all! Mistakes can happen. Intelligent people should understand that.

[GV1:P2036] *Janmana jayate shudrah* (By birth, everyone is a Shudra)

[GV1:P2037] *Karmana jayate dvijah* (By action, one becomes a twice-born)

[GV1:P2038] Is it not shown by all of them through this Gita verse that the time is what the Shudra is entitled to and must achieve through Karma? Has it not been proven that the Shudra lost the ability to understand this? This is exactly what Narayana Guru also did. In order to help the Shudras recognize what Vedic practices and idol installations (Prathishta) are, he gave all of that to them, and then said that none of it is needed anymore and what we need are educational centers. The Murukkumpuzha temple with "Truth, Dharma, Compassion, Empathy" written on it and the Kalavamkodam temple where a mirror was installed, have enlightened us. Despite developing the S.N.D.P. for social growth from the age of thirty to seventy, and abolishing the worship of ghosts and evil spirits, puja rituals, and even the *Kettukalyanam*, they could not understand it because of the severe Shudra nature inherent in them. That is why the Swami had to establish the Dharmasangham. Thinking of the Shudras who had worked until then, he had to regret, "Oh! These poor people will not get this." Even amidst physical ailments, the pain that stood before him was that he could not do anything. When there was no improvement even after the combined treatment of Maman Vaidyar, Olassa Mooss, and Panavally Krishnan Vaidyar, Dr. Samuel was brought in, implying that this treatment was not enough. He evaluated the treatment up to that point and said, "We cannot provide any further treatment beyond this; let us pray for him for five minutes," and then knelt down and prayed with everyone.

[GV1:P2039] When he cried during his Samadhi saying, "I don't have a child," the ignorant devotees of the Swami at that time thought he was grieving over not having a biological child. Thus, the karmic dosha of acting against what the Swami worked for still persists. An explanation of this has been provided in the Santhigiri magazine under the title "The Mistake of Not Knowing What a Guru Is."

[GV1:P2040] Disciple: Then how will the people understand your idea

[GV1:P2041] that is of such magnitude?

[GV1:P2042] Guru: That is why people like you should ask and learn from time to time,

[GV1:P2043] correct it, and put it into practice. This era is suitable for it. What is happening here today can be seen in all the nations of the world. And what happens there can be seen here. Media has expanded that much.

[GV1:P2044] Disciple: Could you indicate how it is put into practice?

[GV1:P2045] Guru: More than what others have shown, as per the divine will (Brahmanischayam), a great capacity

[GV1:P2046] to work for the full period of a Yugadharma has been bestowed upon us as Brahman.

[GV1:P2047] Disciple: Will you explain this and make me understand?

[GV1:P2048] Guru: As you know, I too, like you, had been worshipping in the Trimurti system and,

[GV1:P2049] in particular, served for seventeen years not just at the headquarters of Narayana Guru but at its branches:

[GV1:P2050] Disciple: Could this idea not be introduced and developed through the ideology of

[GV1:P2051] Narayana Guru?

[GV1:P2052] Guru: It is not possible.

[GV1:P2053] Disciple: Why?

[GV1:P2054] Guru: Not only did he work by assimilating everything within the system of idol installation,

[GV1:P2055] but he also established puja rituals and composed hymns and praises. Due to that tradition, the Vedic religion in Kerala has reached a stage where it exists only among the Ezhavas, next to the Brahmins.

[GV1:P2056] Disciple: Cannot the Nairs or other communities belonging to the Shudra varna

[GV1:P2057] adopt this?

[GV1:P2058] Guru: Because the government here fell into the hands of the Nairs in the name of the Brahmins

[GV1:P2059] —

[GV1:P2060] Disciple: What do you mean by saying that it fell into the hands of the Nairs in the name of the

[GV1:P2061] Brahmins?

[GV1:P2062] Guru: When the Nairs gained administrative power, they engaged in Sambandham (alliances) and absurdities

[GV1:P2063] and became Brahmins. Now they have neither Brahminhood, nor Shudrahood, nor Karma, nor Dharma, nor humility. Due to the complete embodiment of arrogance, they have lost everything. The wisdom to respect and assimilate has also been lost. I have proof for that. One Velupillai Swami from Kottarakkara came to the Aluva Advaita Ashram after a journey. He was a householder and a wealthy man who had set out to become a monk. During prayer time, he was sitting under a mango tree, gazing at nature. A Swami went up to him and asked why he was sitting like that at this time.

[GV1:P2064] "I am a Shudra. I do not want any Ezhava prayers"—was the reply. It is clear that the monk Velupillai Swami did not even know what Varna was.

[GV1:P2065] When they had enough to eat and clothe themselves, they were ready to stand as the king's men. They tried to establish it. The reason is the community itself. That is why that community did not accept Sri Chattampi Swami's *Vedadhikara Nirupanam*—which is entirely a denial of the Vedas, as you know. It is because they could not comprehend the greatness of an Acharya's nature that this happened.

[GV1:P2066] Disciple: Is progress possible without assimilation?

[GV1:P2067] Guru: They will assimilate. They will be made to assimilate. Progress is possible. It is the divine will (Brahmanischayam).

[GV1:P2068] Progress will undoubtedly occur in all actions. There are not just one, but many proofs for that even now.

[GV1:P2069] The great country of India transformed into many islands and then became the continent of Asia.

[GV1:P2070] Disciple: Just as it is said 'Jambudvipe Bharatavarshe', was this entire Asia

[GV1:P2071] a single great country?

[GV1:P2072] Guru: Is that not the reason why the idol of the bull is mentioned in the story of

[GV1:P2073] Moses? Polytheism was prevalent everywhere on this continent. Since Moses's attempt to bring people under a single God could not be stopped, when the king and the army there moved together to stop him and his activities, Moses called his followers and left. It is said that all his followers went after him and reached the shore of the Red Sea, and when he struck it with his staff, the sea gave way, and those who tried to pursue Moses and his followers got trapped in the sea and died. Is this not God's grace, so that knowledge could come into the hands of the Shudra? Moses came more than a thousand years after Krishna.

[GV1:P2074] Disciple: Are you saying that Acharyas arrive specifically in accordance with each

[GV1:P2075] era and place?

[GV1:P2076] Guru: Have not attire, language, and nature already moved in different directions?

[GV1:P2077] How many attires are there in India itself? How many languages? Were there not over sixty languages among six hundred native kings? Is that not still prevalent today?

[GV1:P2078] Disciple: You also indicate that an idea brought forward in accordance with an era should spread to various

[GV1:P2079] parts of the world. We indeed see it spreading like that. However, universal ideas create division among people. What do you say is the reason for this?

[GV1:P2080] Guru: There are two or three reasons. It is said that Indians believe in Karma. But there are quite a few who say that there is no Karma. One group claims that Karma itself is a lie, and there is only a sequence of experiences according to one's own mind. Thus, when they lose their standing in society, each one brings up some idea and hangs onto it. They do not care to see whether that idea has any sustainability.

[GV1:P2081] Disciple: It would be helpful if you provided an example.

[GV1:P2082] Guru: When the Russian regime brought forth a purely brutal imperial system,

[GV1:P2083] the masses rose up to challenge it. It had the glory of bestowing upon not just themselves but the whole world a powerful system that could bring the working class to the forefront.

[GV1:P2084] Consequently, communism gradually spread to China as well. This change destroyed Buddhism there, smashing and dismantling the Buddhist monasteries. No matter how many crores of rupees one has, they cannot be rebuilt today. They existed there with such artistic perfection.

[GV1:P2085] Although this aforementioned imperial power of Britain was nurtured and elevated upon the ideology of Jesus, when their arrogance grew, they were ousted in a manner that would destroy them, retaining the same capitalistic nature and the same ideology. Those who were expelled from other countries as thieves and petty creatures are the ones who have grown into a superpower in America.

[GV1:P2086] Here, for this purpose, a man named Ramasamy Naicker brought the Dravidar Kazhagam into practice in Tamil Nadu. However, in Tamil Nadu where all this was preached, uneducated people are still the majority. Moreover, wherever they are, they toil like two-legged beasts and exhibit the farces typical of Tamil Nadu. They also turned temple worship into a bloody battlefield.

[GV1:P2087] Disciple: I did not understand what you meant by turning temple worship into a bloody battlefield.

[GV1:P2088] Guru: Animal sacrifice (slaughtering of goats and cattle) also existed in Kerala. In Chempazhanthy,

[GV1:P2089] a remote village, in the compound of the house where Narayana Guru was born, there were two temples. Both were Bhadrakali temples. In one of those shrines, a portrait of Narayana Guru is kept and worshipped. The other shrine has been dismantled and kept aside. I do not know what its current condition is.

[GV1:P2090] Swami, for the installation, dug a yard deep, removed the blood-stained soil, filled it with fresh soil, and built a pedestal. Now, Narayana Guru's portrait is placed there. An idol—of Bhadrakali, with a broken thumb—which was made in the style of a *Nalambalam*, has been taken and placed facing north. The other one was handed over to a museum.

[GV1:P2091] No one has revealed that back then, Nairs and Ezhavas had temples in the same compound. The ownership of both these temples was given to Narayana Guru. In the temple premises, there was a common performance stage (*Kalithattu*) for both temples. Two pillars were arranged on both sides of it to lean against. On one side of it, the elder (*Karanavar*) of the Nairs would sit. On the other side, the elder of the Ezhavas. Decisions were taken mutually. Today, that stage is not there. It has been demolished. Isn't this much evidence enough?

[GV1:P2092] Disciple: Didn't you say that we can bring about this idea? If such great

[GV1:P2093] spiritual masters could not achieve this, then how do you opine it can be brought about? Dayananda Saraswati was persecuted for speaking about this subject and was eventually poisoned to death. When preceptors and their ideologies are thus defied and persecuted, especially when not only communal hatred but also ideological conflicts are prevalent, how will this be put into practice?

[GV1:P2094] Guru: None of this seems like a great difficulty. For our idea to be implemented,

[GV1:P2095] a conditional pathway has been given as *Brahman*. It is because that one thing was not realized that previous preceptors, such great scholars, and heads of states were unable to function effectively. That is the sole stumbling block.

[GV1:P2096] Disciple: The preceptors who came before were unable to do this. Could the Guru please

[GV1:P2097] explain that in detail?

[GV1:P2098] Guru: You must have heard—saying 'let the stone split apart,'

[GV1:P2099] the powerful and courageous words of Jesus that would make it split. However, in his final moments, he asked the question, 'Father, have you forsaken me?' Both these have come from the same person.

[GV1:P2100] Disciple: Why did it happen like that?

[GV1:P2101] Guru: In the status of the Trinity, there is a state called the third step. Once

[GV1:P2102] ascended to that state, whatever one sees and hears will seem like the absolute truth. In its light, all these great souls are bewildered and become ready to do anything derived from it. And all of it will happen exactly like that. Once this third stage is completed, until reaching the sixth state, the whole world will be against this Mahatma.

[GV1:P2103] Disciple: Can you explain the reason for that?

[GV1:P2104] Guru: In this world, there exist numerous subtle entities and indwellers.

[GV1:P2105] Proof of this is Jesus saying, 'Satan, get behind me.' It is out of inability to tolerate the devil that he also asks, 'Father, have you forsaken me?' This occurs after the completion of the third stage. The Prophet was driven away with whips and brooms at that time. Where he was driven to, it was as hot as fire. Didn't he return after surviving by roasting and eating the hides of dead animals? Was it not after that he used the statement that *Jinns* rule the world?

[GV1:P2106] In the same position, we too had to experience it as evidence up to the sixth state. Had we desired supernatural powers (*Siddhi*) or something similar back then, you would have seen more people in Santhigiri today than what is seen around Sathya Sai Baba. It was because I somehow possessed the knowledge that *Siddhis* are an obstacle to spiritual growth and that one must complete this life path properly, that we did not leap into pursuing such powers. Yet, some of the disciples of that time had urged me, saying, 'We can easily do all these things, right?'

[GV1:P2107] It is not that I have not done a few things. And they have yielded results. There was an incident of *Chathaneru* (poltergeist stone-throwing) and a fire breaking out inside a concrete building at a house below the Varkala Sree Narayana Mission Hospital. Since the owner of the house was not there that day, his younger brother Mahani, a medicine merchant—anyone can inquire and verify this—informed me about the matter. I sent a letter through him. 'To the dear Chathan, please do not harm these poor people anymore. With love, Karunakara Guru.' This was the content of the letter. I instructed them to read it at all four corners of the house, read it at the doorway with a lit lamp, and then frame it and hang it in the front porch. With that, the stone-throwing stopped. I do not know if it is still there today. There are many such instances. Eventually, I decided I did not want such *Siddhis*.

[GV1:P2108] Later, these kinds of things stopped yielding results. All of this happened within this sixth state. The very person who had visions about this state became estranged and left. They themselves do not know why they got upset. Six or seven people who had good visions left along with him. The locals would certainly believe what people who worked so closely say, wouldn't they? That way too, a bad reputation came about. Thousands of people, even those who had personal experiences, have abused me as if they had lost their senses. This much is my experience. Isn't this much experience enough for a single individual?

[GV1:P2109] Thus, don't we have the practice of worshipping various kinds of mantra-deities among the *Jinns*, as well as *Yogeeshwaran*, ghosts and spirits, up to *Ghandakarnan*? And then the divine emanations up to the Trinity. Aren't they all considered bestowers of salvation?

[GV1:P2110] Disciple: That is what we had thought.

[GV1:P2111] Guru: Hasn't it been proven that they are not? Buddha was given pork as alms in his palms.

[GV1:P2112] Buddha contracted cholera and died. Such a thing happened to such a great soul. Jesus was crucified. He was betrayed through his most trusted disciple.

[GV1:P2113] Disciple: For the tragedies of these great souls, are these subtle-bodied entities powerful enough

[GV1:P2114] to exert influence even through close disciples like Judas?

[GV1:P2115] Guru: Yes, they are absolutely powerful. Narayana Guru's reflections on God

[GV1:P2116] also prove that.

[GV1:P2117] Disciple: Is this capability given to subtle forces by God?

[GV1:P2118] Guru: No.

[GV1:P2119] Disciple: There is a story among Christians. Lucifer is chief among the

[GV1:P2120] angels. The name Lucifer means morning star. The most prominent Lucifer tried to usurp the authority of God Himself. What is the meaning of this story?

[GV1:P2121] Guru: It is not a story; it is true. It was a star capable of shining

[GV1:P2122] brighter than a sun.

[GV1:P2123] In the language of the Hindus, the *Isha Upanishad* says:

[GV1:P2124] The golden vessel covers

[GV1:P2125] The face of truth.

[GV1:P2126] O Pushan, uncover it,

[GV1:P2127] So that I, a practitioner of truth and dharma, may behold it.

[GV1:P2128] That too is this very same light. A light that shines like the radiance produced when sunlight hits the lid of a large golden vessel. However, to see the true dharma, it is instructed to strike and open even that. Just because you see something resembling the sun or the moon, you do not have to revere it.

[GV1:P2129] 'Opening it to know the truth' refers to the path of karma that demands the lives of renunciates to be subjected to even greater sacrifice.

[GV1:P2130] Disciple: Could you please clarify that a little more?

[GV1:P2131] Guru: Those fallen yogis (*Yogabhrashtas*) who have reached up to the sixth step, and the yogis who have blindly reached

[GV1:P2132] up to the sixth without knowing the path, as well as their specific powers, are these indwellers. They will not be able to cross the sixth stage. But their radiance will not fade from that state. Errant forms of light will try to misguide a renunciate as well. If a virtuous woman gets cursed, her abilities are not destroyed. However, it is a negative condition. This matter is similar to that.

[GV1:P2133] The *Mandukya Upanishad* explains this very concept in a different language. If a large torch of bound palm leaves (*Kettuchootu*) is lit, and once it is burning well, someone from a distance spins it very rapidly, it will create an illusion of a large circle of fire glowing with that much thickness.

[GV1:P2134] The truth is the bound torch, not the circle of fire. In this manner, great souls have stated and demonstrated many examples for us.

[GV1:P2135] It is those who have almost reached this sixth state who say, 'Upon crossing the six steps and reaching there, one can see Lord Shiva.' Still, the true essence of the subject cannot be expressed.

[GV1:P2136] Disciple: What is the reason for that?

[GV1:P2137] Guru: Only upon reaching the seventh state can one proceed to the divine presence of God.

[GV1:P2138] ...can only be entered. Until then, it belongs to the Trimurti system. For example, you know the mistake made by Devendra, who reached up to the sixth level, and the curse of the sage. There, a wise person (Jnani) knows it as a special power attained together by Parashakti, Moola Ganapathi, and Devendra. But it can be corrected only after crossing this stage.

[GV1:P2139] Disciple: Is this why Narayana Guru happened to say, "Ariya thiruvezhuthaarumundothu

[GV1:P2140] vaanum" (chanting the six sacred letters)?

[GV1:P2141] Guru: Yes, that is what is meant by saying it cannot be corrected. Only what is known

[GV1:P2142] can be said. That is exactly what Narayana Guru has said. Great souls cannot lie.

[GV1:P2143] Disciple: Then how are you able to correct and say it?

[GV1:P2144] Guru: I have told you that many times. It was after reaching the seventh

[GV1:P2145] step that words started coming from the light. There is no form in the seventh step. It means names and forms will not remain. Only a few individual forms that have crossed these stages will remain.

[GV1:P2146] Disciple: Who is meant by "certain individual forms"?

[GV1:P2147] Guru: Only some souls who have departed with the desire for liberation will pass through

[GV1:P2148] like this. If they arrive after completing the sixth state, there is a scriptural rule that the soul can progress by doing penance in the realm it has reached. There is no scriptural rule that one can pass through and do such and such things. However, some of the great souls who go like this are allowed to pass through by that compassionate deity - the Brahma Shakti - as rightful heirs to the actions of the transitioning yugas. They will be born at the beginning of this Kali Yuga and at the end of the Dwapara Yuga. Sree Krishna is one of them. Many belonging to that group were born here during those occasions itself. Prophet, Jesus, Moses, Buddha, Shankaracharya, and the Gurus belonging to the lineage of Thiruvalluvar, up to Narayana Guru, were brought with that desire. Because some of them fell into the path of mystical powers (siddhis), the ideology could not advance. This is why Sathya Sai Baba says, "I have no liberation in this birth; it is possible only in the next birth."

[GV1:P2149] Disciple: Cannot Sri Ramakrishna and Vivekananda be included among the previously mentioned

[GV1:P2150] Gurus?

[GV1:P2151] Guru: Sri Ramakrishna and Vivekananda are realized souls (Jnanis). Other than

[GV1:P2152] seeing and speaking about past events, they could not bring forth a new ideology. Even for those who say the existing ones are not enough, although they could not implement the ideology, there is an action (karma) of it within them. It is just that they are unable to implement it because they could not cross the state.

[GV1:P2153] Disciple: Is it possible for demonic forces to ultimately perish or to attain liberation from

[GV1:P2154] their demonic nature?

[GV1:P2155] Guru: It is possible. I have my own proofs for that. For me,

[GV1:P2156] in this same state (the state after crossing the third step), it was all about abuse, quarrels, and beatings. For seven and a half years, nothing remained but sorrow. Before that, intermittently for about ten years too. During such a troubled time, a word was received from the light. I could not describe what kind of light it was or how it was. I still cannot.

[GV1:P2157] The word received was the Akhandanama (unending chant) present here. It was given to two people. One line to one person and the next line to the other. After six months, one of these two left. After a year, the second person also left. About fifty people who had visions, people who received all this and proved it true, and many thousands of other followers like them left; that day I had a feeling, and I said this would happen. Then many in this group stood up and asked, "What about us? What about us? What about us?" Then I said a word like this: "Should you hear about the festival you are going to see? Isn't it enough to see it? Ninety-nine out of a hundred will have gone," I said definitively.

[GV1:P2158] Not only did they leave, but they also made every possible effort to misinform the world in a bad way. When I was getting into a vehicle, they even stopped me, tore my towel, and beat me. (The one who stopped me died somewhere in North India.)

[GV1:P2159] After that, I came to the place where Santhigiri Ashram is currently located in Pothencode. Back then, it was an uninhabited place where no one entered. Nine months after coming here, the sages under the devas and everyone else agreed to function like before. It yielded ten times the result of the past. Muslim women used to come in rows from Pothencode. They were all cured of their diseases. Within a month and a half, all that stopped. The results started decreasing just like before. Behind that, quarrels, hurdles, and cases up to the Crime Branch were created. Then a message was received, "Remove all this." It is about the old order of worship. Those who received it spent three days in fear, not knowing what to do. On the third day, there was a sudden light and a revelation came, "You were worried, weren't you? It doesn't matter. Tell them to quickly have food and come."

[GV1:P2160] Disciple: What was the reason for telling them to have food?

[GV1:P2161] Guru: At dawn that day, a message was received that no one should drink even cold

[GV1:P2162] water today, and no one should go outside the compound. But someone who came from outside drew water and drank it without listening to what was said. Like algae in a dried-up paddy field, that girl of about seventeen vomited and fainted. She was then given holy water and sacred ash.

[GV1:P2163] Two young men went outside. There used to be a mango tree at the place where the car shed is today. They both got beaten at the base of it. It is not known who beat them. They came back and reported the incident. Everyone started praying as if crying and calling out. There was an instruction to plaster cow dung around the vessel in which food was cooked. Again at five o'clock, there was light. From it, a word emerged - an ethereal voice was heard, "Bathe quickly and have food, I will come again at six o'clock."

[GV1:P2164] Three ailments were cured that very day. The rest were cured over four days. Pattalam Ramakrishnan who was possessed by a Gandharva, a woman possessed by an Esakki, and another woman possessed by a Brahma Preta were still remaining.

[GV1:P2165] "Let this stay there, we will cure it later," a word was received. Then a large group of Acharyas and Devas came. It was written up to three hundred and fifty crores. Then left unwritten. Between four thousand and ten thousand crores are under two thousand four hundred and forty-four Gurus. The count cannot be completely told. All the ailments were cured by the seventeenth day.

[GV1:P2166] A word was received to start the journey. The Brahma Preta alone would not leave. According to the instruction to travel, when the journey started, it came in front and made faces. Gathering all strength, I struck the possessed woman once with my hand. That woman fell over. It has never happened again since then. There were four of us on this journey in the ascetic (Avadhuta) way of life. Chidambaram is the most powerful place in South India. We went there too. We knew beforehand what was at each place. All this gives a vision beforehand. If it is during the time of Puja - "You can enter a little later. The power receiving worship inside will have to move from there" - that is why it is said so. This happened at Chidambaram too. Since then, no temple visits have been made so far. That is when it was understood that there is nothing for me to gain from this Trimurti position.

[GV1:P2167] Then I was told to remain silent for four and a half years. After that, I had to spend another two and a half years like that. Certain things can be done. Certain things should not be done. During these seven years, 'Poortheekaranam' (completion) happened thirty-seven times. Those who came for the prayers held in the name of 'Poortheekaranam' often could go home only after four, five, or seven days. By walking and praying, the stones around the prayer hall loosened and piled up.

[GV1:P2168] Days like twenty-one, ten, fourteen are mentioned as the count. There are instances where it extended up to twenty-seven days. Due to the power of this prayer, a few odd days would be reduced. Saying, "It is completed, you have prayed sincerely," a sign would also be shown in a way that convinced everyone. It was after that, the action (karma) currently happening could be performed.

[GV1:P2169] Disciple: What is this action?

[GV1:P2170] Guru: It is because of this action that we are able to say the word that we

[GV1:P2171] can do it.

[GV1:P2172] These inner controllers (Antaryamis) will not stay if confined in the form of worship. They are moving around as crores of inner controllers. They will not allow crossing the six stages and going beyond.

[GV1:P2173] Disciple: Is that the reason why these Acharyas had to face all these

[GV1:P2174] difficulties?

[GV1:P2175] Guru: No one has been spared.

[GV1:P2176] Disciple: What does that mean?

[GV1:P2177] Guru: No one who crosses the three stages has been spared. When one grows a beard and hair

[GV1:P2178] and walks around according to their respective religious customs, the common people who see them assume that they are great Siddhas or liberated souls. That is not true. They might not have even crossed the third stage. Only a master who has crossed that stage can help another cross it. Those who do not find such masters will develop an inexplicable hallucination stemming from the overconfidence of having attained this light and vision. They will roam around like various kinds of lunatics and like people observing different kinds of ascetic vows. Since some people experience benefits from them and others suffer the greatest harm, the public will be unable to distinguish right from wrong.

[GV1:P2179] My own Guru helped me cross up to the fourth stage. It was Lord Krishna who appeared after seven and a half years to help me cross that. Lord Krishna's stage is the eighth.

[GV1:P2180] Disciple: Is it not true that some people have the experience

[GV1:P2181] of seeing the Guru's form in the form of Lord Krishna?

[GV1:P2182] Guru: Lord Krishna was my Guru in many births. That very same Guru

[GV1:P2183] helped me cross in this birth as well. Those who have helped cross will also come up to the point that has been crossed. That is why it is said that one can cross over while remaining in the body or from the ethereal realm.

[GV1:P2184] Disciple: Having come to guide this world, the world

[GV1:P2185] is unable to absorb this. Why is that?

[GV1:P2186] Guru: Are they not people who are accustomed to

[GV1:P2187] various paths—those of prophets and deities? They cannot suddenly absorb something new. Moreover, the demonic nature of those who lived and died as nobodies exists in the subtle realm. And then there are millions of fallen yogis (*Yogabhrashtas*).

[GV1:P2188] Disciple: Do fallen yogis still exist today?

[GV1:P2189] Guru: Absolutely, they do exist. Men who have grown their hair like women, women who have taken up

[GV1:P2190] false asceticism. There will be many such people. The Bhagavatam mentions this in its description of the Kali Yuga. Among the hundreds of thousands in this group, there might truly be only one or two genuine ones. Some will get lost in their supernatural powers (*Siddhis*). A few people will become engrossed in worshiping their chosen deity and get lost in that. A few people will display their knowledge and its enlightenment, pretending to be heads of monasteries, and having power bestowed upon them by the people. This would be akin to a large library falling into the water. All these people will show more than what they possess and will either lose their way or lead others astray in some manner. Eventually, they will become fallen yogis and inner dwellers.

[GV1:P2191] Disciple: Are you saying that such fallen yogis

[GV1:P2192] truly still exist today?

[GV1:P2193] Guru: Yes, they absolutely do exist. In addition to this, there is another category of

[GV1:P2194] fallen yogis. I will mention someone from my own experience regarding this. Kalladi Masthan. I have had respect and affection for his tradition of wisdom. I had heard about his supernatural powers and wisdom even before meeting him. Thus, I was very eager to see him.

[GV1:P2195] Guru Pathani Swami and I used to sleep under the Valiyathura bridge, which was under construction at that time. From there, we would walk southwards towards the Poonthura beach, conversing about various matters. We would walk like this, occasionally resting at certain spots, sleeping on the beach after brushing away the surface sand, walking again, and sitting in the fishermen's huts used for storing nets when it rained.

[GV1:P2196] There is more wealth in the sea than what can be taken from the land. People do not know that. The wealth in the sea will never run out. It might get exhausted on land. Pathani Swami would say many such things, as well as matters concerning ascetics. Occasionally, he would tell me to look into the depths of the sea and ask me to sit. Once the meditation became steady, what I would then see was the interior of the sea. I could see indescribable animal-like creatures and numerous mountains beneath the ocean, akin to Agasthyarkoodam in our eastern region. If those without experience in such visions were to see this, they might tremble with fear and even lose their lives. One could see creatures approximately a furlong in length and half a furlong in width. I do not know if they were fish. They would swallow numerous creatures, like sea snakes. If caught in their mouths, nothing could escape. However, some smaller creatures could also be seen alongside them. That is, creatures the size of sharks. If two or three creatures of this species stood together, the larger ones would not approach them. If they stood alone, they would approach. For example, a KSRTC bus would take some time to take a turn. Within that time, a small auto-rickshaw would have completed sixteen circles. This is just like that.

[GV1:P2197] It is impossible to describe the myriad colors and types of fish that exist; they can only survive up to a hundred feet below the surface. Very small fish are not seen at the bottom either.

[GV1:P2198] The Guru explained that the smaller ones cannot withstand the pressure at the bottom. The colors of the fish cannot be described. The naked eye cannot see their true colors. My experience is that objects seen with the physical eye appear much brighter in subtle vision. The capabilities of the external eyes have limits.

[GV1:P2199] While living like this, the Guru said one day: "You should go up to the Sannidhanam and come back." By Sannidhanam, the Guru meant Beemapally. When I go like this, I only return when I feel like it.

[GV1:P2200] Upon reaching the gates of Beemapally, I saw Kalladi Masthan. I recognized him from what I had heard. At that time, there were many people who respected him.

[GV1:P2201] Masthan was squatting on the shop-front of a betel-shop owner named Muhammad. It was his habit to grab handfuls of peanuts from his peanut jar, chew them, and spit them inside the glass cabinet.

[GV1:P2202] If anyone went there, he would throw and smash a large soda bottle. No matter what he did, Muhammad would just sit bent over, rolling beedis. He felt that doing all this was an act of grace towards him. Moreover, Masthan would not take such liberties in anyone else's shop.

[GV1:P2203] As soon as I recognized the person, I bought a tea and brought it to him. Immediately, he took water from Muhammad's lemon-water pot, rinsed his mouth, and extending both hands, took the tea and drank it in two gulps. He drank it to the last drop without wasting any. I bought a banana for two annas, placed it there, and returned. For some reason, I did not feel like staying there at that moment. I went straight to the Kunnupara temple.

[GV1:P2204] When I returned the next morning, that shop was closed. I only had one anna in my hand. I gave it and bought a tea. The moment I entered the shop, Kalladi Masthan sat with his hand extended. As soon as I handed over the tea, he drank a mouthful and then stirred his tongue in that tea. He licked the brim, the bottom, and all four sides of the glass.

[GV1:P2205] In the meantime, he sang praises in Urdu. I could not understand what it was. After that, he hugged me and made me drink that half-consumed tea. Having never eaten leftover food from anyone—not even from my mother—until that day, I felt like drinking it, and I drank it. He snatched the glass from my hand and threw it far away. Holding me by both my shoulders, he kept me at a distance, sang praises in Urdu, and kissed my head twenty times. Since I did not know Urdu, I thought he was speaking in Hindi.

[GV1:P2206] I said, "Babuji, I do not know Hindi." Calling out "Appa," he then began praising in Tamil. Then I started to understand. He repeated this many times. "O one who was born as a king in ancient times..." the hymns of praise went on like this.

[GV1:P2207] From that, I realized that the assertion in Islam that there is no rebirth is a superstition. I was also able to witness and understand this later. He just kept singing.

[GV1:P2208] Taking how many, how many births

[GV1:P2209] Becoming a monk how many, how many times

[GV1:P2210] O one who ruled the kingdom how many, how many times...

[GV1:P2211] The song went on like this. I could not comprehend any of the complex Tamil. Finally, he said, "Everything is there, it is there in abundance"; saying this three times, he gave a push. Just like how he threw the glass. Even though I fell, nothing happened to me. All the fishermen who had come to drink tea gathered around.

[GV1:P2212] "Where did this guy come from? He has also come to Baba, and Baba knows him. He has come precisely for this. Even though we have been sitting here, Baba hasn't even looked at us"—the crowd opined like this.

[GV1:P2213] I experienced an even greater wonder than that. I came to the Guru and narrated everything that had happened. Remaining silent until I finished, he said, "He has given you everything that was meant to be given. And a bit more. He will not let you get close to him anymore."

[GV1:P2214] I was convinced of that truth. After that, I have seen him a hundred times. Every time, I would buy him tea. Upon seeing me, he would turn away and murmur something in Urdu. He wouldn't even take the tea. Until his samadhi, he didn't let me come close. This is an experience that surprised me.

[GV1:P2215] "There is a little meanness. You will get rid of it," said Pathani Swami. This was experienced only after his and my Guru's samadhi. I had a few visions. While they were alive, Pushpangadan Vakil, who ran the Sivagiri dining hall, his younger brother Sundaresan, and I went to Beemapally. Kalladi Masthan took off the torn rag he was wearing—which in the language of cabaret dancers was just a torn cloth—and handed it to Pushpan. I immediately went into a shop and bought him a kaili. He wore it. The taken-off cloth was wrapped up and kept safely. Meanwhile, Pushpangadan and I traveled to Maruthvamala and many other places. It was during this time that both of us together built the ashram in Pothencode.

[GV1:P2216] Disciple: Did Swami stay in Pothencode itself after that?

[GV1:P2217] Guru: No. Went back to Varkala. Stayed there itself.

[GV1:P2218] Disciple: Who looked after this place then?

[GV1:P2219] Guru: The neighbors, today's Appu Swami, Divaka-

[GV1:P2220] ran who died by consuming poison, Sasi, and Bhaskara Panicker's children were the ones lighting the lamps. Janardhanan Pillai, who lived nearby, looked after other matters.

[GV1:P2221] Disciple: Why did this Appu Swami leave later?

[GV1:P2222] Guru: I was not here, right. His desire for sannyasa intensified. Then

[GV1:P2223] he came to Varkala and told me about some minor experiences he had. He said he wished to take up sannyasa and asked me to tell him where to go. He said, "I have a family temple in Njekkad. It is a testing place, and my desire is to stay there."

[GV1:P2224] I forbade him, saying it was not good. He would end up in a helpless situation where he couldn't move away from deity worship. I suggested the names of three or four ashrams.

[GV1:P2225] Apart from the Sree Narayana Mission, there is the Sri Ramakrishna Mission. There are no experiences anywhere there. I have experience with Ramadas Ashram in Kanhangad. There is Sivananda Ashram in Vatakara. There is Brahmananda Ashram in Alathur. Kalappara Sivananda has an ashram in Neyyattinkara. It is a branch of the Siddhashram in Vatakara. I have been able to meet some experienced seekers from there. Even if they don't possess immense wisdom, it is better. Yoga is their discipline. I told him that his disciple, a younger brother named Narayanan, is in Thiruvananthapuram.

[GV1:P2226] He left saying, "I will go to the family temple first and then proceed to one of the places you suggested."

[GV1:P2227] Later, when he returned after ten years, it was a time when I had arrived at Pothencode. There is an ashram in Kallikkad. There is a forge. They work there and also conduct bhajans. Believers come there. There is an ashram here too. He invited me to visit there. Since he couldn't see me at the agreed time, he told Thankappan to inform me that he was waiting.

[GV1:P2228] So I went. He had bought and kept a towel for me to sit on. A small southern extension-like structure was built there. During our casual conversation, I told him, "This will get better, this condition will change—just be careful," and then I left. We haven't met since then.

[GV1:P2229] Around that time, I learned that he spoke highly of me to those who went there. Now, I have come to know that he is speaking the exact opposite with the same tongue. I also heard that he used some derogatory words to those who went from here.

[GV1:P2230] Let me continue what I was saying. I told you that I had some visions. From them, I understood that certain demonic forces were standing in my way to mislead me. One of them was the form of Kalladi Masthan. I felt that it had possessed Pushpangadan. That very day, upon reaching Varkala, I called Pushpan, explained the matter, made him bring Masthan's cloth, and together we threw it into the water under the Poovampara bridge. Anyone can verify this by asking Pushpangadan Vakil in Varkala.

[GV1:P2231] Even after that, Pushpan behaved as if he was not quite well. I didn't question any of this. Whoever connected with me approaches Kalladi Masthan, this demonic force will do something to lead them astray.

[GV1:P2232] It was then that my Guru's words—"He has given some demonic nature, which you will discard"—made sense to me. I could only understand it after thirteen years; the words of great souls have long-term effects.

[GV1:P2233] I know many people like this Kalladi Masthan. They are all lying like those who have fallen into a trap. Even though my Guru told me about it then, I was convinced of it only after this experience.

[GV1:P2234] When I stayed in Neyyattinkara, I saw many people like Kesavan Sanyasi, Vatti Swami, Chatti Swami, Chunnampu Swami, Mannenna Swami, Kudil Swami, and Sambrani Swami.

[GV1:P2235] Another place is Samadhithoppu, a place people believe is still running well today. Then there is Mayiyamma in Kanyakumari. All these belong to a chain of fallacies of this kind. Kompa Swami, who showed many siddhis, also falls into this category. He attained samadhi in seven places.

[GV1:P2236] When my Guru sat with me and other disciples on the veranda of the Thuckalay Munsiff Court, he used to criticize all this. I didn't understand it then. I believe the others with me didn't understand it either. When starting to talk about Kattuva Sahib Mala, Swami used to mention all these things. My Guru's words back then—that all these are stuck at a crossroads and cannot move forward from there—are clear to me today. Only today have I understood its completeness and who the Guru truly is.

[GV1:P2237] Yet, I recall my Guru saying that even he couldn't get me completely in his final days. This path is like an ocean. It should not be forgotten that people believed, loved, and respected all of them.

[GV1:P2238] Among this group, there are some who undergo transformation through the knowledge tradition, like Thuckalay Peerukannu Sahib and Gunamkudi Masthan, who went to Mecca and attained samadhi.

[GV1:P2239] You might think that this sounds like speaking ill of such great men.

[GV1:P2240] Disciple: We don't think like that.

[GV1:P2241] Guru: If not you, someone else will think so. You should think like that.

[GV1:P2242] I believe it is good to think. Because my desire today is that no one else should fall into the trap I fell into. Just like other people, I also used to see all this as the truth. The secret of the "indwellers" (Antaryamis) is this.

[GV1:P2265] September 1988

[GV1:P2266] I started speaking only after the age of nine. I studied in an *Ezhuthupallikoodam* (traditional village school). Thus, the only knowledge I acquired was what the *Ashan* (teacher) taught me. Otherwise, I never went to a regular school. The *Ashan* kept me there until I was fourteen. By the time we reached the *Siddharoopam* (basic Sanskrit grammar text), the *Ashan* became physically weak. Therefore, I left that place. I did not study anything after that. Subsequently, it was the *Ashan* himself who took me to the Kalady Ashram. At that time, Swami Agamananda was teaching the *Brahma Sutras* to a person named Swami Jagadiswarananda. After passing the Shastri examination from our region, as he was traveling to North India, a person named Swami Madhavananda in Karnataka took him under his wing and taught him. He lived in Benares for twenty-one years. He had the ability to effortlessly recite texts like the *Siddhanta Kaumudi* fluently, back and forth.

[GV1:P2267] I asked him about this, linking it with my own experience. He replied, "Alas, my child, all of this exists. Although the scriptures state the truth, I have not even seen the light of a lit incense stick. So, I cannot speak about it." I asked many people in this manner. I did not get any evidence from anyone. Later, I met a Pathani Swami. It was from him that I could understand this. Based on his advice, I realized that whatever names exist in this world, they all genuinely exist. If we, consciously or unconsciously, utter a name or conceptualize something, it exists. However, humans have not learned where and how to utilize it. This is what I gathered from my own knowledge.

[GV1:P2268] One can worship using the knowledge up to the *Trimoorthi* (Trinity) system, and one can even see its physical manifestations without any distortion using their naked eyes. But we have never contemplated what they can do, or what we should do about them. That is, we have not thought about the *Dharma* (duty/nature) of Kali Yuga.

[GV1:P2269] If Kali Yuga has its own *Dharma*, it belongs to the Shudra. Many *Brahma-jnanis* (knowers of Brahman) have emerged among the Shudras. Sree Krishna is the evidence for that. Then came the *Parayi Petta Panthirukulam* (the twelve tribes born to a Pariah woman). In the meantime, the eighteen Siddhars also joined in. We have not been able to unite any of these and transmit them through a single language or form, as one unified Indian tradition. We call ourselves Hindus. What we have done so far is behave from behind a system that has been transmitted in such a fragmented way—where small castes have minor gods and upper castes have major gods—making it impossible for us to stand united and pass it on.

[GV1:P2312] We must be cautious of the nature that manifests in various forms such as mischief, glory, love, devotion, and action. We must safeguard our minds. It will take a considerable amount of time just to understand this. This is precisely because our parents or ancestors were not perfect. Their actions and moral principles will affect us to some extent. This is because nature cultivates blood, marrow, and flesh not just in them and us, but in a way that sustains all living beings in the world. It is transmitted to all living beings in their respective natures. There are also transformations for all these. Every thinker has a distinct perspective on all this. This grass—what is it! How many varieties, and similarly, how many species of birds and animals! All of these possess stomachs, functional capacities, and blood vessels. What is this system that operates everything in perfect equilibrium? Similarly, through the magnitude of what great scientists have discovered, it is possible to fly to many places. Even if all that is true, there will still remain millions and billions of things yet to be known in this world, even if countless discoveries are made. If there is a change in this atmospheric nature or the nature of the solar system, how will we know? We are only capable of acknowledging what we already know as good, known, or heard.

[GV1:P2313] The world is like this. How does it permeate within us? This is what we must consider next. When reflecting thus, among those we consider father, mother, husband, or wife—what lineage have they upheld in this? Under the influence of what inherent tendencies (*vasanas*) have they presented themselves? We must clearly explain this to every child, especially the children studying here. You are not making them understand in that manner. The reason is that you lack such inclinations. The first thing to instill in these children is that you yourself must convince them of the flaws and shortcomings of their parents. Then, what are the circumstances of our home and the circumstances of our ancestors? First, they must be made to understand that. Following that, one must be prepared to confess one's own faults. Only then will they comprehend what you teach. Thus, the teacher was able to admit that their father, mother, themselves, and their lineage have faults! That mind is expansive. Otherwise, they will mimic and magnify the antics displayed before them by men and women. No matter how much is said, they will exhibit it. Make this a practice here—our primary task is to encourage them to confess their faults, to observe the misfortunes of their lineage, to repent, and to instill a determination in them to resolve it. The realization should not merely be that one's father, mother, and lineage are at fault and how one can resolve it, but that there are collective flaws spanning from all living beings to the human race. First, make them contemplate how we should perceive this fault. Thus, it should be imparted to children as small, digestible topics. Otherwise, it will veer into Vedanta, and if it moves towards Vedanta, these children will also delve into Vedanta. Vedanta is entirely rationalism. Although some may argue that rationalism is good, it is not. Why? Through rationalism, using intellect, things beyond comprehension will be introduced. Secondly, one might attempt to analyze expansively, thinking, 'Given my parents' condition, I am unlikely to possess this much intellect—yet I have this much intellect.'

[GV1:P2314] This must be communicated to the children first. Only then will a contemplation about themselves be beneficial to them. There are certain brief lines in the *Bhagavata*. These should be read. Certain sections must be read with deep attention. If one says that the sage's advice is good; that it is Vedanta; it implies that several good things have been articulated in it. What needs to be conveyed is about the concepts that thinkers have comprehended through reflection and practically applied. Otherwise, thought and action will bifurcate into two distinct entities—which is never beneficial.
