[GV1:P2324] February 1989

[GV1:P2325] We bear the moral transgressions (*dharmadosham*) that have descended through the karmic actions accumulated by our ancestors. Eradicating these moral transgressions is attainable solely through another resolute action. If we fail to comprehend how the elements termed karmic afflictions and moral transgressions have reached us, and how we harbor them, we will endure the absolute misfortune of being entirely incapable of imparting this knowledge to our children. Therefore, comprehending how this has befallen us is paramount; it is not merely a matter of preventing its recurrence, but by retrieving and examining these past occurrences, we must definitively determine how to resolve these incurred afflictions through our lineage—this is not a solitary issue. In its stead, we must accumulate merit (*punya*) of equal or double magnitude, and portray our very lives as a paradigm of a karmic resolution framework. To manifest such a life, we require profound knowledge.

[GV1:P2326] Among us, within the societal divisions of Brahmin, Kshatriya, Vaishya, and Shudra, it is noted that there exist one hundred and eighty distinct castes even among those who were Vaishyas and Shudras; and these one hundred and eighty castes have conducted themselves with one hundred and eighty divergent dispositions. Consequently, not only has the sense of unity amongst us dissipated, but we have also invited every conceivable indiscretion, corrupting one another in every possible manner. Furthermore, we have arrogated the ownership of karmic actions that even our children cannot approach. We are striving to establish a way of life wherein at least our children might possess the capability to eradicate this karmic burden.

[GV1:P2327] Irrespective of our endeavors, a certain degree of deficiency and injustice inevitably permeates our actions. What must constitute our shared endeavors to rectify this deficiency? There are two pathways to achieve this: through the dutiful actions that must be fulfilled by the responsibilities of a householder; and through the rightful merits we have accumulated. Having traversed the paths of a yogi, a seeker of knowledge (*jnani*), a devotee (*bhakta*), and a practitioner of action (*karmi*), the action that ultimately attains liberation in that karma must also emerge from the foundational bedrock of the actions we perform today. This is not achieved through our independent intellect. Rather, by nurturing within us that profound conviction termed divine will or the will of *Brahman*, we constitute the foundational stone that must impart this wisdom to our young children or to the great souls yet to be born. In this endeavor, there is no distinction between male and female, or young and old. There is no caste, no religion, and no class.

[GV1:P2328] It is fallacious to proclaim that this *Kali Yuga* is worthless! Why? The circumstance exists today wherein a Shudra can enter and operate in any sphere. Even after fully acquiring the rights of a Shudra in this manner, without genuinely comprehending the essence of a Shudra, and by continually aspiring upwards to govern with ambitions of emperorship, the entire Shudra demographic has veered toward the trajectory of ignorance. Consequently, it is not wisdom that has reached their hands. By propagating perversion, passion, caste, and pervasive subdivisions of caste, this ignorance has proliferated to an extent where it can never be wholly eradicated. How must this be resolved? For that, divine determination is imperative. To become a participant in the divine will, we must inevitably adopt either a preceptor's tradition or a prophetic tradition. A definitive path for this has been expounded to us. This path is paramount. The world has hitherto never been presented with such a path. Furthermore, no alternate path can emerge except in the subsequent epoch. We have transmitted such a profound ideology. All preceptors and all prophets, abiding as inner controllers (*antaryamis*), have been safeguarding this ideology on our behalf. We have orchestrated various karmic actions toward this purpose. Henceforth, the actions you perform must adhere to a strict discipline, order, and methodology. It must be a pathway that is traditional to you. In accordance with this prescribed methodology, a bylaw will be drafted.

[GV1:P2329] This is not a task that just anyone can accomplish. Why? There may exist a religious bylaw or a caste-based bylaw. However, this bylaw serves as a minor, yet profound, amendment to all existing bylaws. Whether one is a Hindu, a Christian, a Muslim, a Buddhist, or a Jain, no one can refute its validity. We are laying the foundational groundwork for the drafting of such a bylaw. This document is being meticulously formulated for the united functioning of all of you. By cultivating unity among yourselves—devoid of distinctions such as male or female, young or old, superiority or inferiority—we are offering this to the world as our greatest contribution, to the utmost of our abilities. There is no utility in speaking of endeavors one cannot fulfill. We do it to the best of our abilities. It is not restricted to any specific individual. If one can merely pinch and offer a grain of soil, that is sufficient. This objective must be realized. It is for this very purpose that you have been bestowed with this knowledge.

[GV1:P2330] How can you impart this knowledge moving forward? I am communicating to you the directive I have received: that this must be undertaken collectively. Are you capable of undertaking it or not? We have arrived in this land. It is this land that has been fortunate enough to receive this. If one asks how, the answer remains unknown. Perhaps, in some intrinsic state, this land possessed a latent virtue. Or perhaps, it is intended for this wisdom to transition away from this place where an extensively degraded culture currently resides. Whatever the reason may be, such a profound fortune has accrued to this land. It is not merely impending; it has already arrived. If they choose to deny it, whether knowingly or unknowingly, the fault is not theirs; they have, at the very least, acquired the fortune to have it assimilated by their future descendants. As a precursor to this, we are undertaking the initial imparting. By imparting it, we are demonstrating it to them.

[GV1:P2331] Today, a large number of people are visiting Santhigiri. This is not enough. All of them, transcending caste, religion, or class, must eliminate the karmas accumulated over countless births in order to establish a traditional lineage. It remains attached to the soul. It is the complete manifestation of a great and relentless effort that must be undertaken by cultivating love, faith, glory, devotion, and karma as a tradition. No matter how much we work for this, it will not be sufficient. It is an endeavor where no amount of time spent working will ever be enough. I am stating this as an announcement so that you may all develop the strength to undertake this. All of you must unite and embrace this *Brahmanischayam* (divine will), irrespective of differences such as male or female, great or small. We, being of the ignorant *Shudra* class, must undertake this to the best of our abilities and ensure that others do as well. We must establish the right to usher in the *Satyayuga*, bringing transformation not just to the *Brahmin*, *Kshatriya*, and *Vaishya*, but to all living beings. *Kali* (the Kali Yuga) is the era born for us to attain liberation and claim this right. You must undertake this together by taking a solemn vow.

[GV1:P2332] The pledge, recited and submitted in the holy presence of the Guru and the Guru lineage (*Guruparampara*), is appended below:

[GV1:P2333] 'Correcting the mistakes committed by us and our lineage until this day, we solemnly pledge before the truth of the Guru that we shall transition to the righteous path granted to us as divine grace through the *Guruparampara*, and that we shall, to the best of our understanding, acquaint ourselves with and introduce to others that *Brahmanischayam* in accordance with the divine will, handling it appropriately.'

[GV1:P2335] April 1989

[GV1:P2336] Everything has been brought forth by imposing a specific limit within which every reality grows and organizes itself. This can be observed if one looks at Christianity, Islam, and Buddhism. When peering into the traditional history of the Hindus, it is continually compared with the concepts of various sages (*Rishis*). The *Shakteya* will claim that Shaktism is the greatest. The *Shaiva* will claim that Shaivism is the greatest. The *Vaishnava* will claim that Vaishnavism is the greatest. It is never stated that these three are fundamentally identical and correct. They are also coupled with other karmas possessing contradictory attributes. All that has been said is indeed true. But have we looked deeply enough into the light of time?

[GV1:P2337] A specific history suitable for each era was brought forth. Since world history had not traveled so extensively back then. Why?

[GV1:P2338] Disciple: It was not written down.

[GV1:P2339] Guru: It is not that it was not written down. It was done in their own manner. The Hindus have a history spanning a vast period. Writing existed in those times. Writing of some form or another. Or rather, there was a certain concept. Otherwise, how could such a monumental historical truth emerge? If one examines history from a Western perspective, one finds records of fifteen hundred years; four thousand years; or at most, eight thousand years; a Western history extending beyond this is not seen. The history written in the modern method is only that much. Even before this, life existed everywhere.

[GV1:P2340] How was this life for humanity? Or what were they? It is not easy to reflect upon and comprehend such things about that era. Therefore, it must be left at that. There is no point in becoming exhausted by thinking about it. Regarding what exists today, one must write about India keeping in the forefront the life of the recent prophet, that is, from the time of Moses, or the life of Jesus or the Prophet (Muhammad), or the life of Buddha or Krishna. Otherwise, you will go astray.

[GV1:P2341] Disciple: Hinduism emerged through various paths, namely the paths of Hindu prophets—the *Shaiva*, *Shakteya*, and *Vaishnava* traditions, as well as the paths of numerous other Hindu preceptors. How can this be reconciled with Judaism and the religious traditions of Moses, Jesus, the Prophet, and others? These are prophetic religions. Here too, there were sages (*Rishis*) who resembled prophets. However, it does not clearly appear as a continuous tradition. What does the Guru have to say about this?

[GV1:P2342] Guru: It has appeared clearly. But we lacked the familiarity to elucidate it. What intruded in the meantime is an ignorance akin to a demonic nature. For example, how do you understand Vaishnavism?

[GV1:P2343] Disciple: As a Hindu, I harbored a traditional understanding. All the ten incarnations (*Dashavatara*) are incarnations of Lord Vishnu. Furthermore, Buddha is also included among those incarnations. It was the understanding that *Brahma*, *Vishnu*, and *Maheshwara* are the deities responsible for creation, preservation, and destruction.

[GV1:P2344] Guru: Therefore, because such imaginative *karmas* became ingrained among us, the *karma* that reveals reality became obscured, as if hidden away. Later, upon coming into that *karma* of 'imaginative-karmic-mind' (*Sankalpakarmamanasa*)—consider it merely as a *Shakteya* karma—when observing its primordial root, in order to sustain a certain concept or interest within nature, what man discovered from nature was how to influence or utilize the truths of nature. When the zenith (intensity) of human evolution occurs, man transforms into a deity (*Deva*), a sage (*Rishi*), or an ascetic (*Sannyasin*). After cultivating human intensity, compassion and empathy must be brought back. For example, when peering into the domain of a small insect, what operates there are their respective bonds of affection. If one examines how that bond of affection develops, one can see that it reflects certain phenomena occurring today across this earth, the sea, and the sky. We are in a helpless state where we cannot determine how many celestial bodies exist within this celestial sphere. Now, the Earth is a sphere. The Moon is a sphere, the Sun is a sphere—these three are visible to our eyes. However, it has been scientifically discovered today that there are stars much larger than all these spheres. What must exist within this universe (*Andakadaha*)? What must not exist? This must be determined by a visionary. Or, by a holy personage who can be measured alongside an era. Without reflecting on what the conception of that holy personage is or from where that holy personage obtained it, we simply believe in him, and continue to believe. Or, believing in something, we revolve around it and attempt to develop all aspects of life through it.

[GV1:P2345] Disciple: Were Buddha, Mahavira (Jain), Christ, and the Prophet all such holy personages?

[GV1:P2346] Guru: They were. But it cannot be said that they were all global traditionalists. However, they can be made so. Because if an idea can be imparted to all people—imparting even the smallest idea is sufficient. For example, the Christian ideology.

[GV1:P2347] Disciple: Is the Guru suggesting that it is small?

[GV1:P2348] Guru: Yes.

[GV1:P2349] Disciple: In what way is it small?

[GV1:P2350] Guru: It is small in proportion to its conceptual *karma*.

[GV1:P2351] Disciple: It would be better if this were clarified further.

[GV1:P2352] Guru: It is the sacrifice of Christ that has accorded Christ such a preeminent position. When considering the magnitude of its concept, it is small.

[GV1:P2353] Disciple: Is not sacrifice a great concept?

[GV1:P2354] Guru: Sacrifice becomes great only to the extent of that individual's sacrifice, does it not? Is sacrifice as great as the magnitude of the concept?

[GV1:P2355] Disciple: Do you mean that sacrifice is only one part?

[GV1:P2356] Guru: Yes.

But having grown in that manner, his thought is what returns to show how the atomic principle exists even in these insects.

The very place name Maharajamuttam (Marayamuttam) is a part of this history. There is a house there called Puthuveedu. They received a hundred acres. That was a reward for keeping Marthanda Varma hidden. Similarly, a Muslim woman also received it. While being chased, when he reached that place and could not proceed further, he ran back towards the west and saw an Umma (Muslim mother) sitting there. Saying "Umma.. please save me", he fell onto her lap. Then the Umma took a 'Muttakku' (head covering) and covered him. Then she remained silent. The Ettuveetil Pillamar came and asked this Umma: 'Someone ran here, didn't they? Did you see?' The Umma said that he went that way. They ran in that direction, and Marthanda Varma got up from there and ran. The place where he came running to is Puthuveedu. There is a reason why it is called Puthuveedu. Someone who accompanied him said: This is a Thiyya's - Ezhava's - house. What of it, is it not Puthuveedu (a new house)? When he came to power, a hundred acres were given to them without any tax liability.

A visionary is one who sees what is transpiring inside this solar system. The special transformation involving the earth, the sun, and the moon. Are there not places in some corner of the world where there is neither day nor night, but merely blocks of ice? The light of the sun, the earth, and the moon does not reach there. We have not gone and seen these places ourselves. In these places, during certain periods, the ice parts and gives way. When the ice parts, people pass through. The ice then accumulates again, and thus it has remained there without any destruction for billions of years.

By assigning a duration of fourteen Manvantaras, specifying that a deluge happens in such a manner within it; this is our calculation.

[GV1:P2408] Why was Kamsa, who knew in advance that Krishna would come, prepared to kill his own sister's children one by one? He possessed knowledge about this world to a certain extent. Kamsa, who received a disembodied voice declaring that authority in the Yadava clan was given to him to rule in such a manner, was not an ordinary man. What is that guidance? This Shudra path must be cleared. For that, an administrative system must first be prepared.

[GV1:P2409] A Shudra has the right to rule. It was there in all eras. The claim that they have no right was written down later. In those days, there were kings from all castes. In every era, everyone had the authority to rule and to have governance conducted. Krishna's arrival was to correct all of this. But what happened when that Krishna was tied to the dharma of the Hindu, or rather, the Deva? It turned into a path of war between the Dravidians and the Aryans. Because the old worship was not changed, the power of the Dravidian concept weakened; he intelligently introduced the concept of the Vaishnava and studied the sciences that existed here. The Aryan knew that the era of the Dravidian, whose conceptual power had diminished, was over. The Dravidian remained entangled in Shaivism and Shaktism. In this context, the Vaishnava applied a cunning intellect, studied all these things from here, and made it seem as if the Sanskrit language belonged exclusively to him. He even specifically wrote and created a Samhita. When the Prakrit language was refined into the Sanskrit language, that language became exclusively his own.

[GV1:P2410] Where did this Brahmin come from? A hymn was even composed to establish that they settled here because a celestial body akin to the sun guided their path. That precisely constitutes his prayer on the day of the Avani festival: "We bow to you who granted us the opportunity to reside here"—this is the essence of the Surya Gayatri mantra. From this very fact, one can deduce that he is not indigenous to this land, but rather migrated from the Middle East.

[GV1:P2411] Disciple: You mentioned Shaivism! Was Shiva a guru?

[GV1:P2412] Guru: That is how Shiva is understood. Shiva was not born of a womb (*yoniputra*); rather, it denotes a position. He was a conceptual son (*sankalpaputra*). His origin is not articulated anywhere, whereas the origins of all other entities are explicitly stated. There is no mention of Shiva's genesis. Only Shiva and Parvati existed here. By studying this and recognizing it as belonging to the Treta and Dvapara yugas, he adopted the philosophical path. Thus, the Vaishnava concept was embraced.

[GV1:P2413] Disciple: Is Vishnu a different concept?

[GV1:P2414] Guru: Yes.

[GV1:P2415] Disciple: Is he a conceptual son as well?

[GV1:P2416] Guru: Not a conceptual son in essence, but rather contrived to become one. His conceptualization portrays him resting his arm in the Ocean of Milk. Consequently, he too was transformed into a conceptual son. Everything was uniformly depicted as being permeated by Vishnu (*Vaishnavamayam*). Amidst such conceptualizations, the ignorant must inevitably attain knowledge at some juncture! When might that occur? That realization will unfold in the Kali Yuga. From the onset of the Kali Yuga, this knowledge reached the Shudra as well. The doctrine imparted was that the Vaishya and Shudra are destined to labor, while the other two classes reap the benefits. This is the very history that has been fabricated and inscribed. Furthermore, there is an Advaita philosophy that proclaims all this to be one. This is fundamentally a deception. We must now examine how this was introduced through such conceptualization.

[GV1:P2418] October 1989

[GV1:P2419] A functional capacity that ascended within the human intellect! Through this capacity, he subsequently investigated the deeds of primitive humanity. Having studied this, the intellectual pondered how his contemporaneity could be utilized for the benefit of others. Consequently, he contemplated the phenomena within the sphere of the nine planets; he reflected upon its existence, as well as the evolution, sustenance, and dissolution of the solar system. Initially, he assigned positions to the nine planets. All nine planets revolve. The axis of one is positioned lower, such that all others revolve beneath it. That is the Sun. Why do they revolve in this manner? It is not merely to create day and night; evolution must also occur. Evolution must be catalyzed by the power of the Sun. The lunar cold and atmospheric dust descended upon the Earth, transforming into the essence of seeds. The functional capacity that operates from the five elements (*Panchabhoota*), reaching the five senses (*Panchendriya*), and penetrating the five sheaths (*Panchakosha*), must manifest in this manner. Is there any alternative pathway for this?

[GV1:P2420] Disciple: How, then, does creation take place?

[GV1:P2421] Guru: Exactly. Having studied the nine planets in this manner, he imparts this knowledge to humanity. It manifested as Yugas. Which Yugas could they be? The Treta Yuga is calculated by subtracting the duration of Kali Yuga from the Satya Yuga. The Dvapara Yuga is derived by subtracting the duration of Kali from the Treta Yuga. The Kali Yuga comprises four lakh thirty-two thousand (4,32,000) years. This epoch belongs to the Shudra. The prophetic tradition had never attempted to perceive things in such a manner.

[GV1:P2422] Disciple: Did they not attempt to perceive it, or were they unable to attain it?

[GV1:P2423] Guru: They were indeed unable to attain it. When actions unaligned with truth are observed, a conflict arises between the laborer and the capitalist—claiming, "They do not yield all that they acquire. They seek to destroy us." There exists an exploitative class that merely instigates people to fight by propagating such narratives! A class that incites both groups against each other, suggesting that if the capitalist is ruined, the workers will inherit everything! The result: both will be annihilated. The ownership of the karma to destroy both belongs to this class. This is not what is genuinely required. How long is our lifespan? A hundred years at most. Within this span, one must assess the proportion of merit (*punya*) and sin (*papa*) holistically, determining what actions a human should perform at specific times. There is a karma born within the framework of the nine planets, twelve zodiac signs, and twenty-seven constellations. A trajectory was formulated incorporating these twenty-seven constellations, akin to the equator delineated for the Earth. Similar to that imaginary line, this was constructed, and a mathematical system was devised for it. This calculation was conceptualized in India. India's calculation is the most comprehensive. The aforementioned prophets lacked this mathematical insight. Why? Their thirst for inquiry had not reached those depths. This can only be attained by contemplating the underlying causes for the creation of the Earth, the Moon, and so forth. India possesses such a guiding vision derived through this contemplation. There, as previously mentioned, even an insect is accorded a place (compassion). What was the consequence of proceeding with such compassion? The Aryan religion emerged. Various religions were sequentially established. Subsequently, all of this was consolidated to establish Advaita. Madhva attempted to establish Dvaita. All these individuals articulated what they perceived. No matter how long one argues about these matters or emerges victorious in debates, foresight will not simply materialize. Therefore, it is prudent to set that aside. Based on the nine planets, twelve zodiac signs, and twenty-seven constellations, the *Yama* calculation determines what transpires every two and a half to three hours. A certain number of *Yamas* constitute a day; as that calculation becomes infinitesimally smaller, it reaches the fraction of time it takes a healthy human to pierce two stacked tender leaves of a bael tree or lotus with a stylus, penetrating one leaf to reach the other. Identifying that precise moment is the challenge. Then comes the *Mahani* calculation. One thousand *Mahanis* equate to sixty-two and a half *Vinazhikas*. I have studied all this through writing. India possesses a metric of time far more precise than the calculation of a second.

[GV1:P2424] Disciple: Is this not a branch of astrology?

[GV1:P2425] Guru: Astrology is precisely this. Is astrology not entirely based on calculations?

[GV1:P2426] Disciple: However, when calculations are performed currently, they do not seem accurate!

[GV1:P2427] Guru: That is because sufficient effort is not invested to compute them meticulously. One has to dance to the tunes of the world, after all!

[GV1:P2428] Disciple: It is said that such profound calculations were attained! Yet, they are referred to as visionaries who lacked access to such grand metrics. Nevertheless, they did establish a culture here, did they not?

[GV1:P2429] Guru: That is undeniably our own fault. This intellectual alienated us, preventing the Dravidians from uniting, precluding the Shudras from coming together, and thereby keeping people estranged by denying them education. He appropriated it for himself.

[GV1:P2434] The Aryans were migrants from the Middle East. Upon arriving here and beholding this beautiful land, they established their settlements. [GV1:P2512] Disciple: Did knowledge exist on earth before the Vedic order arrived here? Is the Guru saying that this is not their knowledge?

[GV1:P2513] Guru: Brahmins are those who came from East Asia. They themselves state this in a mantra portion of the Vedas. They came here, established centers of intellect here, made the local Vaishyas and Shudras do the work, and became virtuous themselves, or rather, souls who imparted virtue. By becoming laborers, the Shudras lost their knowledge. Numerous attempts were made to rectify and clarify this. Sree Krishna was born in the Yadava clan. Krishna’s uncle, Kamsa, was also born for this purpose. Kamsa looked up to imperial rule, believed that to be correct, and tried to destroy all this, didn't he? But because it was God's will that Kamsa's model was not right, Krishna emerged. Through a clan called the Yadava clan, this action was transformed into an action of wisdom. But it did not succeed. Therefore, they defeated us by even introducing the Devadasi system (dasiyattam) in the temple tradition. Because of this degradation, they were certain that our ancestors would only stand on this particular side. They had a firm conviction that only as much as the concept in which consciousness is fixed while performing an action will be of use to us. If you go to a plastic company and ask for gold ornaments, will you get them? Just like that, we unknowingly fell into an order. When we saw the color and attire of the object they showed us, we assigned it the value of gold. Not only that, we also desired to realize it and become it. Thus, the intelligent ones globally subdued and ruled the majority of the people within their system. Because we had this shortcoming, the British and the Mughals, who came in the prophetic tradition, were able to subjugate us. And what about those belonging to the society forged by this Vedic religion? If you look at Kerala itself, you will know; in Kozhikode, Thalassery, and Kannur, most people have become Muslims. Even today, they proudly say that they belonged to the Vedic religion, and that their ancestors were Brahmins.

[GV1:P2514] When the Mughals came here, the Vedic people became helpless. The poor people also accepted Islam. When the poor joined the Mughals, there was an anxiety that they would come to the forefront. The king, before this conversion was complete, had someone belonging to the Brahmin clan converted, and imposed ostracization (bhrashtu) on the one who went across the sea to work. Thus, he was made a Muslim. They thought that this way, their own man was not destroyed, and they could also say that he had prospered. The entire Malappuram district is like this.

[GV1:P2515] Disciple: It is said that religious conversion is also a political process, isn't it?

[GV1:P2516] Guru: Yes, it was made so. Those who were converted stood in the opposite camp and attacked us. These poor people were also caught and added to their side. Here, because of caste, one cannot walk freely, cannot eat together, cannot see each other—such meaningless actions flourished. By constantly talking about it, it spread to the lower-strata people. It became caste. God was placed within the caste—the one sitting here is my God. Your God is a little further away. This temple was consecrated by bringing a Namboothiri. In truth, there is no Tantric essence in this. It is just taking a stone, placing it, and entering a trance. Another person will say that there is a Mantramoorthi (deity of mantras) in his family. He is the smartest. When the deity comes over here in a trance, all one needs to do is chant to my Mantramoorthi once. Then nothing will happen. Yet another will say that the God in his sacred grove (kavu) is a Brahmarakshass. It has gone on worshipping Brahman. This is the real Brahmarakshass. Therefore, I will not worship any of these forests and bushes. But who will tell him how to cross his different states of being? Here, a deviation from the path occurs. But there have been paths here that clarified this deviation. As far as South India is concerned, a tradition called 'Parayi Petta Panthirukulam' (the twelve clans born to the Pariah woman) was implemented here. Each of those who belonged to it has proved different things. Even after all this knowledge came, this class called caste turned around and not only destroyed all this knowledge, but even erased their memories. Who eliminated them like this?

[GV1:P2517] Disciple: Wasn't it those who stood at the forefront?

[GV1:P2518] Guru: Yes.

[GV1:P2519] Disciple: Apart from the division between the lower castes and the upper castes, it is heard that there is division among the upper castes themselves. We hear that there was a controversy between the Iyers and the Iyengars regarding how to wear the long caste mark (Nedumkuri) on the forehead.

[GV1:P2520] Guru: All this is an absurdity forged by the Vedic religion. The Iyengar has one extra line. Then he claims that he is the greater one. The other claims, no, he is the greater one. Drawing it blindly without sense, and then studying that it is the greatest—this mischief spread again. That became the religion of the Iyengars. Ego (Ahankara) is his religion.

[GV1:P2523] Disciple: O Guru, whether it is big or small, isn't ego

[GV1:P2524] a common trait?

[GV1:P2525] Guru: God placed an absurdity to mislead the Iyengars—saying, "You play like that." And to the Iyers, "You play like this." You know how it will be. Isn't this trick called God the thing that makes the player play? "You will play like that, won't you? Then let me put down something like this"—that is how He makes them clash.

[GV1:P2526] Disciple: But, as far as we are concerned, this game is a serious matter, isn't it, Guru!

[GV1:P2527] Guru: Yes, as far as we are concerned, it is a serious matter indeed. Just because it is a matter, shouldn't we reach a state where we have to accomplish it?

[GV1:P2528] One shouldn't just create it and then try to work it out in practice. The cause must be generated. It is that cause which is being questioned today. That is what was said earlier. Through a causal action, the cause was made to happen. What is the cause? Why was this established as a cause here? When questioned like this, what we are providing is the explanation for it. Each one of you must think about how this explanation should be established and how it should not be.

[GV1:P2529] Disciple: In what the Guru just said, the flaw called ego is the cause of this division. Seeing how the division arises, what should be done so that there is no ego in this new path of ours and to make everyone cooperate in a pure manner?

[GV1:P2530] Guru: It can only be done through a small path. The opportunity hasn't arrived to do anything completely. There is a reason for that too. Earlier, we talked about each person's classifications, right—Ugramoorthi (fierce deity), Mantramoorthi, Bhadrakali, and so on. A system embracing the grotesqueness of having a thousand heads, a thousand eyes, and scooping up a thousand snakes. What would be the inner spiritual state (atmabhavam) of having worshipped all those monstrosities? Do you believe that for all these monstrosities to be destroyed, this life itself must perish? We believe that a primordial origin of such karma must exist somewhere.

[GV1:P2531] Disciple - It exists across different lifetimes.

[GV1:P2532] Guru: Yes. Therefore, our archetype is based on faith. That foundation is conceptual. This concept constitutes the mindset of karma. Giving a belief, one conceptualizes—this is my God. Even though we returned from that savage nature, cleared the forests, and established temples, what is enshrined there is still the entity that lay in the forest. We bring the elephant that lived in the forest, bathe and decorate it, sit on its back, perform antics, don costumes, establish the concept of God, and worship it. What do our grand-uncles do? Breaking several coconuts and holding the multi-tiered traditional torch (*theevetti*), assuming this ritual to be their prerogative, they wrap a large dhoti around their prominent bellies, tie a large towel over it, and walk around feeling gratified. In the region where I was born, there is an object made of screw-pine leaves used to protect oneself from the rain. It is called a *kuttil*. In some places, it is also known as a *choodal*. They just drape it over themselves. Even during strong winds and heavy rain, one does not feel cold inside it. The warmth remains trapped inside. We have unfortunately engaged in such practices. The grand-uncles fold a sack and drape it like a *kuttil*. Inside, they hold a lamp. They drape this *kuttil* over the elephant and the goddess as well. It is only after this that they hold the eight-wicked torch. No matter how much his arms ache, the grand-uncle insists on holding the largest torch himself. It would consist of eighteen to twenty-four flames. Standing holding it is a matter of great prestige for the grand-uncle. When the uncle does this, how can the successor abstain? He is compelled to hold it. Thus, we possess certain systems of worship and traditions characterized by an ignorance that has simply been passed down. Exploiting this lack of awareness, the Brahmin cleverly orchestrated everything he desired. Where did this Brahmin originate? To which race does the Brahmin who arrived from the Middle East belong?

[GV1:P2533] Disciple: Aryan.

[GV1:P2534] Guru: Let it be Aryan or whatever. What do you call it? What is your understanding regarding it? Apart from the sacred thread worn by these Brahmins, there is another item, isn't there? An item similar to what police officers wear?

[GV1:P2535] Disciple: Crossbelt.

[GV1:P2536] Guru: Exactly. These Iyengars possess it as well.

GURUVANIKAL · August 1990 · Volume 1
Malayalam source paragraphs GV1:P2538 to GV1:P2559

[GV1:P2538] August 1990

[GV1:P2539] Birthday Message

[GV1:P2540] Kings, emperors, and Brahmins possess greater qualifications to wield administrative power compared to the Shudra varna. However, these Vaishya, Kshatriya, and Brahmin rulers lack sufficient knowledge on how to manage administration in accordance with the times once they attain power. The Shudra varna also possesses the qualification to rule. But whenever they attained power, they harbored the delusion that they had become everything. Under that delusion, taking the old Vedic system itself as their model, they were prepared to rule by imitating the upper strata. Consequently, unable to do it themselves, they were forced to have the Brahmins do it for them. Additionally, there is their own *swakarma* (inherent duty). *Swakarma* is one's own duty, after all. The premise is that the result corresponds to the action. In that *karma*, the entire Shudra varna lags behind. It is merely a sort of jumping, dancing, and commotion.

[GV1:P2541] Would the present-day Sabarimala frenzy evoke any sense of devotion, affectionate intellect, reverence, or proper conduct in anyone? Similarly, building Kali temples and indulging in all sorts of undesirable acts there for pleasure has become a custom among them. There is also an obstinate belief that through festivals, God must manifest and accomplish everything. For instance, in my mother's family, there used to be a family temple. It exists even today. And it functions well to this day.

[GV1:P2542] During my childhood, there was a tradition called *Thalappoli* there. They would erect a green pandal on a ground, gather there, and the *Thalappoli* would commence from that point. Before the procession covered half the distance, I witnessed the person who bestowed blessings strike his own head with a very sharp sword in his hand, inflicting a wound upon himself, and applying holy ash and other substances once the *Thalappoli* concluded. Upon reaching the temple and checking, there was neither a wound nor even a mark of the cut visible.

[GV1:P2543] These were the methods of demonstrating tests in those days. That is exactly what the people desired as well. People derived immense exhilaration through this. However, none of this was done with true understanding. Consequently, their entire system of worship descended into such crude practices. The rituals and emotional displays associated with it are all that they know. Today, if one goes to North India, one can witness the practice of cramming everything into a very small room, conducting some form of worship there, and collecting money. This tendency is more prominent in areas where goldsmiths or carpenters reside in clusters. The Vaishyas, standing apart from both these approaches, adopted wealth accumulation and other specific schemes. The entire Shudra varna degenerated because they adopted this level of worship. This is what is meant by the result corresponding to the action. When the era turned in their favor, they were unable to adopt a corresponding form of worship or understand what the outcome of their own actions would be. But Kali (the age of Kali) will not leave without executing its dharma. It will certainly execute it. A correction and a new path are required for this.

[GV1:P2544] The new path implies cultivating good character among the people. Governance is not about inciting the entire population to commit violence and showing off by ruling the state. True administrative authority lies in the merit acquired by submitting oneself to humility, engaging in right action (*karma*), and adhering to righteousness (*dharma*).

[GV1:P2545] Not just the kings of India, but the entire Shudra varna that has existed in the world to date has engaged in this very type of governance. Only if one is born like Buddha, Jesus, the Prophet, or other such great souls can a change be brought to this style of governance. In the past and present, numerous great figures have stated very clearly that there is a place for action. We also believe in their doctrines which have been integrated into our daily experiences. However, just as we have a fundamental lack of fortune in translating them into action, we possess a nature where, no matter what we receive, we discard it and run frantically after something else.

[GV1:P2546] Only if individuals resembling the aforementioned great souls are born among the people of the present generation can actions appropriate for the times be realized. Those who are born in such a manner must be born among us ordinary people. Regardless of where they are born, it will clearly come to the forefront. It will not be like a renunciation (*sannyasa*) adopted halfway through life, a renunciation attained by sitting near a forest and performing pujas, a renunciation achieved by sitting in bhajans at a temple, or some isolated renunciation that has emerged through the systematic practice of rituals. This is a soul that stands desiring birth in a permanent state, or a soul (*karma*) born by divine decree. Sri Krishna came into being in such a manner.

[GV1:P2547] What people can take as evidence is the birth of Sri Krishna. Before the arrival of Sri Krishna, seven were killed. Krishna arrived as the eighth and implemented the dharma of the era (*yuga dharma*). But today, all of that is being intelligently reduced to vulgar spectacles along the streets through poetry and stories. Similarly, a Goddess temple is a place that must be preserved securely. By transforming it with obscenities, toddy, and fish, they have reduced it to such a perverse system of worship that its parallel cannot be found anywhere in the world. What occurs even today at the seat of Calcutta Kali? What happens in other similar Goddess temples? If a good person is born within a system that has rendered action (*karma*) in this manner, how can they be recognized? Only a Guru who is an omniscient seer of the past, present, and future (*trikalajnani*), capable of perceiving the course of karma, can awaken that realization among the people.

[GV1:P2548] Didn't everything Lord Krishna said seem like entirely new concepts to us? If such a person emerges, they will certainly have to suffer hardships. The Prophet came and suffered hardships. Jesus and Sankaracharya also suffered hardships. But there were people willing to accept the hardships suffered by Jesus and the Prophet and make sacrifices. As far as Hindus are concerned, they celebrate this with vows, dances, songs, revelry, and festivals. The concepts they have embraced belong entirely to the Treta Yuga. Or rather, they are the superficial antics manifested in the Dwapara Yuga. We remain stuck in that. The culture required to transcend this can only be attained through a preceptor (Acharya). It is not enough to merely believe in that preceptor; one must also honor and uphold them. If you only believe, you will abandon it halfway. An example of why mere belief is insufficient is the fact that Chattampi Swamikal walked to all Nair households attempting to impart ideas suited for the times, but it did not materialize. The exact same thing happened to Narayana Guru Swami as well. Sankaracharya came and advised that one should live like the children of one father. He proved in every possible way that the existing concept of 'Parayi Petta Panthirukulam' was not the right path. However, not only was the Sudra class unable to grasp it, but they also destroyed it in every conceivable manner. This is *karma*. The majority are those who assign importance to *karma* but perform contrary actions. Then what is *karma*? What is the point of saying all this to those who deliberately think they only want the wages for the work they do, and absolutely nothing beyond that?

[GV1:P2549] Another evidence is that four thousand years ago, Moses brought a new culture and attempted to impart it. What happened was that his followers were severely beaten by soldiers. It is said that when they ran after being beaten and reached the Red Sea, he struck it with his staff, parted the waters, and helped his followers cross to the other side. When the soldiers entered this path, the water rushed back in, and all of them drowned and died. Even after witnessing such profound miracles, the people could not imbibe this inclination. It was after that Jesus and the Prophet demonstrated the model of sacrifice. Until then, only an affinity towards miracles within doctrines was shown. But Jesus and the Prophet operated from the very premise of the rigid Vedanta of the Hindus, which says 'let it happen through him'. Consequently, a number of people became Muslims and Christians. Those who converted to Christianity and Islam back then were a group of ignorant people. Their knowledge was as disparate as the sea and the chaff flower (*kadalum kadaladiyum*). Yet, through the firmness of their faith and conviction, they grew to be on par with others. Moreover, they were able to win others over to their side and suppress several others. Through this, they essentially imbibed another aspect of the ignorance characteristic of Hindus.

[GV1:P2550] The unique characteristic of *Kala Dharma* is that the Sudra class gained the authority to implement the divine will (*Brahma Nischayam*). Following Lord Krishna, numerous preceptors emerged from both the Savarna and Avarna classes to implement *Kala Dharma*. But none of them succeeded. The reason for that is *karma* and the fruits of *karma* itself. Because the souls (*Jivatmas*)—who performed distorted actions instead of righteous deeds and propagated the buffoonery of mischief—carry the strength of ancestors whose positions or zodiac signs have shifted (according to astrology), along with the *karma* and *dharma* of the yogis, you too are standing right there and playing along. You are unable to move away from there. For a transformation to occur, you must grow in monotheism and act by placing faith in a lineage of Gurus capable of realization. You still have time for that. Time has not run out. We are only standing at the beginning of the Kali Yuga. It can be said that Kali has already begun. The *dharma* of Kali will not be fully established in ten or five thousand years. But there will be a change going forward.

[GV1:P2551] In Western countries, during the era when idol worship and polytheism were prevalent, when prophets introduced their doctrines, the people, unable to fully embrace them, remained trapped in their traditions. But even that much cannot be assimilated by those living adamantly in India under the guise of Sanatana Dharma or Hindu Dharma. However, this will be implemented. The children who are born and grow intelligently will implement this. The present generation will be capable of accepting them. They do not possess the ignorance of the past. They are, after all, witnesses to some form of knowledge. There is no doubt that they will continue to search as long as the past testimonies remain incomplete. If they discover something good somewhere in their search, there is no doubt that they will respect and honor what they find, transform it into *karma*, and sustain it as *dharma*. That will undoubtedly happen. Once that *karma* is realized, *dharma* will become theirs. The virtue and its sustenance will rightfully belong to them.

[GV1:P2552] In the West, they were able to accept the visionary doctrines of the prophets to a certain extent. But Indians have not yet been able to attain that standard. This is because the ignorant Sudra class only has the experience of calling it Sanatana Dharma, valuing Vedic Dharma and other lower cultures, being captivated by their buffoonery, and expending money, energy, and dominance on it. At the same time, in Western countries, even if they lacked knowledge, they were prepared to embrace sacrifice with the desire to accept the doctrine. But in India, the rulers are clinging to the base of the Vedic religion—which stands tall displaying vows, offerings, and supremacy—and crying out, 'Oh God, we have no salvation, please save us.' In situations where both Vedic authority and governance rested in the hands of the Brahmin, he alienated the Sudra due to his inherent inclination. However, since the Sudra inherently possesses an inclination for *karma*, when he acquired the right to rule, he collaborated with the Brahmin and became willing to share the victories, defeats, and dedications of war together. The Sudra's inclination for *karma* outwardly consists of elephants, howdahs, umbrellas, torches, dances, songs, and installing the father figure beneath a tree. Since even an elevated Sudra has no *karma* beyond this, there was no awareness to comprehend that the *karma* performed by the Brahmin would bring them no good or that it would ultimately destroy them. That is precisely why this *dharma* deteriorated for such an extended period. The fundamental philosophy of Santhigiri's ideology is its reclamation.

[GV1:P2553] Now, one must reflect upon how the divine will (*Brahma Nischayam*) is to be observed in *karma*. For this, there must be a pleading voice from the people: 'Father, we desire to see the birth of a masculine noble soul qualified to eradicate our destitution, gain recognition for our homes, ensure the survival of the nation, and bring goodness to the world! May God fulfill this.' Growth through a lineage of Gurus is that salvation. Thus, the *karma* of the Guru lineage that emerges according to the divine will will move towards oneness, rather than diverging into multiplicity. Furthermore, no one will be able to deny the explicit opinions expressed by the preceptor of that lineage. There may be those who deliberately deny it. All the preceptors who have appeared thus far have faced such opposition from their contemporaries. You have learned from history that contemporaries employed all conceivable methods to harass the preceptors. It must be presumed that a number of people will be prepared to do the same even now. The people must also be willing to bear a share in these hardships. But you lack the course of *karma* for that. You still harbor the unawareness to grow in the consciousness of mantras, yantras, and tantras that supposedly create miracles upon miracles, and to believe that this karmic potential will be realized through individuals like astrologers who manifest it. This unawareness is the very cause of your destitution.

[GV1:P2554] However, as far as this ideology is concerned, no matter how powerful the opponents may be, their opposition will not sustain.

[GV1:P2555] Could one have even dreamed that the imperial and capitalist regimes that previously existed in India would be replaced by a democratic administration? Yet, did it not come to pass? However, the present rulers are also committing errors. Having attained power, they govern under the delusion that it was acquired through their own astuteness. Be that as it may, let them govern. But a new regime is imminent. The previously mentioned descendants are indeed coming—the descendants born into the lineage of Gurus. They will manifest karma through the power of their command. When that karma is established, dharma will become the heritage of this Guru lineage. The inherent merit accompanying it can no longer remain concealed; it will shine forth as a lineage where merit, virtue, prosperity, and the grace of the Guru are harmoniously integrated. It will possess the moral consciousness to reclaim all lost karmas. Intelligent disciples, comprehending this, will execute their karmas with the singular contemplation of how to integrate this ideology into their lives—contemplating why they were born, why they were raised, why they must live, and why they must die. Numerous disciples possessing this awareness will emerge.

[GV1:P2556] There is an order of rituals observed by Santhigiri. The dharma of that system will be fostered through these disciples. By displacing the contemporary position of the ancestors and altering the dharma of the deity occupying that position, these disciples will integrate it into their observances, much like the verses of the *Guru Gita* enshrined within the *Skanda Purana*. Until then, it will gradually yield results. It will require three hundred and fifty years to attain complete fruition. Within that period, the Guru-disciple lineage will achieve perfection. No one will be able to repudiate this lineage. This is because whatever violent tendencies exist in the world will annihilate each other through internal conflict. It will be as though all ignorance has been entirely eradicated. Karma and dharma will be rigorously implemented in all their depth and magnitude. There are reasons why this did not materialize in the lineage of the Buddha. The Vedic scholars and kings of this land colluded covertly, simultaneously employing Vedic rituals, Tantra, Hinayana, and Mahayana, to completely eradicate that ideology from this region. Furthermore, wherever else it took root, these Vedic stratagems systematically destroyed it. However, its destruction was inevitable. For on such a profoundly corrupted cultural foundation, it is virtually impossible for such a monumental dharma to sustain itself. One must embrace those who are worthy of embrace, reject those who deserve rejection; strike those who must be struck, and execute those who must be executed—this constitutes the paradigm of governance. That paradigm did not manifest within the Buddhist culture.

[GV1:P2557] What is yet to come is not modeled after the Buddhist culture. It will strike those who must be struck and execute those who must be executed. Sri Krishna had done precisely that. Santhigiri will continue this struggle until the forthcoming paradigms of governance and dharma reach their absolute perfection.

[GV1:P2558] Yours, Swami

[GV1:P2560] August 1990

[GV1:P2561] Beloved human souls, please heed this appeal to God.

[GV1:P2562] The news we are currently receiving through newspaper columns and other media is undoubtedly capable of bringing anyone with a human heart to tears. Who would not weep at the events that occurred in Iran a few months ago, and in various other countries prior to that, as well as the news of an entire island being washed away? All those events were so heartbreaking that they compelled a priest to lament, "Father, where are you?" We have already been apprised of that news, published alongside the priest's photograph, as well as other news of similar intensity. Using microphones and notices, the Santhigiri Ashram had conducted extensive campaigns across the land, warning of an impending scarcity of rain and ensuing droughts. Following this, the likelihood of natural disasters was detailed with causal explanations through letters. This is a matter of public knowledge. Numerous individuals in the northern districts of Kerala paid utmost attention to the announcements from Santhigiri. During that period, an influx of letters from those regions continuously reached the ashram. This is also being conveyed to the lineage of ashram believers with that recollection in mind. The transformation that occurred in the state of affairs predicted by the Santhigiri Ashram within that very year was astonishing, even surpassing the forecasts of meteorological observers.

[GV1:P2563] One must reflect on whether prayer yields results

[GV1:P2564] It was nature that unleashed this devastation in Iran, Russia, and Andhra, was it not? Considering the high population density, one cannot even bear to imagine the situation if such a calamity had struck Kerala. Therefore, we must remember one thing: whatever we cast into nature must be done with the thought of God. Let those who act gently continue to do so. Even if they have amassed vast arsenals of war, because they adopt amicable stances without voluntarily preparing for war, only tens of thousands might perish in their lands where millions would have otherwise died. By the grace of God, no major wars will occur anywhere. Pray for divine grace. (As indicated earlier, the Santhigiri Ashram had prophesied impending natural disasters a year in advance, prayed for their mitigation, and urged the lineage of believers to sustain that remembrance. The resultant outcomes must also be observed in this light.) Even if a war occurs, it will only be on a minor scale. Pray for that as well.

[GV1:P2565] There is a possibility of natural disasters occurring on a massive scale; pray that their magnitude is diminished.

[GV1:P2566] Although the administrators are taking numerous measures to raise awareness among the people, they are proving ineffective. The reason for this is that the administrators are not embracing the contemplation of God. We know that many administrators have proclaimed that rivers of milk and honey would flow if they were given power. However, upon attaining power, they are unable to eradicate even the wicked thoughts of the populace. It would be prudent for human souls and administrators alike to reflect upon how even the industrial sector has been irrevocably altered. The contemplation of God is the panacea for all of this. Let us pray that the omnipresent divine forces of the world bless us by bestowing unprecedented goodness.

[GV1:P2567] A plea to those who are striving for wealth and vast fortunes. Are you unable to comprehend that the mischief your children engage in, even if temporarily, in colleges and other places is not only disgraceful but also sheer mockery that sows the seeds for their own destruction and that of the world?

[GV1:P2568] Until 1997, various kinds of hardships are likely to occur globally. Hardships of various kinds, including floods, droughts, and earthquakes. From 1997, they will begin to subside, and from 2005 onwards, tranquility will begin to prevail. As a remedy for these calamities, the people of the world are advised to abandon the concepts of deities such as Madan and Marutha, and conduct collective prayers, appealing to God within the framework of monotheism that is appropriate for this era.

[GV1:P2569] Those who deny the belief in one God* are leading an alien life. That is, they live merely to think, speak, and revel in a depraved existence. They are those who waste their lives by asserting ownership over inflicting as much oscillation as possible in the lives of the outcaste, the king, the ascetic, the wise, and the doer of action. This is the underlying motive behind their historical criticism and destruction of Gurus, and their continued destruction even today. Therefore, Vedic scholars must reflect deeply. The Vedic tradition in the Treta Yuga was conducted as a cruel sport. Need one narrate the story of a man who suffocated a thousand horses to death? The affliction known as Kali has materialized in nature, threatening to devour this human being completely. I hereby convey to you the Divine Word, a decree from the Supreme Nature of Eternal Peace, which loudly proclaims that unless you act with the consciousness that today's custom will become tomorrow's science, you are heading towards actions that will drag the entire world into destruction.

[GV1:P2570] Guruvani

[GV1:P2571] September 1990

[GV1:P2572] Guru: Most of the kings in South India are non-Brahmins. They rule according to the dictates of the Brahmins. Upon seeing a person wearing the sacred thread, if he formally prescribes a few ritualistic practices, the king immediately accords him due reverence, performs *padapuja* (washing the feet), and serves him a grand feast. If the person is slightly more learned, he is welcomed with a *nirakumbham* (a sacred full pitcher). This is considered a duty befitting the royal dignity.

[GV1:P2573] Disciple: But shouldn't this be done to a true knower of Brahman (*Brahmajñāni*)?

[GV1:P2574] Guru: Is this not a reality as well? To speak in the language of you intellectuals, is this not the reality? Do you not believe only what you can see with your own eyes? Do you not dismiss everything unseen as mere blind superstition? Therefore, it is impossible for you to perceive a true Brahmin. Are you not merely embracing a fool and degrading yourselves to the state of a dog?

[GV1:P2575] However, we have a correction for this path. That is why we have performed this *karma*. We have followed the path shown by God. As mentioned earlier, what we have here is either a lineage of billions of followers who believed under one preceptor, or the foundation of a glorious life and *karma* of that tradition. Can we discard this? Even to discard it requires divine permission. That is what is meant by saying it was shown to us.

[GV1:P2576] We discarded what needed to be discarded exactly as instructed. Such a *karma* has been established for the sake of future generations. Once one becomes part of this lineage, they can grasp (connect with) the ancestors (*pitrus*). No one else has the permission to grasp the ancestors. Only we possess that authority.

[GV1:P2577] Disciple: In the ancestral purification (*pitrushuddhi*) of the old methods—as the Guru mentioned, the practice of grasping the ancestors—such a method existed among the Hindus, didn't it? Does it not have any value at all?

[GV1:P2578] Guru: In the present context, it has no value. This is because the ancestors (*pitrus*) have been tied beneath the deities (*devas*). *Kali Yuga* is not the era of the deities. *Kali* emerged as a correction to the sage (*rishi*) tradition. It belongs to the *Shudra*. That correction must come from the *Shudra* himself. For the correction to emerge from a *Shudra*, who must he become? The *Shudra* must become a sage, a realized soul (*jnani*), and a liberated one (*mukta*). He must rise above the deities. There are several individuals mentioned in our scriptures—sages like Agastya, Pulastya, etc. They are of such nature. Twenty-five percent of them belong to the lower castes (*Shudras*). We failed to imbibe the wisdom that originated from them. Sri Krishna is the primordial Guru (*Adiguru*) of that lineage. Unable to honor Sri Krishna, we ended up in the mockery we witness today. We fell victim to the haste of transforming Krishna into Vishnu and presenting him in another form. It is no longer possible to draw anything from that. It refers to the multitude of preceptors born from then until now. Imagine, despite giving birth to so many Gurus over the past five thousand years, we could not assimilate their wisdom! The world produced individuals everywhere. Despite being born in myriad forms—as sages, realized souls, prophets, ascetics, Gurus, and yogis—we failed to understand them. However, all of them were looking backward at what their predecessors had said. Perhaps observing this, Ashan (the poet Kumaran Asan) said, "fortresses were built early on by the *Smritis*." They proved that fortresses could be built using *Shrutis* and *Smritis*. The preceptors who came before were unfortunately unable to break through this barrier. Because such a dead-end scriptural system prevailed here, if anyone came with a new idea and was seen ready to grant freedom to the poor, they did not hesitate to destroy that idea completely. Furthermore, when they looked backward, they became just like today's intellectuals.

[GV1:P2579] What are the intellectuals doing here? They are unable to control themselves or their own households. What else can they achieve then? If they groom a few youngsters to be like them, what disaster will not befall this land? Is anything else required for the downfall of a nation? They brought about *karma* merely through literacy. The Westerners achieved all this with just twenty-six letters. Growth inside a block of ice!

[GV1:P2580] We have a climate where we can survive with just a small towel (*thorthu*), or even without one if necessary. Changing all this, they made us adopt all the attires they used to protect themselves from extreme cold. And we accepted it. They provided us with every means possible to make a mockery of us. We embraced it. Thus, arriving as traders, they looted all the greatness that existed here and established plastic companies in its place. Is this not all that we have managed to achieve?

[GV1:P2581] Disciple: We have lost everything due to orthodox customs. We currently stand in a state of cultural and spiritual slavery. Can we attain liberation from that slavery through this new path of ours?

[GV1:P2582] Guru: What I am stating is a matter beyond any doubt. A gross manifestation of what can be practically implemented is established here. *Sankalpa Karma Manasa* is given as the medium of intention (*sankalpa*). That is, we have the authority to grasp the ancestors as mentioned earlier. Along with that, the authority to grasp the deity and as many ancestors who have gone under the deity's domain. The authoritative action (*karma*) that, having grasped them, grants liberation to what needs liberation, *karma* to what needs *karma*, *dharma* to what needs *dharma*, and destroys what needs to be destroyed. We are doing this much for a family. After doing this for a family, in that place, worship of God (*Ishvara Bhajana*) is given as the path of the Guru. This refers to the ancestors who have been worshipped, ranging from those placed in sacred groves (*kavus*) to the *Brahmarakshas*. Thus, the Guru represents the glory of a tradition that operates by knowing everything. What does that glory ordain? The *karma* of molding the masters of *dharma* by bringing them to the realm of wisdom-action (*jnana-karma*). Do you not understand that a family man (*dharmī*) who thus becomes the master of *dharma* is entitled to everything? This is our path.

[GV1:P2583] Guruvani

GURUVANIKAL · October 1990 · Volume 1
Malayalam source paragraphs GV1:P2584 to GV1:P2602
English line for line; each paragraph carries its Malayalam source number.

[GV1:P2584] October 1990

[GV1:P2585] Disciple: We know that it was revealed as a divine voice (*ashareeri*) that Santhigiri's is a religion of liberation.

[GV1:P2586] Guru: Yes. It is a religion of liberation. A religion that liberates all *karmas* and brings forth the reality. In bringing it forth, we are not casting it away. It is liberating itself. We only need to perform this particular *karma*. We do not need to do anything else. Even if this *karma* is driven away, it will not leave. Suppose an affectionate dog is raised in a house. If someone beats and chases it away without any reason, will it leave the house? Similarly, we are performing this *karma* with authority.

[GV1:P2587] Disciple: What is the reason for taking a dog as an example?

[GV1:P2588] Guru: We grew up like dogs, adopting the attire and language of others. Now, if we try to chase away that attire, language, *karma*, and custom by saying we don't want them, will they disappear? Aren't we merely fighting among ourselves like a pack of brawling dogs? Do you not realize that we lack even the sense of a dog? At least the dog knows it should not leave the house. But we do not have this understanding. We only have the mentality of "If you hit me, I'll show you." Even if it's a father, he shouldn't hit me unnecessarily. Just because one is a father doesn't mean he has the right to do anything. One should act with that understanding. This is our sense of freedom and sense of democracy.

[GV1:P2589] This is the direction our modernity has taken. But is there liberation from slavery through modern thinking? Liberation will not happen so suddenly. True liberation is possible only through spirituality, or the subtle realm. We are solidifying that *dharma* which is designated as *karma*. It will operate at the subtle levels of human existence.

[GV1:P2590] Disciple: How should those who join this lineage uphold this *dharma*?

[GV1:P2591] Guru: First of all, a disciplined way of life must be imparted to the family. Speaking of a disciplined way of life, hasn't the Vedic scholar provided a discipline of his own? A sorcerer has his own discipline. Similarly, we too need a discipline of our own. This does not mean completely discarding what currently exists. Let all that is old remain in its place. Without destroying any of it, we will extract its spiritual essence. However, we will certainly destroy what is base and vile. This is our modernity.

[GV1:P2592] Disciple: Does that mean the external appearance of temples and churches will remain exactly as they are?

[GV1:P2593] Guru: Yes. But, over the course of time, new principles will be introduced into them. It will only be achieved over time. As stated earlier, it will operate at subtle levels. Sudden changes will not be made in external rituals. It is also not right to attempt such changes. This is because people will become bewildered. If done so, they will be left in a state of not knowing what to do. One must seek spiritual merit through actions, and fortune through spiritual merit. That fortune will become the foundation of everything. Such fulfillment of action is our discipline and objective.

[GV1:P2594] Disciple: Could you elucidate a basic duty to be performed as a believer here? Beyond believing and gaining strength in that belief, as an individual in life, how should his behavior, love, and humility towards others be? What should be his code of conduct?

[GV1:P2595] Guru: A family consisting of his father, mother, wife, and children. In this family, there exists the course of karma performed by the ancestors. Unify them by explaining and making them understand what that course of karma is. He must also have a steadfast belief regarding knowledge, wealth, and mastery. Based on that belief and understanding, he should be guided to act by telling him that doing a particular thing is sufficient. Thus, through the Guru, the course of his karma from birth to death will be explained to him and put into practice. Then his resolve is in the Guru, his capacity for action is in the Guru, his moral strength is in the Guru; his knowledge, wealth, and mastery are in the Guru—in this way, the Guru principle has already influenced him like the Brahmasutra.

[GV1:P2596] Disciple: For that, shouldn't consciousness and action become self-evident to this individual?

[GV1:P2597] Guru: It is required, and that is exactly the level at which it is operated. That itself is what is called a Guru lineage. The Sikhs are such a steadfast lineage. Now they commit violence. The reason for that is the tenure of that Guru's path has ended. Before they started the violence, they were indeed followers of a virtuous path. Now they act in a way that makes it difficult even to say they are followers of that path. One could say violence is an instrumental cause, as the era of that Guru's path has concluded.

[GV1:P2598] People will accept our traditional growth as something beneficial to the world. To make it so, we only need to remember one thing: act with humility. It is enough not to think about destroying everything else. Whatever else exists, let it remain in its place. We hold no animosity towards anyone.

[GV1:P2599] We have our path, and our path is not one meant for conflict. If we engage in conflict, another conflict will grip us. Therefore, we should only act according to our own principles. Then we ourselves will become endowed with intellect, action, righteousness, humility, and capability. No one else will be able to destroy that. If we proceed to act peacefully, everything will come to us. This is our foundation.

[GV1:P2600] Disciple: What is the Guru's message for us?

[GV1:P2601] Guru: We lack the capacity for action. Whatever action you do, foresee it beforehand. There is no rule that only a specific action must be done; any action should be accomplished. The word received in the vision is that you have a lack of capability. Therefore, perform every action with resolve and prayer. If so, by the grace of God, everything will become complete, and our effort to build an action that can impart peace to the land, its people, and the world itself will bear fruit. Dedicate yourselves by telling, understanding, and resolving among yourselves that what we have been doing is a universal action. Otherwise, do not waste time gossiping and boasting wherever you go. The Divine Word is that prayer will yield very auspicious results. You just need to act with humility towards that word.

[GV1:P2602] Guruvani

GURUVANIKAL · November 1990 · Volume 1
Malayalam source paragraphs GV1:P2603 to GV1:P2613

[GV1:P2603] November 1990

[GV1:P2604] There are quite a few people who have experienced and understood the nature of the action taking place in Santhigiri. Even we ourselves have not been able to comprehend why this was made to be done, or to reflect upon the things that have occurred and been done up until this very moment. This is because there is no action in this that resided within us, that we had imagined, or that we had adopted by seeing some other model. It only contains a course of dharma that was continuously modified, instructed, and executed through us at every moment. In short, it contains only those actions that we never had the qualification to perform.

[GV1:P2605] This is an action over which even the Trimurti system, which replaced Manu's dharma that somehow faded away, has no authority. How has this action come to replace the action that denied Vedic rights to the Vaishya and the Shudra? It cannot be explained how. Because this action stands beyond even the laws of Manu. One must remember: the Shudra, who stands lost in the dharmic system constructed by the Vedic religion, is never going to come forward. Why? Wherever there is a festival, Chenda percussion, horse racing, and Padayani, wherever there are traditional dances (Koothu), at the forefront of all these, this Shudra stands ready to dance to the rhythm of the Chenda. Wherever there are Bhadrakali temples, the noisy rituals and administration of them are in his hands. Wherever there is a temple festival (Pooram) with elephants, these elders stand at the front, holding these twenty-four-flamed torches, bringing and spending the oil required for it, eager to maintain their status as elders. When his course of action involves sending his daughters for Thalappoli, exposing that semi-nudity before others, it is not difficult to understand what his intellect is! The justification he gives for encouraging our girls into temple dancing (Dasiyattam) is that it is a dance for the Lord. As if the Lord is that vile! Where has this course of karma led!

[GV1:P2606] To eliminate these obscenities, many great souls have come since the time of Sri Krishna. What did they intellectually turn even Sri Krishna into? The one who demonstrated all the karmas of this world through eighteen chapters and bore all the sorrow within it was depicted as what? He was depicted as the husband of sixteen thousand and eight women. It is the capability of a cunning intellectual stratagem to ensure that the Universal Guru is not accepted as such. As part of that stratagem, even the Gita Govinda has been written and published. We are the masters of a wretched course of karma that proclaims the presence of erudition, Vedanta, and heaven knows what else in all this.

[GV1:P2607] There is a poem by Changampuzha Krishna Pillai. In it, there is a double tragedy. At least four or five men and women will not fail to die in a single day. We are the ones who spread the word that this is good poetry. But what does this poem encourage? The suicide of several individuals. There are numerous cultures around us striving to cultivate such poetic imaginations. Those who watch movies exhibit modernity by killing their grandfathers. We, who depict great souls as evil, are several times worse than evil itself. We are a lineage that has become so corrupted.

[GV1:P2608] Ours is a duty bestowed by God to transform this lineage. We must accomplish it by doing it and making it done. We must understand it, and we must accumulate and provide that understanding for the world. God has given us the message that it is for the children of the world.

[GV1:P2609] There are shortcomings in all the actions we have performed so far. We are always being informed that this is because we haven't accomplished it properly. We are unable to accomplish it. But today, we have been given the courage that we can accomplish it. However, some of us still struggle until dawn and then go to sleep when it dawns. Isn't this the custom of the old Bhadrakali temple festivals? The more you struggle, the more it should remain in your hands. When it is time to reap the benefits, you should not go and fall asleep. We have been informed that if you accomplish it, you will be able to see the fruits of your actions yourself. Whether you do it here or at home, wherever you sit and do it, you must do it by acquiring the necessary merit.

[GV1:P2610] It should not be done with the presumption that one has walked alongside the Guru or interacted closely with him. One should consider that God is making us do it, and that we have been blessed with the fortune to do so. If I have received the opportunity to put a basket of soil, if I have received the opportunity to lay a stone, if I could spend a crore of rupees or even a penny for it, that is my fortune. It is that fortune that should be made useful. We are doing this to eliminate the traditional mistakes made by our ancestors. We respect the greatness that has created an institution for this. Therefore, we should think about what must be done to immerse ourselves in sacrifice as much as possible. Our actions should not be like the backstabbing of politicians.

[GV1:P2611] God has given us the course of action to make sacrifices for this lineage. Every small deed done for it must be performed with determination, strength, and prosperity. Everyone must reflect on how much courage there is in their actions.

[GV1:P2612] This fortune is not something I had known or even thought about; it just came my way as if found by chance from somewhere. What is needed is the determination to gather it up somehow. For that, what is required is not the stubbornness of fighting based on caste, religion, and class, saying "I will show you by winning, I will show you by defeating, I will show you by destroying." Whatever good is done is indeed good. Whether a learned person does it or an unlettered person does it, good is always good. Everyone must strive to undertake actions that are always inherently good.

[GV1:P2613] Guruvani

GURUVANIKAL · December 1990 · Volume 1
Malayalam source paragraphs GV1:P2614 to GV1:P2620
